「『不记得，』我说，大为诧异，因为他整张脸都因期待而涨红了。『那一天有什么值得我记起的？』他笑了笑，把脸凑近我的脸。『你可曾在戴伊街一家小饭铺里，跟一位嗓门颇高的绅士有过一小段对话——你还得不住嘴地冲他说「嘘！」——难道你不记得了？』我瞪着那人，你可想而知，心里多少以为他是个四处游荡的疯子。『我从没在戴伊街的任何饭铺里用过餐，』我断然道，一边招手叫一个侍者过来。那人看在眼里，猛地转身对着我。『你以为我会在乎你弄这等小题大做的*把戏*么？』他问，拿眼朝我唤来救场的那位身形瘦小之人一摆，同时暗暗端详我的脸，看我听了这话是什么反应。
「我猛地一惊。我忍不住；这几乎是我个人专用的一个说法，他这般用出来，分明告诉我这人对我的了解远比我想象的更深。我不由自主地挥手把那侍者打发走，转而以探询之色望向那人。」

===Original===
"'I thought you might consider it worth your while to listen,' said he, smiling with the air of one who has or thinks he has a grip upon you. Then suddenly, 'You are a rich man, are you not? a proud man and an honored one. You hold a position of trust and are considered worthy of it; how would you like men to know that you once committed a mean and dirty trick; that those white hands that have the handling of such large funds at present, have in days gone by been known to dip into such funds a little too deeply; that, in short, you, Bertram Sylvester, cashier of the Madison Bank, and looking forward to no one knows what future honors and emoluments, have been in a position better suited to a felon's cell than the trusted agent of a great and wealthy corporation?'
"I did not collar him; I was too dumb-stricken for any such display of indignation. I simply stared, feeling somewhat alarmed as I remembered my late interview with Mr. Stuyvesant, and considered the possibility of a plot being formed against me. He smiled again at the effect he had produced, and drew me into a corner of the room where we sat down. 'I am going to tell you a story,' said he, 'just to show you what a good memory I have. One day, a year and more ago, I sauntered into an eating-house on Dey Street. I have not always been what you see me now, though to tell you the truth, I was but little better off at the time of which I speak, except that I did have a dime or so in my pocket, and could buy a meal of victuals—if I wished.' And his eyes roamed for the first time to the tables stretching out before him down the room. 'The proprietor was an acquaintance of mine, and finding I was sleepy as well as hungry, let me go into a certain dark pantry, where I curled up amid all sorts of old rubbish and went to sleep. I was awakened by the sound of voices talking very earnestly. The closet in which I was hidden was a temporary affair built up of loose boards, and the talk of a couple of men seated against it was easy enough to be heard. Do you want to know what that conversation was?'

===Chinese===
「『我原想你必会觉得值得一听，』他说，带着一种——要么当真攥着你的把柄、要么自以为攥着——之人的神情一笑。接着他话锋一转：『你是个有钱人，不是么？一个骄傲的人，一个受人敬重的人。你身居一桩信托之职，众人也认为你当之无愧；倘若旁人知道你曾干过一桩卑鄙龌龊的勾当，知道你如今把持着大笔款项的那双白净之手，在过去也曾有过把手伸进这等款项、伸得稍稍过深的时候，简而言之，知道你——伯特兰·西尔维斯特，麦迪逊银行的出纳主任，前途未卜的种种荣耀与厚禄尚不知有几多在等着你——竟曾身处一个更配进囚室、而不配做一家殷实富庶的大公司之受托代理人的境地，你心里会作何感想？』
「我并未一把揪住他的衣领；我惊得哑口无言，已无从做出这等义愤之举。我只是怔怔地瞪着，一面想起方才与斯泰弗森特先生的那番对话，一面暗忖有人正设下圈套谋害我的可能，心里不由生出几分惊惧。他见自己所造成的反应，又是一笑，把我拉到屋子的一角，我们坐了下来。『我要给你讲一个故事，』他说，『只是想让你瞧瞧，我记性有多好。一年多以前的一天，我踱进戴伊街的一家小饭铺。我并非一向是你眼下所见的这副光景，不过说实话，我所讲的那个时候也好不到哪里去，唯独口袋里倒还有那么一角两角的硬币，能买一顿饭吃——只要我愿意。』他的目光这才头一回游向面前那排一直延伸到屋子深处的桌子。『那老板与我本是相识的，他见我又困又饿，便让我进了一间黑黢黢的小配餐室去，我在那堆满各式陈年破烂的角落里蜷作一团，睡了过去。我是被一阵极其热切的说话声吵醒的。我藏身的那间壁橱是临时用几块松板搭起来的，靠在它上面坐着谈话的两个人所说的话，轻易便能听得清清楚楚。你想不想知道那番对话讲的是什么？』」

===Original===
"My curiosity was roused by this time and I said yes. If this was a plot to extort money from me, it was undeniably better for me to know upon just what foundations it rested. I thought the man looked surprised, but with an aplomb difficult to believe assumed, he went on to say, 'The voices gave me my only means of judging of the age, character, or position of the men conversing, but I have a quick ear, and my memory is never at fault. From the slow, broken, nervously anxious tone of one of the men, I made up my mind that he was elderly, hard up, and not over scrupulous; the other voice was that of a gentleman, musical and yet pronounced, and not easily forgotten, as you see, sir. The first words I heard aroused me and convinced me it was worth while to listen. They were uttered by the gentleman.' 'You come to me with such a dirty piece of business! What right have you to suppose I would hearken to you for an instant!' 'The right,' returned the other, 'of knowing you have not been above doing dirty work in your life time.' The partition creaked at that, as though one of the two had started forward, but I didn't hear any reply made to this strange accusation. 'Do you think,' the same voice went on, 'that I do not know where the five thousand dollars came from which you gave me for that first speculation? I knew it when I took it, and if I hadn't been sure the operation would turn out fortunately, you would never have been the man you are today. It came out of funds entrusted to you, and was not the gift of a relative as you would have made me believe.' 'Good heaven!' exclaimed the other, after a silence that was very expressive just then and there, 'and you let me—' 'Oh we won't go into that,' interrupted the less cultivated voice. 'All you wanted was a start, to make you the successful man you have since become. I never worried much about morals, and I don't worry about them now, only when you say you won't do a thing likely to make my fortune, just because it is not entirely free from reproach, I say, remember what I know about you, and don't talk virtue to me.'

===Chinese===
「到这时我的好奇心已被勾起，便答了声愿意。倘若这是冲着我来讹钱的圈套，那么弄清它究竟立在什么样的根基之上，对我而言无疑是更为有利的。我看那人的神色似乎有些诧异，可他却以一种令人难以置信的厚颜从容接着说道：『那两人的嗓音是我判断他们年岁、品性与身份的唯一依据，好在我耳力灵锐，记性也从不出错。从其中一人那缓慢、断续、神经质般焦灼的腔调，我断定他年事已高、手头拮据、行事也并非顶讲究；另一人的嗓音则是位绅士的嗓音，悦耳而又斩截，并不易于忘怀——这您也看得出来，先生。我所听到的头几句话便叫我警觉起来，也让我深信值得一听。那几句话是那位绅士说的。』「你带着这么一桩肮脏的买卖来找我！你凭什么以为我会听你哪怕片刻！」『凭的是，』另一位答道，『我知道你平生也并非不曾干过龌龊的勾当。』隔板在那里头嘎吱一响，仿佛两人之中有一人猛地向前一扑，可我没听见这一句古怪的指控有什么回音。『你以为，』仍是方才那个嗓音接着说，『我不知道你给我做头一桩投机的那五千块钱是从哪儿来的吗？我接那钱的时候便知道，要不是有把握这桩买卖能成事，你绝不会有今日这般的局面。那钱是从托付给你的款项里挪出来的，并非像你哄我相信的那样，是哪位亲戚的赠与。』『天哪！』另一位沉默了片刻才失声喊道——那阵沉默在彼时彼地颇有意谓——『你竟由着我——』『噢，这个我们不提了，』那个教养较差的嗓音打断道。『你想要的不过是个发家的由头，好叫你成为日后那样一个成功之人。我从不太把道德放在心上，如今也不放在心上，只是当你说你不肯做一桩能叫我发财的事、仅仅因为这事的并非全然无可指摘之时，我便要说，你且记着我知道你的那些底细，莫要跟我谈什么操守。』」

===Original===
"'I am rightly punished,' came from the other, in a tone that proved him to be a man more ready to do a wrong thing than to face the accusation of it. 'If I ever did what you suppose, the repentance that has embittered all my success, and the position in which you have this day placed me, is surely an ample atonement.' 'Will you do what I request?' inquired the other, giving little heed to this expression of misery, of which I on the contrary took special heed. 'No,' was the energetic reply; 'because I am not spotless it is no sign that I will wade into filth. I will give you money as I have done scores of times before, but I will lend my hand to no scheme which is likely to throw discredit on me or mine. Were you not connected to me in the way in which you are—' 'You would pursue the scheme,' interrupted the other; 'it is because you know that I cannot talk, that you dare repudiate it. Well I will go to one—' 'You shall not,' came in short quick tones, just such tones as you used to me, sir, when we first entered this room. 'You shall leave the country before you do anything more, or say anything more, to compromise me or yourself. I may have done wrong in my day, but that is no reason why I should suffer for it at your hands, tempter of youth, and deceiver of your own flesh and blood! *You* shall never bring back those days to me again; they are buried, and have been stamped out of sight by many an honest dealing since, and many as I trust before God, good and sterling action. I have long since begun a new life; a life of honor, and pure, if successful, dealing. Not only my own happiness, but that of one who should be considered by you, depends upon my maintaining that life to the end, unshadowed by unholy remembrances, and unharrassed by any such proffers as you have presumed to make to me here today. If you want a few thousand dollars to leave the country, say so, but never again presume to offend my ears, or those of anyone else we may know, with any such words as you have made use of today.' And the spiritless creature subsided, sir, and said no more to that rich, honored, and successful man who was so sensitive to even the imputation of guilt.

===Chinese===
「『我这是自作自受，』另一位说道，语调之中表明他这个人宁愿做下错事，也不愿直面别人对此的指斥。『若我果真做过你所揣度的那等事，那么令我一切成功都染上苦味的悔恨，再加上你今日把我逼入的境地，想来已是够充分的赎罪了。』「你愿不愿做我所求之事？」另一位追问道，对这一番痛苦之辞全不在意，我倒是恰恰相反，格外留了心。『不，』是斩钉截铁的回答；『我纵非白璧无瑕，也并不表示我便肯涉足污浊。我可以给你钱，正如我从前几十次所做的那样，但我绝不会把一只手伸进任何可能使我和我家人蒙羞的勾当里。要不是你与我有着如今这层关系——』「你便会着手那桩勾当，」另一位打断道；「正是因为你知道我开不得口，你才敢把它推个一干二净。好，我便去找一个——」「你休想，」几个短促而凌厉的字眼冲了过来，正是您，先生，初次进这间屋子之时用来对付我的那种字眼。「在做下任何更多之事、说出任何更多之话、连累我又或连累你自己之前，你得先离开这个国家。我平生或曾有过不是，可这并不是我便该在你手里为此吃苦头的理由，你这引诱少年入歧途的人，你这蒙骗自己亲骨肉的人！*你*休想再把那些日子重新带回我的眼前；它们早已埋葬，早已被此后的许多次清白交易，以及许多次——我在上帝面前敢说是——善良而敦实的行为踩入地下，不见天日。我早已开始了新的生活；一种体面的生活，纵然谈得上成功，也清清白白。不仅是我的幸福，还有一个——本也该被你记挂的人——的幸福，都系于我把这种生活维持到底，不为不洁的回忆投下阴影，也不受你今日在此竟敢向我提出的这等提议所滋扰。若是你想要几千块钱离开这个国家，你只管开口，可你休想再放肆地用你今日所说的这等话，来冒犯我的耳朵，或冒犯任何我们可能认识之人的耳朵。」那个毫无骨气的人便偃旗息鼓了，先生，再没对那个富有、受人敬重、功成名功、却连一丝罪名的影都忌惮万分的男人多说半个字。」

===Original===
"But I am not spiritless and just where he dropped the affair, I took it up. 'Here is a chance for me to turn an honest penny,' thought I, and with a deliberation little to be expected of me, perhaps, set myself to spot that man and make the most out of the matter I could. Unfortunately I lost the opportunity of seeing his face. I was too anxious to catch every word they uttered, to quit my place of concealment till their conversation was concluded, and then I was too late to be sure which of the many men leaving the building before me was the one I was after. The waiters were too busy to talk, and the proprietor himself had taken no notice. Happily as I have before said, I never forget voices; moreover one of the two speakers had made use of a phrase peculiar enough to serve as a clue to his identity. It was in answer to some parting threat of the older man, and will remind you of an expression uttered by yourself an hour or so ago. 'Do you suppose I will let such a little fuss as that deter me?' It was the cue to his speech, by which I intended to hunt out my man from amongst the rich, the trusted and the influential persons of this city, and when found, to hold him.'

===Chinese===
「『可我并非没有骨气，他丢下这档子事的地方，恰恰是我把它拾起来的地方。『这可是我赚几个干净钱的好机会，』我心想，于是以一种——也许不大像是我会有的——那般沉着，定意要盯牢那个人，并把这桩买卖里头能榨出的油水尽数榨出来。不幸的是，我错失了看见他面孔的机会。我太急于听清他们说的每一个字，不肯在他们谈话结束之前离开藏身之处，而等我出来已为时太晚，无从确定在我之前离屋的那许多人之中，究竟哪一个才是我所要找的人。侍者们忙得没工夫搭理，老板本人也未曾留意。所幸——正如我方才所说——我从不忘却嗓音；何况那两个说话人之中，有一个用过一句相当独特、足以当作追查其身份之线索的话语。那是对那年长之人临别威胁的回敬，且会令您想起您一个钟头前后所说的一句。『你以为我会让那点区区小题大做绊住我么？』这正是他言语的招牌，我打算凭此从本城那些富有的、受信的、有头有脸的人物里头，把我那位『先生』猎出来，一旦猎到，便攥在手里。』」

===Original===
"'And you think you have done this?' said I, too conscious of the possible net about my feet to be simply angry. 'I know it,' said he; 'every word you have uttered since we have been here has made me more and more certain of the fact. I could swear to your voice, and as to your use of that telltale word, it was not till I thought to inquire of a certain wide-awake fellow downtown, who amongst our business men were in the habit of using that expression, and was told Mr. Sylvester of the Madison Bank, that I was enabled to track you. I know I have got my hand on my man at last and—' He looked down at his threadbare coat and around at the tables with their smoking dishes, and left me to draw my own conclusion.
"Uncle, there are crises in life which no former experience teaches you how to meet. I had arrived at such a one. Perhaps you can understand me when I say I was well nigh appalled. Denial of what was imputed to me might be wisdom and might not. I felt the coil of a deadly serpent about me, and knew not whether it was best to struggle or to simply submit. The man noted the effect he had made and complacently folded his arms. He was of a nervous organization and possessed an eye like a hungry wolf, but he could wait. 'This is a pretty story,' said I at last, and I reject it altogether. 'I am an honest man and have always been so; you will have to give up your hopes of making anything out of me.' 'Then you are willing,' said he, 'that I should repeat this story to one of the directors of your bank, whom I know?'

===Chinese===
「『那么你以为你已经得手了？』我说，我对脚下或已布下的罗网太过清醒，已不能仅仅是发怒。『我晓得是得手了，』他说；『自我们到了这里，你所说的每一个字，都越发令我确信这一事实。我敢凭你的嗓音起誓，至于你用那句露了底的字眼——我是直到想起去向城里某个消息灵通的小子打听、问我们的商界人物里头是谁惯用这种说法，并被告知是麦迪逊银行的西尔维斯特先生之时，才得以循线追到你。我晓得我终于把手按到了我所要找的人身上，并且——』他低头看了看自己那件磨得露了线的旧外套，又环顾四周那些热气腾腾的菜肴，余下的话便让我自己去体会了。
「叔叔，人这一生有些关口，是从前任何经历都未曾教会你如何应对的。我已到了这样的一个关口。也许你能体会我的意思——当我说我几乎惊惶失措之时。对我所被指称之事加以否认，也许是明智，也许不是。我只觉一条毒蛇已将身子盘绕在我身上，却不知挣扎的好，还是俯首听命的好。那人把他所造成的效果看在眼里，得意地把双臂抱了起来。他的神经质颇为敏锐，一双眼睛像饿狼一般，可他能等。『倒是一段好听的故事，』我终于说道，且我全然不予承认。『我是个诚实人，且一向如此；你休想从我身上捞到什么好处，这念头你只得打消。』「那么你甘愿，」他说，『让我把这故事去跟你那家银行的一位董事——我认识他——复述一遍了？』」

===Original===
"I looked at him; he returned my gaze with a cold nonchalence more suggestive of a deep laid purpose, than even his previous glance of feverish determination. I immediately let my eye run over his scanty clothing and loose flowing hair and beard. 'Yes,' said I, with as much sarcasm as I knew how to assume, 'if you dare risk the consequences, I think I may.' He at once drew himself up. 'You think,' said he, 'that you have a commonplace adventurer to deal with; that my appearance is going to testify in your favor; that you have but to deny any accusation which such a hungry-looking, tattered wretch as I, may make, and that I shall be ignominiously kicked out of the presence into which I have forced myself; that in short I have been building my castle in the-air. Mr. Sylvester, I am a poor devil but I am no fool. When I left Dey Street on the twenty-fifth of February two years ago, it was with a sealed paper in my pocket, in which was inscribed all that I had heard on that day. This I took to a lawyer's office, and not being, as I have before said, quite as impecunious in those days as at present, succeeded in getting the lawyer, whom I took care should be a most respectable man, to draw up a paper to the effect that I had entrusted him with this statement—of whose contents he however knew nothing—on such a day and hour, to which paper a gentleman then present, consented at my respectful solicitation to affix his name as witness, which gentleman, strange to say, has since proved to be a director of the bank of which you are the present cashier, and consequently the very man of all others best adapted to open the paper whose seal you profess to be so willing to see broken.'

===Chinese===
「我看着他；他以一种冷冷的漫不经心回望我，那神情比他先前那热病般决绝的一眼，更暗示着一桩蓄谋已久的图谋。我随即让目光从他单薄的衣衫、蓬乱的长发与胡须上一路扫过。『是啊，』我说，尽量摆出我所能装出的讽刺之态，『倘若你敢冒那后果，我想我倒甘愿。』他当即挺直了身子。『你以为，』他说，『你所对付的不过是个寻常的冒险家；以为我这副尊容会替你作证；以为你只需否认这么个饿相毕露、衣衫褴褛的可怜虫所提出的任何指控，我便会被一脚踢出我硬闯进来的这间屋子；以为简而言之，我不过是在空中盖楼阁罢了。西尔维斯特先生，我是个穷光蛋，可我不是傻子。两年前的二月二十五日，我离开戴伊街之时，口袋里揣着一份封好的文件，里头记下了我那日所听见的全部内容。我把它带到了一家律师事务所以——而且我那时并不像如今这般一文不名——竟说动了那位律师——我特意挑了一位极有声望的人——草拟了一份文书，言明我曾于某日某时将这份陈述托付于他——至于其中写的是什么，他却一无所知——这份文书，又有一位当时在场的绅士，在我恭敬的恳求之下，同意签下他的名字作为见证；而这位绅士——说来也奇——后来竟被发现是您如今充任出纳主任的那家银行的一位董事，于是乎，在所有的人当中，他便恰恰是最适合拆开那份您口口声声那么乐于见其封印被毁的文件之人了。』」

===Original===
"'His name!' It was all that I could say. 'Stuyvesant,' cried the man, fixing me with his eye in which I in vain sought for some signs of secret doubt or unconscious wavering. I rose; the position in which I found myself was too overwhelming for instant decision. I needed time for reflection, possibly advice—from you. A resolution to brave the devil must be founded on something more solid than impulse, to hold its own unmoved. I only stopped to utter one final word and ask one leading question. 'You are a smart man,' said I, 'and you are also a villain. Your smartness would give you food and drink, if you exercised it in a manner worthy of a man, but your villainy if persisted in, will eventually rob you of both, and bring you to the prison's cell or the hangman's gallows. As for myself, I persist in saying that I am now and always have been an honest man, whatever you may have overheard or find yourself capable of swearing to. Yet a lie is an inconvenient thing to have uttered against you at any time, and I may want to see you again; if I do, where shall I find you?' He thrust his hand into his pocket and drew out a small slip of folded paper, which he passed to me with a bow that Chesterfield would have admired. 'You will find it written within,' said he 'I shall look for you any time tomorrow, up to seven o'clock. At that hour the lawyer of whom I have spoken, sends the statement which he has in his possession to Mr. Stuyvesant.' I nodded my assent, and he moved slowly towards the door. As he did so, his eyes fell upon a roll of bread lying on a counter. I at once stepped forward and bought it. Vile as he was, and deadly as was the snare he contemplated drawing about me, I could not see that wolfish look of hunger, and not offer him something to ease it. He took the loaf from my hands and bit greedily into it but suddenly paused, and shook his head with a look like self-reproach, and thrusting the loaf under his arm, turned towards the door with the quick action of one escaping. Instantly, and before he was out of sight or hearing, I drew the attention of the proprietor to him. 'Do you see that man?' I asked. 'He has been attempting a system of blackmail upon me.' And satisfied with thus having provided a witness able of identifying the man, in case of an emergency, I left the building.

===Chinese===
「『那人姓甚名谁！』这便是我所能说出的全部了。『斯泰弗森特，』那人喊道，一双眼睛定定地锁住我，我徒然在那眼里寻一丝暗藏的疑虑或无意识的动摇，却一无所获。我站起身来；我所陷入的境地太过压倒一切，不容人立时决断。我需要时间思量，也许还需要——向你来讨个主意。要胆敢与那魔鬼相抗，所下的决心必须立在比一时冲动更为坚实的根基之上，方能岿然不动。我仅仅停下来留下一句临别之言，又问了一个关键之问。『你是个精明人，』我说，『可你同时也是一个恶棍。你这份精明若是用得像个堂堂男儿，原可换得你的饮食；可你这恶棍行径若是一意孤行下去，迟早会把这两样一并夺走，把你送进囚室，又或送上绞架。至于我，我偏要说，我如今是个诚实人，且一向如此，无论你可能偷听到了什么、又或自以为能凭之起誓。然而一句谎言，在何时被人安到头上都是一桩麻烦事，我说不定还要再见你一面；若当真要见，我去哪里寻你？』他把手伸进口袋，摸出一张折叠的小纸条，一鞠身递到我手里，那鞠身的姿态切斯特菲尔德见了一定赞赏。『上面写着呢，』他说，『明日任何时辰，七点之前，我恭候您大驾。一到七点，我所说到的那位律师，便会将他手头的那份陈述寄交斯泰弗森特先生。』我点头应允，他便缓步向门口走去。正在这时，他的目光落在柜台上的一卷面包上。我当即上前把它买了下来。他纵然卑劣，他所盘算着要套到我身上的罗网纵然致命，可我见了那饿狼般的神色，却不能不递上一点东西为他解一解。他从我手中接过那卷面包，贪婪地一大口咬下去，却突然顿住，摇了摇头，那神情像是自责，把面包往腋下一夹，便以一个逃命之人的利落身段转向门口。我当下里，趁他还在视野与听觉所及的范围之内，便把老板的注意引到了他身上。『你看见那个人了吗？』我问，『他方才一直在对我施以一套讹诈之术。』就这样心满意足地安排下了一个在紧急之时能够指认此人的见证人之后，我便离开了那间屋子。」

===Original===
"And now you know it all," concluded he; and the silence that followed the utterance of those simple words, was a silence that could be felt.

===Chinese===
「如此，你便尽知了，」他收尾道；这句简简单单的话说罢，随之而来的是一阵寂静——一阵几乎能叫人觉察到的寂静。

---

===Original===
"Bertram?"
The young man started from his fixed position, and his eyes slowly traversed toward his uncle.
"Have you that slip of paper which the man gave you before departing?"
"Yes," said he.
"Let me have it, if you please."
The young man with an agitated look, plunged his hand into his pocket, drew out the small note and laid it on the table between them. Mr. Sylvester let it lie, and again there was a silence.
"If this had happened at any other time," Bertram pursued, "one could afford to let the man have his say; but now, just as this other mystery has come up—"
"I don't believe in submitting to blackmail," came from his uncle in short, quick tones.

===Chinese===
「伯特兰？」
年轻人从那呆立的姿势里一惊而起，目光缓缓转向叔父这边。
「那人临走之前给你的那张纸条，可在你身上？」
「在。」他说。
「请把它给我。」
年轻人神色激动，把手伸进口袋，摸出那张小纸条，搁在两人之间的桌上。西尔维斯特先生任它搁在那里，一时又是无言。
「这事若是在别个时候发生，」伯特兰接着说，「人倒也由得那家伙去说他的；可偏在眼下这另一桩疑案刚刚冒头之时——」
「我可不主张向讹诈低头。」短促而凌厉的几个字从叔父嘴里蹦了出来。

===Original===
Bertram gave a start. "You then advise me to leave him alone?" asked he, with unmistakable emotion.
His uncle dropped the hand which till now he had held before his face, and hastily confronted his nephew. "You will have enough to do to attend to the other matter without bestowing any time or attention upon this. The man that robbed Mr. Stuyvesant's box, can be found and must. It is the one indispensable business to which I now delegate you. No amount of money and no amount of diligence is to be spared. I rely on you to carry the affair to a successful termination. Will you undertake the task?"
"Can you ask?" murmured the young man, with a shocked look at his uncle's changed expression.
"As to this other matter, we will let it rest for tonight. Tomorrow's revelations may be more favorable than we expect. At all events let us try and get a little rest now; I am sure we are both in a condition to need it."

===Chinese===
伯特兰猛地一惊。「那么你是劝我不要去招惹他？」他带着一种不容错认的激切之情问道。
他的叔父放下方才一直遮在脸前的那只手，急急地直面他的侄子。「光是料理那另一桩事已够你忙的了，不必再在这上头浪费半点工夫和心神。盗走斯泰弗森特先生箱中物的那个人，能找出来，也必须找出来。这便是我眼下委派于你的唯一一桩不可推卸之事。无论花多少钱、费多少心力，都在所不惜。我将此事全权托付于你，务求办得妥帖圆满。你可愿担下这桩差事？」
「您还要问吗？」年轻人喃喃道，看见叔父那变了的神情，一脸的骇然。
「至于那另一桩事，今晚我们就先搁一搁。明日或有比我们所料更为有利的揭示也说不定。无论如何，且让我们现在稍事歇息；我敢说，以你我眼下的光景，都是该歇一歇的了。」

===Original===
Bertram rose. "I am at your command," said he, and moved to go. Suddenly he turned, and the two men stood face to face. "I have no wish," pursued he, "to be relieved of my burden at the expense of anyone else. If it is to be borne by anyone, let it be carried by him who is young and stalwart enough to sustain it." And his hand went out involuntarily towards his uncle.
Mr. Sylvester took that hand and eyed his nephew long and earnestly. Bertram thought he was going to speak, and nerved himself to meet with fortitude whatever might be said. But the lips which Mr. Sylvester had opened, closed firmly, and contenting himself with a mere wring of his nephew's hand, he allowed him to go. The slip of paper remained upon the table unopened.
That night as Paula lay slumbering on her pillow, a sound passed through the house. It was like a quick irrepressible cry of desolation, and the poor child hearing it, started, thinking her name had been called. But when she listened, all was still, and believing she had dreamed, she turned her face upon her pillow, and softly murmuring the name that was dearest to her in all the world, fell again into a peaceful sleep.
But he whose voice had uttered that cry in the dreary emptiness of the great parlors below, slept not.

===Chinese===
伯特兰站起身。「我听您差遣。」他说着，便要告辞。忽然他又转过身来，叔侄二人面对面立着。「我并不愿，」他接着说，「把这副担子从我自己肩上卸下来、转嫁到旁人身上。若是这副担子非得有人来扛，那便让它由一个年轻健壮、扛得起它的人来扛吧。」他的手不由自主地朝叔父伸了出去。
西尔维斯特先生握住那只手，久久地、恳切地端详着他的侄子。伯特兰以为他要开口，便暗暗振作精神，预备以坚忍迎受任何可能说出的话。然而西尔维斯特先生那张开的双唇，却又坚定地合上了，他仅仅用力握了握侄子的手，便放他去了。那张纸条仍旧搁在桌上，原封未启。
那夜，宝拉侧卧枕上酣眠之时，一个声响穿过了整座宅子。那像是一声短促的、再也按捺不住的凄凉呼喊，可怜的孩子听见了，猛地一惊，还以为是有人在叫她的名字。可她侧耳细听，一切却又寂然无声，便只当自己是做了梦，把脸重新埋进枕头，轻轻唤着那于她比全世界都更可亲的名字，重又沉沉地睡熟了。
然而，那个在楼下空旷寂寥的大客厅里发出这一声呼喊的人，却彻夜未眠。

## XIV A Day at the Bank / 十四 银行里的一天

===Original===
> "There's a divinity that shapes our ends,
> Rough-hew them how we will."

There are days when the whole world seems to smile upon one without stint or reservation. Bertram Sylvester wending his way to the bank on the morning following the reception, was a cheerful sight to behold. Youth, health, hope spake in every lineament of his face and brightened every glance of his wide-awake eye. His new life was pleasant to him. Bach, Beethoven and Chopin were scarcely regretted now by the ambitious assistant cashier of the Madison Bank, with a friend in each of its directors and a something more than that in the popular president himself. Besides he had developed a talent for the business and was in the confidence of the cashier, a somewhat sickly man who more than once had found himself compelled to rely upon the rapidly maturing judgment of his young associate, in matters oftentimes of the utmost importance. The manner in which Bertram found himself able to respond to these various calls, convinced him that he had been correct in his opinion of his own nature, when he informed his uncle that music was his pleasure rather than his necessity.

===Chinese===
> 「有一种神明塑造我们的结局，
> 不论我们如何粗凿，终归徒然。」

世上有那样一些日子，整个世界仿佛对一个人毫无保留、毫不吝啬地微笑着。招待会过后的那个上午，伯特兰·西尔维斯特（Bertram Sylvester）一路往银行走去，看上去便是一幅叫人见了便心生愉悦的光景。青春、健康与希望写在他面貌的每一根线条里，点亮了他那双警醒眼睛的每一道目光。这种新生活让他觉得惬意。巴赫、贝多芬和肖邦，此刻已几乎不再为这位雄心勃勃的麦迪逊银行（Madison Bank）助理出纳员所怀念——他在各位董事那里都各有一位朋友，而在那位深得人心的行长本人那里，所得的更不止于友谊。况且他已在这门营生上显露出了一种天分，也得到了那位出纳员的信任——那是一个身子颇为单薄的人，不止一次发觉自己不得不在若干往往至关紧要的事务上，仰仗这位年轻同事那迅速成熟起来的判断力。伯特兰发觉自己竟能从容应对这林林总总的差使，这使他更加确信自己当初对叔父所言不谬：音乐于他不过是所好，而非所需。

===Original===
Entering the building by way of Pearl Street, he was about to open the door leading into the bank proper, when he heard a little piping voice at his side, and turning, confronted the janitor's baby daughter. She was a sweet and interesting child, and with his usual good nature Bertram at once stopped to give her a kiss.

"I likes you," prattled she as he put her down again after lifting her up high over his head, "but I likes de oder one best."

"I hope the other one duly appreciates your preference," laughed he, and was again on the point of entering the bank when he felt or thought he felt a hand laid on his arm. It was the janitor himself this time, a worthy man, greatly trusted in the bank, but possessed of such an extraordinary peculiarity in the way of a pair of protruding eyes, that his appearance was always attended by a shock.

===Chinese===
他从珍珠街（Pearl Street）那头走进大楼，正要推开通往银行正堂的那扇门，忽听见身旁一个细细尖尖的孩童嗓音；一回头，正遇上那个看门人的小女儿。她是个又甜又惹人疼的孩子，伯特兰照例一副好脾气，立刻停下身来，俯下去亲了她一下。

「我喜欢你，」他把她高举过头顶、又重新放下后，她咿咿呀呀地说，「可我更喜欢那一个。」

「但愿那一位没有辜负你的偏爱。」他笑道，正要再度进门，忽然觉得——或者自以为觉得——有一只手搭上了他的胳膊。这回是那看门人本人了；他是个为人厚道、在银行里极受信任的人，可偏偏长着一对极其古怪的凸眼睛，那副模样生得实在特别，每回叫人见着，总不免要吓一跳。

===Original===
"Well, Hopgood, what is it?" cried Bertram, in his cheery tone.

The janitor drew back and mercifully shifted his gaze from the young man's face. "Nothing sir; did I stop you? Beg pardon," he continued, half stammering, "I'm dreadful awkward sometimes." And with a nod he sidled off towards his little one whom he confusedly took up in his arms.

===Chinese===
「喂，霍普古德（Hopgood），什么事？」伯特兰用他那明快的腔调喊道。

看门人往后缩了一步，算是发慈悲地把目光从那年轻人的脸上移开了。「没事，先生；我挡着您了吗？失敬，」他半磕巴着往下说，「我这个人有时候笨手笨脚得要命。」说着点了下头，便侧着身子朝他的小女儿挪过去，迷迷糊糊地把孩子抱进了怀里。

===Original===
Now Bertram was sure the man had touched him and that, too, with a very eager hand, but being late that morning and consequently in somewhat of a hurry, he did not stop to pursue the matter. Hastening into the Bank, he assisted the teller in opening the safe, that being his especial duty, and was taking out such papers as he himself required, when he was surprised to catch another sight of those same extraordinary organs of which I have just spoken, peering upon him from the door by which he had previously entered. They vanished as soon as he encountered them, but more than once during the morning he perceived them looking upon him from various quarters of the bank, till he felt himself growing seriously annoyed, and sending for the man, asked him what he meant by this unusual surveillance. The janitor seemed troubled, flushed painfully and fixed his eyes in manifest anxiety on the cashier who, engaged in some search of his own, was just handling over the tin boxes that lined the vault before them. Not till he had seen him shove them back into their place and leave the spot, did he venture upon his reply. "I'm sure, sir, I'm very sorry if I have annoyed you, but do you think Mr. Sylvester will be down at the usual hour?"

===Chinese===
伯特兰这会儿已确信那人方才确曾碰过他，而且用的还是一只极其急切的手；只是那天早上他起得迟，正有些赶，便没停下追究。他匆匆进了银行，帮着那个出纳员把保险柜打开——这本是他分内的差使——又把自己要用的几份单据往外拿，却冷不防又瞥见了方才我说到的那对非同寻常的眼珠子，正从他自己先前走进来的那扇门后头朝他窥视。待他目光一与之相接，那对眼珠便即刻消失了。可那一上午，他不只一次又察觉到它们从银行各处投向他，直到他觉得当真恼了起来，便差人把那看门的叫来，问他这般反常的盯梢究竟是什么意思。看门人似乎很是为难，痛苦地涨红了脸，目光显然焦灼地落在那位出纳员身上——出纳员正忙着寻自己的什么东西，恰好伸手在动他们面前那保险库里一排锡匣子。直等到看见他把匣子推回原处、离开了那地方，他才敢开口答话。「我敢说，先生，要是我扰了您，我实在对不住得很；可您看西尔维斯特先生今儿还会照往常的钟点下来吗？」

===Original===
"I know of no reason why he should not," returned Bertram.

"I have something to say to him when he comes in," stammered the man, evidently taken aback by Bertram's look of surprise. "Will you be kind enough to ring the bell the first moment he seems to be at leisure? I don't know as it is a matter of any importance but—" He stopped, evidently putting a curb upon himself. "Can I rely on you, sir?"

===Chinese===
「据我所知，他没有不下来的道理。」伯特兰答道。

「等他进来，我有几句话要跟他说。」那人磕磕巴巴地说，显然被伯特兰惊讶的眼神吓了一跳。「等他一得空，您肯不肯赏个脸，替我拉一下铃？我也不知道这事算不算要紧，可是——」他打住了，显然在竭力按捺自己。「我能指望您吗，先生？」

===Original===
"Yes, certainly, I will tell my uncle when he comes in that you want to speak to him. He will doubtless send for you at once."

The man looked embarrassed. "Excuse me, sir, but that's just what I'd rather you wouldn't do. Mr. Sylvester is always very busy and he might think I wished to annoy him about some matters of my own, sir, as indeed I have not been above doing at odd times. If you would ring when he comes in, that is all I ask."

===Chinese===
「会的，自然会的；等叔父进来，我便告诉他你有话同他说。他想必会立刻着人传你去。」

那人神情颇为窘迫。「失敬了，先生，可您若不那样做，我才更感激。西尔维斯特先生向来十分忙碌，他只当我又想为着自己的一点私事去搅扰他，先生——说句实话，这种事从前后院里零零碎碎的时辰，我也确乎不是没做过。只要等他进来时您肯拉一下铃，我所求的便只这一桩。」

===Original===
Bertram thought this a strange request, but seeing the man so anxious, gave the required promise, and the janitor hurried off. "Curious!" muttered Bertram. "Can anything be wrong?" And he glanced about him with some curiosity as he went to his desk. But everyone was at his post as usual and the countenances of all were equally undisturbed.

===Chinese===
伯特兰觉得这一请求古怪得很，但见那人急成那副模样，便依他所请应承下来，看门人随之匆匆去了。「蹊跷！」伯特兰咕哝了一声，「莫不是出了什么事？」他朝四下里扫了一眼，带了几分狐疑，走向自己的办公桌。可每个人都照旧在各自的位子上，众人的面色也无不泰然如常。

===Original===
It was a busy morning and in the rush of various matters Bertram forgot the entire occurrence. But it was presently recalled to him by hearing someone remark, "Mr. Sylvester is late today," and looking up from some papers he was considering, he found it was a full hour after the time at which his uncle was in the habit of appearing. Just then he caught still another sight of the protruding eyes of Hopgood staring in upon him from the half-opened door at the end of the bank.

"The fellow's getting impatient," thought he, and experienced a vague feeling of uneasiness.

===Chinese===
那一上午诸事繁杂，伯特兰在种种事务的忙乱里，把方才那桩事整个儿忘了。可不一会儿，它又被勾了起来——他听见有人说了一句「西尔维斯特先生今天来迟了」，从手边正审阅的几份单据上抬起头来，才发现已过了叔父惯常到行的时间整整一个钟头。就在这时，他又一次瞥见霍普古德那双凸出的眼珠，从银行那一头半掩着的门后头朝他直瞪。

「这汉子等得不耐烦了。」他心想，只觉一阵隐隐的不安。

===Original===
Another half hour passed. "What can have detained Mr. Sylvester?" cried Mr. Wheelock the cashier, hastily approaching Bertram.

"There is to be an important meeting of the Directors today, and some of the gentlemen are already coming in. Mr. Sylvester is not accustomed to keep us waiting."

"I don't know, I am sure," returned Bertram, remembering with an accession of uneasiness, the abruptness with which his uncle had left the entertainment the evening before.

===Chinese===
又过了半个钟头。「西尔维斯特先生究竟能被什么事绊住了？」出纳员威洛克（Wheelock）先生匆匆朝伯特兰走来，失声说道。

「今天董事们还有一次要紧的会议，有几位先生已经进来了。西尔维斯特先生向来不是叫人干等的。」

「我实在说不上来。」伯特兰答道，心头那一股不安又添了几分——他记起了前一夜叔父从那场宴会上离席时的仓促。

===Original===
"Shall I telegraph to the house?"

"No, that is not necessary. Besides Folger says he passed him on Broadway this morning."

"Going down street with a valise in his hand," that gentlemen quietly put in. Folger was the teller. "He was looking very pale and didn't see me when I nodded."

"What time was that?" asked Bertram.

"About twelve; when I went out to lunch."

===Chinese===
「要不要往宅子里拍个电报？」

「不必，没那个必要。况且福尔杰说，今早在百老汇还瞧见他来着。」

「手里拎着一只旅行包，往南街上走。」那位先生不动声色地插了一句。福尔杰（Folger）便是那个出纳员。「他脸色瞧着很白，我冲他点头，他也没瞧见我。」

「那是几点的事？」伯特兰问。

「十二点光景；我出去吃午饭那会儿。」

===Original===
A quick gasp sounded at their side, followed by a hurried cough. Turning, Bertram encountered for the fifth time the eyes of Hopgood. He had entered unperceived by the small door that separated the inner enclosure from the outer, and was now standing very close to them, eying with sidelong looks the safe at their back, the faces of the gentleman speaking, yes, and even the countenances of the clerks, as they bent busily over their books.

"Did you ring, sir?" asked he, catching Bertram's look of displeasure.

"No."

===Chinese===
他们身侧忽地传出一声急促的倒抽气，紧接着是一阵慌忙的咳嗽。伯特兰一转身，第五次对上了霍普古德的那双眼。他竟没人留意地从那扇隔开里外的小门溜了进来，这会儿已站得离他们极近，斜着眼打量他们背后的那只保险柜，打量说话的那位先生的脸——没错，甚至连那些正埋头忙着翻账的办事员们的脸，也一并斜睨着。

「是您拉铃了吗，先生？」他问，正撞见伯特兰那满脸的不快。

「没有。」

===Original===
The man seemed to feel the rebuke implied in this short response, and ambled softly away. But in another moment he was stopped by Bertram.

"What is the matter with you today, Hopgood? Can you have anything of real importance on your mind; anything connected with my uncle?"

The janitor started, and looked almost frightened. "Be careful what you say," whispered he; then with a keen look at Mr. Wheelock just then on the point of entering the directors' room, he was turning to escape by the little door just mentioned, when it opened and Mr. Stuyvesant came in. With a look almost of terror the janitor recoiled, throwing himself as it were between the latter and the door of the safe; but recovering himself, surveyed the keen quiet visage of the veteran banker with a rolling of his great eyes absolutely painful to behold. Mr. Stuyvesant, who was somewhat absorbed in thought, did not appear to notice the agitation he had caused, and with just a hurried nod followed Mr. Wheelock into the Directors' room. Instantly the janitor drew himself up with an air of relief, and shortly glancing at the clock which lacked a few minutes yet of the time fixed for the meeting, slided hastily away from Bertram's detaining hand, and disappeared in the crowd without. In another moment Bertram saw him standing at the outer door, looking anxiously up and down the street.

===Chinese===
那人似乎觉出了这短短两个字里所含的训斥，便蹑着脚步慢慢走开了。可下一刻，他又被伯特兰叫住。

「你今天是怎么了，霍普古德？可是有什么当真要紧的事搁在心上；有什么与我叔父相关的事？」

看门人猛地一激灵，神情几近惊恐。「说话小心些。」他低声说；随即朝正要踏进董事会议室的威洛克先生投去一道锐利的目光，便转身要由方才说到的那扇小门脱身——门偏偏在这时开了，斯泰弗森特先生（Mr. Stuyvesant）走了进来。看门人脸上一副近乎惊骇的神色，直直往后一缩，整个人像是横在了来人与保险柜的门之间；但他随即镇定下来，转动那两只大眼端详着这位老资格银行家那张沉静而锐利的脸——那两只眼珠转得叫人看着简直难受。斯泰弗森特先生正沉浸在自己的思绪里，似乎并未觉察自己所引起的那一阵骚动，只匆匆点了下头，便跟着威洛克先生进了董事会议室。看门人立时挺直了身子，松了一口气，不多时又瞥了一眼时钟——离会议定下的时间尚差几分钟——便匆匆从伯特兰想要拦住他的手里挣了开去，消失在外头的人群里。再一晃眼，伯特兰已看见他立在大门外，焦灼地朝街上两头张望。

===Original===
"Something *is* wrong," murmured Bertram. "What?" And for a moment he felt half tempted to return Mr. Stuyvesant's friendly bow with a few words expressive of his uneasiness, but the emphasis with which Hopgood had murmured the words, "Be careful what you say," unconsciously deterred him, and concealing his nervousness as best he might, he entered the Directors' office.

===Chinese===
「果真是*出了*什么事。」伯特兰喃喃道。「可到底是什么呢？」有那么一刻，他几乎想趁着回斯泰弗森特先生那友善的一颔首，附上几句说出自己心头的惴惴；可霍普古德方才低声那一句「说话小心些」，那语气里那份郑重，不知不觉便把他拦住了。他尽力掩住自己的忐忑，迈步走进了董事们的办公室。

===Original===
It was now time for the meeting to open, and the gentlemen were all seated around the low green baize table that occupied the centre of the room. Impatience was written on all their countenances. Mr. Stuyvesant especially was looking at the heavy gold watch in his hand, with a frown on his deeply wrinkled brow that did not add to its expression of benevolence. The empty seat at the head of the table stared upon Bertram uncompromisingly.

"My wife gives a reception today," ventured one gentleman to his neighbor.

"And I have an engagement at five that won't bear postponement."

"Sylvester has always been on hand before."

"We can't proceed without him," was the reply.

Mr. Wheelock looked thoughtful.

===Chinese===
会议这时本该开了，诸位先生都已围着屋子正中那张铺着绿呢的低桌坐定。不耐烦之色明明白白地写在每个人脸上。斯泰弗森特先生尤其如此，正瞧着手上那只沉甸甸的金表，那满是深纹的眉头皱着，越发叫他那张素来宽厚的脸少了几分慈和。桌首那把空椅子毫不通融地瞪着伯特兰。

「我内人今天办招待会。」一位先生大着胆子向邻座说。

「我五点钟还有一个推不得的约。」

「西尔维斯特从前总是到场的。」

「没有他，我们开不成了。」对方答道。

威洛克先生面露思忖之色。

===Original===
With a nod of his head towards such gentlemen as met his eye, Bertram hastened to a little cupboard devoted to the use of himself and uncle. Opening it, he looked within, took down a coat he saw hanging before him, and unconsciously uttered an exclamation. It was a dress-coat such as had been worn by Mr. Sylvester the evening before.

"What does this mean! My uncle has been here!" were the words that sprang to his lips; but he subdued his impulse to speak, and hastily hanging up the coat, relocked the door. Proceeding at once to the outer room, he asked two or three of the clerks if they were sure Mr. Sylvester had not been in during the day. But they all returned an unequivocal "no," and that too with a certain stare of surprise that at once convinced him he was betraying his agitation too plainly.

===Chinese===
伯特兰朝所遇见的几位先生颔首为礼，便赶忙走向一只专供他与叔父使用的小橱。他打开橱门朝里张望，伸手取下眼前挂着的一件外衣，不由自主地发出一声惊呼。那是一件礼服，正是西尔维斯特先生前一夜穿过的那一件。

「这是什么意思！叔父来过了！」几句话直冲到他嘴边；但他按下了这股冲动，把那件衣服匆匆挂回去，重新锁上了橱门。他径直走到外间，向两三个办事员打听，究竟拿不拿得稳西尔维斯特先生今日当真没有到行里来过。可他们个个都回了一个毫不含糊的「没有」二字，而且说时还带着一种惊讶的瞪视，立刻便叫他明白：自己心头的惶乱已袒露得太明显了。

===Original===
"I will telegraph whether Wheelock considers it necessary or not," thought he, and was moving to summon a messenger boy when he caught sight of Hopgood slowly making his way in from the street. He was very pale and walked with his eyes fixed on the ground, ominously shaking his great head in a way that bespoke an inner struggle of no ordinary nature. Bertram at once sauntered out to meet him.

"Hopgood," said he, "your evident anxiety is infectious. What has happened to make my uncle's detention a matter of such apparent import? If you do not wish to confide in me, his nephew almost his son, speak to Mr. Wheelock or to one of the directors, but don't keep anything to yourself which concerns his welfare or—What are you looking at?"

===Chinese===
「不管威洛克觉着有没有那个必要，我都要拍个电报。」他心想，正要过去唤一个送电报的孩童，却一眼瞧见霍普古德正从街上慢慢吞吞地挪进来。他脸白得厉害，垂着眼盯着地上走，那只大脑袋不祥地一下一下晃着，那副模样显是心里头正经历着一场非同小可的挣扎。伯特兰当即踱出去迎他。

「霍普古德，」他说，「你这副显而易见的焦灼是会过人的。究竟出了什么事，叫我叔父这一时的迟误成了这等了不得的勾当？你若不肯对我——他的侄子、几乎与儿子无异地——吐露，那就去同威洛克先生、或者哪位董事说去；可凡是关系着他安危的事，你别一个人闷在肚里——你这么直勾勾地瞧着什么？」

===Original===
The man was gazing as if fascinated at the keys in Bertram's hand.

"Nothing sir, nothing. You must not detain me; I have nothing to say. I will wait ten minutes," he muttered to himself, glancing again at the clock. Suddenly he saw the various directors come filing out of the inner room, and darted for the second time from Bertram's detaining hand.

"I hope nothing has happened to Mr. Sylvester," exclaimed one gentleman to another as they filed by.

"If he were given to a loose ends' sort of business it would be another thing."

"He looked exceedingly well at the reception last night," exclaimed another; "but in these days—"

===Chinese===
那人正死死盯着伯特兰手里的钥匙，像被什么摄住了似的。

「没什么，先生，没什么。您可别留我；我没什么可说的。我再等十分钟。」他自顾自地嘟囔着，又瞥了一眼那座钟。忽然，他看见各位董事一个接一个地从里间鱼贯而出，便再一次从伯特兰想要拦住他的手里一闪身溜了去。

「但愿西尔维斯特先生没有出什么事。」一位先生在鱼贯而过时向另一位说道。

「若他是那种做事没个定准、东游西荡的人，便又当别论了。」

「昨晚在那招待会上，他看着精神好得很呐。」又一个失声道；「可这些年头——」

===Original===
Suddenly there was a hush. A telegraph boy had just entered the door and was asking for Mr. Bertram Sylvester.

"Here I am," said Bertram, hastily taking the envelope presented him. Slightly turning his back, he opened it. Instantly his face grew white as chalk.

"Gentlemen," said he, "you will have to excuse my uncle today; a great misfortune has occurred to him." Then with a slow and horror-stricken movement, he looked about him and exclaimed, "*Mrs. Sylvester is dead*."

===Chinese===
忽然四下一静。一个送电报的孩童刚进门，正打听伯特兰·西尔维斯特先生。

「我在这里。」伯特兰说着，匆匆接过递上来的那封信封。他微微侧过身去，拆开了它。顷刻之间，他的脸白得像粉笔。

「诸位先生，」他说，「家叔今日怕是不能奉陪了；他遭了一场大不幸。」随即，他以一种缓慢而惊惧万状的动作环顾四周，失声喊道：「*西尔维斯特夫人去世了*。」

===Original===
A confused murmur at once arose, followed by a hurried rush; but of all the faces that flocked out of the bank, none wore such a look of blank and helpless astonishment as that of Hopgood the janitor, as with bulging eyes and nervously working hands, he slowly wended his way to the foot of the stairs and there sat down gazing into vacancy.

===Chinese===
一阵纷乱的低语立时涌起，紧接着是一阵忙乱的奔走；可从银行里涌出的那一众面孔里，没有哪一张，比那看门人霍普古德的脸更显得那样一片茫然、那样束手无策的错愕——他眼珠凸着，两只手紧张地不住搓动，慢慢地挪到楼梯脚下，在那里坐下，两眼直瞪着一片虚空。

## II A Discussion / 二 一场讨论

===Original===
> "Young men think old men fools, and old men know young men to be so."

"And you are actually in earnest?"
"I am."

===Chinese===
> 「年轻人觉得老年人是傻瓜，而老年人知道年轻人确实如此。」

「你当真是认真的？」
「当真。」

===Original===
The first speaker, a fine-looking gentleman of some forty years of age, drummed with his fingers on the table before him and eyed the face of the young man who had repeated this assent so emphatically, with a certain close scrutiny indicative of surprise.

"It is an unlooked-for move for you to make," he remarked at length. "Your success as a pianist has been so decided, I confess I do not understand why you should desire to abandon a profession that in five years' time has procured you both competence and a very enviable reputation—for the doubtful prospects of Wall Street, too!" he added with a deep and thoughtful frown that gave still further impressiveness to his strongly marked features.

===Chinese===
先开口的那位是个相貌堂堂的绅士，约莫四十岁，用手指在面前的桌上敲着鼓点，仔细打量着那年轻人——这年轻人把那声应答重复得如此斩钉截铁——目光中带着一种说明他颇为惊异的审视。

「这一着，可真出人意料，」他终于开口道。「你作为钢琴家的成就已是板上钉钉，我承认我不明白你为何要放弃一门短短五年便已使你既获温饱、又赢得令人艳羡声誉的职业——况且还是为了华尔街那般前途未卜的营生！」他深深皱起眉头，若有所思，使他本就轮廓鲜明的面容更显凝重。

===Original===
The young man with a sweep of his eye over the luxurious apartment in which they sat, shrugged his shoulders with that fine and nonchalant grace which was one of his chief characteristics.

"With such a pilot as yourself, I ought to be able to steer clear of the shoals," said he, a frank smile illumining a face that was rather interesting than handsome.

The elder gentleman did not return the smile. Instead of that he remained gazing at the ample coal-fire that burned in the grate before him with a look that to the young musician was simply inexplicable. "You see the ship in haven," he murmured at last; "but do not consider what storms it has weathered or what perils escaped. It is a voyage I would encourage no son of mine to undertake."

===Chinese===
那年轻人目光一扫两人所坐的这间华美厅堂，耸了耸肩，带着那种优雅而漫不经心的风度——这正是他最显著的特点之一。

「有您这样的领航员，我总该能绕开暗礁了吧。」他说，坦率的微笑照亮了一张称不上俊美却颇为耐看的脸。

年长的绅士没有回以微笑。他只是凝视着面前炉栅里熊熊燃烧的旺火，神情对这年轻音乐家而言简直无法理解。「你看见的是船已入港，」他终于低声道；「却不去想它经历过怎样的风暴、逃脱过怎样的险境。这一趟航程，我不会鼓励我的任何一个儿子去尝试。」

===Original===
"Yet you are not the man to shrink from danger or to hesitate in a course you had marked out for yourself, because of the struggle it involved or the difficulties it presented!" the young man exclaimed almost involuntarily as his glance lingered with a certain sort of fascination on the powerful brow and steady if somewhat melancholy eye of his companion.

"No; but danger and difficulty should not be sought, only subdued when encountered. If you were driven into this path, I should say, 'God pity you!' and hold you out my hand to steady you along its precipices and above its sudden quicksands. But you are not driven to it. Your profession offers you the means of an ample livelihood while your good heart and fair talents insure you ultimate and honorable success, both in the social and artistic world. For a man of twenty-five such prospects are not common and he must be difficult to please not to be satisfied with them."

===Chinese===
「可您绝不是那种面对危险会退缩，也不会因为一段路途需要挣扎、布满艰难便在自己标定的方向上踟蹰不前的人！」年轻人几乎是脱口而出，他的目光带着某种着迷停留在同伴那宽阔的额头和沉稳却略带忧郁的眼睛上。

「不错；但危险与艰难不应去主动追寻，只应在遭遇时加以克服。倘若你是被逼上这条路的，我会说：『愿上帝怜悯你！』并伸出手，在悬崖边、在骤然出现的流沙之上扶你一把。可你并非被逼无奈。你的本行已为你提供了丰足的生计，而你善良的心地和不错的才华，也保证你在社交界与艺术界最终都将获得体面的成功。对二十五岁的人来说，这样的前景并不多见，除非极难伺候，否则没有不满足的。」

===Original===
"Yes," said the other rising with a fitful movement but instantly sitting again; "I have nothing to complain of as the world goes, only—Sir," he exclaimed with a sudden determination that lent a force to his features they had hitherto lacked, "you speak of being driven into a certain course; what do you mean by that?"

"I mean," returned the other; "forced by circumstances to enter a line of business to which many others, if not all others are preferable."

===Chinese===
「是啊，」对方说着，一阵冲动似地站起身，却又立刻坐了下去；「就世道而言，我没什么可抱怨的，只是——先生，」他忽然以一种此前不曾有过的决断之态喊道，这决断使他的面貌增添了一种力量，「您说到被逼上某一条路；您这话是什么意思？」

「我的意思是，」另一位答道，「为境况所迫，而投身一门几乎任何别的行当——若非所有别的行当——都比它更可取的生意。」

===Original===
"You speak strongly, speculation evidently has none of your sympathy, notwithstanding the favorable results which have accrued to you from it. But excuse me, by circumstances you mean poverty, I suppose, and the lack of every other opening to wealth and position. You would not consider the desire to make a large fortune in a short space of time a circumstance of a sufficiently determining nature to reconcile you to my entering Wall Street speculation?"

The elder gentleman rose, not as the other had done with a restless impulse quickly subsiding at the first excuse, but forcibly and with a feverish impatience that to appearance was somewhat out of proportion to the occasion. "A large fortune in a short space of time!" he reiterated, pausing where he had risen with an eagle glance at his companion and a ringing tone in his voice that bespoke a deep but hitherto suppressed agitation. "It is the alluring inscription above the pitfall into which many a noble youth has fallen; the battle-cry to a struggle that has led many a strong man the way of ruin; the guidepost to a life whose feverish days and sleepless nights offer but poor compensation for the sudden splendors and as sudden reverses attached to it. I had rather you had accounted for this sudden freak of yours by the strongest aspiration after power than by this cry of the merely mercenary man who in his desire to enjoy wealth, prefers to win it by a stroke of luck rather than conquer it by a life of endeavor."

===Chinese===
「您说得很重，投机显然丝毫得不到您的同情，尽管您自己从中获益匪浅。但恕我直言，所谓境况所迫，我想您指的是贫穷，是除了这一条之外再无别的通往财富与地位的门路。您不至于认为，想要在短时间内发一笔大财这一念头，算得上是一种足以令您调和心境、容忍我投身华尔街投机的决定性境况吧？」

年长的绅士站起身来，他不像对方那样一阵坐立不安的冲动、随即因头一个借口便平息下去，而是带着一股猛力，一种近乎狂躁的焦灼——这焦灼看上去与眼前的场合多少有些不相称。「在短时间内发一笔大财！」他反复念道，停在起身之处，以鹰隼般的一瞥望向同伴，嗓音里有一种铿锵的调子，透露出一种深沉而此前一直被压抑着的激动。「那是写在陷阱之上、诱使多少高贵青年坠落的迷人铭文；是一场厮杀的战吼，这厮杀已把多少强壮的汉子引上了毁灭之路；是一根指向某种人生的路标，那人生狂热的白昼与不眠的夜晚，对于随之而来的骤然辉煌与骤然倾覆，只能提供可怜的补偿。我宁愿你用对权势最强烈的渴求来解释你这一时的心血来潮，也不愿你用那唯利是图之人的呼喊来解释——那人在贪图享受财富之时，宁可凭一时运气去赢取它，也不愿以毕生的奋进去征服它。」

===Original===
He stopped. "I am aware that this tirade against the ladder by which I myself have risen so rapidly, must strike you as in ill-taste. But Bertram, I am interested in your welfare and am willing to incur some slight charge of inconsistency in order to insure it," and here he turned upon his companion with that expression of extreme gentleness which lent such a peculiar charm to his countenance and explained perhaps the almost unlimited power he held over the hearts and minds of those who came within the circle of his influence.

===Chinese===
他停下。「我明白，这番痛斥那正是我自己借以迅速攀升的阶梯的话，在你听来一定很不中听。可是伯特兰，我关心你的福祉，为此甘愿招来一点言行不一的小小非议。」说到这里，他转向同伴，脸上带着那种极度温柔的神情——正是这种神情赋予了他的面容一种独特的魅力，也许也解释了他对那些进入他影响范围之内的人的心智为何拥有几乎不受限制的掌控力。

===Original===
"You are very good, sir," murmured his young friend, who to explain matters at once was in reality the nephew of this Wall Street magnate, though from the fact of his having taken another name on entering the musical profession, was not generally known as such. "No one, not even my father himself, could have been more considerate and kind; but I do not think you understand me, or rather I should say I do not think I have made myself perfectly intelligible to you. It is not for the sake of wealth itself or the éclat attending its possession that I desire an immediate fortune, but that by means of it I may attain another object dearer than wealth, and more precious than my career."

===Chinese===
「您太好了，先生，」他那位年轻的朋友低声道。说穿了一件事：他其实是这位华尔街巨擘的侄子，只因当初踏入音乐这一行时另起了一个姓氏，一般人并不知道这层关系。「没有人，连我父亲本人在内，能比您更体贴、更厚道了；但我想您并不理解我，或者我该说，我想我没能向您把话说得完全明白。我之所以渴望立刻得到一笔财产，并非为了财富本身，也非为了拥有它时所附带的荣耀，而是想借此达到另一个比财富更可贵、比我的事业更珍重的目的。」

===Original===
The elder gentleman turned quickly, evidently much surprised, and cast a sudden inquiring glance at his nephew, who blushed with a modest ingenuousness pleasing to see in one so well accustomed to the critical gaze of his fellow-men.

"Yes," said he, as if in answer to that look, "I am in love."

===Chinese===
年长的绅士迅速转过身来，显然十分惊讶，向侄子投去一道突兀的探询目光；侄子带着一种谦逊而坦诚的神情红了脸——对这样一个早已习惯众人挑剔目光的人来说，这副模样颇令人赏心悦目。

「是的，」他仿佛是在回答那一眼似的说道，「我恋爱了。」

===Original===
A deep silence for a moment pervaded the apartment, a sombre silence almost startling to young Mandeville, who had expected some audible expression to follow this announcement if only the good-natured "Pooh! pooh!" of the matured man of the world in the presence of ardent youthful enthusiasm. What could it mean? Looking up he encountered his uncle's eye fixed upon him with the last expression he could have anticipated seeing there, namely that of actual and unmistakable alarm.

"You are displeased," Mandeville exclaimed. "You have thought me proof against such a passion, or perhaps you do not believe in the passion itself!" Then with a sudden remembrance of the notable if somewhat indolent loveliness of his uncle's wife, blushed again at his unusual want of tact, while his eye with an involuntary impulse sought the large panel at their right where, in the full bloom of her first youth, the lady of the house smiled upon all beholders.

===Chinese===
深沉的寂静一时弥漫了整个房间，一种阴郁的寂静，几乎让年轻的曼德维尔（Mandeville）吃了一惊；他原以为这番宣告之后会听到些什么声响，哪怕只是那位老于世故的成熟之人在面对年轻人的炽热激情时，发出一声好脾气的「嗤！嗤！」。这是什么意思？他抬起头，正遇上叔父的目光定定地落在他身上，那目光中所带的，是他最最意想不到的神情——一种真真切切、不容误解的惊惶。

「您不高兴，」曼德维尔喊道。「您以为我对这样的激情免疫，又或者您根本不信有这种激情！」随即猛然记起他婶母那种虽略显慵懒却颇为出众的美貌，又因自己这一反常态的不知分寸而红了脸，同时他的目光不由自主地投向右边那块巨大的画板——在那里，正值韶华的全盛时期，这宅子的女主人对所有的观者含笑而立。

===Original===
"I do not believe in that passion influencing a man's career," his uncle replied with no apparent attention to the other's embarrassment. "A woman needs be possessed of uncommon excellences to justify a man in leaving a path where success is certain, for one where it is not only doubtful but if attained must bring many a regret and heartache in its train. Beauty is not sufficient," he went on with sterner and sterner significance, "though it were of an angelic order. There must be worth." And here his mind's eye if not that of his bodily sense, certainly followed the glance of his companion.

"I believe there is worth," the young man replied; "certainly, it is not her beauty that charms me. I do not even know if she *is* beautiful," he continued.

"And you believe you love!" the elder exclaimed after another short pause.

===Chinese===
「我并不相信那种激情足以左右一个男人的一生事业，」他的叔父答道，似乎全然没有留意对方的窘迫。「一个女人必须具备非凡的优长，才能叫一个男人有理由离开一条成功在望的路，转而踏上另一条不仅前途未卜、即便侥幸达成也必将带来诸多悔恨与心痛的路。仅仅美貌是不够的，」他越说越严厉，意味越来越深长，「即便那是天使般的美貌。她必须有值得敬重之处。」说到这里，他心中的眼——若不是肉眼的话——必定是追随着他同伴的目光而去了。

「我相信她有值得敬重之处，」年轻人答道；「当然，迷住我的并非她的美貌。我甚至不知道她*是否*称得上美。」他接着说。

「而你还相信你在爱！」稍停片刻，年长的那位失声喊道。

===Original===
There was so much of bitterness in the tone in which this was uttered, that Mandeville forgot its incredulity. "I think I must," returned he with a certain masculine naivete not out of keeping with his general style of face and manner, "else I should not be here. Three weeks ago I was satisfied with my profession, if not enthusiastic over it; today I ask nothing but to be allowed to enter upon some business that in three years' time at least will place me where I can be the fit mate of any woman in this land, that is not worth her millions."

"The woman for whom you have conceived this violent attachment is, then, above you in social position?"

"Yes, sir, or so considered, which amounts to the same thing, as far as I am concerned."

===Chinese===
这话里的苦涩之味那样浓重，以至于曼德维尔反倒忘了其中的不以为然。「我想我必须是了，」他以一种男子气的天真答道——这天真与他整个面貌举止并不相悖，「否则我不会在这里。三周以前，我对自己的本行还算满意，若说不上热烈；而今日，我只求能被允许投身一门生意，使我在至少三年之后，得以成为本国任何一位女子——只要她不是以百万计的身家——的般配伴侣。」

「那么，使你生出这等狂热依恋的女子，在社会地位上高过你？」

「是的，先生，至少人们这样认为，而就我而言，这二者并无分别。」

===Original===
"Bertram, I have lived longer than you and have seen much of both social and domestic life, and I tell you no woman is worth such a sacrifice on the part of a man as you propose. No woman of today, I should say; our mothers were different. The very fact that this young lady of whom you speak, obliges you to change your whole course of life in order to obtain her, ought to be sufficient to prove to you—" He stopped suddenly, arrested by the young man's lifted hand. "She does not oblige you, then?"

"Not on her own account, sir. This lily," lifting a vase of blossoms at his elbow, "could not be more innocent of the necessities that govern the social circle it adorns, than the pure, single-minded girl to whom I have dedicated what is best and noblest in my manhood. It is her father—"

"Ah, her father!"

===Chinese===
「伯特兰，我活得比你久，见过许多社交与家庭生活，我告诉你，没有哪一个女人值得一个男人如你这般牺牲。应当说，当今没有一个女人值得；我们的母亲那一代不同。你所说的这位小姐竟要你改变整个人生道路才能得到她，仅凭这一点，就应当足以向你证明——」他猛地停住，被年轻人举起的手止住了。「那么，她并没有要你这样做？」

「不是为她自己，先生。这株百合，」他举起手边一瓶盛放的花，「对于主宰它所点缀的社交圈的种种规矩不闻不问；而我以男子之身为之奉献一切最善最美之物的那个纯洁、心思单纯的姑娘，其不闻不问也不过如此。是她的父亲——」

「啊，她的父亲！」

===Original===
"Yes, sir," the young man pursued, more and more astonished at the other's tone. "He is a man who has a right to expect both wealth and position in a son-in-law. But I see I shall have to tell you my story, sir. It is an uncommon one and I never meant that it should pass my lips, but if by its relation I can win your sympathy for a pure and noble passion, I shall consider the sacred seal of secrecy broken in a good cause. But," said he, seeing his uncle cast a short and uneasy glance at the door, "perhaps I am interrupting you. You expect someone!"

"No," said his uncle, "my wife is at church; I am ready to listen."

The young man gave a hurried sigh, cast one look at his companion's immovable face, as if to assure himself that the narrative was necessary, then leaned back and in a steady businesslike tone that softened, however, as he proceeded, began to relate as follows:

===Chinese===
「是的，先生，」年轻人继续说，对另一位语调中的异样越来越惊异。「他是一位有权指望女婿既富且贵的人。但我看，我只好把我的故事告诉您了，先生。这是一桩不寻常的故事，我本从未打算让它出口，可若是讲述出来能为您对一份纯朴高贵的激情生出几分同情，我便算是为一个正当理由打破那神圣的秘密之印了。不过，」他说，见叔父朝门那边投去短促而不安的一眼，「也许我打扰您了。您在等人！」

「没有，」他的叔父说，「我妻子去做礼拜了；我愿意听你说。」

年轻人匆匆叹了一口气，朝同伴那张纹丝不动的脸看了一眼，仿佛要确认这一番叙述确有必要，然后向后一靠，以一种沉稳而公事公办般的腔调开始讲述——不过随着讲述的推进，那腔调渐渐柔和了下来。他是这样说的：

## VI A Hand Clasp / 六 一次握手

===Original===
Once arrived at a settled conclusion, I put every thought of wavering out of my mind. Deciding that with such a friend in business circles as yourself, I needed no other introducer to my new life, I set apart this evening for a confab with you on the subject. Meanwhile it is pretty generally known that I make no more engagements to appear through the country.

I have but one more incident to relate. Last Sunday in walking down Fifth Avenue I met her. I did not do this inadvertently. I knew her custom of attending Bible class and for once put myself in her way. I did not give her time to remonstrate.

===Chinese===
一旦定下了主意，我便把一切动摇的念头逐出了脑海。我暗自盘算：既有您这样一位在商界举足轻重的朋友，我踏入新生活便不再需要别的引路人，于是约定今晚就此事与您一谈。与此同时，我已大致公之于众：不再接受任何在国内各地登台出演的邀约。

我还有一桩小事要讲。上个星期日，我顺着第五大道（Fifth Avenue）走去，与她碰了面。这并非出于无意。我晓得她每星期日去上读经班的习惯，便破天荒地把自己送到了她必经的路上。我并不给她留下劝阻的工夫。

===Original===
"Do not express your displeasure," said I, "this shall never be repeated. I merely wish to say that I have concluded to leave a profession so little appreciated by those whose esteem I most desire to possess; that I am about entering a banker's office where it shall be my ambition to rise if possible, to wealth and consequence. If I succeed—you shall then know what my incentive has been. But till I succeed or at least give such tokens of success as shall insure respect, silence must be my portion and patience my sole support. Only of one thing rest assured, that until I inform you with my own lips that the hope which now illumines me is gone, it will continue to burn on in my breast, shedding light upon a way that can never seem dark while that glow rests upon it." And bowing with the ceremonious politeness our positions demanded, I held out my hand. "One clasp to encourage me," I entreated.

===Chinese===
「请不要表露您的不快，」我说，「这种事往后绝不会再有。我只是想告诉您，我已经决心放弃那一行——那一行如此得不到我最渴望博得其敬重之人的赏识；我将要走进一家银行的事务所，在那里，但愿能一步一步地攀升，若有可能，直至财富与地位。倘若我成功——届时您便会知道，激励我的究竟是什么。可在我成功之前，至少在拿出足以确保他人敬重的成功凭证之前，沉默将是我的本分，忍耐将是我唯一的倚仗。只有一桩请您放心：除非我亲口告诉您，说此刻照亮我的这一线希望已经熄灭，否则它就会一直在我胸中燃烧下去，把光洒在一条路上——只要这道光还照着，那条路便永远不会显得幽暗。」说罢，我以你我之间身份所要求的那种郑重礼数鞠了一躬，伸出了手。「握一下，好给我些鼓励。」我恳求道。

===Original===
It seemed as if she did not comprehend. "You are going to give up music, and for—for—"

"You?" said I. "Yes, don't forbid me," I implored; "it is too late."

===Chinese===
她仿佛并不明白。「您要放弃音乐，竟是为了——为了——」

「为了您？」我说。「是的，请不要禁止我，」我哀求道；「已经太迟了。」

===Original===
Like a lovely image of blushing girlhood turned by a lightning flash into marble, she paused, pallid and breathless where she was, gazing upon me with eyes that burned deeper and deeper as the full comprehension of all that this implied gradually forced itself upon her mind.

"You make a chaos of my little world," she murmured at length.

"No," said I, "*your* world is untouched. If it should never be my good fortune to enter it, you are not to grieve. You are free, Miss Preston, free as this sunshiny air we breathe; I alone am bound, and that because I must be whether I will or no."

===Chinese===
宛如一尊可爱的、泛着少女红晕的雕像，被一道闪电化作了大理石，她停在那里，苍白而无喘息地凝望着我；随着这其中的全部含义一点一点地、不可抗拒地涌入她心头，她那双眼睛也越烧越深。

「您把我这小小的世界搅成了一团乱。」她终于喃喃地说。

「不，」我说，「*您的*世界分毫未动。纵使我有生之年始终无缘走进它，您也不必为此伤怀。您是自由的，普雷斯顿小姐（Miss Preston），自由得一如我们此刻呼吸的这片阳光朗照的空气；受束缚的只有我一人，而那是因为我无论情愿与否，都非如此不可。」

===Original===
Then I saw the woman I had worshipped in this young fair girl shine fully and fairly upon me. Drawing herself up, she looked me in the face and calmly laid her hand in mine. "I am young," said she, "and do not know what may be right to say to one so generous and so kind. But this much I can promise, that whether or not I am ever able to duly reward you for what you undertake, I will at least make it the study of my life never to prove unworthy of so much trust and devotion."

And with the last lingering look natural to a parting for years, we separated then and there, and the crowd came between us, and the Sunday bells rang on, and what was so vividly real to us at the moment, became in remembrance more like the mist and shadow of a dream.

===Chinese===
就在这一刻，我看见了我所崇拜的那位女子——她在这位年轻的、美丽的少女身上，完完全全、坦坦荡荡地朝我焕发出光来。她挺直了身，直视我的脸，平静地将手放进我的掌心。「我还年轻，」她说，「不知道对一个如此慷慨、如此厚道的人，怎样开口才算得体。可这一桩我能应承：无论我将来能否恰如其分地报答您所承担的一切，我至少要把这一生用来——绝不辜负这般深厚的信任与一片痴心。」

于是，带着那种一别数年所特有的、最后流连不去的一眼，我们便当场分了手；人群涌上来隔在了我们中间，安息日的钟声悠悠地敲着不停；而方才那一刻对我们如此真切、如此实在的一切，在回忆里竟越来越像是一场梦的薄雾与阴影。

## XXVI A Man's Justice and a Woman's Mercy / 二十六 一个男人的公正与一个女人的慈悲

===Original===
> "Fair is foul, and foul is fair."

"Have you ever seen a man whose instantaneous effect upon you was electrical; in whose expression, carriage, or manner, there was concealed a charm that attracted and interested you, apart from his actual worth and beauty? Such a one was Mr. Roger Holt, the gentleman I now discerned entering the gate with Jacqueline's lover. It was not that he was handsome. He could not for one moment bear any comparison with his brother in substantial attraction, and yet when they were both in the room, you looked at him in preference to the other, and was vexed with yourself for doing so. He seemed to be the younger as he was certainly the smaller; yet he took the lead, even in coming up the walk. Why had he not taken it in the deeper and more important matter? Was it because he did not love her?

===Chinese===
> 「美即丑恶，丑即美。」

「你可曾见过这样一个人，他一瞬间在你身上产生的效应如同电击；在他的神情、举止或仪态之中，潜藏着一种魅力，使你为之吸引、为之着迷，而这魅力与他实际的才貌并无关系？罗杰·霍尔特先生（Mr. Roger Holt）便是这样一个人——我此刻看见的这位绅士，正与雅克琳的心上人一同走进院门。倒不是他生得俊美。就实在的吸引力而言，他一刻也无法与他的兄弟相提并论，然而当两人同处一室时，你却宁可看他而不看另一位，又为自己这一偏好感到恼怒。他显得更年轻，无疑也更为瘦小；然而走在前头的却是他，就连沿小径走上来时也是如此。为何在更深刻、更重大的那桩事上，他却不走在前头呢？莫非是因为他并不爱她？

===Original===
"I was not present when Jacqueline greeted her guests and presented Mr. Roger Holt to her father. But later in the day I spent a half hour with them and saw enough to be able to satisfy myself as to the falsity of my last supposition. Never had I seen on a human countenance the evidences of a wilder passion than that which informed his features, as he sat in the further window of the parlor, presumably engaged in admiring the autumn landscape, but really occupied in casting short sidelong glances at Jacqueline, who sat listening with a superb nonchalence, but with a restless gleam in her wandering eye, to the genial talk between her acknowledged lover and the Colonel. I half feared he would rise from his seat, and flinging himself before her, demand then and there an explanation of her engagement.

"But beyond the impatience of those short burning glances, he controlled himself well, and it was Jacqueline who moved at last.

===Chinese===
「雅克琳迎候宾客、把罗杰·霍尔特先生引见给她父亲时，我并不在场。但当日晚些时候，我与他们共处了半个钟头，所见已足以令我确信，我方才那番揣测实属谬误。我从未在哪一张人脸上，见过比此刻充盈于他面容之上的更为狂热的激情的痕迹——他坐在客厅最里头那扇窗前，看模样是在赏玩秋日的景致，实则不住地朝雅克琳投去短促而斜睨的目光；而她坐在那里，以一种绝佳的漫不经心，倾听着她那位名正言顺的心上人与上校之间热络的交谈，只是那双游移的眼睛里闪着不安的光。我几乎担心他会从座位上起身，一个箭步冲到她跟前，当场要求她为这桩婚约作出交代。

「然而，除了那几道短促而灼热的目光所泄露的焦躁之外，他把自己克制得很好；终归是雅克琳先动了。

===Original===
"I saw the purpose growing in her eyes long before she stirred. The face which had been a mystery to me from her cradle, was in the presence of this man, like an open page which all might read. Its letters were flame, but that did not make them any less clear. I felt her swaying towards him, before an eyelash trembled or a quiver shook her tall form.

"He may have understood her purpose also, for his eye wandered towards the open piano. She rose like a queen.

"'Mr. Roger Holt is a singer,' said she in passing her father, 'I am going to ask him to give us one of the old ballads you profess to like so much.'

===Chinese===
「在她身形未动之前许久，我已看见那意图在她眼中渐渐成形。那张从她襁褓之时起便对我是个谜的脸，在此人面前，却如同一页摊开的书，人人可读。那上面的字字句句是火焰写成，可这并不使其有半分减损清晰。在她的一根睫毛颤动、或一缕颤栗掠过她高挑的身形之前，我便已感到她正朝他倾去。

「他或许也读懂了她的用意，因为他的目光游向了那架敞开的钢琴。她如女王般站起身来。

「『罗杰·霍尔特先生是位歌唱家，』她经过父亲身边时说道，『我正要请他为我们唱一支您自称那般喜爱的古老民谣。』

===Original===
"The conversation at once ceased. The Colonel who made no secret of his fondness for music, turned at once towards the stranger, with an expression of great courtesy. Instantly that gentleman rose, and meeting the request of his hostess with a profound bow, proceeded at once to the piano. 'He will not leave it till he has spoken to her,' thought I. Nor did he, for that very moment as they stood turning her music over, I perceived his lips move in a hurried question, to which she as briefly responded, whereupon he caught up a sheet of music from the pile, and flinging back his head with a victorious smile, began to sing.

"Had I known what lay behind his words, I would have braved everything rather than have allowed him to utter a note in that room which had once rung with the carols of Jacqueline's mother. But what could I guess of the possible evil underlying the natural ebullition of unrestrained passion that from some cause of pride or pique, had met with a strange inexplicable check. So I sat still, shuddering perhaps, but quiet in my corner; while the haunting tones of his strange and thrilling voice, rose and fell in the most uncanny of Scottish love songs. Nor did I do more than wonder with all my agitated soul, when at the conclusion Jacqueline came back, and pausing beside the man to whom she had given her troth, looked down in his beaming face and smiled with that overflow of delight, which she dared not bestow upon his brother.

===Chinese===
「交谈顿时止住了。上校素来不掩饰自己对音乐的喜爱，当即转向那位陌生人，神情十分殷勤有礼。那位先生立刻起身，对女主人的请求深鞠一躬，随即走向钢琴。『他不到与她搭话之时不会离开那架琴的，』我心想。果不其然，就在他们站在那里翻动她的乐谱的当儿，我看见他的嘴唇翕动，匆匆问了一句，她同样简短地作答；于是他从那一摞乐谱中抽出一张，头向后一仰，露出一个得胜的微笑，便开口唱了起来。

「倘若我知晓他那番话背后藏着什么，我便宁可豁出一切，也决不容许他在这间屋子——这间曾经回荡着雅克琳母亲歌声的屋子——里唱出一个音符。可是，那本是无拘束激情的自然迸发，只因某种出于自尊或怄气的原因，遭遇了一场古怪而费解的遏制——如此之下可能潜藏的祸患，我又能揣度出几分呢？于是我便静静地坐着，或许在发抖，却安守在我的角落里；任凭他那奇异而动人心魄的嗓音，那萦绕不去的声调，在一支最为诡异的苏格兰情歌之中起落沉浮。待一曲终了，雅克琳走回来，停在那位她已许以终身的男子身边，俯望他那张神采飞扬的脸，露出那一抹满溢的欢愉之笑——这笑容她不敢施予他的兄弟——此时我也只能以整个激荡的灵魂暗暗诧异罢了。

===Original===
"Another little incident of that hour remains engraven upon my memory. She had been showing to the gentlemen a rare plant that stood in the front parlor window, and was dilating upon its marvels, when Mr. Robert Holt, her accepted lover, took in his clasp the small white hand wandering so invitingly among the leaves of the huge palm, and glancing at the finger which should have worn his ring, looked inquiringly into her face.

"'O,' said she, interrupting her little speech to draw away her hand, 'you miss your diamond? I have it, sir. It lies very safe in my pocket; it is a beautiful gem, but *your ring does not fit me*.'

"The way she said those words and the air with which she tossed back her head, must have made one heart in that room beat joyously, but it did not reassure me or subdue my secret apprehension.

"'Not fit!' her lover responded; and begged her to allow him to try it on and see, but she shook her head with wilful coquetry, and turning to the piano, commenced singing a gay little song that was like silver bells, shaken by a sudden and mighty tempest.

===Chinese===
「那一时辰里还有一桩小事，深深刻入我的记忆之中。她方才正向前厅窗前那盆珍奇的植物指点给诸位先生看，正详述它的种种奇处，这时，她那位名正言顺的心上人罗伯特·霍尔特先生（Mr. Robert Holt），一把握住了那只在巨棕榈的叶片间惹人地游移着的小巧白手，瞥了一眼本该戴上他戒指的那根手指，探询地望向她的脸。

「『哦，』她打断了自己的小段话，把手抽了回去，『您惦记您的钻石了？我带着呢，先生。它稳稳当当地躺在我口袋里；那确是一颗美丽的宝石，不过*您的戒指并不合我手指*。』

「她说这几个字时的口吻，以及她把头向后一昂的神态，必定使那屋里某一颗心欢跃地跳动了起来，却既不能安抚我，也不能平息我心底的隐忧。

「『不合！』她的心上人应道；便求她让他试戴一下看个究竟，她却带着任性的卖弄摇了摇头，转身走向钢琴，唱起一支轻快的小曲，那声音如同被一场骤然袭来的猛烈风暴所撼动的银铃。

===Original===
"Even the Colonel felt the change in his daughter, though he never guessed the cause, and came and went during the evening that followed, with certain odd sighs that made my heart ache with strange forebodings. Only her lover was unconscious, or if he felt the new and wayward force and fire in her manner, attributed it to his own presence and unspeakable devotion. Mr. Roger Holt, on the contrary, thoroughly understood it. Though he was strangely calm, as calm now as he had previously been alert and fiery, he never lost a gleam of her eye in his direction, or a turn of her form towards the chair where he sat. But the smile with which he contemplated her was not pleasant to me. It was informed with self-consciousness, and a certain hard triumph, that made it almost sinister. 'She has given her hand to the true man,' I mused, 'wherever her heart may be. But had she given it?' I began to doubt as I began to muse. With that uncontrollable will of hers, she was capable of anything; did she intend to break with Robert, now that she had seen Roger? I detected no signs of it beyond the evident delight they took in each other's presence. They were guilty of no further conversation of a secret or intimate character, and when with the striking of the clock at ten, Mr. Robert Holt rose to leave, his brother followed without any demur, even preceding him in his departure and limiting his farewell to a short brotherly pressure of Jacqueline's fair hand.

===Chinese===
「连上校也感觉到了女儿身上的变化，尽管他从未猜到缘由，在随后那个夜晚里进进出出时，他发出几声古怪的叹息，使我心中因莫名的预感而隐隐作痛。唯有她的心上人毫无察觉，或者即便他感觉得到她举止之中那股新奇而任性的力与火，也把它归因于自己的在场与那难以言喻的痴情。罗杰·霍尔特先生则恰恰相反，他对此洞若观火。他此刻异乎寻常地平静——正如方才他机警而炽烈，此刻他同样地平静——可她投向他的每一道眼波、她身形朝他所坐那张椅子的每一次转动，他一都不曾错过。只是他端详她时所带的那抹微笑，于我而言却并不愉快。那微笑里满是自知之明，以及一种冷硬的得意，几乎使之带上几分阴险。『她已把自己交给了那个对的人，』我暗自思忖，『无论她的心究竟归向何处。可她果真交出去了么？』我才开始细想，便也开始怀疑。以她那不可驾驭的意志，她什么事都做得出来；莫非她既已见到罗杰，便有意与罗伯特一刀两断？除了他们彼此相处时那份显而易见的欢愉之外，我窥不出别的端倪。他们再没有进行任何带有隐秘或亲昵性质的交谈，待到十点钟声敲响、罗伯特·霍尔特先生起身告辞时，他的兄弟毫无异议地随之告辞，甚至在离去时走在他前头，临别仅以短短的一下兄妹般的手上轻握，作别了雅克琳那白皙的手。

===Original===
"But much may be conveyed in a pressure, or so I began to think as I heard the low laugh that rippled from Jacqueline's lips as she turned to go up to her room; and if I had been her mother—

"But that is not what you want to hear. Enough that I did not follow her, that I did not even acquaint Colonel Japha with my fears, that indeed I did nothing but lie awake, praying and asking what I ought to do. There had been so little said; there had been so little done. A word, a sentence between them, the interchange of a couple of songs, and—What else that I could communicate to another?

===Chinese===
「然而，一握之间可以传达许多——或者说，当我听见雅克琳转身回房时唇间漾起的那声低笑，我便开始这般想了；倘若我是她的母亲——

「可那并非你想听的。说到底便是我没有跟随她去，我甚至未曾把我的忧虑告知雅法上校（Colonel Japha），事实上我什么也没做，只是彻夜未眠，一边祈祷一边自问该如何是好。他们说的话那样少；他们做的事那样少。只言片语、一两个句子在他们之间，几支歌彼此唱和，以及——此外还有什么，是我能向旁人转述的呢？

===Original===
"A week, two weeks passed, and her look of wilful happiness did not fly. She was flooded with notes from her accepted lover, whose handwriting I had learned by this time to distinguish, but not one, so far as I could learn, from any other source; yet her feet tripped lightly through the house, and her form had a rich grace in its every movement, that bespoke a mind settled in some deep joy or quiet determination. I felt the impenetrability of a secretly cherished hope, whenever I looked at her. If I had not known to the contrary, I should have said that her prospective marriage had become to her a dream of unfathomable delight. Whence then came this rapture? Through what communication was born this secret hope? I could not guess, I could only watch and wait.

"Meanwhile some random guesses at the truth had been made by the neighbors. Jacqueline had a lover. That lover was a gentleman; but the Colonel was critical; he had refused his consent and the young people had parted. Such was the talk, begotten perhaps by the persistency with which Jacqueline remained in the house, and the almost severe look with which Colonel Japha trod the streets of his native village, which he soon felt would lose all their charm in the departure of his only child. I scarcely ventured out more than Jacqueline; for I have but little control over my feelings and did not know what I would do, if anyone should closely press me with questions.

===Chinese===
「一周过去了，两周过去了，她脸上那任性的欢愉之色并未消散。她那位名正言顺的心上人的便笺如雪片般飞来——他的笔迹此时我已能辨认——但据我所知，再没有一封来自任何别的来路；然而她的脚步轻盈地穿梭于宅中，她的身形在每一个动作里都带着一种丰盈的优雅，透出一颗安住于某种深沉喜悦或沉静决断之中的心。每次望向她，我都能感到一种暗自珍藏着希望之下的不可窥透。若非我所知另有隐情，我定会说，她那桩指日可待的婚事，于她已成了一场深不可测的欢愉之梦。那么，这份狂喜从何而来？这份隐秘的希望又是借由何种暗通款曲而生？我猜不透，只能留意，只能等待。

「与此同时，邻居们对真相已有了些漫无边际的揣测。雅克琳有了一位心上人。那位心上人是个绅士；可上校眼高于顶；他不肯首肯，两个年轻人就此分开了。传言便是如此——这或许是因为雅克琳执意足不出户，也因为雅法上校走在自己故里街巷间时那副近乎严峻的神情，他不久便已感到，独女的离去将使这些街巷尽失其魅力。我几乎与雅克琳一样不敢外出；因为我驾驭不住自己的感情，倘若有人紧追不舍地拿问题盘问我，我不知道自己会做出什么来。

===Original===
"The unexpected discovery that our pretty young servant girl was in the habit of stealing into Jacqueline's room late at night, was the first thing that startled me into asking whether or not my supposition was true, that Jacqueline received no messages from Mr. Robert Holt. And scarcely had I become certain that a clandestine correspondence was being carried on between them through the medium of this girl, then the climax came, and knowledge on my part and secrecy on hers availed no longer.

"It was a day in October. The stoves had been put up in the house, and seeing Jacqueline roaming about the halls, in a renewed fit of that strange restlessness which had affected her the day before Mr. Roger Holt's visit, I went into her room to light a fire, and make everything look cheerful before dusk. I found the atmosphere warm, and going to the stove, discovered that a fire had been already kindled there, but had gone out for want of fuel. I at once commenced to rake away the ashes, in order to make preparations for a new one, when I came upon several scraps of half burned paper.

===Chinese===
「我那意外的一发现——我们家那位年轻貌美的女仆，竟惯于深更半夜偷偷溜进雅克琳的房间——头一件叫我大吃一惊、迫使我自问雅克琳是否当真再没有收到罗伯特·霍尔特先生任何消息的事，便是这个。而我刚刚确信他们之间正借这姑娘之手暗通书信，事态便到了紧要关头，我这边的知情与她那边的隐瞒都已无济于事。

「那是十月里的一天。屋里已经装起了炉子，我看见雅克琳在走廊里徘徊，又犯了那阵古怪的不宁——与罗杰·霍尔特先生来访前一日困扰她的如出一辙——便走进她的房间，打算生上一炉火，赶在天黑前把一切都弄得喜庆些。我发觉屋里暖融融的，走到炉前一看，发现里面已生过一炉火，却因添柴不足而熄了。我当即开始把炉灰扒开，好重新生火，就在这时，我翻出了几片烧了一半的纸屑。

===Original===
"Jacqueline had been burning letters. Do you blame me for picking out those scraps and hastening with them to another room, when I tell you they were written in a marked and characteristic hand that bore little or no resemblance to that of her accepted lover, and that the words which flashed first upon my eye were those ominous ones of *my wife*!

"They were three in number, and while more or less discolored and irregular, were still legible. Think child with what a thrill of horror and sharp motherly anguish, I read such words as 'Love you! I would press you in my arms if you were plague-stricken! The least turn of your head makes my blood cringe, as if a flame had touched me. I would follow you on my knees, if you led me round the world. Let me see Robert take your hand again and I will—'

"'Forget you! Do we forget the dagger that has struck us? I am another man since—'

"'I will have you if Robert goes mad and your father kills me. That I am burdened with a wife, is nothing. What is a wife that I do not—' 'You shall be my true wife, my—'

"'Tonight then, be ready; I will wait for you at the gate. A little resolution on your part, and then—'

===Chinese===
「雅克琳一直在烧信件。当我告诉你，那些纸屑上的笔迹独特别致、与她的名正言顺的心上人的笔迹几乎毫无相似之处，而最先映入我眼帘的字样，竟是那不祥的*我的妻子*二字——你可会怪我拾起那些纸屑、急匆匆地拿着它们躲进另一间屋子？

「纸屑一共三片，虽已多少褪色发黄、边缘残缺，却仍看得清楚。孩子，你想想，我读到这样的话时，那股毛骨悚然、那阵如割的慈母之痛是何等滋味——『爱你！即便你身染瘟疫，我也要把你拥进怀里！你头那么轻轻一转，便叫我血为之凝，仿佛有火焰触了我一般。你若引我环游世界，我愿跪着追随你。让我再看罗伯特握一次你的手，我便要——』

「『忘了你！我们会忘了那刺中我们的匕首么？自那以后我已是另一个人——』

「『即便罗伯特发疯、你父亲杀了我，我也要得到你。我负着一个妻子之名，算不了什么。一个我不——的妻子又算什么——』『你必作我真正的妻子，我的——』

「『那么今晚，准备好了；我会在院门前等你。只要你拿定一点主意，然后——』

===Original===
"I could read no further. The living, burning truth had forced itself upon me, that Jacqueline, our darling, our pride, the soul of our life, stood tottering upon the brink of a gulf horrible as the mouth of hell. For I never doubted for an instant what her answer would be to this entreaty. In all her past life, God pity us, there had been no tokens of that immovable hold on virtue, that would save her in such an extremity as this. Nevertheless, to make all sure, I flew back to her room, and tearing open bureau drawers and closet doors, discovered that her prettiest things had been sent away. She was going, then, and on that very night! and her father did not even know she was untrue to her betrothed lover. The horror of the situation was too much for me; I faltered as I left her room, her dainty, maidenly room, and actually crouched against the wall like a guilty thing, as I heard the sound of her voice singing some maddening strain in the parlors below. What should I do? Appeal to her, or warn her father of the frightful peril in which his honor and happiness stood? Alas, any appeal to her would be useless. In the glare of this awful revelation I had come to a full comprehension of her nature. But her father was a man; he could command as well as entreat, could even force obedience if all other methods failed. To him, then, must I go; but I had rather have gone to the rack. He was so proud a man! Had owned to such undeviating trust in his daughter's honor, as a Japha and his child! The blow would kill him; or daze him so, he might better have been killed. My knees shook under me, as I traversed the hall to his little study over the parlor, and when I came to the door, I rather fell against it than knocked, so great was my own anguish, and so deep my terror of his. He was a ready man and he came to the door at once, but upon seeing me, drew back as if his eye had fallen upon a phantom.

===Chinese===
「我再读不下去了。那活生生、火辣辣的真相已强加于我：雅克琳，我们的心肝、我们的骄傲、我们生命的灵魂，正摇摇欲坠地站在一道深渊的边上，那深渊犹如地狱之口一般可怖。因为我一刻也不曾怀疑，她对这一恳求将作何答复。在她过去的一生里，老天宽恕我们，从未有过任何迹象显示出那种对美德不可撼动的坚守，足以在此等绝境之中挽救她。尽管如此，为求万全，我飞奔回她的房间，一把拉开五斗橱的抽屉和衣橱的门，发现她那些最娇美的衣裳都已被送走。那么她是要走了，而且就在今夜！而她的父亲竟还不知她已背叛了未婚的心上人。这处境的恐怖叫我承受不住；我离开她的房间——她那精致、少女的房间——时步履踉跄，听见她从楼下客厅里传来唱着某段叫人发狂的曲调的声音，我竟像做贼心虚一般蜷缩着靠在了墙上。我该怎么办？是恳求她，还是去警告她的父亲，他的名誉与幸福正陷于何等可怖的危险之中？唉，对她作任何恳求都是徒劳。在这桩骇人真相的强光之下，我已彻底看清了她的本性。可她的父亲是个男子汉；他既会恳求也会命令，万一别的方法都不成，他甚至可以强行勒令服从。那么，我必须去找他；可我宁愿上刑架也不愿去。他是那样一个骄傲的人！他曾坦然表白过对女儿身为雅法家一员、身为他骨肉的名节有着何等坚定不移的信赖！这一击会要了他的命；或使他神志昏乱到还不如一死了之。我穿过走廊，走向他在客厅上方的那间小书房，双膝在我脚下打颤；走到门前时，我与其说是敲门，不如说是跌撞在门上——我自己的苦痛如此之深，我对他的苦痛之忧如此之切。他是个反应敏捷的人，当即来到门前，可一见到我，便猛地退了一步，仿佛目光撞见了一个鬼影。

===Original===
"'Hush!' said I, scarcely knowing what I uttered; and going in, I closed the door and latched it firmly behind me. 'I have come,' said I in a voice that made him start, 'to ask you to save your daughter. She is in deadly peril; she—' a strain of her song came in at that moment from the staircase. She was ascending to her room. He looked at me in a doubt of my sanity.

"'Not physical peril,' I stammered, 'but *moral*. She loves madly, unreasonably, and with a headlong passion that laughs at every obstacle, a man whom neither you nor heaven can look upon with aught but execration. She—'

"'Mrs. Hamlin!'—How well I remember his cool, calm voice, so deliberate in his impressive moments, so deliberate now, when perhaps she was donning hat and shawl for her elopement—'You are laboring under a great mistake. Instead of execrating Mr. Holt, I admire him most profoundly. Since the time has come for me to give up my daughter, I know of no one to whom I would rather surrender her.'

===Chinese===
「『嘘！』我说，几乎不知自己嘴里蹦出的是什么；走进去后，我关上门，在身后把门牢牢插上。『我来，』我用一种令他为之一震的声音说道，『是来求您救您的女儿。她身处万劫不复的危险之中；她——』这时一段歌声从楼梯口传了进来。她正上楼回自己的房间。他以一种怀疑我是否神志清醒的目光看着我。

「『并非身体上的危险，』我结结巴巴地说，『而是*道德上的*。她爱得痴狂、爱得毫无道理，以一种藐视一切阻碍的鲁莽激情，爱上了一个您与上苍都只能唾弃咒骂的人。她——』

「『哈姆林夫人（Mrs. Hamlin）！』——我至今仍清楚地记得他那冷静从容的嗓音，在他郑重的时刻总是那样从容不迫，此刻也这样从容——也许此刻她正戴好帽子、披上披肩准备私奔——『您陷入了一个极大的误会。我非但不唾弃霍尔特先生，反而对他推崇备至。既然我已到了不得不把女儿托付出去的时分，我想不出还有谁比我更情愿将她相托。』

===Original===
"'But Mr. Holt is not the man,' I cried, half wild in my fear and desperation. 'Do you remember the gentleman who came with him on his last visit? He called him his brother, and he is I believe, but—'

"The way he turned his grand white forehead towards me at that, made every fibre in my being quiver. 'Jacqueline does not love *him*!' exclaimed he. How sharp his voice, how changed his eye! I shrank back, trembling as I bowed my head, thinking of the word yet to be said.

"'But he won't compare—' he went on with a severe intonation. 'Besides her honor is engaged. You are dealing in fancies, Mrs. Hamlin.'

===Chinese===
「『可是霍尔特先生并非那个人，』我喊道，恐惧与绝望之下已是半疯了。『您可记得他上次来访时与他同来的那位先生？他称他作兄弟，我相信他也确是，可是——』

「他将那高贵而白皙的额头朝我一转的神情，使我浑身上下每一根神经都为之一颤。『雅克琳并不爱*他*！』他喊道。他的声音何等尖锐，他的眼神变得何等厉害！我瑟缩着退后，低着头浑身发抖，心里想着那尚未说出口的一个字。

「『可他简直不能相提并论——』他以严厉的声调继续道。『况且她的名节已有所属。您这是在凭空臆想，哈姆林夫人。』

===Original===
"I tore out of my breast the scraps of paper which had enlightened me so horribly, and held them towards him; then bethought myself, and drew back. 'I have proof,' said I; 'but first I must tell you that Jacqueline is not as good a girl as you have thought her. She is not her mother's child in the qualities of love and honor. She is destined to bring a great woe upon your head. In her passion for this man, she has forgotten your trust in her, the incorruptibility of your name, the honor of your house. Be strong, sir, for God is about to smite you in your tenderest spot.

"Ah, with what pride he towered upon me! this white-haired, stately gentleman before whom I had hitherto held my breath in admiring awe; towered upon me though his face was ghostly pale and his hand trembled like an aspen as he held it out!

"'Give me the papers you hold there,' cried he. 'Either you are gone mad, or else—Who wrote these lines?' he demanded, glancing down upon the hard, firm scrawl that blackened the bits of paper I had given him.

"'Mr. Roger Holt,' I returned unhesitatingly. 'I found those bits in Jacqueline's stove. Her clothes have been sent away, sir,' I continued as I saw his face grow fixed above the scraps he consulted. 'Twilight is coming on and—Mr. Roger Holt is a married man!'

"'What!'

===Chinese===
「我从怀里掏出那几片令我毛骨悚然地窥见真相的纸屑，朝他递了过去；转念一想，又缩了回来。『我有证据，』我说；『但我必须先告诉您，雅克琳并非您所想的那般好姑娘。在爱与名节上，她不像是她母亲的女儿。她注定要给您带来一场大祸。她为这男人之故，已忘了您对她的信赖、您姓氏的清白、您门楣的光荣。先生，您要坚强，因为上苍即将击打您最柔软之处。』

「啊，他以何等的傲岸俯视着我！这位白发苍苍、气度庄严的绅士——在他面前我一向屏息仰慕敬畏——如今这般俯视着我，尽管他的脸惨白如鬼，他伸出的那只手抖得像一片白杨叶！

「『把您手里拿的纸给我，』他喊道。『不是您疯了，便是——这几行字是谁写的？』他一面问，一面瞥着那些被我递到他手里的、被那硬而刚劲的字迹涂得乌黑的纸片。

「『罗杰·霍尔特先生，』我毫不迟疑地答道。『我在雅克琳的炉子里找到了这些碎片。她的衣裳都已被送走了，先生，』我见他低头看着那几张纸屑、脸上渐渐凝成一副死相，便接着说。『暮色正在降临，而——罗杰·霍尔特先生是个有妇之夫！』

「『什么！』

===Original===
"I never saw such a look flash from a human face as that which darted from his at that terrible moment. I thought he would have fallen, but he only dropped the papers out of his hand. 'Heaven forgive us!' murmured I, calmed by a sight of his misery, into some semblance of self-control, 'but we have never understood Jacqueline. She is not to be led, sir, by principles or duty. She loves this man, and love with her is a stormy wind, capable of sweeping her into any abyss of contumely or suffering. If you would save her, kill her love; the death of her lover would only transform her into a demon.'

"He looked at me as if I had told him the world had come to an end. 'My Jacqueline!' he murmured in a low, incredulous voice of the tenderest yearning. 'My Jacqueline!'

===Chinese===
「在那骇人的一刻，从他脸上射出来的那一种神情，我从未在任何人脸上见过。我以为他会倒下，可他只是把手里的纸松开掉了下去。『上天宽恕我们！』我喃喃道，见他这般痛苦，我反倒平静下来，恢复了几分自持之态，『可我们从未真正懂过雅克琳。她不是能被信条或本分牵着走的人，先生。她爱这个男人，而爱在她是一股暴风，能将她卷入任何羞辱与苦难的深渊。您若要救她，便杀了她的爱；杀了她的情人，只会把她变成一个魔鬼。』
