「他望着我，仿佛我刚告诉他世界已到了尽头。『我的雅克琳！』他以一种难以置信的、最最柔肠寸断的低语喃喃道。『我的雅克琳！』

===Original===
"'Oh!' I shrieked, torn by my anguish for him and the terror of her escaping while we were yet talking, 'God knows I had rather have died than contaminate her by such words as I have uttered. She is dear to me as my soul; dearer to me than my life. I have a mother's feeling for her, sir. If to fling myself headlong from that window, would delay her feet from going down the stairs to meet her guilty lover, I would gladly do it. It is her danger makes me speak. O sir, realize that danger and hasten before she has taken the irrevocable step.'

"He started like a man pricked by a sudden dart. 'She is going—you believe she is going to meet him?'

"'I do,' said I.

"He gave me a terrible look and started for the door. I hurriedly picked up the scraps that had fallen to the floor, and rushed around by an inner passageway to my own little room, hiding my head and waiting as for the crash of a falling avalanche.

===Chinese===
「『哦！』我尖叫道，既为他心如刀绞，又害怕我们说着话的当儿她便逃走了——『老天知道，我宁可死去，也不愿用我方才说出的话玷污了她。她于我宝贵如我的灵魂；于我比我的生命更宝贵。我对她怀着一位母亲的感情，先生。倘若从我一头栽出那扇窗，便能拖延她走下楼梯去会那罪孽情人的脚步，我甘愿如此。正是她的危险叫我开口。哦，先生，认清那危险吧，趁她还未来得及迈出那不可挽回的一步，赶紧去。』

「他猛地一震，仿佛被一支突如其来的飞镖刺中。『她要去——您相信她是要去会他？』

「『我相信。』我说。

「他投给我可怕的一眼，便朝门冲去。我匆忙拾起落在地上的纸屑，绕着内侧的过道奔回自己的小房间，把头藏起来，仿佛等待着雪崩崩塌时的轰然巨响。

===Original===
"Suddenly a cry rose in the hall.

"There are some sounds that lift you unconsciously to your feet. Dashing out of my room, I detected the face of the servant-girl whom I have before mentioned, looking out of her door some distance down the corridor. Hastening towards her, I uttered some words about her being a busybody, and thrusting her inside her room, locked the door upon her. Then I hastened with what speed I might to the front of the house, and coming out upon the grand staircase, met a sight that shook me to the very soul. You have been up the stairs; you know how they branch off to left and right from the platform near the top. The left branch led in those days to Colonel Japha's room, the right to the apartments occupied by Jacqueline and myself. Coming upon them, then, as I did from my side of the house, I found myself in full view of the opposite approach, and there on the topmost step I beheld Colonel Japha, standing in an attitude of awful denunciation, while halfway down the staircase, I beheld the figure of Jacqueline, hindered in her gliding course towards the front door by the terrible, 'Stop!' whose echo had reached me in my room and caused me to rush quaking and horrified to this spot. I leaned back sick and horror-stricken against the wall. There was no mercy in his voice: he had awakened to a full realization of the situation and the pride of the Japhas had made him steel.

===Chinese===
「忽然，一声喊从走廊里升起。

「有些声音会让你不由自主地一跃而起。我冲出房间，瞥见我先前提过的那个女仆的脸，正从走廊那头她自己的房门里探出来张望。我急忙奔向她，骂了她几句多管闲事之类的话，把她推进屋里，反锁在房里。然后我拼尽全力朝宅子的前头赶去，刚一踏上那座大楼梯，便撞见一幅令我灵魂为之震颤的景象。你上过那楼梯；你知道它在将近顶端的那个平台处如何一分为二，向左向右各分出一段。那时左边那一段通向雅法上校的房间，右边则通向雅克琳和我所住的几间屋子。于是，我既从宅子我这一侧走上前来，便将对面那一路的景象尽收眼底：只见最上面一级台阶上立着雅法上校，姿态之间尽是骇人的声讨斥责之意；而在楼梯半道之上，我看见雅克琳的身影，正被那一声可怖的『站住！』拦住了朝前门飘然而去的去路——那一声的回响传到我的房里，正是它叫我战栗惊恐地冲到此地。我靠在墙上，恶心欲呕，惊骇欲绝。他的声音里毫无怜悯：他已彻底看清了处境，而雅法家族的骄傲已使他化作了一块顽铁。

===Original===
"'You are my child!' he was saying. 'I have loved you and do still; but proceed one step farther towards the man that awaits you at the gate, and the door that opens upon you, *shuts* never to open again!'

"'Colonel!' I exclaimed, starting forward; but he heard me no more than he would a fly buzzing or a bird singing.

"'I desire it to shut; I have no wish to come back!' issued from the set white lips of the girl beneath us. 'There is no such charm for me in this humdrum house, that I should wish to exchange life with the man I adore, for its droning, spiritless existence!' And she lifted her foot to proceed.

===Chinese===
「『你是我的孩子！』他正说着。『我曾爱你，如今仍爱；可是你若再朝那个在院门前等你的人迈出一步，那扇为你开启的门，便会*关上*，永不再开！』

「『上校！』我失声喊道，冲上前去；可他听不见我的声音，正如听不见一只苍蝇的嗡嗡或一只鸟儿的鸣叫。

「『我巴不得它关上；我也无意再回来！』从我们下方那个姑娘紧抿的惨白嘴唇里吐出这样的话。『这沉闷乏味的宅子里，于我可没有什么 charm 珍贵到令我情愿以与我崇拜之人共度的人生，去换取这里这般嗡嗡作响、毫无生气的日子！』说着她抬起脚，便要继续往下走。

===Original===
"'Jacqueline!' I shrieked, leaning forward in my turn, and holding her by my anguish, as I never believed she could be held by anything, 'Think, child, think what you do! It is not life you are going to but death. A man who can take a young girl from her father's house, from her lover's arms, from her mother's grave, from the shrine of all that is pure and holy, to dash her into a pit of all that is corrupt, loathsome and deadly, is not one with whom you can *live*. You say you adore him: can one adore falsehood, selfishness and depravity? Does hypocrisy win love? Can the embraces of a serpent bring peace? Jacqueline, Jacqueline, you are yet pure; come back to our love and our hearts, before we die here in our shame at the head of the stairs, where your mother was carried out to her grave!'

"She trembled. I saw the hand that clutched the banister loosen its grip; she cast one quick look behind her, and her eyes flashed upon her father's face; it was set like a flint.

===Chinese===
「『雅克琳！』我也失声尖叫，身子前倾，以我的苦痛将她攫住——我从不知她能被任何东西所攫住——『想一想，孩子，想一想你在做什么！你走向去的不是生，而是死。一个男人，能把一个年轻姑娘从她父亲的宅中、从她心上人的怀抱里、从她母亲的坟前、从一切纯洁神圣的神龛之前夺走，把她掷入一个尽是腐败、可憎、致死的深渊——这样的人，你是不能与他*共度一生*的。你说你崇拜他：人能崇拜虚伪、自私与堕落么？伪善能赢得爱么？蛇的拥抱能带来安宁么？雅克琳，雅克琳，你如今还是纯洁的；回到我们的爱、我们的心里来吧，趁我们还未在这楼梯顶上、在你母亲当年被抬出去下葬之处，因羞愧而死！』

「她颤栗了。我看见紧攥着栏杆的那只手松了松；她飞快地向身后瞥了一眼，目光闪向父亲的脸；那张脸坚如磐石。

===Original===
"'If you come back,' cried he, leaning towards her, but not advancing a step from where he stood, 'you must come back of your own free will. I will hold no creature prisoner in my house. I must trust you implicitly, or not at all. Speak then, which shall it be?' And he raised his hand above his head, with a supreme and awful gesture, 'a father's blessing or a father's curse?'

"'A father's curse, then! since you command me to choose,' rang out from her lips in a burst of uncontrollable passion. 'I want no blessing that separates me from *him*!' And she pointed towards the door with a look that, defiant as it was, spoke of a terrible love before which all our warnings and entreaties were but as empty air.

===Chinese===
「『你若要回来，』他喊道，朝她倾过身子，却并不从他立身处再迈一步，『你必须凭你自己的自由意志回来。我不会在我家里囚禁任何人。我必须毫无保留地信赖你，否则便一点也不。那么说吧，要哪一样？』说着他把手举过头顶，以一种凌驾一切而又可怖的姿态——『是父亲的祝福，还是父亲的诅咒？』

「『那么，父亲的诅咒！既然您命我选择，』她唇间迸出的话，带着一股不可遏制的激情。『我不要那将我与*他*分开的祝福！』她朝门一指，那神情虽是桀骜，却流露出一种可怕的爱，在它面前，我们一切警告与恳求都不过是虚空。

===Original===
"'Curses then upon your head, slayer of a family's honor, a father's love, and a mother's memory! Curses upon you, at home and abroad! in the joy of your first passion and in the agony of your last despair! May you live to look upon that door as the gateway to heaven, and find it shut! May your children, if you are cursed with them, turn in your face, as you are turning now in mine! May the lightning of heaven be your candle, and the blackness of death your daily food and your nightly drink!' And with a look in which all the terrors he invoked, seemed to crash downward from his reeling brain upon her shrinking terror-crouched head, he gave one mighty gasp and fell back stricken to the floor.

"'God!' burst from her lips, and she rushed downwards to the door like a creature hunted to its quarry. I saw her white face gleam marble-like in the fading light that came in from the chinks about the door. I saw her trembling hand fumbling with the knob, and rousing from my stupor, called down to her with all the force of a breaking heart,

"'Jacqueline, beware!'

===Chinese===
「『那么，诅咒临到你头上吧，你这个家族名誉的扼杀者、父爱的扼杀者、母亲记忆的扼杀者！诅咒你，无论在家在外！在你初恋的欢愉之中，也在你最后绝望的苦痛之中！愿你终有一日把那扇门当作通向天堂的入口，却发现它已然紧闭！愿你的儿女——若你当真不幸有儿有女——有朝一日也背过脸去对你，正如此刻你背过脸去对我！愿上天的闪电作你的烛火，愿死亡的幽暗作你日日的粮食、夜夜的饮！』话音落下之时，他的神情之中，仿佛他所唤起的一切恐怖，都从他摇摇欲坠的脑海之中轰然坠落，砸在她那瑟缩的、因恐惧而蜷伏的头上——他猛地倒抽一口大气，朝后一仰，中风般倒在了地上。

「『老天！』一声惊呼从她唇间迸出，她像一个被追到猎物前的猎物一般朝楼下那扇门扑去。我看见她那张苍白的脸，在从门缝里透进来的将尽天光之中如大理石般闪着惨白。我看见她那只发抖的手在门把上摸索；我从呆若木鸡之中惊醒，以一种心碎欲裂的力量朝楼下喊道：

「『雅克琳，当心！』

===Original===
"She turned once more. There was something in my voice she could not withstand. 'I do not hope to keep you,' cried I, 'but before you go, hear this. In the days to come, when the face that now beams upon you with such longing, shall have learned to turn from you in weariness, if not distaste, when hunger, cold, contumely and disease shall have blasted that fair brow and seared those soft cheeks, know, that although a father can curse, a woman who loves like a mother can forgive.' The father cries, 'Once go out of that door and it shuts upon you never to open!' 'Once come to *that* door, say I,' pointing in the direction of the house's other entrance, 'and if I live and if I move, it shall open to you, were you as defiled and wretched and forsaken as Magdalen. Remember! Each day at this hour will I watch for you, kneeling upon its threshold. In sickness or in health, in joy or in sorrow, in cold or in heat. The hour of six is sacred. Some one of them shall see you falling weeping on my breast!'

"She gave me a quick stare out of her wide black eyes, then a mocking smile curled her lips, and murmuring a short, 'You rave!' opened the door, and rushed out into the falling dusk. With a resounding clang like the noise of a stone rolled upon an open grave, the great door swung to, and I was left alone in that desolated house with my stricken master.

===Chinese===
「她又转过身来。我的声音里有某种她无法抗拒的东西。『我并不指望留住你，』我喊道，『可是在你走之前，听我这一句。来日方长，待那张此刻以如此渴慕之情向你微笑的脸，学会了——即便不是出于厌恶——也出于厌倦而背过你去；待饥馑、寒冷、羞辱与疾病摧残了那光洁的额头、烙伤了那柔嫩的双颊——到那时，要知道，纵然父亲能诅咒，一个怀着母爱一般深情的女人，却能宽恕。』那位父亲喊道：『一旦你走出那扇门，它便在你身后关上，永不再开！』『可你一旦来到*那*扇门前，』我说，一面朝这宅子的另一处入口指去，『只要我还在、还能动，它便会为你而开，哪怕你已如抹大拉的马利亚（Magdalen）那般污秽、凄惨、为人所弃。记住！每一天的此时，我都会跪在门槛上等你。无论疾病还是康健，无论欢乐还是哀愁，无论严寒还是酷暑。六点钟这个时辰是神圣的。它们之中总有一日，会看见你泪流满面地扑倒在我怀里！』

「她睁着那双乌黑的大眼，飞快地瞪了我一眼，随即唇边漾起一抹讥诮的笑，低低地抛下一句：『你在说梦话！』便推开门，冲进了渐沉的暮色之中。只听得一声轰然巨响，如同一块石头滚落在敞开的坟墓之上——那扇大门阖上了，我被独自留在了那座荒凉的宅子里，与我的主人——一个身受重击的人，相对无言。

## III A Mysterious Summons / 三 一次神秘的召唤

===Original===
> "Without unspotted, innocent within,
> She feared no danger, for she knew no sin."

It was after a matinée performance at —— Hall some two weeks ago that I stopped to light a cigar in the small corridor leading to the back entrance. I was in a dissatisfied frame of mind. Something in the music I had been playing or the manner in which it had been received had touched unwonted chords in my own nature. I felt alone. I remember asking myself as I stood there, what it all amounted to? Who of all the applauding crowd would watch at my bedside through a long and harassing sickness, or lend their sympathy as they now yielded their praise, if instead of carrying off the honors of the day I had failed to do justice to my reputation. I was just smiling over the only exception I could make to this sweeping assertion, that of the pale-eyed youth you have sometimes observed dogging my steps, when Briggs came up to me.

===Chinese===
> 「外无瑕垢，内有天真，
> 她不畏危难，因她不知有罪。」

大约两周前，在——音乐厅的一场日场演出之后，我停在通往后门的那条小走廊里点一支雪茄。我心绪不宁。我所奏的那支乐曲中，或是它被接纳的方式中，有某种东西触动了我天性中平时不轻易拨动的弦。我感到孤独。我记得自己站在那里时曾问：这一切到底算得了什么？那一群鼓掌的人当中，有谁会在一场漫长而折磨人的病中守在我床边？又有谁会像此刻奉上赞辞那般奉上同情——倘若我未能保住名声、未能赢得当日的荣光？我正为这番斩钉截铁的断言中唯一的例外——便是你有时会注意到那个老跟在我身后、眼神苍白无力的青年——微微一笑，布里格斯（Briggs）走上前来。

===Original===
"There is a woman here, sir, who insists on seeing you; she has been waiting through half the last piece. Shall I tell her you are coming out?"

"A woman!" exclaimed I, somewhat surprised, for my visitors are not apt to be of the gentler sex.

"Yes sir, an old one. She seems very anxious to speak to you. I could not get rid of her no how."

===Chinese===
「先生，这里有位太太，非要见您不可；最后那支曲子她都等了半场了。要我去告诉她您这就出来吗？」

「一个女人！」我喊道，颇为惊讶，因为我的访客向来不大会是女性。

「是的先生，一位上了年纪的。她好像急着要跟您说话。我怎么也打发不走她。」

===Original===
I hurried forward to the muffled figure which he pointed out cowering against the wall by the door. "Well, my good woman, what do you want?" I asked, bending towards her in the hopes of catching a glimpse of the face she held partly concealed from me.

"Are you Mr. Mandeville?" she inquired in a tone shaken as much by agitation as age.

I bowed.

"The one who plays upon the piano?"

"The very same," I declared.

"You are not deceiving me," she went on, looking up with a marked anxiety plainly visible through her veil. "I haven't seen you play and couldn't contradict you, but—"

"Here!" said I calling to Briggs with a kindly look at the old woman, "help me on with my coat, will you?"

The "Certainly, Mr. Mandeville," with which he complied seemed to reassure her, and as soon as the coat was on and he was gone, she grasped me by the arm and drew my ear down to her mouth.

===Chinese===
我快步走向他所指的那个裹得严严的身影，她正蜷缩在门边的墙根。「好了，好婆婆，你有什么事？」我俯身向她问道，想借机瞥一眼她有意对我半遮半掩的面容。

「您是曼德维尔先生吗？」她问道，那声音因激动与年迈而同样地颤动着。

我鞠了一躬。

「是弹钢琴的那一位？」

「正是在下。」我答道。

「您没有骗我，」她接着说，抬起头来，隔着面纱也分明看得出那种显著的焦虑。「我没见过您弹琴，也没法反驳您，不过——」

「布里格斯！」我招呼他，同时和善地看了那老妇人一眼，「帮我把外套穿上，好吗？」

他那声「好的，曼德维尔先生」似乎使她安下心来，等外套一穿好、他一走开，她便一把抓住我的胳膊，把我的耳朵拉到她嘴边。

===Original===
"If you are Mr. Mandeville, I have a message for you. This letter," slipping one into my hand, "is from a young lady, sir. She bade me give it to you myself. She is young and pretty," she pursued as she saw me make a movement of distaste, "and a lady. We depend upon your honor, sir."

I acknowledge that my first impulse was to fling her back the note and leave the building; I was in no mood for trifling, my next to burst into a laugh and politely hand her to the door, my last and best, to open the poor little note and see for myself whether the writer was a lady or not. Proceeding to the door, for it was already twilight in the dim passage way, I tore open the envelope which was dainty enough and took out a sheet of closely written paper. A certain qualm of conscience assailed me as I saw the delicate chirography it disclosed and I was tempted to thrust it back and return it unread to the old woman now trembling in the corner. But curiosity overcame my scruples, and hastily unfolding the sheet I read these lines:

===Chinese===
「您若是曼德维尔先生，我便有一桩口信给您。这封信，」她把一封信塞进我手里，「是一位小姐写的，先生。她吩咐我亲手交给您。她又年轻又漂亮，」见我露出不悦之色她追了一句，「而且是一位小姐。我们全凭您的君子之风了，先生。」

我承认我的头一个念头是把信掷还给她、径自离开；我全无逢场作戏的心情；第二个念头是大笑一声、客客气气地把她送出门；最后一个，也是最好的一个念头，是拆开这可怜的小信，亲自看看写信的人是不是一位小姐。我走向门口——昏暗的过道里已是薄暮时分——撕开了那相当精致的信封，抽出一张写满了密密麻麻小字的信纸。看到纸上那娟秀的字迹，我心中涌起一阵良心上的不安，竟想把信塞回去，原封不动地还给此刻在角落里瑟瑟发抖的老妇人。但好奇心战胜了顾忌，我匆匆展开信纸，读到这样几行：

===Original===
> "I do not know if what I do is right; I am sure aunty would not say it was; but aunty never thinks anything is right but going to church and reading the papers to papa. I am just a little girl who has heard you play, and who would think the world was too beautiful, if she could hear you say to her just once, some of the kind things you must speak every day to the persons who know you. I do not expect very much—you must have a great many friends, and you would not care for me—but the least little look, if it were all my own, would make me so happy and so proud I should not envy anybody in the world, unless it was some of those dear friends who see you always.
> "I do not come and hear you play often, for aunty thinks music frivolous, but I am always hearing you no matter where I am, and it makes me feel as if I were far away from everybody, in a beautiful land all sunshine and flowers. But nurse says I must not write so much or you will not read it, so I will stop here. But if you *would* come it would make someone happier than even your beautiful music could do."

===Chinese===
> 「我不知道我这样做对不对；我敢肯定姑姑不会说它对；可姑姑除了去做礼拜、给爸爸读报纸，从不觉得什么事是对的。我只是一个小姑娘，听过您弹琴；倘若她能听您对她说上一次——哪怕只有一次——您每天必定对认识您的人说的那些亲切话语，她便会觉得这世界美得不像话了。我不敢奢望太多——您一定有很多朋友，您也不会在意我——但哪怕是最小的一个眼神，只要它是完全属于我的，就会让我那样快乐、那样骄傲，全世界的人我都不羡慕了，至多只羡慕那些总能见到您的亲爱的朋友们。
> 「我不常来听您弹琴，因为姑姑觉得音乐轻浮，但无论我在哪里，我总听见您；那使我感到仿佛自己远离了一切人，置身于一片阳光与鲜花的美地。可是保姆说我不能写这么多，否则您就不看了，所以我就写到这里。可要是您*肯*来，那会使一个人比您最美的音乐所能做到的还要快乐。」

===Original===
That was all; there was neither name nor date. A child's epistle, written with a woman's circumspection. With mingled sensations of doubt and curiosity I turned back to the old woman who stood awaiting me with eager anxiety.

"Was this written by a child or woman?" I asked, meeting her eye with as much sternness as I could assume.

"Don't ask me—don't ask me anything. I have promised to bring you if I could, but I cannot answer any questions."

===Chinese===
就这些；既没有署名，也没有日期。一封孩子的信，却带着一个成年女子的谨慎。怀着疑虑与好奇交织的心情，我转向那老妇人，她正焦灼地等着我的回答。

「这是一个孩子写的，还是一个女人写的？」我问道，尽可能板起脸与她对视。

「别问我——什么也别问我。我答应过，只要能便把您请去，可我什么问题也不能回答。」

===Original===
I stepped back with an incredulous laugh. Here was evidently an adventure. "You will at least tell me where the young miss lives," said I, "before I undertake to fulfil her request."

She shook her head. "I have a carriage at the door, sir," said she. "All you have got to do is to get into it with me and we shall soon be at the house."

===Chinese===
我退后一步，发出一声难以置信的笑。这显然是一桩奇遇了。「在我答应她的请求之前，你至少该告诉我这位小姐住在哪里吧。」我说。

她摇了摇头。「门口有马车等着呢，先生，」她说，「您只消跟我一起上车，我们很快就能到那宅子。」

===Original===
I looked from her face to the letter in my hand, and knew not what to think. The spirit of simplicity and ingenuousness that marked the latter was scarcely in keeping with this air of mystery. The woman observing my hesitation moved towards the door.

"Will you come, sir?" she inquired. "You will not regret it. Just a moment's talk with a pretty young girl—surely—"

"Hush," said I, hearing a hasty step behind me. And sure enough just then my intimate friend Selby came along and grasping me by the arm began dragging me towards the door. "You are my property," said he. "I've promised, on my word of honor as a gentleman and a musician, to bring you to the Handel Club this afternoon. I was afraid you had escaped me, but—" Here he caught sight of the small black figure halting in the doorway, and paused.

"Who's this?" said he.

===Chinese===
我从她的脸看到手中的信，不知该作何想法。信中所透出的那份质朴与天真，与眼前这种神秘气氛实在不相称。那妇人看出我的犹豫，便朝门边走去。

「您来吗，先生？」她问。「您不会后悔的。不过同一个漂亮小姑娘说几句话——总归——」

「嘘，」我说，听见身后有一阵急促的脚步声。果不其然，这时我的挚友塞尔比（Selby）走了过来，一把抓住我的胳膊，拽着我朝门口走。「你是我的，」他说，「我以绅士与音乐家的名誉担保过，今天下午要把你带到亨德尔俱乐部去。我还怕你溜了呢，不过——」说到这里，他瞥见那个停在门口的矮小黑影，便顿住了。

「这是谁？」他问。

===Original===
I hesitated. For one instant the scale of my whole future destiny hung trembling in the balance, then the demon of curiosity got the better of my judgment, and with the rather unworthy consideration that I might as well enjoy my youth while I could, I released myself from my friend's detaining hand and replied, "Someone with whom I have very particular business. I cannot go to the Handel Club today," and darting out without further delay, I rejoined the old woman on the sidewalk.

Without a word she drew me towards a carriage I now observed standing by the curbstone a few feet to the left. As I got in I remember pausing a moment to glance at the man on the box, but it was too dark for me to perceive anything but the fact that he was dressed in livery. More and more astonished I leaned back in my seat and endeavored to open conversation with my mysterious companion. But it did not work. Without being actually rude, she parried my questions in such a way that by the end of five minutes I found myself as far from any knowledge of the real situation of the case as when I started. I therefore desisted from any further attempts and turned to look out, when I made a discovery that for the first time awoke some vague feelings of alarm within my breast. This was, that the window was not covered by a curtain as I supposed, but by closed blinds which when I tried to raise them resisted all my efforts to do so.

===Chinese===
我犹豫了。有那么一刹那，我一生的命运如同一架颤抖的天平悬而未决；随后好奇的魔鬼压过了我的判断力，我怀着一种颇为卑下的念头——趁还能享受青春便享受罢——挣脱了朋友拉住我的手，答道：「我有一桩非常要紧的事要见的人。今天不能去亨德尔俱乐部了。」说罢便不再耽搁地冲了出去，重新回到人行道上那老妇人身旁。

她一言不发，把我拉向一辆我此时才注意到的、停在左边几步外路边的马车。我上车时记得停了一停，朝车夫座上那人瞥了一眼，但天色太暗，我只看出他穿着号衣。我越发惊异，靠在座位上，试图与我这位神秘的同伴攀谈。可这没有用。她虽不至真的失礼，却把我的问题挡得滴水不漏，等到五分钟过去，我发现自己对实情的了解，竟与刚出发时一样茫然。于是我不再尝试，转头朝外看去——这时我发现了一件事，头一次在我胸中唤起一阵隐隐的惊惶：那窗户遮蔽的并非如我所想的是一道帘子，而是紧闭的百叶窗，我试图把它们拉起来时，它们纹丝不动。

===Original===
"It is very close here," I muttered, in some sort of excuse for this display of uneasiness. "Cannot you give us a little air?" But my companion remained silent, and I felt ashamed to press the matter though I took advantage of the darkness to remove to a safer place a roll of money which I had about me.

Yet I was far from being really anxious, and did not once meditate backing out of an adventure that was at once so piquant and romantic. For by this time I became conscious from the sounds about me that we had left the side street for one of the avenues and were then proceeding rapidly up town. Listening, I heard the roll of omnibuses and the jingle of car-bells, which informed me that we were in Broadway, no other avenue in the city being traversed by both these methods of conveyance. But after awhile the jingle ceased and presently the livelier sounds of constant commotion inseparable from a business thoroughfare, and we entered what I took to be Madison Avenue at Twenty-third Street.

===Chinese===
「这里头好闷，」我咕哝了一句，多少算是为自己这份不安的流露找个借口。「能不能给我们透点气？」可我的同伴一言不发，我也不好意思再追问，只是趁着黑暗把身上带着的一卷钞票挪到了更稳妥的地方。

不过我远远谈不上当真焦虑，也压根没想过要退出这场既刺激又浪漫的奇遇。因为这时我从周围的声音中觉察到，我们已经从那条小街拐上了一条大道，正迅速向城北驶去。我侧耳倾听，听见公共马车的辚辚声与有轨马车的铃铛叮当声，这告诉我我们在百老汇（Broadway）——城里没有第二条大道同时通行这两种交通工具。但过了一阵，叮当声止息，不久，那条商业大街所特有的、一刻不停的喧嚣的更活泼的声响也消失了，我们驶入的，据我推断是二十三街处的麦迪逊大道（Madison Avenue）。

===Original===
Instantly I made up mind to notice every turn of the carriage, that I might fix to some degree the locality towards which we were tending. But it turned but once and that after a distance of steady travelling that quite overthrew any calculation I was able to make at that time of the probable number of streets we had passed since entering the avenue. Having turned, it went but about half a block to the left when it stopped. "I shall see where I am when I get out," thought I; but in this I was mistaken.

First we had stopped in the middle of a block of houses built, as far as I could judge, all after one model. Next the fact of the front door being open, though I saw no one in the hall, somewhat disconcerted me, and I hurried across the sidewalk and up the stoop in a species of maze hardly to be expected from one of my naturally careless disposition. The next moment the door closed behind me and I found myself in a well-lighted hall whose quiet richness betokened it as belonging to a private dwelling of no mean pretensions to elegance.

This was the first surprise I received.

===Chinese===
我立刻打定主意，注意马车每一个转弯，好多少固定一下我们所去之处的方位。可它只转了一次弯，而且是在笔直行驶了一段距离之后才转的——那段距离足以彻底推翻我当时所能做出的、关于自驶上大道以来经过了多少条街的任何估算。转弯之后，它只向左走了约莫半个街区便停下了。「下车时我总能看清自己在哪儿吧，」我心想；可这一点我想错了。

首先，我们停在了一排房屋的中段，那些房屋据我判断是照同一个模子建造的。其次，前门虽开着，门厅里我却看不见一个人，这多少使我手足无措，我几乎是迷迷瞪瞪地快步穿过人行道、登上台阶的——这种状态实在不像我向来大大咧咧的性子。紧接着，门在我身后关上了，我发现自己置身于一个灯火通明的门厅，那沉静的富丽说明它属于一座对雅致颇有讲究的私人宅邸。

这便是我的头一个意外。

===Original===
"Follow me," said the old woman, hurrying me down the hall and into a small room at the end. "The young lady will be here in a moment," and without lifting her veil or affording me the least glimpse of her features, she retired, leaving me to face the situation before me as best I might.

It was anything but a pleasant one as it appeared to me at that moment, and for an instant I seriously thought of retracing my steps and leaving a domicile into which I had been introduced in such a mysterious manner. Then the quiet aspect of the room, which though sparsely furnished with a piano and chairs was still of an order rarely seen out of gentlemen's houses, struck my imagination and reawakened my curiosity, and nerving myself to meet whatever interview might be accorded me, I waited. It was only five minutes by the small clock ticking on the mantelpiece, but it seemed an hour before I heard a timid step at the door, and saw it swing slowly open, disclosing—well, I did not stop to inquire whether it was a child or a woman. I merely saw the shrinking modest form, the eager blushing face, and bowed almost to the ground in a sudden reverence for the sublime innocence revealed to me. Yes, it did not take a second look to read that tender countenance to its last guileless page. Had she been a woman of twenty-five I could not have mistaken her expression of pure delight and timid interest, but she was only sixteen, as I afterwards learned, and younger in experience than in age.

===Chinese===
「跟我来，」那老妇人说，催着我穿过门厅，走进尽头的一间小屋。「小姐一会儿就来，」她说着便退了出去，既不揭开面纱、也不让我瞥见她容貌的一丝半点，把我丢在那里，让我自己尽量去面对眼前的处境。

那一刻我觉得这处境怎么也算不上愉快，有一瞬间我当真认真地想过转身离去，离开这座以如此神秘方式把我引介进来的宅子。然而那房间宁静的面貌——虽说陈设简素，只有一架钢琴和几把椅子，却仍是绅士之家之外罕见的格调——触动了我的想象，重新唤起了我的好奇，我壮起胆子准备应对任何可能获准的会面，便等着。壁炉台上那只小钟滴答了不过五分钟，我却觉得过了一个钟头，才听到门口怯怯的脚步声，看见门缓缓打开，露出——唉，我根本没停下追究来的是孩子还是女人。我只看见那瑟缩而矜持的身形、那张热切涨红的脸，便几乎触地般深深鞠了一躬，出于对向我展现的那份崇高的天真之骤然的敬意。是的，不用看第二眼便能把那张温柔的脸读到最后一页无邪。纵然她是二十五岁的女子，我也不可能误解她那种纯粹的喜悦与怯生生的关切；可她只有十六岁——这是我后来才知道的——而且阅历之浅甚于年纪之小。

===Original===
Closing the door behind her, she stood for a moment without speaking, then with a deepening of the blush which was only a child's embarrassment in the presence of a stranger, looked up and murmured my name with a word or so of grateful acknowledgment that would have called forth a smile on my lips if I had not been startled by the sudden change that passed over her features when she met my eyes. Was it that I showed my surprise too plainly, or did my admiration manifest itself in my gaze? an admiration great as it was humble, and which was already of a nature such as I had never before given to girl or woman. Whatever it was, she no sooner met my look than she paused, trembled, and started back with a confused murmur, through which I plainly heard her whisper in a low distressed tone, "Oh, what have I done!"

"Called a good friend to your side," said I in the frank, brotherly way I thought most likely to reassure her. "Do not be alarmed, I am only too happy to meet one who evidently enjoys music so well."

===Chinese===
她在身后关上门，站了片刻没说话，随即那红晕更深了一层——那不过是孩子面对生人时的窘迫——她抬起头，低声唤出我的名字，带着一两个字的感激致意；这原本会令我嘴角绽出微笑，若非她迎上我的目光时，脸上忽地掠过那一种变化叫我吃了一惊。是我把自己的惊讶表现得太露骨了，还是我的倾慕流露在了我的目光里？那种倾慕，既巨大又谦卑，而且已是我从未施与任何女孩或女子的一种。无论是什么，她一碰上我的目光便顿住、发颤，倒退一步，发出一声慌乱的低语，我清清楚楚听见她以痛苦的低声喃喃道：「哦，我都做了什么呀！」

「把一位好朋友叫到了你身边，」我以坦率的、兄长般的口吻说，我觉得这最能令她安心。「别害怕，能见到一位显然如此热爱音乐的人，我真是再高兴不过了。」

===Original===
But the hidden chord of womanhood had been struck in the child's soul, and she could not recover herself. For an instant I thought she would turn and flee, and struck as I was with remorse at my reckless invasion of this uncontaminated temple, I could not but admire the spirited picture she presented as, with form half turned and face bent back, she stood hesitating on the point of flight.

I did not try to stop her. "She shall follow her own impulse," said I to myself, but I felt a vague relief that was deeper than I imagined, when she suddenly relinquished her strained attitude, and advancing a step or so began to murmur:

"I did not know—I did not realize I was doing what was so very wrong. Young ladies do not ask gentlemen to come and see them, no matter how much they desire to make their acquaintance. I see it now; I did not before. Will you—can you forgive me?"

===Chinese===
然而，女子之天性那根隐秘的弦已在孩子灵魂中被拨响，她无法恢复如常。有一瞬间我以为她要转身逃走；而尽管我为自己莽撞闯入这座未受玷污的神殿而痛悔不已，却仍不禁欣赏她此刻所呈现的那幅生动的图景——身形半转、脸却回望，她在将逃未逃之间踟蹰伫立。

我没有试图拦她。「让她顺着自己的冲动行事吧，」我对自己说，可当她忽然卸下那紧绷的姿态，向前迈了一两步，开始低声说道时，我感到一种比想象中更深的、隐隐的释然：

「我不知道——我没意识到我在做一件这样不对的事。年轻小姐不会请先生来看她们，无论她们多么想结识对方。我现在明白了；以前不明白。您能不能——您能不能原谅我？」

===Original===
I smiled; I could not help it. I could have taken her to my heart and soothed her as I would a child, but the pallor of womanhood, which had replaced the blush of the child, awed me and made my own words come hesitatingly.

"Forgive you? You must forgive me! It was as wrong for me," I went on with a wild idea of not mincing matters with this pure soul, "to obey your innocent request, as it was for you to make it. I am a man of the world and know its convenances; you are very young."

"I am sixteen," she murmured.

The abrupt little confession, implying as it did her determination not to accept any palliation of her conduct which it did not deserve, touched me strangely. "But very young for that," I exclaimed.

===Chinese===
我笑了；忍不住。我本可以把她揽入怀中，像哄孩子一般安抚她，可是属于女子而非孩子的那份苍白取代了孩子的红晕，令我心生敬畏，使我自己的话也变得嗫嚅。

「原谅你？该是你原谅我！我顺从你那天真的请求，」我接着说，怀着一种不愿与这纯洁灵魂含糊其辞的冲动念头，「和你提出这请求一样地不对。我是个阅历世事的男子，懂得世上的规矩；你还太小。」

「我十六了。」她低声说。

这句突兀的小小自白——其中隐含着她不肯接受任何她不该得的替自己开脱之意——奇异地触动了我。「可对于那件事，还是太小了。」我喊道。

===Original===
"So aunty says, but no one can ever say it any more," she answered. Then with a sudden gush, "We shall never see each other again, and you must forget the motherless girl who has met you in a way for which she must blush through life. It is no excuse," she pursued hurriedly, "that nurse thought it was all right. She always approves of everything I do or want to do, especially if it is anything aunt would be likely to forbid. I have been spoiled by nurse."

"Was nurse the woman who came for me?" I asked.

She nodded her head with a quick little motion inexpressibly charming. "Yes, that was nurse. She said she would do it all, I need only write the note. She meant to give me a pleasure, but she did wrong."

===Chinese===
「姑姑也这么说，可再也不会有人能这么说了。」她答道。随即一阵汹涌：「我们再也不会相见了，你一定要忘记这个以令她终生都要脸红的方式与你相见的、没有母亲的姑娘。这不能算借口，」她急急地往下说，「保姆觉得这没什么。她总是赞成我做的或想做的每一件事，尤其是姑姑可能不准的事。我被保姆惯坏了。」

「保姆就是来接我的那个妇人吗？」我问。

她点了点头，那个急促的小动作有着说不出的可爱。「是的，那是保姆。她说一切由她来办，我只需写那张便条。她原想给我一点快乐，可她做错了。」

===Original===
"Yes," thought I, "how wrong you little know or realize." But I only said, "You must be guided by someone with more knowledge of the world after this. Not," I made haste to add, struck by the misery in her child eyes, "that any harm has been done. You could not have appealed to the friendship of anyone who would hold you in greater respect than I. Whether we meet again or not, my memory of you shall be sweet and sacred, I promise you that."

But she threw out her hand with a quick gesture. "No, do not remember me. My only happiness will lie in the thought you have forgotten." And the last remnants of the child soul vanished in that hurried utterance. "You must go now," she continued more calmly. "The carriage that brought you is at the door; I must ask you to take it back to your home."

===Chinese===
「是啊，」我心想，「你哪里知道、哪里意识到有多错。」可我只是说：「今后你该让一个更通晓世事的人来引导你。不过，」见她孩子气的眼中那份痛苦，我连忙补了一句，「并没有造成什么损害。你不可能找到一个比我更尊重你的人来寄托友谊了。无论我们是否再见，我对你的记忆都将是甜蜜而神圣的，我向你保证。」

可她猛地一伸手。「不，别记着我。我唯一的快乐，将寄托在你已忘却的念头上。」孩子灵魂最后的余烬，在这句急促的话语中消散了。「你现在得走了，」她较为平静地接着说，「送你来的那辆马车就在门口；我得请你坐它回家。」

===Original===
"But," I exclaimed with a wild and unbearable sense of sudden loss as she laid her hand on the knob of the door, "are we to part like this? Will you not at least trust me with your name before I go?"

Her hand dropped from the knob as if it had been hot steel, and she turned towards me with a slow yearning motion that whatever it betokened set my heart beating violently. "You do not know it, then?" she inquired.

"I know nothing but what this little note contains," I replied, drawing her letter from my pocket.

"Oh, that letter! I must have it," she murmured; then, as I stepped towards her, drew back and pointing to the table said, "Lay it there, please."

===Chinese===
「可是，」当她把手放到门把手上时，我怀着一种骤然失去的、狂乱而无法忍受之感喊道，「我们就这样分别吗？在我走之前，你难道不愿至少把你的名字告诉我吗？」

她的手从门把上落下，仿佛那是一块烧红的铁，她带着一种缓缓的、渴慕的动作转向我——无论那意味着什么，都使我的心猛烈地跳了起来。「那么，你不知道？」

「除了这张小条子里写的，我什么都不知道。」我答道，从口袋里掏出她的信。

「哦，那封信！我得要回它。」她低声道；随即，当我向她迈步时，她退后一步，指着桌子说：「请把它放在那里。」

===Original===
I did so, whereupon something like a smile crossed her lips and I thought she was going to reward me with her name, but she only said, "I thank you; now you know nothing;" and almost before I realized it she had opened the door and stepped into the hall.

As I made haste to follow her, the sound of a low, "He is a gentleman, he will ask no questions," struck my ear, and looking up, I saw her just leaving the side of the old nurse who stood evidently awaiting me half down the hall. Bowing with formal ceremony, I passed her by and proceeded to the front door. As I did so I caught one glimpse of her face. It had escaped from all restraint and the expression of the eyes was overpowering. I subdued a wild impulse to leap back to her side, and stepped at once over the threshold. The nurse joined me, and together we went down the stoop to the street.

===Chinese===
我照做了，于是一抹近似微笑的神情掠过她的唇，我以为她要以她的名字作为酬报，可她只说了一句：「我谢您；如今您什么都不知道了；」几乎不等我回过神来，她已打开门，跨进了门厅。

我急忙跟上去，一句低低的「他是个君子，他不会多问的」传入我耳中，抬头一看，她正从那老保姆身边走开——保姆显然在门厅中段等着我。我郑重其事地鞠了一躬，与她擦肩而过，朝前门走去。这时我瞥见了她一眼脸。那张脸上的所有矜持都已卸尽，那双眼睛里的神情压倒一切。我压下一股扑回她身边的狂野冲动，径直跨过了门槛。保姆跟上来，我们一同走下台阶，来到街上。

===Original===
"May I inquire where you wish to be taken?" she asked.

I told her, and she gave the order to the coachman, together with a few words I did not hear; then stepping back she waited for me to get in. There was no help for it. I gave one quick look behind me, saw the front door close, realized how impossible it would ever be for me to recognize the house again, and placed my foot on the carriage step. Suddenly a bright idea struck me, and hastily dropping my cane I stepped back to pick it up. As I did so I pulled out a bit of crayon I chanced to have in my pocket, and as I stooped, chalked a small cross on the curbstone directly in front of the house, after which I recovered my cane, uttered some murmured word of apology, jumped into the carriage and was about to shut the door, when the old nurse stepped in after me and quietly closed it herself. By the pang that shot through my breast as the carriage wheels left the house, I knew that for the first time in my life, I *loved*.

===Chinese===
「请问您要被送到哪里去？」她问。

我告诉了她，她向车夫下了命令，又说了几句我没听见的话；然后退后一步，等着我上车。别无他法了。我飞快地回头看了一眼，看见前门关上了，意识到我从此再也无法认出这座宅子，便把脚踩上了马车的踏级。忽然一个妙计涌上心头，我急忙把手杖弄掉，退后一步去捡。借着弯腰的工夫，我从口袋里掏出一截恰好带在身上的粉笔，俯身在屋前正对的路缘石上画了一个小小的十字，然后捡起手杖，含含糊糊地道了声歉，跳上马车，正要关门——老保姆跟在我身后，亲自轻轻把门带上了。当马车的车轮驶离宅子，一阵锐痛穿过我的胸膛，那一刻我知道：这是我有生以来头一次，我*爱*了。

## XXXI A Question / 三十一 一个问题

===Original===
> "Think on thy sins."

The next morning when Mr. Sylvester came down to breakfast, he found on the library-table an exquisite casket, similar to the one he had given Paula the night before, but larger, and filled with flowers of the most delicious odor.
"For Miss Fairchild," explained Samuel, who was at that moment passing through the room.
With a pang of jealous surprise, that, however, failed to betray itself in his steadily composed countenance, Mr. Sylvester advanced to the side of the table, and lifted up the card that hung attached to the beautiful present. The name he read there seemed to startle him; he moved away, and took up his paper with a dark flush on his brow, that had not disappeared when Miss Belinda entered the room.
"Humph!" was her immediate exclamation, as her eye rested upon the conspicuous offering in the centre of the apartment. But instantly remembering herself, advanced with a cheerful good morning, which however did not prevent her eyes from wandering with no small satisfaction towards this fresh evidence of Mr. Ensign's assiduous regard.

===Chinese===
> 「想想你自己的罪吧。」

次日上午，西尔维斯特先生下楼用早餐时，在书房桌上看见一只精美的匣子，与他前一夜赠给宝拉的那只相仿，却更大些，里面满满盛着花香最为醉人的鲜花。
「费尔柴尔德（Fairchild）小姐的。」正穿过房间的塞缪尔（Samuel）解释道。
一阵嫉恨的惊愕刺中西尔维斯特先生，然而那情绪并未在他那一贯沉稳从容的面容上露出来；他走到桌边，拈起系在那件美丽礼物上的名片。他读到的那名字似乎令他一惊；他走开了，拿起报纸，额上罩着一层阴沉的红潮——这红潮直到贝琳达小姐走进房间时仍未褪去。
「哼！」她的目光一落在屋子正中那件显眼的馈赠上，便立即脱口喊了一声。可她随即记起了自己的身份，上前快活地道了声早安，然而这并不妨碍她的目光怀着不小的满足，频频飘向恩赛恩（Ensign）先生殷勤情意的这一新佐证。

===Original===
"Paula is remembered by others than ourselves," remarked Mr. Sylvester, probably observing her glance.
"Yes; she has a very attentive suitor in Mr. Ensign," returned Miss Belinda shortly. "A pleasant appearing young man," she ejaculated next moment; "worthy in many respects of success, I should say."
"Has he—do you mean to say that he has visited you in Grotewell?" asked Mr. Sylvester, his eye upon the paper in his hand.
"Certainly; a few more interviews will settle it."
The paper rustled in Mr. Sylvester's grasp, but his voice was composed if not formal, as he observed, "She regards his attentions then with favor?"
"She wears his flowers in her bosom, and brightens like a flower herself when he is seen to approach. If allowed to go her way unhindered, I have but little doubt as to how it will end. Mr. Ensign is not handsome, but I am told that he has every other qualification likely to make a gentle creature like Paula happy."
"He is a good fellow," exclaimed Mr. Sylvester under his breath.

===Chinese===
「除我们之外，惦记宝拉的还大有人在。」西尔维斯特先生说道，大概是留意到了她的目光。
「是的；恩赛恩先生对她可是个十分殷勤的求婚者。」贝琳达小姐简短地回道。「是个模样讨人喜欢的年轻人，」她紧接着又冒出一句；「就许多方面而言，他配得上赢得这门亲事，我该这么说。」
「他可——你是说，他到格罗特韦尔（Grotewell）看过你们？」西尔维斯特先生问道，眼睛盯着手里那张报纸。
「当然；再会几次面，这事就能定下来了。」
报纸在西尔维斯特先生手中簌簌作响，但他说话的声音却沉稳、近乎客套：「那么，她对他的殷勤是另眼相看的了？」
「她把他送的花别在胸前，远远看见他走近，自己便也像一朵花似地亮了起来。倘若由着她不受妨碍地走下去，这件事会如何收场，我几乎毫无疑虑。恩赛恩先生算不上俊美，但听说除了相貌之外，凡是足以让宝拉这般温柔性情的女子幸福的条件，他一应俱全。」
「他是个好人。」西尔维斯特先生低声叹道。

===Original===
"And goodness is the first essential in the character of the man who is to marry Paula," inexorably observed Miss Belinda. "An open, cheerful disposition, a clear conscience and a past with no dark pages in its history, must mark him who is to link unto his fate our pure and sensitive Paula. Is it not so, Mr. Sylvester?"
The advertisements in that morning's *Tribune* must have been unusually interesting, judging from the difficulty which Mr. Sylvester experienced in withdrawing his eyes from them. "The man whom Paula marries," said he at last, "can neither be too good, too kind, or too pure. Nor shall any other than a good, kind, and pure man possess her," he added in a tone that while low, effectually hushed even the slow-to-be-intimidated Miss Belinda. In another moment Paula entered.

===Chinese===
「而善良，正是要娶宝拉的男子的人品中所不可或缺的头一条。」贝琳达小姐毫不通融地说。「一个坦荡开朗的性情，一颗清白的良心，一段没有污暗篇章的过往——这些都是要把我们纯洁而敏感的宝拉与自己命运相系之人所必须具备的。难道不是这样吗，西尔维斯特先生？」
那天早晨《论坛报》（*Tribune*）上的广告想必格外有趣，因为西尔维斯特先生要把目光从上面移开，竟有那样大的困难。「宝拉所嫁的人，」他终于开口道，「再怎么善良、再怎么厚道、再怎么纯洁，都不过分。而且，除一个善良、厚道、纯洁的男子之外，谁也不会得到她。」他又以一种虽低却令连那不易被吓住的贝琳达小姐也噤了声的口吻补上一句。说话间，宝拉走了进来。

===Original===
Oh, the morning freshness of some faces! Like the singing of birds in a prison, is the sound and sight of a lovely maiden coming into the grim, gray atmosphere of a winter breakfast room. Paula was exceptionally gifted with this auroral cheer which starts the day so brightly. At sight of her face Mr. Sylvester dropped his paper, and even Miss Belinda straightened herself more energetically. "Merry Christmas," cried her sweet young voice, and immediately the whole day seemed to grow glad with promise and gaysome with ringing sleigh-bells. "It's snowing, did you know it? A world of life is in the air; the flakes dance as they come down, like dervishes in a frenzy. It was all we lacked to make the day complete; now we have everything."
"Yes," said Miss Belinda, with a significant glance at the table, "everything."
Paula followed her glance, saw the silver box with its wealth of blossoms, and faltered back with a quick look at Mr. Sylvester's grave and watchful countenance.

===Chinese===
哦，有些脸庞上的那种清晨般的清新！一个可爱的少女走进冬日早餐室那阴沉灰暗的气息里，那声音、那身影，便如同牢狱之中鸟儿的歌唱。宝拉格外得天独厚地拥有这种晨曦般的明朗，能把一日的开端照得如此明媚。一见她的脸，西尔维斯特先生放下了报纸，连贝琳达小姐也挺直了腰板，更精神了几分。「圣诞快乐。」她那甜美的年轻嗓音喊道，霎时间，这一整天都仿佛因希望而欢悦起来，因叮当作响的雪橇铃铛而热闹起来。「下雪了，你们知道吗？空气里满是生机；雪花落下来时翩翩起舞，像发了狂的托钵僧。这正是我们唯独欠缺的、能使今日圆满的一样东西；如今我们样样齐全了。」
「是啊，」贝琳达小姐说着，意味深长地朝桌上看了一眼，「样样齐全。」
宝拉顺着她的目光望去，看见了那只银匣和其中满满的花，她迟疑着向后一缩，飞快地瞥了一眼西尔维斯特先生那凝重而审视的面容。

===Original===
"Mr. Ensign seems to be possessed of clairvoyance," observed Miss Belinda easily. "How he could know that you were to be in town today, I cannot imagine."
"I wrote him in my last letter that in all probability I should spend the holidays with Mr. Sylvester," explained Paula simply, but with a slow and deepening flush, that left the roses she contemplated nothing of which to boast. "I did so, because he proposed to visit Grotewell on Christmas."
There was a short silence in the room, then Mr. Sylvester rose, and remarking with polite composure, "It is a very pretty remembrance," led the way into the dining-room. Paula with a slow drooping of her head quickly followed, while Miss Belinda brought up the rear, with the look of a successful diplomat.

===Chinese===
「恩赛恩先生简直有千里眼。」贝琳达小姐从容地说道。「他怎么会知道你今日要进城，我可猜不透。」
「我在上一封信里告诉过他，我很可能会到西尔维斯特先生这里过节。」宝拉坦然地解释道，脸上却慢慢泛起一层越深越浓的红晕，相形之下，她所注目的那些玫瑰再没有什么可夸耀之处。「我那样写，是因为他提议圣诞节到格罗特韦尔来。」
屋中静了片刻，随后西尔维斯特先生站起身来，以客套而从容的口吻说了一句「这番心意倒是十分可人」，便带头往餐厅走去。宝拉缓缓垂着头，紧随其后，贝琳达小姐殿在最后，一副得意外交家的神情。

===Original===
A meal in the Sylvester mansion was always a formal affair, but this was more than formal. A vague oppression seemed to fill the air; an oppression which Miss Belinda's stirring conversation found it impossible to dissipate. In compliance to Mr. Sylvester's request, she sat at the head of the table, and was the only one who seemed able to eat anything. For one thing she had never seen Ona in that post of honor, but Paula and Mr. Sylvester could not forget the graceful form that once occupied that seat. The first meal above a grave, no matter how long it has been dug, must ever seem weighted with more or less unreality.
Besides, with Paula there was a vague unsettled feeling, as if some delicate inner balance had been too rudely shaken. She longed to fly away and think, and she was obliged to sit still and talk.

===Chinese===
在西尔维斯特先生的宅邸里用膳，向来是拘于礼数的事，而今日这一餐却比拘礼更甚。一种说不清的压抑似乎弥漫在空气里；这种压抑，便是贝琳达小姐那活跃的谈兴也无法驱散。应西尔维斯特先生之请，她坐了上首，也是唯一一个似乎还吃得下东西的人。一则她从未见过奥娜坐过那个主位，可宝拉和西尔维斯特先生却忘不了曾经端坐在那位置上的那优雅身影。在一座新坟之上吃的第一顿饭，无论那坟挖下已有多少时日，总难免带着几分不真实之感。
何况，宝拉心里还有一种说不清的不安，仿佛内心某种精微的平衡被过于粗暴地撼动了。她渴望能飞走、独自去想一想，却不得不端坐不动、应酬说话。

===Original===
The end of the meal was a relief to all parties. Miss Belinda went upstairs, thoughtfully shaking her firm head; Mr. Sylvester sat down again to his paper, and Paula advanced towards the dainty gift that awaited her inspection on the library table. But halfway to it she paused. A strange shyness had seized her. With Mr. Sylvester sitting there, she dared not approach this delicate testimonial of another's affection. She did not know as she wished to. Her eyes stole in hesitation to the floor. Suddenly Mr. Sylvester spoke:
"Why do you not look at your pretty present, Paula?"
She started, gave him a quick glance, and advanced hurriedly towards the table; but scarcely had she reached it when she paused, turned and hastened over to his side. He was still reading, or appearing to read, but she saw his hand tremble where it grasped the sheet, though his face with its clear cut profile, shone calm and cold against the dark background of the wall beyond.

===Chinese===
这一餐的结束，对各方都是一种解脱。贝琳达小姐上了楼，若有所思地摇着她那坚定的脑袋；西尔维斯特先生重新坐下看报，宝拉则走向书房桌上那件等着她赏玩的精巧礼物。可走到一半，她停住了。一种莫名的羞怯攫住了她。有西尔维斯特先生坐在那里，她不敢去触碰这另一个人情意的如此 delicate 的信物。她甚至不知自己是否愿意去碰。她的眼光犹犹豫豫地偷落向地板。忽然，西尔维斯特先生开了口：
「你怎么不看看你那件漂亮的礼物呢，宝拉？」
她一惊，飞快地瞥了他一眼，匆匆朝桌子走去；可刚到桌前她又停住了，转过身，快步走到他身旁。他仍在读报，或装作在读，但她看见他握着报纸的手在发抖，尽管他那轮廓分明的侧脸，在身后幽暗墙壁的映衬下，显得冷静而冷淡。

===Original===
"I do not care to look at it now," said she, with a hurried interlacing of her restless fingers.
He turned towards her and a quick thrill passed over his countenance. "Sit down, Paula," said he, "I want to talk to you."
She obeyed as might an automaton. Was it the tone of his voice that chilled her, or the studied aspect of his fixed and solemn countenance? He did not speak at once, but when he did, there was no faltering in his voice, that was lower than common, but deep, like still waters that have run into dark channels far from the light of day.

===Chinese===
「我现在不想看它了。」她说着，那双不得安宁的手指匆匆交缠在一起。
他转向她，一道迅速的颤动掠过他的面容。「坐下，宝拉，」他说，「我要跟你说话。」
她像个自动木偶似地服从了。是他的语调令她心寒，还是他那刻意摆出来的、凝重而肃穆的面容？他没有立刻开口，可当他终于说话时，声音里没有半点犹疑，那声音比平日低沉，却深沉，如同流进了远离天光的幽暗河道里的静水。

===Original===
"Paula, I want to ask you a question. What would you think of a man that, with deliberate selfishness, went into the king's garden, and plucking up by the roots the most beautiful flower he could find there, carried it into a dungeon to pant out its exquisite life amid chill and darkness?"
"I should think," replied she, after the first startled moment of silence, "that the man did well, if by its one breath of sweetness, the flower could comfort the heart of him who sat in the dungeon."
The glance with which Mr. Sylvester regarded her, suddenly faltered; he turned with quickness towards the fire. "A moment's joy is, then, excuse for a murder," exclaimed he. "God and the angels would not agree with you, Paula."

===Chinese===
「宝拉，我要问你一个问题。你会怎样看待一个人——他蓄意地、自私地，走进国王的花园，把那里所能寻见的最美的一朵花连根拔起，带进一座地牢，让它在阴寒与黑暗之中喘息着耗尽它精致的生命？」
「我会觉得，」她在最初那一惊的沉默之后答道，「这个人做得对——倘若那花的一缕香甜之气，能够安慰那个坐在地牢里的人的心。」
西尔维斯特先生投向她的目光忽然失了定；他迅速转过身去对着炉火。「那么，片刻的欢愉便是谋杀的借口了。」他失声喊道。「上帝和众天使都不会赞同你的，宝拉。」

===Original===
There was a quivering in his tone, made all the more apparent by its studied self-possession of a moment before. She trembled where she sat, and opened her lips to speak, but closed them again, awed by his steady and abstracted gaze, now fixed before him in gloomy reverie. A moment passed. The clock ticking away on the mantelpiece seemed to echo the inevitable "Forever! never!" of Longfellow's old song. Neither of them moved. At length, in a low and trembling voice, Paula spoke:
"Is it murder, when the flower loves the dark of the dungeon more than it does the light of day?"

===Chinese===
他的语调里有某种颤动，因方才那种刻意维持的自持而显得愈发明显。她在座上发着抖，张了张嘴想说话，却又合上，被他那沉稳而出神的目光所震慑——那目光此刻定定地落在前方，沉浸在阴郁的遐想之中。片刻过去了。壁炉架上滴答作响的时钟，仿佛在应和着朗费罗（Longfellow）那首老歌里那无可回避的「永远！决不！」。两人都没动。终于，宝拉以低而颤抖的声音开了口：
「倘若那花爱地牢的幽暗，胜过爱白昼的光明，这还算谋杀吗？」

===Original===
With a subdued but passionate cry he rose hastily to his feet. "Yes," said he, and drew back as if he could not bear the sight of her face or the glance of her eye. "Sunshine is the breath of flowers; sweet wooing gales, their natural atmosphere. He who meddles with a treasure so choice does it at his peril." Then as she hurriedly rose in turn, softened his whole tone, and assuming his usual air of kindly fatherhood, asked her in the most natural way in the world, what he could do to make her happy that day.
"Nothing," replied she, with a droop of her head; "I think I will go and see Cicely."
A short sigh escaped him. "The carriage shall be ready for you," said he. "I hope your friend's happiness will overflow into your own gentle bosom, and make the day a very pleasant one. God bless your young sweet heart, my Paula!"

===Chinese===
他压抑而激烈地喊了一声，匆匆站起身来。「是的。」他说着，向后退了一步，仿佛承受不住她的脸容或她的目光。「阳光是花的呼吸；温柔的求爱之风，才是它们的天然气息。谁若染指这般珍贵的一件宝物，便是自蹈险地。」随即，见她也急忙起身，他便放软了整个语调，重又摆出他平日那种慈父般的神气，用世上最自然的口吻问她，今日他能为她做些什么，好让她高兴。
「什么也不用。」她垂着头答道；「我想去看看西塞莉（Cicely）。」
他短促地叹了一口气。「马车会给你备好。」他说。「但愿你那位朋友的幸福会溢进你温柔的胸怀里，使这一天十分愉快。上帝保佑你那颗年轻甜蜜的心，我的宝拉！」

===Original===
Her breast heaved, her large, dark, mellow eyes flashed with one quick glance towards his face, then she drew back, and in another moment left his side and quietly glided from the room. His very life seemed to go with her, yet he did not stir; but he sighed deeply when, upon turning towards the library-table, he found that she had carried away with her the silent testimonial of another and more fortunate man's love and devotion.

===Chinese===
她的胸膛起伏了一下，那一双幽深、乌黑、柔和的眼睛朝他的脸一闪，随即她退后一步，不多时便离开了他身旁，悄无声息地出了房间。他的整个生命仿佛都随她而去了，可他一动未动；只是当他转身望向书房桌时，发现她已把另一个、也更为幸运的男子那份无声的情意与痴心一并带走了，他便深深地叹了一口气。

## I A Wanderer / 一 流浪者

===Original===
> "There's no such word."

===Chinese===
> 「世间没有这样的字眼。」

===Original===
A wind was blowing through the city. Not a gentle and balmy zephyr, stirring the locks on gentle ladies' foreheads and rustling the curtains in elegant boudoirs, but a chill and bitter gale that rushed with a swoop through narrow alleys and forsaken courtyards, biting the cheeks of the few solitary wanderers that still lingered abroad in the darkened streets.

In front of a cathedral that reared its lofty steeple in the midst of the squalid houses and worse than squalid saloons of one of the dreariest portions of the East Side, stood the form of a woman. She had paused in her rush down the narrow street to listen to the music, perhaps, or to catch a glimpse of the light that now and then burst from the widely swinging doors as they opened and shut upon some tardy worshipper.

===Chinese===
一阵风正穿过这座城市。不是那拂动淑女额前发丝、在雅致闺房里窸窣作响帷幔的温润和风，而是一股凛冽刺骨的狂飙，它呼啸着扑入逼仄的小巷和荒废的庭院，咬噬着那几个仍在昏暗街头流连的孤身行人的脸颊。

东区（East Side）最萧索的地段之一，破败的房屋与比破败更不堪的酒肆之间，矗立着一座大教堂，高高的尖塔直指夜空。教堂门前站着一个女人的身影。她是在沿着窄街疾行时停下了脚步——也许是为了聆听那乐声，也许是为了瞥一眼那从大开的门扇里时时迸射出的灯光：那些门随着某位姗姗来迟的礼拜者进出而一开一合。

===Original===
She was tall and fearful looking; her face, when the light struck it, was seared and desperate; gloom and desolation were written on all the lines of her rigid but wasted form, and when she shuddered under the gale, it was with that force and abandon to which passion lends its aid, and in which the soul proclaims its doom.

===Chinese===
她身材高挑，面容可怖；灯光打到她脸上时，那是一张刻满创伤、绝望至极的脸；阴郁与荒凉写满了她那僵直却消瘦的躯体上的每一道纹路；当她在狂风中战栗时，那是一种唯有激情为之推波助澜的猛烈与放纵，是灵魂在宣告自己的劫数。

===Original===
Suddenly the doors before her swung wide and the preacher's voice was heard: "Love God and you will love your fellow-men. Love your fellow-men and you best show your love to God."

She heard, started, and the charm was broken. "Love!" she echoed with a horrible laugh; "there is no love in heaven or on earth!"

And she swept by, and the winds followed and the darkness swallowed her up like a gulf.

===Chinese===
忽然，她面前的大门洞开，传出了讲道人的声音：「爱上帝，你就会爱你的同胞。爱你的同胞，便是最好地彰显你对上帝的爱。」

她听见了，猛然一惊，那魔咒随之破碎。「爱！」她以一声可怕的笑回声般地应道；「天上地下，都没有爱！」

她一掠而过，风紧随其后，黑暗如深渊般将她吞噬。

## XV An Adventure—Or Something More / 十五 一场奇遇——抑或更多

===Original===
> "Bliss was it in that dawn to be alive,
 But to be young was very heaven."

A ride in the Central Park is an everyday matter to most people. It signifies an indolent bowling over a smooth road all alive with the glitter of passing equipages, waving ribbons and fluttering plumes, and brightened now and then by the sight of a well known face amid the general rush of old and young, plain and handsome, sad and gay countenances that flash by you in one long and brilliant procession.

But to Paula and her friend Miss Stuyvesant starting out in the early freshness of a fair April morning, it meant new life, reawakening joy, the sparkle of young leaves just loosed from the bonds of winter, the sweetness and promise of spring airs, and all the budding glory of a new year with its summer of countless roses and its autumn of incalculable glories. Not the twitter of a bird was lost to them, not the smile of an opening flower, not the welcome of a waving branch. Youth, joy, and innocence lived in their hearts and showed them nothing in the mirror of nature that was not equally young, joyous and innocent. Then they were alone, or sufficiently so. The stray wanderers whom they met sitting under the flowering trees, were equally with themselves lovers of nature or they would not be seated in converse with it at this early hour; while the laugh of little children startled from their play by the prance of their high-stepping horses, was only another expression of the sweet but unexpressed delight that breathed in all the radiant atmosphere.

===Chinese===
> 「在那个黎明，活着便是福祉，
>  而青春正盛，则宛如置身天堂。」

对大多数人而言，在中央公园（Central Park）骑马兜风是再寻常不过的事。那不过是沿着一条平滑的车道慵懒地疾驰而过，整条路都因络绎不绝的车驾而熠熠生辉——飘扬的缎带、颤动的羽饰，还不时因瞥见一张熟识的面孔而添了亮色；老与少、美与丑、愁与欢的面容，在你眼前汇成一支绵长而辉煌的队列，一闪而过。

可对宝拉和她的朋友斯泰弗森特小姐（Miss Stuyvesant）来说，在四月一个晴好清晨的清新气息中出门驰骋，却意味着新生，意味着苏醒的喜悦，意味着初从冬日枷锁中解脱的嫩叶上那一点闪光，意味着春日空气里的甜美与期许，意味着一个新年所有正在吐蕊的荣光——它那数不清玫瑰的夏日，它那不可估量壮丽的秋天。没有一声鸟啼被她们错过，没有一朵初绽之花的微笑，没有一枝迎风招展的树枝的致意。青春、喜悦与天真住在她们心里，使她们在自然的明镜中所见的，无一不同样年轻、喜悦而天真。况且她们是独处的，或差不多算独处。她们遇见的、坐在繁花树下歇息的零星游人，与她们自己一样都是自然的爱好者——否则不会在这般早的时辰坐在这里与自然相对絮语；而那些幼童，因她们那高抬步的马儿小跑而过受了惊、从嬉戏中发出的笑声，也不过是那弥漫于整个灿烂氛围之中、那份甜蜜而未曾道出的欢愉的又一种表达罢了。

===Original===
"We are two birds who have escaped thralldom and are taking our first flight into our natural ether," cried Miss Stuyvesant gaily.

"We are two pioneers lit by the spirit of adventure, who have left the cosy hearth of wintry-fires to explore the domains of the frost king, and lo, we have come upon a Paradise of bloom and color!" responded the ringing voice of Paula.

"I feel as if I could mount that little white cloud we see over there," continued Cicely with a quick lively wave of her whip. "I wonder how Dandy would enjoy an empyrean journey?"

"From the haughty bend of his neck I should say he was quite satisfied with his present condition. But perhaps his chief pride is due to the mistress he carries."

"Are you attempting to vie with Mr. Williams, Paula?"

===Chinese===
「我们是两只逃脱了樊笼的鸟儿，正第一次飞向属于我们的太虚。」斯泰弗森特小姐快活地喊道。

「我们是两名为冒险精神所照亮的拓荒者，离开了冬日炉火旁温暖的炉膛，前去探查霜之王（the frost king）的领地——瞧啊，我们竟撞入了一座花光绚烂的乐园！」宝拉那清亮的嗓音应道。

「我觉得自己简直能飞上我们那边所见的那朵白云，」西塞莉（Cicely）接着说，手中的马鞭轻快地一挥。「不知丹迪（Dandy）对这趟九霄之旅会作何感想？」

「瞧他那傲然弯曲的颈项，我倒要说，他对眼下的处境已是心满意足了。不过他这份得意，或许大半是因他所驮的那位女主人而起吧。」

「宝拉，你这是想跟威廉姆斯（Williams）先生一较高下吗？」

===Original===
Mr. Williams was the meek-eyed, fair complexioned gentleman, whose predilection for compliment was just then a subject of talk in fashionable circles.

"Only so far as my admiration goes of the most charming lady I see this morning. But who is this?"

Miss Stuyvesant looked up. "Ah, that is someone with whom there is very little danger of your falling in love."

Paula blushed. The gentleman approaching them upon horseback was conspicuous for long side whiskers of a decidedly auburn tinge.

"His name is—" But she had not time to finish, for the gentleman with a glance of astonished delight at Paula, bowed to the speaker with a liveliness and grace that demanded some recognition.

Instantly he drew rein. "Do I behold Miss Stuyvesant among the nymphs!" cried he, in those ringing pleasant tones that at once predispose you towards their possessor.

"If you allude to my friend Miss Fairchild, you certainly do, Mr. Ensign," the wicked little lady rejoined with a waiving of her usual ceremony that astonished Paula.

===Chinese===
威廉姆斯先生是位目光温驯、面色白皙的绅士，他那嗜好恭维的脾性，眼下正成了时髦圈子里的一桩谈资。

「我对今早所见最迷人的那位女士的钦慕之情，也不过到那种地步罢了。可这是谁？」

斯泰弗森特小姐抬起头。「啊，那可是位你几乎不大可能爱上的人物。」

宝拉红了脸。骑马向她们迎来的那位绅士，最惹眼之处便是两腮那一部长长的、色调分明的赤褐色络腮鬓。

「他名叫——」她却没来得及把话说完，因为那位绅士带着一脸见了宝拉似的惊喜之色，向说话的她一躬身，那活泛与风度都到了叫人不能不还礼的地步。

他随即勒住缰绳。「我竟在众仙女之间瞧见了斯泰弗森特小姐！」他喊道，嗓音清亮悦耳——这样的嗓音，一入耳便叫你对它的主人先存了好感。

「倘若您所指的就是我这朋友费尔柴尔德（Fairchild）小姐，那您确实瞧见了，恩赛恩（Ensign）先生。」这位促狭的小姐回道，一改平日的客套，倒叫宝拉吃了一惊。

===Original===
Mr. Ensign bestowed upon them his most courtly bow, but the flush that mounted to his brow—making his face one red, as certain of his friends were malicious enough to observe on similar occasions—indicated that he had been taken a little more at his word than perhaps suited even one of his easy and proverbially careless temperament. "Miss Fairchild will understand that I am not a Harvey Williams—at least before an introduction," said he with something like seriousness.

But at this allusion to the gentleman whose name had been upon their lips but a moment before, both ladies laughed outright.

"I have just been accused of attempting the role of that gentleman myself," exclaimed Paula. "If the fresh morning air will persist in painting such roses on ladies' cheeks," continued she, with a loving look at her pretty companion "what can one be expected to do?"

"Admire," quoth the red bannered cavalier with a glance, however, at the beautiful speaker instead of the demure little Cicely at her side.

Miss Stuyvesant perceived this look and a curious smile disturbed the corners of her rosy lips. "What a fortunate man to be able to do the right thing at the right time," laughed she, gaily touching up her horse that was beginning to show symptoms of restlessness.

===Chinese===
恩赛恩先生朝她们施了一个最为殷勤的礼，可涌上额头的红潮——直把他的脸涨得通红，正如他的几位朋友在某些类似场合恶意津津乐道的那样——却表明他这话被人在字面上当得太真了些，纵然以他那随和、出了名的大大咧咧脾气而论，怕也有些不大自在。「费尔柴尔德小姐当会明白，我可不是哈维·威廉姆斯（Harvey Williams）那号人——至少，在尚未经人引见之前不是。」他说这话时带着几分认真的意味。

可这一提到方才还挂在两人嘴边的那位绅士的名字，两位女士竟都纵声大笑起来。

「方才还有人指控我正想扮一扮那位先生的角色呢。」宝拉喊道。「若是这清新的晨风偏要在女士们的两颊绘上这样的玫瑰色，」她接着说，含着怜爱的目光望向身边漂亮的同伴，「那还能指望人怎么办呢？」

「欣赏呗。」这位擎着红旗的骑士答道，然而他这一眼，却是投向那位说话的美人，而不是她身旁那娴静的小西塞莉。

斯泰弗森特小姐察觉了这一眼，嘴角那玫瑰色的唇角被一抹古怪的笑意牵动了牵动。「能在这般恰好的时机做恰好的事，真是个有福之人啊。」她笑着，轻快地催了催自己那匹开始露出些躁动苗头的马。

===Original===
"If Miss Stuyvesant will put that in the future tense and then assure us she has been among the prophets, I should be singularly obliged," said he with a touch of his hat and a smiling look at Paula that was at once manly and gentle, careless and yet respectful.

"Ah, life is too bright for prophesies this morning. The moment is enough."

"Is it Miss Fairchild?" queried Mr. Ensign looking back over his shoulder.

She turned just a bit of her cheek towards him. "What Miss Stuyvesant declares to be true, that am I bound to believe," said she, and with the least little ripple of a laugh, rode on.

"It is a pity you have such a dislike for whiskers," Cicely presently remarked with an air of great gravity.

Paula gave a start and cast a glance of reproach at her companion. "I did not notice his whiskers after the first word or two," said she, fixing her eyes on a turn of the road before them. "Such cheerfulness is infectious. I was merry before, but now I feel as if I had been bathed in sunshine."

Cicely's eyes flashed wide with surprise and her face grew serious in earnest. "Mr. Ensign is a delightful companion," observed she; "a room is always brighter for his entrance; and with all that, he is the only young man I know, who having come into a large fortune, feels any of the responsibilities of his position. The sunshine is the result of a good heart and pure living, and that is what makes it infectious, I suppose."

"Let us canter," said Paula. And so the glad young things swept on, life breaking in bubbles around them and rippling away into unfathomable wells of feeling in one of their pure hearts at least.

===Chinese===
「倘若斯泰弗森特小姐肯把这话换成将来时，再向我们保证她曾在众先知之列，那我便要感激不尽了。」他触了触帽檐，含笑望了宝拉一眼，那目光既豪爽又温柔，既漫不经心又不失恭敬。

「啊，今早的生命太亮了，亮得不耐烦作什么预言。眼前这一刻，便已足够。」

「这位是费尔柴尔德小姐吗？」恩赛恩先生回头问道。

她把半边脸颊略略转向他。「斯泰弗森特小姐既说这是真的，那我自然只得信了。」她说着，伴着极轻极轻的一声笑，策马而去。

「真可惜你对络腮鬓这般反感。」西塞莉随后摆出一副极郑重的神气说道。

宝拉猛地一惊，向同伴投去一道嗔怪的目光。「开初一两个字之后，我便没再留意他的络腮鬓了。」她说，把目光定在前面路的一个拐弯处。「这种快活是会传染的。我本来就已经很高兴了，可这会儿我觉得自己像是浸在阳光里沐浴过了一样。」

西塞莉的眼睛惊得大大地一闪，脸色当真严肃了起来。「恩赛恩先生是个极讨人喜欢的伴儿，」她评道，「只要有他一进门，屋里总要亮上几分；何况他还是我所认识的年轻人里头唯一一个——既然得了偌大一份家财，竟还能对身处之位感到几分责任的人。那份阳光，是一颗好心与一段清白日子的结果，我想，这也正是它之所以会传染的缘故。」

「我们快跑吧。」宝拉说。于是这两个快活的年轻人一路驰骋而去，生命在她们四周化作泡沫迸裂，又荡漾开去，至少在她们某一颗纯洁的心里，淌入了无底的深井。

===Original===
Suddenly a hand seemed to swoop from heaven and dash them both back in dismay. They had reached one of those places where the foot path crosses the equestrian and they had run over and thrown down a little child.

"O heaven!" cried Paula leaping from her horse, "I had rather been killed myself." The groom rode up and she bent anxiously over the child.

It was a boy of some seven or eight years, whose misfortune—he was lame, as the little crutch fallen at his side sufficiently denoted—made appear much younger. He had been struck on his arm and was moaning with pain, but did not seem to be otherwise hurt. "Are you alone?" cried Paula, lifting his head on her arm and glancing hurriedly about.

The little fellow raised his heavy lids and for a moment stared into her face with eyes so deeply blue and beautiful they almost startled her, then with an effort pointed down the path, saying,

"Dad's over there in the long tunnel talking to someone. Tell him I got hurt. I want Dad."

===Chinese===
蓦地，仿佛有一只手从天而降，把两人都惊愕地摔回了原地。她们到了那种人行道横穿马道的地方，竟碾过、撞翻了一个小孩子。

「啊，天哪！」宝拉翻身下马喊道，「倒不如被压死的是我自己。」马夫策马上前，她焦急地俯身向那孩子看去。

那是个七八岁上下的小男孩，可他的不幸——他是瘸的，从掉在身旁的那只小拐杖已足以看出——使他显得比实际年纪小了许多。他的胳膊被撞了一下，正痛得呻吟，旁处似乎倒没受什么伤。「就你一个人吗？」宝拉喊着，一只手托起他的头，一面匆忙地四下张望。

那小家伙吃力地掀起沉重的眼皮，有那么一刻直直地盯着她的脸——那双眼幽蓝得那样深沉、那样美丽，几乎把她都惊了一下——随后费力地朝小径前方一指，说道：

「爸就在那边那个长长的地道里头，正跟人说话呢。告诉他我受伤了。我要爸。」

===Original===
She gently lifted him to his feet and led him out of the road into the apparently deserted path where she made him sit down. "I am going to find his father," said Paula to Cicely, "I will be back in a moment."

"But wait; you shall not go alone," authoritatively exclaimed that little damsel, leaping in her turn to the ground. "Where does he say his father is?"

"In the tunnel, by which I suppose he means that long passage under the bridge over there."

Holding up the skirts of their riding-habits in their trembling right hands, they hurried forward. Suddenly they both paused. A woman had crossed their path; a woman whom to look at but once was to remember with ghastly shrinking for a lifetime. She was wrapped in a long and ragged cloak, and her eyes, startling in their blackness, were fixed upon the pain-drawn countenance of the poor little hurt boy behind them, with a gleam whose feverish hatred and deep malignant enjoyment of his very evident sufferings, was like a revelation from the lowest pit to the two innocent-minded girls hastening forward on their errand of mercy.

===Chinese===
她轻轻把他扶起来，牵着他走出马道，到那条看上去空无一人的小径上让他坐下。「我去找他父亲，」宝拉对西塞莉说，「我一会儿就回来。」

「且慢；你不许一个人去。」这位小个子姑娘以不容置疑的口吻喊道，自己也翻身跳下马来。「他说他父亲在哪儿？」

「在地道里，我想他指的是那边那座桥底下那条长通道。」

她们右手颤抖着提起骑装裙摆，一路紧赶。突然两人都停住了。一个女人横过了她们的去路；这女人，看上一眼便足以叫人一辈子想起来都不寒而栗。她裹着一件又长又破的斗篷，那双眼睛黑得惊人，定定地落在身后那个可怜的受伤小男孩那张因疼痛而扭曲的小脸上，眼中那种狂热的恨意、以及对他那显而易见的苦楚所怀的深深的恶毒快意，在这两个心地纯洁、正匆匆赶着去行善的女孩看来，简直像是来自最深地狱的一则启示。

===Original===
"Is he much hurt?" gasped the woman in an ineffectual effort to conceal the evil nature of her interest. "Do you think he will die?" with a shrill lingering emphasis on the last word as if she longed to roll it like a sweet morsel under her tongue.

"Who are you?" asked Cicely, shrinking to one side with dilated eyes fixed on the woman's hardened countenance and the white, too white hand with which she had pointed as she spoke of the child.

"Are you his mother?" queried Paula, paling at the thought but keeping her ground with an air of unconscious authority.

"His mother!" shrieked the woman, hugging herself in her long cloak and laughing with fiendish sarcasm: "I look like his mother, don't I? His eyes—did you notice his eyes? they are just like mine, aren't they? and his body, poor weazen little thing, looks as if it had drawn sustenance from mine, don't it? His mother! O heaven!"

===Chinese===
「他伤得重吗？」那女人喘着气问道，徒劳地想掩饰她那份关切背后那恶毒的本质。「您觉得他会死吗？」最后这个字她拖出尖利的一声余韵，仿佛恨不得把它当作一粒甘甜的碎屑在舌下反复滚动。

「你是谁？」西塞莉问，缩到一边，圆睁的眼睛定在那女人那张麻木的脸上，以及她方才提到孩子时所抬起的那只白得过分的手上。

「你是他母亲吗？」宝拉问道，一念及此脸色便白了，却仍带着一种浑然不觉的威严立在原地。

「他母亲！」那女人尖声喊道，用那件长斗篷紧紧裹住自己，发出魔鬼般讥讽的笑，「我瞧着像他母亲，是吗？他那双眼睛——你留意到他那双眼睛没有？跟我的一模一样，是不是？还有他那身架子，那副干瘪可怜的小模样，瞧着倒像是从我身子里汲取过养分似的，不是吗？他母亲！啊，老天！」

===Original===
Nothing like the suppressed force of this invocation seething as it was with the worst passions of a depraved human nature, had ever startled those ears before. Clasping Cicely by the hand, she called out to the groom behind them, "Guard that child as you would your life!" and then flashing upon the wretched creature before her with all the force of her aroused nature, she exclaimed, "If you are not his mother, move aside and let us pass, we are in search of assistance."

For an instant the woman stood awestruck before this vision of maidenly beauty and indignation, then she laughed and cried out with shrill emphasis:

"When next you look like that, go to your mirror, and when you see the image it reflects, say to yourself, 'So once looked the woman who defied me in the Park!'"

With a quick shudder and a feeling as if the noisome cloak of this degraded being had somehow been dropped upon her own fair and spotless shoulders, Paula clasped the hand of Cicely more tightly in her own, and rushed with her down the steps that led into the underground passage towards which they had been directed.

===Chinese===
这般压抑的力量，这般因堕落到极点的人性中最恶劣的种种情欲而翻腾蒸腾的呼唤，她们的耳朵还从未被惊动过。宝拉一把抓住西塞莉的手，回头朝身后的马夫喊：「你看好那孩子，像保你自己的命一样保他！」随即以整个被唤醒的本性全部的力量，向眼前这个可悲的生灵投去一瞥，喊道：「你既不是他母亲，便让开，放我们过去，我们正要去找人帮忙。」

有那么一瞬，那女人竟在那少女的美貌与义愤这一番显现之前呆立、生了畏怯，随即她又笑了起来，尖锐地加重了语气叫道：

「下回你再露出这副神情，就去照照镜子，等你看见镜中所映的那个影像，便对自己说：『在公园里顶撞我的那个女人，曾经就是这般模样！』」

宝拉猛地打了个寒噤，只觉仿佛这个堕落生灵那件恶臭的斗篷，不知怎的竟已落到她自己那洁白无瑕的双肩之上了；她把西塞莉的手攥得更紧，拉着她冲下通往那条地下通道的台阶——正是方才那孩子指给她们的方向。

===Original===
There were but two persons in it when they entered. A short thickset man and another man of a slighter and more gentlemanly build. They were engaged in talking, and the latter was bringing down his right hand upon the palm of his left with a gesture almost foreign in its expressive energy.

"I tell you," declared he, with a voice that while low, reverberated through the hollow vault above him with strange intensity, "I tell you I've got my grip on a certain rich man in this city, and if you will only wait, you shall see strange things. I don't know his name and I don't know his face, but I do know what he has done, and a thousand dollars down couldn't buy the knowledge of me."

"But if you don't know his name and don't know his face, how in the name of all that's mischievous are you going to know your man?"

"Leave that to me! If I once meet him and hear him talk, one more rich man goes down and one more poor devil goes up, or I've not the wit that starvation usually teaches."

===Chinese===
她们走进去时，里头只有两个人。一个矮胖结实的汉子，另一个身材较为瘦削、气质也较为绅士些。两人正谈得起劲，后者正把右手一下一下地拍在左掌上，那手势带着一种近乎外国式的、富于表现力的劲头。

「我告诉你，」他宣称道，嗓音虽低，却以一种奇异的强度在头顶那空心的拱顶间回荡，「我告诉你，我已经攥住了这城里某一个阔人的把柄，只要你肯等，你就能看到些稀奇事。我不知道他的名字，也不知道他的脸，可我的确知道他干过什么，一千块现大洋也休想从我嘴里买走这桩秘密。」

「可你既不知道他名字，又不知道他长相，凭一切捣鬼之神的名义，你怎么认得出你要找的人？」

「这个交给我！只要我与他照上一面、听他说上几句话，便多一个阔人栽下去，多一个穷鬼爬上来——要不然，我便白受了饥饿通常能教会人的那份机灵。」

===Original===
The nature of these sentences together with the various manifestations of interest with which they were received, had for a moment deterred the two girls in their hurried advance, but now they put away every thought save that of the poor little creature awaiting his Dad, and lifting up her voice, Paula said,

"Are either of you the father of a little lame lad—"

Instantly and before she could conclude, the taller of the two, who had also been the chief speaker in the above conversation, turned, and she saw his hand begrimed though it was with dirt and dark with many a disgraceful trick, go to his heart in a gesture too natural to be anything but involuntary.

"Is he hurt?" gasped he, but in how different a tone from that of the woman who had used the same words a few minutes before. Then seeing that the persons who addressed him were ladies and one of them at least a very beautiful one, took off his hat with an easy action, that together with what they had heard, proved him to be one of that most dangerous class among us, a gentleman who has gone thoroughly and irretrievably to the bad.

===Chinese===
这几句话的性质，连同对方听时所现出的种种饶有兴味的神色，一时倒把这两个匆匆赶路的姑娘吓住了，但此刻她们撇开一切念头，只想着那个正等着爸爸的可怜小生灵，于是宝拉扬起声音说：

「你们二位，可有谁是一个瘸腿小男孩的——」

话还没说完，那两人之中身材较高的一个——也就是方才那段话的主要发言者——立刻转过身来，她看见他那只虽沾满污垢、因干过许多见不得人的勾当而发黑的手，抬起来按到了自己心口上，那手势太自然了，不可能是别的，只能是无意识的。

「他伤着了？」他喘着气问，可这语气与几分钟前那个女人说同样三个字时，是何等不同。随即他见搭话之人是两位女士，其中至少有一位是十分貌美的，便以一种从容的动作摘下帽来——这动作连同她们方才所听到的那一番话，都证明他属于我们之间最危险的那一类人：一个彻彻底底、无可挽回地堕落了的绅士。

===Original===
"I am afraid he is, sir," said Paula. "He was attempting to cross the road, and a horse advancing hurriedly, struck him." She had not courage to say her horse in face of the white and trembling dismay that seized him at these words.

"Where is he?" cried he. "Where's my poor boy?" And he bounded up the steps, his hat still in his hand, his long unkempt locks flying, and his whole form expressive of the utmost alarm.

"Down by the carriage road," called out Paula, finding it impossible for them to keep up with such haste.

"But is he much injured?" cried a smooth voice at their side.

They turned; it was the short thickset man who had been the other's companion in the conversation above recorded.

"We trust not," answered Cicely; "his arm received the blow, and he suffers very much, but we hope it is not serious;" and they hurried on.

===Chinese===
「恐怕是的，先生。」宝拉说。「他正要穿过马道，一匹马急匆匆冲上前去，撞了他。」面对他闻言时那一脸煞白、发着抖的惊惶，她竟没有勇气说出是她自己的马。

「他在哪儿？」他喊道。「我那可怜的孩子在哪儿？」他一跃冲上台阶，帽还捏在手里，那头又长又乱、从不梳理的乱发飘散着，整个身形都写满了最大的惊惶。

「在车马道那头。」宝拉朝后喊道，发现以那般脚程她们根本追不上他。

「可他伤得重吗？」身旁一个圆滑的声音问道。

她们回头；是那个矮胖结实的汉子，正是方才那段对话里另一个人的同伴。

「但愿不重。」西塞莉答道；「他胳膊挨了一下，痛得很厉害，可我们希望并不严重；」说罢她们又急急赶路。

===Original===
They found the father seated on the grass holding the little fellow in his arms. The look on his once handsome but now thoroughly corrupt and dissipated face, made their hearts melt within them. However wicked he might be—and that sly treacherous eye, that false impudent lip, that settling of the whole face into the mould which Vice applies to all her votaries, left no doubt of his complete depravity—he dearly loved his child, and love, no matter how it is expressed, or in what garb it appears, is a sacred and beautiful thing, and ennobles for the time being any creature who displays it.

"'Twas a hard knock up, Dad," came from the white lips of the child as he felt his father's trembling hand feel up and down his arm, "but I guess the 'little fellar' can stand it." "Little feller" was evidently the name by which his father was accustomed to address him.

"There are no bones broken," said the father. "To be lame and maimed too would be—"

He did not finish, for a delicately gloved hand was here laid on his sleeve, and a gentle voice whispered, "Money cannot pay for an injury like that, but please accept this;" and Paula thrust a purse into his hand.

===Chinese===
她们找到那位父亲时，他正坐在草地上，把那小家伙抱在怀里。他那张曾一度英俊、如今却彻底腐化堕落的脸上的神情，直叫她们的心在胸膛里都融化了。无论他有多么邪恶——那只狡黠阴险的眼睛，那两片虚伪厚颜的嘴唇，以及整张脸沉淀进恶习（Vice）施加于她所有信徒的那副模子里——都叫人对他彻底的堕落再无半点怀疑——他却是深切地爱着他这孩子的，而爱，无论它如何表达，又披着怎样的外衣，都是一件神圣而美丽的事物，会在它显现的那一刻，使任何一个流露它的生灵都为之高贵起来。

「这一下撞得可不轻啊，爸。」孩子那张发白的小嘴里吐出这句话，他感到父亲那只颤抖的手在他胳膊上上下摸着，「可我猜『小家伙』还撑得住。」「小家伙」（little feller）显然是父亲惯常用来称呼他的名字。

「骨头没断。」父亲说。「已经瘸了一条腿，要是再缺一截——」

他没把话说完，因为一只戴着精致手套的手这时落到了他的袖上，一个温柔的声音低低说道：「这样的伤，金钱是赔不起的，但还是请收下这个吧；」宝拉说着，把一只钱袋塞进了他手里。

===Original===
He clutched it eagerly, but at her next request that he should tell her where he lived that they might inquire after the boy, he shook his head with a return of his old emphasis.

"The haunts of bats and jackals are not for ladies." Then as he caught sight of her pitiful face bending in farewell over the little urchin, some remembrance perhaps of the days when he had a right to stoop to the ear of beautiful women and walk unrebuked at their side, returned to him from the past, and respectfully lowering his voice, he asked her name.

She gave it and he seemed to lay it away in his mind; then as the ladies turned to remount their horses, rose and began carrying the little fellow off. As he vanished in the turn of the path that led towards the main entrance, they perceived a tall dark figure arise from a seat in the distance and stand looking after him, with a leer on its face and a malicious hugging of itself in a long black cloak, that proclaimed her to be the same ominous being who had before so grievously startled them.

===Chinese===
他急切地把它紧紧攥住，可等她接着请他告知住处、好让她们日后探问那孩子的伤情时，他却摇了摇头，又恢复了先前那副断然的劲头。

「蝙蝠与豺狼出没之地，原不是太太小姐们去得的。」随即，他瞥见她那张怜悯的脸正俯身在那小顽童身上作别，往昔或许有过的某些记忆——那时他还有资格俯到美貌女子的耳畔说话，还能不受呵斥地走在她们身旁——又从旧日里泛了上来，于是他恭恭敬敬地压低了声音，请教她的姓名。

她说出了自己的名字，他似乎把它郑重地收进了心里；接着两位女士转身重新上马，他也站起身，开始抱着那小家伙离去。当他消失在通向正门那条小径的拐角处时，她们看见一个高高的黑色身影从远处的一张座椅上立起，站在那里目送他远去，脸上带着一道斜睨的目光，又用一件长长的黑斗篷恶毒地把自己紧紧裹住——这一看便知，正是方才那样厉害地惊过她们一场的那个不祥之人。

## XXXVIII Blue-Beard’s Chamber / 三十八 蓝胡子的密室

===Original===
> "Present fears
> Are less than horrible imaginings."

===Chinese===
> 「眼前的恐惧，远不及那可怕的想象。」

===Original===
Clarence Ensign was not surprised at the refusal he received from Paula. He had realized from the first that the love of this beautiful woman would be difficult to obtain, even if no rival with more powerful inducements than his own, should chance to cross his path. She was one who could be won to give friendship, consideration, and sympathy without stint; but from the very fact that she could so easily be induced to grant these, he foresaw the improbability, or at least the difficulty of enticing her to yield more. A woman whose hand warms towards the other sex in ready friendship, is the last to succumb to the entreaties of love. The circle of her sympathies is so large, the man must do well, who of all his sex, pierces to the sacred centre. The appearance of Mr. Sylvester on the scene, settled his fate, or so he believed; but he was too much in earnest to yield his hopes without another effort; so upon the afternoon of this eventful day, he called upon Paula.

===Chinese===
克拉伦斯·安辛（Clarence Ensign）对从宝拉那里得到的拒绝并不感到意外。他从一开始便明白，要赢得这位美丽女子的爱情将何等不易，即便并没有一个手中筹码比他更为雄厚的对手偶然闯到他人生的道上。她是一个不难争取来毫不吝惜地给予友谊、体恤与同情的人；但恰恰因为她如此轻易便能被引得付出这些，他早已预见到，要诱使她付出更多，几乎不可能，至少也是难上加难。一个对异性能随时热络地伸出友谊之手的女子，恰恰最不易在爱情的恳求前低头。她的同情之圈是如此辽阔，普天下男子之中，非得有真正出类拔萃者，方能穿透到那神圣的中心。西尔维斯特先生的出场，已经定了他的命运——至少他这样相信；然而他太过真心实意，不肯未曾再作一番努力便就此放弃希望；于是，在这多事之日的一个下午，他登门拜访了宝拉。

===Original===
The first glimpse he obtained of her countenance, convinced him that he was indeed too late. Not for him that anxious pallor, giving way to a rosy tinge at the least sound in the streets without. Not for him that wandering glance, burning with questions to which nothing seemed able to grant reply. The very smile with which she greeted him, was a blow; it was so forgetful of the motive that had brought him there.

===Chinese===
他第一眼看见她的面容，便确信自己确实来迟了。那份焦灼的苍白——街上一有丝毫动静便泛起一层红晕——不是为他而生的。那游移的目光，燃烧着似乎万物都无从作答的疑问，也不是投向他的。她迎接他的那一笑本身便是一记打击；那笑容如此全然忘却了他此来的动机。

===Original===
“Miss Fairchild,” he stammered, with a generous impulse to save her unnecessary pain, “you have rejected my offer and settled my doom; but let me believe that I have not lost your regard, or that hold upon your friendship which it has hitherto been my pleasure to enjoy.”

===Chinese===
「费尔柴尔德（Fairchild）小姐，」他结结巴巴地开口，一时心肠慷慨，想替她免去那不必要的痛楚，「您拒绝了我的求婚，也定下了我的命运；但请让我相信，我并未失去您的看重，也并未失去那份对您友谊的把握——一直以来，能享有那份友谊于我已是幸事。」

===Original===
She woke at once to a realization of his position. “Oh Mr. Ensign,” she murmured, “can you doubt my regard or the truth of my friendship? It is for me to doubt; I have caused you such pain, and as you may think, so ruthlessly and with such lack of consideration. I have been peculiarly placed,” she blushingly proceeded. “A woman does not always know her own heart, or if she does, sometimes hesitates to yield to its secret impulses. I have led you astray these last few weeks, but I first went astray myself. The real path in which I ought to tread, was only last night revealed to me. I can say no more, Mr. Ensign.”

===Chinese===
她顿时醒悟到他的处境。「哦，安辛先生，」她低声道，「您怎么会怀疑我的看重，或我友谊的真心？该怀疑的是我；我给您造成了这样的痛楚，您也许还觉得，那样无情，那样欠缺体谅。我的处境有些特殊，」她红着脸继续说。「一个女人并不总能认清自己的心，即便认清了，有时也会犹豫着不肯顺从它那隐秘的冲动。这几个星期我把您引上了歧路，可我自己先走上了歧路。我真正应当走的那条路，直到昨夜才向我显明。我不能再多说了，安辛先生。」

===Original===
“Nor is it necessary,” replied he. “You have chosen the better path, and the better man. May life abound in joys for you, Miss Fairchild.”

===Chinese===
「也无须再多说了，」他答道。「您选了更好的路，也选了更好的人。愿您此生欢乐无尽，费尔柴尔德小姐。」

===Original===
She drew herself up and her hand went involuntarily to her heart. “It is not joy I seek,” said she, “but—”

“What?” He looked at her face lit with that heavenly gleam that visited it in rare moments of deepest emotion, and wondered.

“Joy is in seeing the one you love happy,” cried she; “earth holds none that is sweeter or higher.”

===Chinese===
她挺直了身，手不由自主地按到了心口。「我所寻求的并非欢乐，」她说，「而是——」

「是什么？」他望着她的脸，那脸上正亮起一抹天上的光辉——这光辉只在极少数最为动情的时刻才会降临其上——他怔住了。

「欢乐，便是看见你所爱的人幸福，」她喊道；「世间再没有比这更甜美、更高尚的欢乐了。」

===Original===
“Then may that be yours,” he murmured, manfully subduing the jealous pang natural under the circumstances. And taking the hand she held out to him, he kissed it with greater reverence and truer affection than when, in the first joyous hours of their intercourse, he carried it so gallantly to his lips.

===Chinese===
「那么，愿这欢乐归于您，」他低声道，以男子气概压下了此情此景之下自然而生的那阵妒意之痛。他接过她伸给他的手，凑到唇边吻了下去，这一吻比在他们初交往的那段欢愉时光里，他殷勤地将这只手举到唇边时，怀着更深的敬意，也更真的情意。

===Original===
And she—oh, difference of time and feeling—did not remember as of yore, the noble days of chivalry, though he was in this moment, so much more than ever the true knight and the reproachless cavalier.

===Chinese===
而她——唉，时过境迁、情随事迁——已不复如往昔那样想起骑士时代那些高贵的旧事，尽管此刻的他，比以往任何时候都更是一位真正的骑士、一位无可指摘的绅士。

===Original===
For Paula’s heart was heavy. Fears too unsubstantial to be met and vanquished, had haunted her steps all day. The short note which Mr. Sylvester had written her, lay like lead upon her bosom. She longed for the hours to fly, yet dreaded to hear the clock tick out the moments that possibly were destined to bring her untold suffering and disappointment. A revelation awaiting her in Mr. Sylvester’s desk upstairs? That meant separation and farewell; for words of promise and devotion can be spoken, and the heart that hopes, does not limit time to hours.

===Chinese===
因为宝拉的心情沉重。那些太过虚无、无从迎击也无从击退的恐惧，整日萦绕着她的脚步。西尔维斯特先生写给她的那张短笺，像铅一样压在她胸口。她盼着时辰飞逝，却又怕听见时钟一声声敲出那些也许注定要给她带来无尽痛苦与失望的片刻。楼上西尔维斯特先生的书桌里，有一桩真相等着她去揭晓？那意味着分离与诀别；因为山盟海誓、痴情一片的话语，尽可以说得出口，而一颗怀着希望的心，从不把时间囿于区区几个时辰之内。

===Original===
With Bertram’s entrance, her fears took absolute shape. Mr. Sylvester was not coming home to dinner. Thenceforward till seven o’clock, she sat with her hand on her heart, waiting. At the stroke of the clock, she rose, and procuring a candle from her room, went slowly upstairs. “Watch for me,” she had said to Aunt Belinda, “for I fear I shall need your care when I come down.”

===Chinese===
伯特兰一进门，她的恐惧便有了确切的形状。西尔维斯特先生不回家吃晚饭了。此后直到七点，她一直坐着，手按在心口，等待着。时钟敲响那一刻，她站起身，从自己房里取了一支蜡烛，缓缓上楼。「等着我，」她曾对贝琳达姨妈说，「因为我怕自己下楼时会需要您的照看。」

===Original===
What is there about a mystery however trivial, that thrills the heart with vague expectancy at the least lift of the concealing curtain! As Paula paused before the door, which never to her knowledge had opened to the passage of any other form than that of Mr. Sylvester, she was conscious of an agitation wholly distinct from that which had hitherto afflicted her. All the past curiosity of Ona concerning this room, together with her devices for satisfying that curiosity, recurred to Paula with startling distinctness. It was as if the white hand of that dead wife had thrust itself forth from the shadows to pull her back. The candle trembled in her grasp, and she unconsciously recoiled. But the next moment the thought of Mr. Sylvester struck warmth and determination through her being, and hastily thrusting the key into the lock, she pushed open the door and stepped across the threshold.

===Chinese===
一桩谜团——无论多么微不足道——当那层遮蔽的帷幕哪怕稍稍掀起一角，为何便能使人心因一种朦胧的期待而怦怦直跳！宝拉在那扇门前停下脚步——据她所知，这扇门除了西尔维斯特先生的身影之外，从未为别的任何人的进出而开启过——她意识到自己此刻心头的激动，与先前折磨着她的那种激动截然不同。奥娜（Ona）从前对这间屋子的一切好奇，连同她为满足那好奇而使过的种种心思，此刻都一齐以一种惊人的清晰涌回宝拉的心头。那情形，仿佛是那位亡妻苍白的手从阴影里伸出来，要将她拽回去。蜡烛在她手中发颤，她不由自主地退了一步。但下一刻，一念及西尔维斯特先生，一股暖意和决断便贯通了她的全身，她匆匆把钥匙插入锁孔，推开门，跨过了门槛。

===Original===
Her first movement was that of surprise. In all her dreams of the possible appearance of this room, she had never imagined it to be like this. Plain, rude and homely, its high walls unornamented, its floor uncovered, its furniture limited to a plain desk and two or three rather uncomfortable-looking chairs, it struck upon her fancy with the same sense of incongruity, as might the sight of a low-eaved cottage in the midst of stately palaces and lordly pleasure-grounds. Setting down her candle, she folded her hands to still their tremblings, and slowly looked around her. This was the spot, then, to which he was accustomed to flee when oppressed by any care or harassed by any difficulty; this cold, bare, uninviting apartment with its forbidding aspect unsoftened by the tokens of a woman’s care or presence! To this room, humbler than any in her aunt’s home in Grotewell, he had brought all his griefs, from the day his baby lay dead in the rooms below, to that awful hour which saw the wife and mother brought into his doors and laid a cold and pulseless form in the midst of his gorgeous parlors! Here he had met his own higher impulses face to face, and wrestled with them through the watches of the night! In this wilderness of seeming poverty, he had dreamed, perhaps, his first fond dream of her as a woman, and signed perhaps his final renunciation of her as the future companion of his life! What did it mean? Why a spot of so much desolation in the midst of so much that was lordly and luxurious? Her fears might give her a possible interpretation, but she would not listen to fears. Only his words should instruct her. Going to the desk, she opened it. A sealed envelope addressed to herself, immediately met her eyes. Taking it out with a slow and reverent touch, she began to read the long and closely written letter which it contained.

===Chinese===
