Mr. Sylvester was seen returning from the supper-room, looking decidedly anxious, and while Paula was ignorant of what had transpired to annoy him, her ready spirit caught the alarm, and she was about to rush up to him and address him, when one of the waiters approached, and murmuring a few words she did not hear, handed him a card upon which she descried nothing but a simple circle. Instantly a change crossed his already agitated countenance, and advancing to the ladies with a word or two that while seemingly cheerful, struck Paula as somewhat forced, excused himself with the information that a business friend had been so inconsiderate as to importune him for an interview in the hall. And with just a nod towards Mr. Ensign, who had drawn back at his advance, left them and disappeared in the crowd about the door.

"I do not like these interruptions from business friends in a time of pleasure," cried Paula, looking after him with anxious eyes. "Did you notice how agitated he seemed, Cicely? And half an hour ago he was the picture of calm enjoyment."

"Business is beyond our comprehension, Paula," returned her friend evasively. "It is something like a neuralgic twinge, it takes a man when he least expects it. Have you told Mr. Ensign of our adventure?"

"No, but I informed Mr. Sylvester, and he said such good, true words to me, Cicely. I can never forget them."

"And I told papa; but he only frowned and made some observation about the degeneracy of the times, and the number of scamps thrown to the top by the modern methods of acquiring instantaneous fortunes."

"Your papa is sometimes hard, is he not, Cicely?"

===Chinese===
但她们的谈话很快便被打断了。只见西尔维斯特先生从晚餐厅那边走回来，神色之间分明带着焦急，宝拉虽不知是何事惹恼了他，她那敏感的天性却已先一步警觉起来，正要冲上前去与他搭话，一名侍者却走上前来，低声说了几句她没听清的话，递给他一张卡片，那卡片上她只隐约辨出一个简单的圆圈。顷刻之间，他那张本已激动的脸上掠过一层变化，他向两位女士走来，说了几句看似欢快、却让宝拉觉得颇为勉强的话，随后告罪一声，说是有位生意上的朋友竟如此不知趣，非要在前厅里求见他。他只朝退后一步的恩赛恩先生略一点头，便撇下她们，消失在门口那群人之中。

「我不喜欢在寻欢作乐之时，被生意上的朋友这样打断，」宝拉叫道，焦虑的目光追随着他。「您可注意到他像是受了很大的惊动，西塞利？半个钟头前，他还一幅悠然自得的样子呢。」

「生意上的事我们无从理解，宝拉，」她的朋友闪闪烁烁地答道。「那东西有点像神经痛的发作，在人最料不到的时候把他攫住。您把我们那场意外告诉恩赛恩先生了吗？」

「没有，可我禀告了西尔维斯特先生，他对我说了一番多么善良、多么真挚的话呀，西塞利。我永远也忘不了。」

「我也告诉了爸爸；可他只是皱了皱眉，发表了一通议论，说这是世风日下，说那些靠现代手段暴富起来的无赖之徒，有那么多都被推到了顶层。」

「您的爸爸有时未免太严苛了，是吧，西塞利？」

===Original===
With a flush Miss Stuyvesant allowed her eye to rest for a moment on the crowd shifting before her. "He was dug from a quarry of granite, Paula. He is both hard and substantial; capable of being hewn but not of being moulded. Of such stuff are formed monuments of enduring beauty and solidity. You must do papa justice."

"I do, but I sometimes have a feeling as if the granite column would fall and crush me, Cicely."

"You, Paula?"

Before she could again reply, Mr. Sylvester returned. His face was still pale, but it had acquired an expression of rigidity even more alarming to Paula than its previous aspect of forced merriment. Lifting her by the hand, he drew her apart.

"I shall have to leave you somewhat abruptly," said he. "An important matter demands my instant attention. Bertram is somewhere here, and will see that you and Ona arrive home in safety. You won't allow your enjoyment to be clouded by my hasty departure, will you?"

"Not if it will make you anxious. But I would rather go home with you now. I am sure Cousin Ona would be willing."

"But I am not going home at present," said he; and she ventured upon no further remonstrance.

===Chinese===
斯泰弗森小姐脸上泛起一阵红晕，让目光在面前流动的人群上停留了片刻。「他可是从花岗岩的采石场里凿出来的，宝拉。他又坚硬又结实；只可雕凿，不可塑造。历久不衰、坚固美观的纪念碑，都是用这种材料做成的。您得当公道地评价爸爸。」

「我自是公道的，可我有时却有一种感觉，仿佛那根花岗岩的柱子会倒下来把我压碎似的，西塞利。」

「您，宝拉？」

她还没来得及再答话，西尔维斯特先生便回来了。他面色仍然苍白，却添了一种僵硬之态，比先前那副勉强的欢颜更叫宝拉心惊。他执起她的手，把她拉到一旁。

「我不得不稍微仓促地告辞了，」他说。「有一桩要紧事需我立即过目。伯特兰（Bertram）就在这附近某处，他会照应您和奥娜（Ona）平安到家的。您不会因为我这匆匆离去而扫了兴吧？」

「若它会让您挂心，便不会。可我倒情愿现在就跟您一道回家。我确信奥娜表姐会愿意的。」

「可我眼下并不打算回家。」他说；她便不敢再行劝阻。

===Original===
But her enjoyment was clouded; the sight of suffering or anxiety on that face was more than she could bear; and ere long she said good night to Cicely, and accepting the arm of Mr. Ensign, who was never very far from her side, proceeded to search for her cousin.

She found her standing in the midst of an admiring throng to whom her diamonds, if not her smiles, were an object of undoubted interest. She was in the full tide of one of her longest and most widely rambling speeches, and to Paula, with that stir of anxiety at her breast, was an image of self-satisfied complacency from which she was fain to drop her eyes.

"Mrs. Sylvester shares the honors with her husband," remarked Mr. Ensign as they drew near.

"But not the trials, or the pain, or the care?" was Paula's inward comment.

Mrs. Sylvester was not easily wooed away from a circle in which she found herself creating such an impression, but at length she yielded to Paula's importunities, and consented to accept young Mr. Sylvester's attendance to their home. The next thing was to find Bertram. Mr. Ensign engaged to do this. Leaving Paula with her cousin, who may or may not have been pleased at this sudden addition to her circle, he sought for the young man who as Mr. Mandeville was not unknown to any of the fashionable men and women of the day. It was no easy task, nor did he find him readily, but at last he came upon him leaning out of a window and gazing at a white lily which he held in his hand. Without preamble, Mr. Ensign made known his errand, and Bertram at once prepared to accompany him back to the ladies.

"By Jove! I didn't know the fellow was so handsome!" thought the former, and frowned he hardly knew why. Bertram was not handsome, but then Clarence Ensign was plain, which Bertram certainly was not.

===Chinese===
可她的兴致到底是被蒙上了一层阴影；那张脸上受苦或焦虑的神情，是她所不堪承受的；不久她便向西塞利道了晚安，又挽着从未离她很远的恩赛恩先生的手臂，动身去寻她的表姐。

她看见她正立在一群艳羡的看客当中，对那群人而言，她的钻石——若不是她的微笑——无疑是令他们大感兴趣的对象。她正滔滔不绝地说着一篇她最长、最漫无边际的闲话，而宝拉心头怀着那一阵焦虑，眼前所见的是一幅志得意满的自满之态，叫她不禁垂下了眼帘。

「西尔维斯特夫人与她的丈夫共享荣光。」她们走近时，恩赛恩先生说道。

「却不共享那些磨难、那些痛楚、那些忧烦吧？」这是宝拉心里的暗语。

西尔维斯特夫人（Mrs. Sylvester）是不易从这样一个她自觉大出风头的圈子里被劝走的，但终于她拗不过宝拉的苦求，答应让小西尔维斯特先生（Mr. Sylvester）护送她们回家。接下来便是去找伯特兰。恩赛恩先生主动承揽此事。他把宝拉留在她表姐身边——她表姐对这个突然多出来的同伴心里究竟是喜是恼，就不得而知了——自己去寻那位年轻人；那人作为曼德维尔先生（Mr. Mandeville），在时下时髦的男男女女之中并非无名之辈。这并非易事，他也不易寻见，但终归看见他正探身窗外，凝视着手中的一枝白百合。恩赛恩先生开门见山，将来意说明，伯特兰当即准备随他回到两位女士那里。

「天哪！我竟不知这小子生得这般俊！」前者暗想，又几乎不知为何地皱起了眉。伯特兰算不上俊美，可克拉伦斯·恩赛恩却相貌平庸，而伯特兰却绝非如此。

===Original===
It was to Mr. Ensign's face however that Paula's eyes turned as the two came up, and he with the ready vivacity of his natural temperament observed it, and took courage.

"I shall soon wish to measure that loophole of which I have spoken," said he.

And the soft look in her large dark eye as she responded, "It is always open to friends," filled up the measure of his cup of happiness; a cup which unlike hers, had not been darkened that day by the falling of earth's most dismal shadows.

===Chinese===
然而两人走近之时，宝拉的目光却投向了恩赛恩先生的脸，他凭着天性中那种敏捷的活泼察觉到了，便壮起了胆。

「我不久便要量一量我所说的那扇窥窗了。」他说。

她那双黑色的大眼睛中所流露的柔和之色，随着她一声「对朋友，它永远敞开」，把他那杯幸福的杯盏斟到了满溢；那杯盏与她那杯不同，今日并未因尘世最阴惨的阴影投下而黯淡无光。

## XL Half-Past Seven / 四十 七点半

===Original===
> "I would it were midnight, Hal, and all well."

The library was dim; Bertram, who had felt the oppressive influence of the great empty room, had turned down the lights, and was now engaged in pacing the floor, with restless and uneven steps, asking himself a hundred questions, and wishing with all the power of his soul, that Mr. Sylvester would return, and by his appearance cut short a suspense that was fast becoming unendurable.

He had just returned from his third visit to the front door, when the curtain between him and the hall was gently raised, and Paula glided in and stood before him. She was dressed for the street, and her face where the light touched it, shone like marble upon which has fallen the glare of a lifted torch.

===Chinese===
> 「但愿已是午夜，哈尔，万事平安。」

书房里光线昏暗；伯特兰原本就感到这间空旷的大书房里那种压迫感，便把灯捻暗了，此刻正来回踱步，步子又急又乱，心里不住地自问，千遍万遍地盼着西尔维斯特先生快些回来，好以他的现身，了结这一桩正迅速变得难以忍受的悬念。

他刚从大门口折返，这是他第三次去探看，就在这时，隔开他和前厅的那幅帘子轻轻掀起，宝拉一闪而入，立在他面前。她已是一身外出的打扮，灯光映及之处，她的脸庞如大理石般闪着冷光，仿佛是举起的火把投在它上面的反照。

===Original===
"Paula!" burst from the young man's lips in surprise.

"Hush!" said she, her voice quavering with an emotion that put to defiance all conventionalities, "I want you to take me to the place where Mr. Sylvester is gone. He is in danger; I know it, I feel it. I dare not leave him any longer alone. I might be able to save him if—if he meditates anything that—" she did not try to say what, but drew nearer to Bertram and repeated her request. "You will take me, won't you?"

===Chinese===
「宝拉！」这名字伴着惊异，从那年轻人唇间脱口而出。

「嘘！」她说，嗓音因一种情绪而颤栗，那情绪把一切世俗礼法都置之度外，「我要你带我去西尔维斯特先生去的地方。他有危险；我知道，我感觉得到。我再也不敢让他独自一人了。我也许能救他——只要——只要他正打算做什么——」她没有试图说出那是什么，只是向伯特兰靠得更近，重申她的请求。「你会带我去，对不对？」

===Original===
He eyed her with amazement, and a shudder seized his own strong frame. "No," cried he, "I cannot take you; you do not know what you ask; but I will go myself if you apprehend anything serious. I remember where it is. I studied the address too closely, to readily forget it."

"You shall not go without me," returned Paula with steady decision. "If the danger is what I fear, no one else can save him. I must go," she added, with passionate importunity as she saw him still looking doubtful. "Darkness and peril are nothing to me in comparison with his safety. He holds my life in his hand," she softly whispered, "and what will not one do for his life!" Then quickly, "If you go without me I shall follow with Aunt Belinda. Nothing shall keep me in the house tonight."

===Chinese===
他惊愕地望着她，一阵战栗也攫住了他强健的身躯。「不，」他喊道，「我不能带你去；你不知道你在求什么；不过你若当真担心出了什么大事，我自己去。我还记得那地方在哪儿。那个地址我看得太仔细了，不会轻易就忘掉。」

「你不带我去，我也不让你一个人去，」宝拉以沉定的决断回道。「如果那危险正是我所害怕的那种，除了我，再没人能救他。我必须去，」见他仍面露犹疑，她又以热烈的执拗加上一句，「较之于他的安危，黑暗与凶险于我都算不得什么。他把我的性命攥在他手里，」她低低地耳语，「而为了他的性命，又有哪一样是做不到的呢！」随即又急急说道：「你若不带我去，我便和贝琳达姑妈一同前往。今夜再没有什么能把我留在这屋子里。」

===Original===
He felt the uselessness of further objection, yet he ventured to say, "The place where he has gone is one of the worst in the city; a spot which men hesitate to enter after dark. You don't know what you ask in begging me to take you there."

"I do, I realize everything."

With a sudden awe of the great love which he thus beheld embodied before him, Bertram bowed his head and moved towards the door. "I may consider it wise to obtain the guidance of a policeman through the quarter into which we are about to venture. Will you object to that?"

===Chinese===
他明白再争辩也是徒然，却仍冒险一试：「他去的那个地方是全城最坏的去处之一；那种地方，天黑之后男人也要犹豫再三才敢踏入。你不知道你求我带你去那里，意味着什么。」

「我知道，我什么都明白。」

面对着眼前这般现于肉身的至大之爱，伯特兰忽然生出一种敬畏，他垂下头，朝门口走去。「我想，为稳妥起见，不妨请一位警察为我们引路，穿过我们即将踏入的那片街区。你不会反对吧？」

===Original===
"No," was her quick reply, "I object to nothing but delay."

And with a last look about the room, as if some sensation of farewell were stirring in her breast, she laid her hand on Bertram's arm, and together they hurried away into the night.

===Chinese===
「不，」她立刻答道，「除了耽搁，我什么都不反对。」

她又向室内投去最后一瞥，仿佛胸中正涌起一种告别之情，随后将手搭上伯特兰的手臂，两人一同匆匆出门，没入夜色之中。

## XXII Hopgood / 二十二 霍普古德

===Original===
> "Give it an understanding but no tongue."

Hopgood was a man who could keep a secret, but who made so much ado in the process that he reminded one of the placard found posted up somewhere out west which reads, "A treasure of gold concealed here; don't dig!" Or so his wife used to say, and she ought to know, for she had lived with him five years, three of which he had spent in the detective service.
"If he would only trust the wife of his bosom with whatever he's got on his mind, instead of ambling around the building with his eyes rolling about like peas in a cauldron of boiling water, one might manage to take some comfort in life, and not hurt anybody either. For two days now, ever since the wife of Mr. Sylvester died and Mr. Sylvester has been away from the bank, he's acted just like a lunatic. Not that that has anything to do with his gettin up of nights and roamin down five pair of stairs to see if the watchman is up to his duty, or with his askin a dozen times a day if I remembers how Mr. Sylvester found him and me, well nigh starvin in Broad Street, and gave him the good word which got him into this place? O no! O no, of course not! But *something* has, and while he persists in shutting out from his breast the woman he swore to love, honor, and cherish, that woman is not bound to bear the trials of life with patience. Every time he jumps out of his chair at the sound of Mr. Sylvester's name, and someone is always mentionin' it, I plumps me down on mine with an expression of my views regarding a kitchen stove that does all its drawin' when the oven's empty."

===Chinese===
> 「以心会之，勿以口宣。」

霍普古德（Hopgood）是个能守秘密的人，只不过守秘密的过程大费周章，倒叫人想起西部某处贴着的一张告示，上头写着：「此处藏有黄金一宗；切勿挖掘！」至少他太太常这么说，而她应该最清楚，因为和他同住了五年，其中三年他是在侦探部门里当差的。
「他要肯把心里那点事告诉他那『枕边人』，就不会像一颗颗豌豆在大锅开水里似的，瞪着眼珠子在楼里晃来晃去，人也还能过几天舒心日子，又不碍着谁。打两天前西尔维斯特太太去世、西尔维斯特先生也不在银行那天起，他简直跟个疯子一般。这倒不是说他半夜爬起来、摸下五段楼梯去看更夫有没有尽忠职守跟那有关，也不是说他一天问上十来遍『我可还记得西尔维斯特先生是怎么在布罗德街（Broad Street）撞见我俩、都快饿死了，是他一句话提点才得了这份差事』跟那有关。哦不！哦不，当然不是！可*总有那么点什么*有关，而他既要执意把发过誓要爱、要敬、要珍重的女人关在心门之外，那女人也没那个义务耐着性子忍受生活里的种种熬煎。每回一听见西尔维斯特先生的名字——还总有人提起这名字——他就从椅子上跳起来，我就一屁股坐回我那把椅子上，顺带发几句牢骚，说说我们家那口灶：灶膛空着的时候抽风抽得倒欢。」

===Original===
So spake Mrs. Hopgood to her special crony and constant visitor, Mrs. Kirkshaw of Water Street, pursing up a mouth that might have been good-natured if she had ever given it an opportunity. But Mrs. Kirkshaw who passed for a gossip with her neighbors, was a philosopher in the retirement of the domestic circle and did not believe in the blow for blow system.
"La!" quoth she, with a smoothing out of her apron suggestive of her employment as laundress, "show a dog that you want his bone and you'll never get it. Husbands is like that very stove you've been a slanderin of. Rattle on coal when the fire's low and you put it out entirely; but be a bit patient and drop it on piece by piece, coaxing-like, and you'll have a hot stove afore you know it."
Which suggestion struck Mrs. Hopgood like a revelation, and for a day and night she resorted to the coaxing system; the result of which was to send Mr. Hopgood out of the room to sit on the stairs in mortal terror, lest his good nature should get the better of his discretion. His little daughter, Constantia Maria—so named and so called from two grandmothers, equally exacting in their claims and equally impecunious as regards their resources—was his sole solace in this long vigil. Her pretty innocent prattle scarcely disturbed his meditation, while it soothed his nerves, and with no one by but this unsuspecting child, he could roll his great eyes to his heart's content without fear of her descrying anything in them, but the love with which her own little heart abounded.

===Chinese===
霍普古德太太就是这样跟她特别要好的密友、常来串门的沃特街（Water Street）的柯克肖太太（Mrs. Kirkshaw）说话的，说时抿着一张嘴——若给过它机会，那张嘴倒也显出几分和善。可柯克肖太太，虽说在街坊邻里间算个出了名的长舌妇，关起门来在自己家里却是个明事理的，并不信奉那种以牙还牙的路数。
「哎呀！」她开口道，一面抹平围裙——这动作透出她干的是洗衣妇的营生，「让一条狗看出你想要它的骨头，你就永远甭想拿到手。丈夫就跟你方才编排的那口灶一个样。火弱的时候哗啦倒煤，反倒把火整个浇灭了；耐着点性子，一块一块往里添，哄着些，不知不觉你就有一炉旺火了。」
这番话对霍普古德太太不啻天启，于是她照着这哄的法子试了一天一夜；结果是——霍普古德先生被逼得出了屋子坐到楼梯上，提心吊胆，生怕他那点好脾气压过了他的分寸。他年幼的小女儿康斯坦蒂娅·玛丽亚（Constantia Maria）——这名字取自两位外祖母，叫也这么叫，两位祖母论要面子同样不让人，论手头同样拮据——是他这漫长守夜里唯一的慰藉。她那稚气无邪的咿呀絮语几乎不打扰他的沉思，反倒抚平了他绷紧的神经；身边只有这一个全无所疑的孩子，他尽可以把那一双大眼睛随心所欲地乱转，不必怕她从中看出什么——除了她自己那颗小小的心里满满盛着的爱。

===Original===
On the morning after the funeral, however, Constantia Maria was restored to his wife's arms on the plea that she did not seem quite well, and Hopgood went out and sat alone. In a few minutes, however, he returned, and ambling restlessly up and down the room, stopped before his persistently smiling wife and said somewhat tremulously:
"If Mr. Sylvester takes a notion to come up and see Constantia Maria today, I hope you'll take the opportunity to finish your ironing or whatever else it is you may have to do. I've noticed he seems a little shy with the child when you are around."
"Shy with the child when I am around! well I do declare!" exclaimed she, forgetting her late role in her somewhat natural indignation. "And what have I ever done to frighten Mr. Sylvester? Nothing but putting on of a clean apron, when he comes in and a dustin' of the best chair for his use. It's a trick of yours to get a chance of speakin' to him alone, and I'll not put up with it. As if it wasn't bad enough to have a kettle with the nozzle dangling, without living with a man who has a secret he won't share with his own wife and the mother of his innocent babe."

===Chinese===
可是在葬礼之后的那个早上，康斯坦蒂娅·玛丽亚被送回了他太太的怀里，借口是孩子似乎有些不大舒服；于是霍普古德独自出门坐了一会儿。不一会儿他又回来了，在屋里焦躁地来回踱步，末了在那张一直笑吟吟的太太面前停住，声音有些发颤地说：
「要是西尔维斯特先生今天动了兴致上楼来看康斯坦蒂娅·玛丽亚，我希望你趁这工夫把你那摊熨衣的活计，或者别的什么该做的活儿干完。我留意到他好像——你在跟前的时候，他对孩子多少有点局促。」
「我在跟前他对孩子就局促！嘿，可真有此理！」她叫起来，忘了自己方才那副哄的角色，露出几分自然的愤慨。「我对西尔维斯特先生做过什么吓着他了？无非是他进来的时候换上一条干净围裙，替他掸一掸那把最好的椅子请他坐。这不过是你耍的花招，好寻个机会单独跟他说话，我可不依。像是我们家那口水嘴耷拉着的茶壶还不够受似的，偏又摊上一个心里藏事、不肯跟自己太太——他那无辜孩子的娘——说半句的男人。」

===Original===
With a start the worthy man stared at her till he grew red in the face, probably with the effort of keeping his eyes steady for so long a time. "Who told you I had a secret?" said he.
"Who told me?" and then she laughed, though in a somewhat hysterical way, and sat down in the middle of the floor and shook and shook again. "Hear the man!" she cried. And she told him the story of the placard out west and then asked him, "if he thought she didn't remember how he used to act when he was a chasin' up of a thief in the days when he was on the police force."

===Chinese===
那老实人一惊，直直盯着她，直盯得脸涨通红，多半是睁着眼这么久还得稳住不眨的功夫憋的。「谁跟你说我心里有事？」他说。
「谁跟我说？」说着她笑了起来，笑得却带着几分歇斯底里，一屁股坐到屋子正中，前仰后合地笑个不住。「听听这话！」她嚷。她把西部那张告示的故事讲给他听，又问他，「他是不是以为她不记得从前他在警署当差、追小偷那阵子是个什么做派。」

===Original===
"But," he cried, quite as pale now as he had been florid the moment before, "I'm not in the police force now and you are acting quite silly and I've no patience with you." And he was making for the door, presumably to sit upon the stairs, when with a late repentance she seized him by the arm and said:
"La now," an expression she had caught from Mrs. Kirkshaw, "I didn't mean nothin' by my talk. Come back, John; Constantia Maria is not well, and if Mr. Sylvester comes up to see her, I'll just slip out and leave you alone."
And upon that he told her she was a good wife and that if he had any secret from her it was only because he was a poor man. "Honesty and prudence are all the treasures I possess to keep us three from starving. Shall I part with either of them just to satisfy your curiosity?" and being a good woman at heart, she said "no," though she secretly concluded that prudence in his case involved trust in one's wife first, and disbelief in the rest of the world afterward; and took her future resolutions accordingly.

===Chinese===
「可是，」他叫道，这会儿脸白得跟方才的红一个样，「我现在不在警署当差了，你这副模样蠢得很，我可没那个耐性跟你周旋。」说罢就朝门口走去——多半是又要去坐楼梯；她这才如梦初醒，一把抓住他的胳膊，说：
「哎呀你这人，」这话是她跟柯克肖太太学来的，「我方才那些话没什么恶意。回来，约翰；康斯坦蒂娅·玛丽亚不大舒服，西尔维斯特先生要上来看她，我自会悄悄出去，让你独个儿待着。」
于是他夸她是个好太太，又说他若对她还藏着什么秘密，那也只是因为他是个穷汉子。「我手里能保我们一家三口不挨饿的，无非是诚实和谨慎这两样家当。难道为了满足你的好奇心，我就得丢掉其中一样？」她心地到底是好的，便说了声「不会」，可暗自下的结论却是：在他这里，所谓谨慎，头一条便是信自己的妻子，然后再去疑这世上其余所有的人；她此后的种种决断便照此拿定。

===Original===
"Well, Hopgood, you look anxious; do you want to speak to me?"
The janitor eyed the changed and melancholy face of his patron, with an expression in which real sympathy for his trouble, struggled with the respectful awe which Mr. Sylvester's presence was calculated to inspire.
"If you please," said he, speaking very low, for more or less of the bank employees were moving busily to and fro, "Constantia Maria is not well and she has been asking all day for the *dear man*, as she insists upon calling you, sir, with many apologies for the freedom."

===Chinese===
「嗯，霍普古德，你一脸的心事；可有话要跟我说？」
门房望着恩人那张憔悴忧郁、判若两人的脸，神情里真情替他的难处揪心，又夹杂着西尔维斯特先生的出现所不免激起的那份敬畏。
「劳驾，」他说，声音压得极低，因为或多或少总有银行职员在来来往往忙碌着，「康斯坦蒂娅·玛丽亚不大舒服，她这一整天都在念叨那位*亲爱的先生*——她非要这么称呼您不可，先生，再三为这孩子的没规矩告罪。」

===Original===
Mr. Sylvester smiled with a faint faraway look in his dark eye that made Hopgood stare uneasily out of the window. "Sick! why then I must go up and see her," he returned in a matter-of-fact way that proved his visits in that direction were of no uncommon occurrence. "A moment more and I shall be at liberty."
Hopgood bowed and renewed his stare out of the window, with an intensity happily spared from serious consequences to the passersby, by the merciful celerity with which Mr. Sylvester procured his overcoat, put such papers in his pocket as he required, and joined him.

===Chinese===
西尔维斯特先生微微一笑，那双深色的眼睛里含着一种隐约而悠远的神情，叫霍普古德坐立不安，扭头去望窗外。「病了！那我得上去看看她，」他用一种理所当然的口吻答道——可见他往那边去串门并不稀罕。「再过片刻我就得空了。」
霍普古德鞠了一躬，又闷头盯住窗外，那股劲头幸好没给过路的人招来什么祸殃——全亏西尔维斯特先生动作麻利，三下两下取了大衣、把要用的文件塞进口袋，便过来与他同行。

===Original===
"Constantia Maria, here is Mr. Sylvester come to see you."
It was a pleasure to observe how the little thing brightened in her mother's arms, where but a moment before she had lain quite pale and still, and slipping to the ground rushed up to meet the embrace of this stern and melancholy-faced man. "I am so glad you have come," she cried over and over again; and her little arms went round his neck, and her soft cheek nestled against his, with a content that made the mother's eyes sparkle with pleasure, as obedient to her promise, she quietly left the room.

===Chinese===
「康斯坦蒂娅·玛丽亚，西尔维斯特先生来看你了。」
看这小东西怎样在母亲怀里一下子亮起来，煞是动人——方才她还直挺挺地躺着，又白又静——她滑到地上，跑过去迎接这位神情冷峻、面带忧郁的男人的拥抱。「我真高兴您来了，」她叫了一遍又一遍；两条小胳膊搂住他的脖子，柔软的面颊贴着他的面颊，那份满足让做母亲的眼里也迸出欢喜的光——她依着自己许下的诺言，悄悄退出了房间。

===Original===
And Mr. Sylvester? If anyone had seen the abandon with which he yielded to her caresses and returned them, he would have understood why this child should have loved him with such extraordinary affection. He kissed her forehead, he kissed her cheek, and seemed never weary of smoothing down her bright and silky curls. She reminded him of Geraldine. She had the same blue eyes and caressing ways. From the day he had come upon his old friend Hopgood in a condition of necessity almost of want, this blue-eyed baby had held its small sceptre over his lonely heart, and unbeknown to the rest of the world, had solaced many a spare five minutes with her innocent prattle. The Hopgoods understood the cause of his predilection and were silent. It was the one thing Mrs. Hopgood never alluded to in her gossips with Mrs. Kirkshaw. But today the attentions of Mr. Sylvester to the little one seemed to make the janitor restless. He walked up and down the narrow room uneasily surveying the pair out of the corner of his great glassy eyes, till even Mr. Sylvester noticed his unusual manner and put the child down, observing with a sigh, "You think she is not well enough for any excitement?"

===Chinese===
至于西尔维斯特先生？倘若有人瞧见他是怎样毫无保留地听凭这孩子的爱抚、又怎样加以回报，便会明白这孩子为何会爱他爱得这样非同寻常。他吻她的额头，吻她的脸颊，仿佛永不厌倦地抚她那一头亮泽如丝的卷发。她让他想起杰拉尔丁（Geraldine）。一样的蓝眼睛，一样爱娇的脾性。自打他遇见老朋友霍普古德处于几乎难以为继的困境那一天起，这个蓝眼睛的婴孩就在他那颗孤寂的心上握起了小小的权杖，不为人知地，用她那无邪的咿呀絮语，抚慰了他许多一个半个钟头的闲暇。霍普古德夫妇明白他这份偏爱的缘由，便绝口不提。这是霍普古德太太与柯克肖太太东家长西家短时从不涉及的一桩。可今天，西尔维斯特先生对这个小东西的关切，似乎反而叫这位门房坐立难安。他在狭窄的屋里走来走去，不安地从那双玻璃般的大眼角斜睨着这一老一小，连西尔维斯特先生也觉察出他异样的神态，把孩子放下，叹一口气道：「你觉得她身体还受不住什么兴奋？」

===Original===
"No sir, it is not that," returned the other uneasily, with a hasty look around him. "The fact is, I have something to say to you, sir, about—a discovery—I made the other day." His words came very slowly, and he looked down with great embarrassment.
Mr. Sylvester frowned slightly, and drew himself up to the full height of his very imposing figure. "A discovery," repeated he, "when?"
"The day you paid that early visit to the bank, sir, the day Mrs. Sylvester died."
The frown on Mr. Sylvester's brow grew deeper. "The day—" he began, and stopped.
"Excuse me, sir," exclaimed Hopgood with a burst. "I ought not to have mentioned it, but you asked me *when*, and I—"
"What was this discovery?" inquired his superior, imperatively.

===Chinese===
「不是的先生，不是为这个，」对方不安地答道，匆匆四顾。「实不相瞒，先生，我有一件事要跟您说——一桩发现——前两天我作的。」他说得很慢，窘迫地低着头。
西尔维斯特先生微微皱眉，挺直了他那十分气派的身板。「一桩发现，」他重复道，「什么时候？」
「就是您那天清早造访银行的日子，先生，西尔维斯特太太去世的那天。」
西尔维斯特先生眉间的阴云更沉了。「那一天——」他开口，又顿住。
「恕我冒昧，先生，」霍普古德突地冒出一句。「我原不该提的，可您问我*什么时候*，而我——」
「这桩发现是什么？」上峰断然追问。

===Original===
"Nothing much," murmured the other now all in a cold sweat. "But I felt as if I ought to tell you. You have been my benefactor, sir, I can never forget what you have done for me and mine. If I saw death or bereavement between me and any favor I could do for you, sir, I would not hesitate to risk them. I am no talker, sir, but I am true and I am grateful." He stopped, choked, and his eyes rolled frightfully. Mr. Sylvester looked at him, grew a trifle pale, and put the little child away that was nestling up against his knee.

===Chinese===
「不算什么大事，」对方嘟囔着，这会儿一身冷汗。「可我觉得总该禀告您。您是我的恩人，先生，您待我一家所作所为，我永世不敢忘。倘若为您能尽一份力的事，横在我和死亡、和丧亲之间，我也绝不犹豫，冒了也认。先生，我嘴上不来事，可我实诚，我知恩。」他停下，喉头一哽，眼珠可怕地乱转。西尔维斯特先生看着他，脸也白了几分，把那依偎在他膝边的小女孩轻轻推开。

===Original===
"You have not told me what you have discovered," said he.
"Well, sir, only this." And he took from his pocket a small roll of paper which he unfolded and held out in his hand. It contained a gold toothpick somewhat bent and distorted.
A flush dark and ominous crept over Mr. Sylvester's cheek. He glanced sternly at the trembling janitor, and uttered a short, "Well?"
"I found it on the floor of the bank just after you went out the other morning," the other pursued well-nigh inaudibly. "It was lying near the safe. As it was not there when you went in, I took it for granted it was yours. Am I right, sir?"
The anxious tone in which this last question was uttered, the studied way in which the janitor kept his eyes upon the floor could not have been unnoticed by Mr. Sylvester, but he simply said,
"I have lost mine, that may very possibly be it."

===Chinese===
「你还没告诉我你发现了什么。」他说。
「是这样，先生，不过这个。」他从口袋里掏出一小卷纸，展开，托在手心里。里头是一支金牙签，略有弯曲，变了形。
一道阴沉不祥的红晕爬上西尔维斯特先生的脸颊。他严厉地瞥了一眼瑟缩发抖的门房，短促地吐出一个字：「嗯？」
「那天早上您一出门，我就在银行的地上捡着了它，」对方接下去，声音几乎听不见。「就躺在保险柜边上。您进去之前它并不在那儿，所以我就当它是您的。我没认错吧，先生？」
这最后一问问得何其焦灼，门房又那样刻意地盯着地板——这一切西尔维斯特先生不可能不察觉，可他只说：
「我那支丢了，这很可能就是它。」

===Original===
The janitor held it towards him; his eyes did not leave the floor. "The responsibility of my position here is sometimes felt by me to be very heavy," muttered the man in a low, unmodulated tone. It was his duty in those days previous to the Manhattan Bank robbery, to open the vault in the morning, procure the books that were needed, and lay them about on the various desks in readiness for the clerks upon their arrival. He had also the charge of the boxes of the various customers of the bank who chose to entrust their valuables to its safe keeping; which boxes were kept, together with the books, in that portion of the vault to which he had access. "I should regret my comfortable situation here, but if it was necessary, I would go without a murmur, trusting that God would take care of my poor little lamb."

===Chinese===
门房把东西递向他；眼睛仍不离地板。「我这个位子的担子，有时我觉得沉重得很，」他低声、平板地嘟囔。在那个年月——曼哈顿银行（Manhattan Bank）劫案之前——早晨开保险柜、取出要用的账簿、分放到各张桌上备好给来上班的职员，都是他的差事。他还掌管着银行各客户寄存的财物箱——这些客户乐得把贵重物品托付给银行妥为保管——这些箱子连同账簿一道，放在保险柜里他够得着的那一部分。「我是舍不得这份舒服差事的，可若万不得已，我也走得毫无怨言，信上帝会照应我这只可怜的小羊羔。」

===Original===
"Hopgood, what do you mean?" asked Mr. Sylvester somewhat sternly. "Who talks about dismissing you?"
"No one," responded the other, turning aside to attend to some trivial matter. "But if ever you think a younger or a fresher man would be preferable in my place, do not hesitate to make the change your own necessities or that of the Bank may seem to require."
Mr. Sylvester's eye which was fixed upon the janitor's face, slowly darkened.
"There is something underlying all this," said he, "what is it?"

===Chinese===
「霍普古德，你这是什么意思？」西尔维斯特先生问，语气颇为严厉。「谁说要辞退你了？」
「没人说，」对方答，转过身去顾自忙一桩琐碎的事。「可您哪天要是觉得换一个更年轻、更利索的人在我这位置上更称心，不必犹豫——您自己或银行方面的需要看来要求这样换，您就换。」
西尔维斯特先生那双定在门房脸上的眼睛，缓缓地阴沉下来。
「这一切底下还压着什么，」他说，「是什么？」

===Original===
At once and as if he had taken his resolution, the janitor turned. "I beg your pardon," said he, "I ought to have told you in the first place. When I opened the vaults as usual on the morning of which I speak, I found the boxes displaced; that was nothing if you had been to them, sir; but what did alarm me and make me feel as if I had held my position too long was to find that one of them was unlocked."
Mr. Sylvester fell back a step.
"It was Mr. Stuyvesant's box, sir, and I remember distinctly seeing him lock it the previous afternoon before putting it back on the shelf."
The arms which Mr. Sylvester had crossed upon his breast tightened spasmodically. "And it has been in that condition ever since?" asked he.

===Chinese===
门房蓦地转过身，仿佛一下拿定了主意。「对不起，」他说，「我本该一开头就跟您讲。我刚才说的那天早晨，照常开了保险柜，发现箱子挪了位；先生，这不算什么，倘若您动过它们；可叫我着慌、叫我觉得自己在这位子上坐得太久了的，是发现其中一只开着锁。」
西尔维斯特先生退后一步。
「那是斯泰弗森特先生的箱子，先生，前一天下午他放回架子上之前亲手锁上，我看得清清楚楚、记得明明白白。」
西尔维斯特先生抱在胸前的双臂痉挛般地收紧。「从那以后就一直这样？」他问。

===Original===
The janitor shook his head. "No," said he, taking his little girl up in his arms, possibly to hide his countenance. "As you did not come down again on that day, I took the liberty of locking it with a key of my own when I went to put away the books and shut the vault for the night." And he quietly buried his face in his baby's floating curls, who feeling his cheek against her own put up her hand and stroked it lovingly, crying in her caressing infantile tones,
"Poor papa! poor tired papa."
Mr. Sylvester's stern brow contracted painfully. The look with which his eye sought the sky without, would have made Paula's young heart ache. Taking the child from her father's clasp, he laid her on the bed. When he again confronted the janitor his face was like a mask.

===Chinese===
门房摇了摇头。「没有，」他说，把小女儿抱进怀里，也许是借机遮一遮脸面。「您那一天没有再下来，所以我去放好账簿、晚上关保险柜的时候，便自作主张，用我自己的一把钥匙把它锁上了。」他不动声色地把脸埋进婴孩飘垂的卷发里，孩子感到他的脸贴着自己的脸，便抬起小手，怜爱地抚摸，用她那娇嗔的婴孩腔调叫着：
「可怜的爸爸！可怜的累坏的爸爸。」
西尔维斯特先生冷峻的眉痛苦地皱起。他那望向窗外天色的一眼，所含的神情会让宝拉（Paula）那年少的心为之作痛。他从父亲怀里抱过孩子，把她放到床上。等他再面对门房时，那张脸已像一张面具。

===Original===
"Hopgood," said he, "you are an honest man and a faithful one; I appreciate your worth and have had confidence in your judgment. Whom have you told of this occurrence beside myself?"
"No one, sir."
"Another question; if Mr. Stuyvesant had required his box that day and had found it in the condition you describe, what would you have replied to his inquiries?"

===Chinese===
「霍普古德，」他说，「你是个诚实人，也是个忠心人；我看重你的好处，也信得过你的判断。这事除了我，你还告诉过谁？」
「没有，先生。」
「再问一句；倘若那天斯泰弗森特先生要用他的箱子，发现它正处在你说的情况，你会怎么回他的盘问？」

===Original===
The janitor colored to the roots of his hair in an agony of shame Mr. Sylvester may or may not have appreciated, but replied with the straightforward earnestness of a man driven to bay, "I should have been obliged to tell him the truth sir; that whereas I had no personal knowledge of anyone but myself, having been to the vaults since the evening before, I was called upon early that morning to open the outside door to you, sir, and that you came into the bank," (he did not say looking very pale, agitated and unnatural, but he could not help remembering it) "and finding no one on duty but myself—the watchman having gone upstairs to take his usual cup of coffee before going home for the day—you sent me out of the room on an errand, which delayed me some little time, and that when I came back I found you gone, and everything as I had left it except that small pick lying on the floor."
The last words were nearly inaudible but they must have been heard by Mr. Sylvester, for immediately upon their utterance, the hand which unconsciously had kept its hold upon the toothpick, opened and with an uncontrollable gesture flung the miserable telltale into the stove near by.

===Chinese===
门房羞得头发根都红了，那份痛苦的羞惭，西尔维斯特先生未必尽能体会，可他仍像一个被逼到绝路的人那样，坦诚恳切地答道：「我便不得不跟他说实话，先生；那就是——从头天傍晚以来，除了我自己，我并不能凭亲身所知说有谁去过那些保险柜——那天一大早我被叫去给您开外面那扇门，先生，您就进了银行，」（他没说『脸色煞白、神情激动、一副反常模样』，可他不由得记着这事）「又见当班的只有我一个人——更夫已上楼去喝他照例那杯咖啡，喝完便要回家歇着——您就差我出屋去办件事，耽误了我好一阵子，等我回来，您已经走了，一切都如我离开时那样，只是地上躺着那支小小的牙签。」
最后几个字几乎听不见，可西尔维斯特先生必然是听见了，因为话音一落，那只一直无意识地攥着牙签的手便张开，一个收束不住的动作，把这件害人露馅的小玩意儿甩进了旁边的炉子。

===Original===
"Hopgood," said the stately gentleman, coming nearer and holding him with his eyes till the poor man turned pale and cold as a stone, "has Mr. Stuyvesant had occasion to open his box since you locked it?"
"Yes sir, he called for it yesterday afternoon."
"And who gave it to him?"
"I sir."
"Did he appear to miss anything from it?"
"No, sir."
"Do you believe, Hopgood, that there was anything missing from it?"

===Chinese===
「霍普古德，」这位气派的绅士说着，走近一步，用一双眼睛将他镇住，直镇得这可怜人又白又冷，像一块石头，「自你锁上之后，斯泰弗森特先生可有开过他的箱子？」
「开过，先生，他昨天下午来取的。」
「谁递给他的？」
「我，先生。」
「他像是发觉少了什么没有？」
「没有，先生。」
「霍普古德，你信不信，箱子里少了什么？」

===Original===
The janitor shrank like a man subjected to the torture. He fixed his glance on Mr. Sylvester's face and his own gradually lightened.
"No sir!" said he at last, with a gasp that made the little one lift her curly head from her pillow and shake it with a slow and wistful motion strange to see in a child of only two years.

===Chinese===
门房像受刑的人那样一缩。他把目光定在西尔维斯特先生脸上，自己的脸色渐渐开朗起来。
「没有，先生！」他终于说，倒抽一口气，惊得那小东西把她那颗生着卷发的头从枕上抬起，缓缓地、若有所思地摇了一摇——在个才两岁的孩子身上见到这种神情，煞是古怪。

===Original===
The proud man bowed, not with the severity however that might have been expected; indeed his manner was strangely shadowed, and though his lip betrayed no uneasiness and his eye neither faltered or fell, there was a vague expression of awe upon his countenance, which it would take more than the simple understanding of the worthy but not over subtle man before him, to detect much less to comprehend.

===Chinese===
那骄傲的人鞠了一躬，却不带人们也许料想得到的那份冷峻；他的神情倒奇怪地笼罩着一片阴影，虽说嘴唇不见局促，眼神既不游移也不躲闪，他脸上却有一种隐隐的惶然——要把它看出来已属不易，更莫说领悟；那不是他面前这位老实却谈不上机敏的人，单凭一点朴素的了解所能及。

===Original===
"You may be sure that Mr. Stuyvesant will never complain of anyone having tampered with his effects while you are the guardian of the vaults," exclaimed Mr. Sylvester in clear ringing tones. "As for his box being open, it is right that I should explain that it was the result of a mistake. I had occasion to go to a box of my own in a hurry that morning, and misled by the darkness and my own nervousness perhaps, took up his instead of my own. Not till I had opened it—with the toothpick, Hopgood, for I had been to a reception and did not have my keys with me—did I notice my mistake. I had intended to explain the matter to Mr. Stuyvesant, but you know what happened that day, and since then I have thought nothing of it."

===Chinese===
「尽可放心，只要你看守着这些保险柜，斯泰弗森特先生绝不会抱怨有人动过他的东西，」西尔维斯特先生以清朗铿锵的声调说。「至于他的箱子开着，我理应解释一下：那是一个误会所致。那天早上我急匆匆要取自己的一只箱子，许是被黑暗和我自己的紧张所误，拿了它的而不是我自己的。直到打开它——是用那支牙签打开的，霍普古德，因为我刚赴过一个招待会，身上没带钥匙——我才发觉自己弄错了。我本打算把这事跟斯泰弗森特先生说明白，可你知道那天出了什么事，自那以后我就再没把它放在心上。」

===Original===
The janitor's face cleared to its natural expression. "You are very kind, sir, to explain yourself to me," said he; "it was not necessary." But his lightened face spoke volumes. "I have been on the police force and I know how to hold my tongue when it is my duty, but it is very hard work when the duty is on the other side. Have you any commands for me?"
Mr. Sylvester shook his head, and his eye roamed over the humble furniture and scanty comforts of this poor man's domicile. Hopgood thought he might be going to offer him some gift or guerdon, and in a low distressed tone spoke up:
"I shall not try to ask your pardon, sir, for anything I have said. Honesty that is afraid to show itself, is no honesty for me. I could not meet your eye, knowing that I was aware of any circumstance of which you supposed me ignorant. What I know, you must know, as long as I remain in the position you were once kind enough to procure for me. And now that is all I believe, sir."

===Chinese===
门房的脸放晴了，恢复了本来的神情。「您太客气了，先生，肯费神跟我解释，」他说；「其实大可不必。」可他那张放晴的脸已胜过千言万语。「我在警署当过差，该闭嘴的时候懂得闭嘴，可这份差事要的是另一头，那就难得多了。您可有什么吩咐给我？」
西尔维斯特先生摇摇头，目光在这可怜人的住所里那些简陋的家具和寥寥几样舒适之物上逡巡。霍普古德以为他大概要赏他点什么礼物或酬报，便以低低的、不安的声调开口道：
「先生，我方才说的话，不会求您原谅。见不得光的诚实，在我看来算不得诚实。我既知道您以为我不知道的情况，就没法跟您对视。我所知道的，您也必须知道——只要我还待在您当年好心为我谋来的这个位子上。就这些了，先生，我想。」

===Original===
Mr. Sylvester dropped his eyes from the bare walls over which they had been restlessly wandering, and fixed them for a passing moment on the countenance of the man before him. Then with a grave action he lifted his hat from his head, and bowed with the deference he might have shown to one of his proudest colleagues, and without another look or word, quietly left the room.

===Chinese===
西尔维斯特先生把眼睛从那几面他方才不安地游目其上的光秃秃的墙上收回，在面前这人脸上驻留了一瞬。随后他做一个郑重的动作，从头上摘下帽子，鞠了一躬——那份恭谨，便是对他最骄傲的同僚他也未必拿得出。不再看一眼，不再说一字，他悄无声息地退出了房间。

===Original===
Hopgood in his surprise stared after him somewhat awestruck. But when the door had quite closed, he caught up his child almost passionately in his arms, and crushing her against his breast, asked, while his eye roamed round the humble room that in its warmth and comfort was a palace to him, "Will he take the first opportunity to have me dismissed, or will his heart forgive the expression of my momentary doubts, for the sake of this poor wee one that he so tenderly fancies?"
The question did not answer itself, and indeed it was one to which time alone could reply.

===Chinese===
霍普古德一脸惊愕，带着几分敬畏目送他出去。可等门完全合上，他近乎痴迷地把孩子一把抱进怀里，紧紧地贴上胸口，一面问，一面那双眼睛在这朴素的屋子里四处游移——在他眼里，就凭这份温暖与舒坦，这屋子便是宫殿：「他会趁头一个机会把我辞了，还是看在这可怜的小东西——他那样温柔地疼爱着——的份上，宽恕我这一时疑心的表露呢？」
这问题并未自答，事实上，也只有时间才能回答。

## XLIV In Mr. Stuyvesant’s Parlors / 四十四 在斯泰弗森特先生的客厅里

===Original===
> "Was I deceived, or did a sable cloud
Turn forth her silver lining on the night?"

"Unworthy?"

"Yes."

===Chinese===
> 「是我受了蒙蔽，还是那乌黑的云／真的在黑夜里翻出了它的银边？」

「不配？」

「是的。」

===Original===
Cicely stared at her father with wide-open and incredulous eyes. "I cannot believe it," she murmured; "no, I cannot believe it."

Her father drew up a chair to her side. "My daughter," said he, with unusual tenderness, "I have hesitated to tell you this, fearing to wound you; but my discretion will allow me to keep silence no longer. Bertram Sylvester is not an honest man, and the sooner you make up your mind to forget him, the better."

"Not honest?" You would scarcely have recognized Cicely's voice. Her father's hand trembled as he drew her back to his side.

"It is a hard revelation for me to make to you, after testifying my approval of the young man. I sympathize with you, my child, but nonetheless I expect you to meet this disappointment bravely. A theft has been committed in our bank—"

"You do not accuse him of theft! Oh father, father!"

===Chinese===
西塞莉（Cicely）睁大了一双难以置信的眼睛，怔怔地望着父亲。「我不相信，」她喃喃道，「不，我不相信。」

她父亲把一张椅子拉到她身旁。「我的女儿，」他说，语调中带着一种异乎寻常的温柔，「我一直犹豫着不肯告诉你这件事，怕伤你的心；可再谨慎也不能让我继续沉默下去了。伯特兰·西尔维斯特（Bertram Sylvester）不是个诚实的人，你越早下定决心忘掉他，就越好。」

「不诚实？」你几乎认不出这是西塞莉的声音了。他把她拉回自己身边时，那只手不住地颤抖。

「在表示过对那年轻人的赞许之后，这事实对我是桩难堪的揭露。我同情你，我的孩子，但我仍旧指望你能勇敢地面对这次失望。我们银行里发生了一桩盗窃——」

「您不是在指控他盗窃吧！哦，父亲，父亲！」

===Original===
"No," he stammered. "I do not accuse him, but facts look very strongly against someone in our trust, and—"

"But that is not sufficient," she cried, rising in spite of his detaining hand till she stood erect before him. "You surely would not allow any mere circumstantial evidence to stand against a character as unblemished as his, even if he were not the man whom your daughter—"

He would not let her continue. "I admit that I should be careful how I breathed suspicion against a man whose record was unimpeached," he assented, "but Bertram Sylvester does not enjoy that position. Indeed, I have just received a communication which goes to show, that he once actually acknowledged to having perpetrated an act of questionable integrity. Now a man as young as he, who—"

===Chinese===
「不，」他结结巴巴地说。「我没有指控他，可是种种事实对受我们信托的某一个人极为不利，而且——」

「可那还不够，」她喊道，不顾他挽留的手，径自站了起来，挺直在他面前。「您总不至于任凭区区旁证，去坐实一个像他那般清白无瑕的人——哪怕他并不是令嫒所——」

他不让她再说下去。「我承认，对一个记录从未受过指摘的人，我在吐露怀疑时本应如何审慎，」他应道，「可是伯特兰·西尔维斯特并不处在那种地位。事实上，我刚刚收到一份文书，足以表明他有一次竟亲口承认犯过一桩有亏操守之事。一个像他这般年纪轻轻就——」

===Original===
"But I cannot believe it," she moaned. "It is impossible, clearly impossible. How could he look me in the face with such a sin on his conscience! He could not, simply could not. Why, father, his brow is as open as the day, his glance clear and unwavering as the sunlight. It is some dreadful mistake. It is not Bertram of whom you are speaking!"

Her father sighed. "Of whom else should it be? Come my child, do you want to read the communication which I received last night? Do you want to be convinced?"

"No, no;" she cried; but quickly contradicted herself with a hurried, "Yes, yes, let me be made acquainted with what there is against him, if only that I may prove to you it is all a mistake."

===Chinese===
「可我不能相信，」她呜咽道。「这不可能，分明不可能。他若良心上背着这样一桩罪孽，怎能直视我的眼睛！他不能，断断不能。父亲啊，他的额头坦荡如白昼，他的目光清朗、毫不动摇如阳光。这必是某种可怕的误会。您所说的，根本不是伯特兰！」

她父亲叹了口气。「还能是谁呢？来吧，我的孩子，你要不要读一读我昨夜收到的那份文书？你要不要心服口服？」

「不，不，」她喊着；可随即又匆忙改口，「是的，是的，让我知道那些对他不利的说法吧，哪怕只是为了向您证明，这全是一场误会。」

===Original===
"There is no mistake," he muttered, handing her a folded paper. "This statement was written two years ago; I witnessed it myself, though I little knew against whose honor it was directed. Read it, Cicely, and then remember that I have lost bonds out of my box at the bank, that could only have been taken by someone connected with the institution."

She took the paper in her hand, and eagerly read it through. Suddenly she started and looked up. "And you say that this was Bertram, this gentleman who allowed another man to accuse him of a past dishonesty?"

"So the person declares who forwarded me this statement; and though he is a poor wretch and evidently not above making mischief, I do not know as we have any special reason to doubt his word."

===Chinese===
「并没有误会，」他低声道，递给她一张折好的纸。「这份陈词是两年前写下的；是我亲眼见证的，虽然那时我全然不知它所指的究竟是何人的名誉。读吧，西塞莉，读完就请记住，我那只存放在银行里的保管箱里丢失了债券，而这些债券只可能是由与该所有瓜葛的人取走的。」

她接过那张纸，急切地从头读到尾。忽然她一惊，抬起头来。「您是说，这写的就是伯特兰，就是这位任凭旁人指控他过去不诚实的先生？」

「把这份陈词转寄给我的人是这么声明的；那人虽然是个可怜虫，显然也不无兴风作浪之嫌，可我并不认为我们有什么特别的理由去怀疑他的话。」

===Original===
Cicely's eyes fell and she stood before her father with an air of indecision. "I do not think it was Bertram," she faltered, but said no more.

"I would to God for your sake, it was not!" he exclaimed. "But this communication together with the loss we have sustained at the bank, has shaken my faith, Cicely. Young men are so easily led astray nowadays; especially when playing for high stakes. A man who could leave his profession for the sake of winning a great heiress—"

"Father!"

"I know he has made you think it was for love; but when the woman whom a young man fancies, is rich, love and ambition run too closely together to be easily disentangled. And now, my dear, I have said my say and leave you to act according to the dictates of your judgment, sure that it will be in a direction worthy of your name and breeding." And stooping for a hasty kiss, he gave her a last fond look and quietly left the room.

===Chinese===
西塞莉垂下眼睛，带着犹豫不决的神情立在父亲面前。「我想那不是伯特兰，」她嗫嚅道，却没有再说下去。

「为了你，我但愿不是！」他喊道。「可是这份文书连同我们在银行所受的损失，已经动摇了我的信心，西塞莉。如今的年轻人太容易被引入歧途了；尤其是在下了重注的时候。一个男人，为了赢得一位巨产的女继承人竟肯舍弃自己的本行——」

「父亲！」

「我知道他已让你以为，那是为了爱；可当一个小伙子心仪的女子有钱时，爱情与野心走得太近，要想理清是极难的。好了，亲爱的，我的话已经说完，剩下的就由你依照自己判断的指引去行事吧，我确信那方向必不负你的姓氏和教养。」他弯下身匆匆吻了她一下，投去最后慈爱的一瞥，便悄然离开了房间。

===Original===
And Cicely? For a moment she stood as if frozen in her place, then a great tremble seized her, and sinking down upon a sofa, she buried her face from sight, in a chaos of feeling that left her scarcely mistress of herself. But suddenly she started up, her face flushed, her eyes gleaming, her whole delicate form quivering with an emotion more akin to hope than despair.

"I cannot doubt him," she whispered; "it were as easy to doubt my own soul. He is worthy if I am worthy, true if I am true; and I will not try to unlove him!"

===Chinese===
至于西塞莉？她有一瞬如冻在原地般僵立不动，随即一阵大颤攫住了她，她瘫倒在一张沙发上，把脸埋了起来不让人看见，陷于一片纷乱的情绪之中，几乎不能自主。可忽然她一跃而起，双颊绯红，双目生光，整个人纤细的身形都因一种更近于希望而非绝望的情绪而颤动。

「我不能怀疑他，」她低语道，「怀疑他，就同怀疑我自己的灵魂一般不易。我若配得上，他便也配得上；我若忠贞，他便也忠贞；我决不去勉强不爱他！」

===Original===
But soon the reaction came again, and she was about to give full sway to her grief and shame, when the parlor door opened—she herself was sitting in the extension room—and she saw Mr. Sylvester and Paula come in. She at once rose to her feet; but she did not advance. A thousand hopes and fears held her enchained where she was; besides there was something in the aspect of her friends, which made her feel as though a welcome even from her, would at that moment be an intrusion.

"They have come to see father," she thought "and—"

Ah what, Cicely?

===Chinese===
可不久那反弹又来了，她正要任凭自己的悲愤与羞愧倾泻而出，客厅的门开了——她本人坐在外间——只见西尔维斯特先生和宝拉走了进来。她立刻站起身来；却没有上前。千百种希望与恐惧把她牢牢锁在原地；何况两位朋友的神色之间有些什么，使她觉得，此刻即便由她出声招呼，也是多有不妥。

「他们是来看父亲的，」她想，「而且——」

而且什么，西塞莉？

===Original===
Paula, who was too absorbed in her own feelings to glance into the extension room beyond, approached Mr. Sylvester and laid her hand upon his arm. "Whatever comes," said she, "truth, honor and love remain."

And he bowed his head and seemed to kiss her hand, and Cicely observing the action, grew pale and dropped her eyes, realizing as by a lightning's flash, both the nature of the feeling that prompted this unusual manifestation on his part, and the possible sorrows that lay before her dearest friend, if not before herself, should the secret suspicions she cherished in regard to Mr. Sylvester prove true. When she had summoned up courage to glance again in their direction, Mr. Stuyvesant had entered the parlor and was nervously welcoming his guests.

===Chinese===
宝拉一心沉浸在自己的情绪里，不曾朝再里面的外间瞥上一眼，径自走到西尔维斯特先生跟前，把手放在他臂上。「无论发生什么，」她说，「真理、荣誉与爱都长存。」

他低下头去，似乎在吻她的手；西塞莉看在眼里，脸色发白，垂下了眼睛，仿佛一道闪电划过，她顿然明白了他此举背后那份感情的真相，也明白了倘若她私下对西尔维斯特先生所怀的那些疑虑果真不虚，她最亲爱的朋友——若不是她自己——前面可能等着的是怎样的苦痛。等到她鼓起勇气再朝他们那边看去时，斯泰弗森特先生已经走进客厅，正神情紧张地招待着客人。

===Original===
Mr. Sylvester waited for no preamble. "I have come," said he, in his most even and determined tones, "to speak to you in regard to a communication from a man by the name of Holt, which I was told was to be sent to you last evening. Did you receive such a one?"

Mr. Stuyvesant flushed, grew still more nervous in his manner and uttered a short, "I did," in a tone severer than he perhaps intended.

"It will not be too much for me, then, to conclude, that in your present estimation my nephew stands committed to a past dishonesty?"

===Chinese===
西尔维斯特先生不等任何寒暄。「我来，」他以最平稳而坚决的声调说道，「是为了一位姓霍尔特（Holt）的人写的一封文书，来与您一谈。我被告知，这文书昨夜就要送到您手上。您可曾收到这样一封？」

斯泰弗森特先生脸上一红，举止更见局促，短促地答了一声：「收到了。」语气的严厉，恐怕连他自己也始料未及。

「那么，我据此推断，在您眼下看来，我的侄子已被坐实了一桩过往的不诚实，这话不算过分吧？」

===Original===
"It has been one of my chief sources of regret—one of them I say," repeated Mr. Stuyvesant, "that any loss of esteem on the part of your nephew, must necessarily reflect upon the peace if not the honor of a man I hold in such high regard as yourself. I assure you I feel it quite as a brother might, quite as a brother."

Mr. Sylvester at once rose. "Mr. Stuyvesant," declared he, "my nephew is as honest a man as walks this city's streets. If you will accord me a few minutes private conversation, I think I can convince you so."

===Chinese===
「我一直深以为憾——这是其一，我说，这是其一，」斯泰弗森特先生重复道，「贵侄任何敬意的失落，都必连带影响到一位我所如此推崇之人的安宁，若非其名誉——而那位便是您本人。我向您保证，我之感同身受，与一位兄弟无异，与一位兄弟无异。」

西尔维斯特先生当即起身。「斯泰弗森特先生，」他断言道，「我的侄子是行走在这座城市街巷间最诚实的人之一。您若肯赐我几分钟私下交谈，我想我能使您也信服这一点。」

===Original===
"I should be very glad," replied Mr. Stuyvesant, glancing towards the extension-room where he had left his daughter. "I have always liked the young man." Then with a quick look in the other's face, "You are not well, Mr. Sylvester?"

"Thank you, I am not ill; let us say what we have to, at once, if you please." And with just a glance at Paula, he followed the now somewhat agitated director from the room.

===Chinese===
「那再好不过，」斯泰弗森特先生答道，朝他刚才留下女儿的外间瞥了一眼。「我一向喜欢这年轻人。」随即又迅速看了一眼对方的脸，「您身体不适吗，西尔维斯特先生？」

「多谢，我并非抱恙；若蒙允许，我们有什么话，就立刻说吧。」他只朝宝拉看了一眼，便跟着此刻颇为激动的这位董事走出了房间。

===Original===
Cicely who had started forward at their departure, glanced down the long parlor before her, and hastily faltered back; Paula was praying. But in a few moments her feelings overcame her timidity, and hurrying into her friend's presence, she threw her arms about her neck and pressed her cheek to hers. "Let us pray together," she whispered.

Paula drew back and looked her friend in the face. "You know what all this means?" she asked.

"I guess," was the low reply.

===Chinese===
西塞莉在他们走后本要抢步上前，朝眼前这间长长的客厅望去，又仓皇地缩了回来；宝拉正在祷告。可片刻之后，情感便压过了胆怯，她快步走到朋友跟前，双臂搂住她的脖子，把自己的脸颊贴上她的脸颊。「我们一起祷告吧。」她低声说。

宝拉往后退了一步，直视着朋友的脸。「这一切意味着什么，你知道？」她问。

「我猜得到。」是那低低的回答。

===Original===
Paula checked a sob and clasped Cicely to her bosom. "He loves me," she faltered, "and he is doing at this moment what he believes will separate us. He is a noble man, Cicely, noble as Bertram, though he once did—" She paused. "It is for him to say what, not I," she softly concluded.

"Then Bertram is noble," Cicely timidly put in.

"Have you ever doubted it?"

"No."

===Chinese===
宝拉强忍下一声呜咽，把西塞莉紧紧搂到胸前。「他爱我，」她颤抖地说，「而他此刻所做的，正是他自信会把我们分开的事。他是个高贵的人，西塞莉，和伯特兰一样高贵，尽管他曾经——」她顿住。「那曾经的是什么，该由他来说，不该由我。」她柔柔地结语。

「那么伯特兰是高贵的了，」西塞莉怯怯地插了一句。

「你可曾怀疑过？」

「不曾。」

===Original===
And hiding their blushes on each other's shoulders, the two girls sat breathlessly waiting, while the clock ticked away in the music-room and the moments came and went that determined their fate. Suddenly they both rose. Mr. Stuyvesant and Mr. Sylvester were descending the stairs. Mr. Sylvester came in first. Walking straight up to Paula, he took her in his arms and kissed her on the forehead.

"My betrothed wife!" he whispered.

With a start of incredulous joy, Paula looked up. His glance was clear but strangely solemn and peaceful.

===Chinese===
两个姑娘各自把红晕埋在对方的肩头，屏息而待；音乐室里的钟滴答作响，决定她们命运的时刻一个一个地来了又去。忽然两人一同站了起来。斯泰弗森特先生与西尔维斯特先生正从楼梯上下来。西尔维斯特先生先一步进屋。他径直走到宝拉面前，把她拥入怀中，吻了她的额头。

「我订了婚的妻！」他低语道。

宝拉带着一种不敢置信的欣喜，蓦地抬起头来。他的目光清朗，却透着一种奇异的庄严与安宁。

===Original===
"He has heard all I had to say," added he; "he is a just man, but he is also a merciful one. Like you he declares that not what a man was, but what he is, determines the judgment of true men concerning him." And taking her on his arm, he stood waiting for Mr. Stuyvesant who now came in.

"Where is my daughter?" were that gentleman's words, as he closed the door behind him.

"Here, papa."

===Chinese===
「我该说的话，他都听过了，」他又道，「他是个公正的人，但也是个仁慈的人。他和你一样宣称：决定真正的男子对一个男子的评判的，不是他曾经是什么，而是他现在是什么。」他让她挽住自己的手臂，立着等候此刻进屋来的斯泰弗森特先生。

「我女儿在哪里？」那位绅士随手关上身后的门，开口便是这一句。

「在这里，爸爸。」

===Original===
He held out his hand, and she sprang towards him. "Cicely," said he, not without some tokens of emotion in his voice, "it is only right that I should inform you that we were all laboring under a mistake, in charging Mr. Bertram Sylvester with the words that were uttered in the Dey Street coffeehouse two years ago. Mr. Sylvester has amply convinced me that his nephew neither was, nor could have been present there at that time. It must have been some other man, of similar personality."

"Oh thank you, thank you!" Cicely's look seemed to say to Mr. Sylvester. "And he is quite freed from reproach?" she asked, with a smiling glance into her father's face.

===Chinese===
他伸出手，她便朝他扑了过去。「西塞莉，」他说，声音里不无几分激动的痕迹，「我理应告知你：我们把两年前在戴伊街咖啡馆里说出的那番话，归罪于伯特兰·西尔维斯特先生名下，这全是我们大家的一场误会。西尔维斯特先生已令我充分信服，他的侄子当时既不在场，也不可能在场。那必定是另一个相貌相近的人。」

「哦，谢谢您，谢谢您！」西塞莉的眼神仿佛在对西尔维斯特先生这样说。「那么，他是完全洗清嫌疑了？」她问，含笑瞥了父亲一眼。

===Original===
A hesitancy in Mr. Stuyvesant's manner, struck with a chill upon more than one heart in that room.

"Yes," he admitted at last; "the mere fact that a mysterious robbery has been committed upon certain effects in the bank of which he is cashier, is not sufficient to awaken distrust as to his integrity, but—"

At that moment the doorbell rung.

===Chinese===
斯泰弗森特先生举止间的一丝迟疑，让屋里不止一颗心都为之一冷。

「是的，」他终于承认，「他身为那家银行的出纳主任，银行里某些财物遭了一桩离奇的失窃，单凭这一事实，尚不足以唤起对他操守的疑心，但是——」

就在这时，门铃响了。

===Original===
"Your father would say," cried Mr. Sylvester, taking advantage of the momentary break, to come to the relief of his host, "that my nephew is too much of a gentleman to desire to press any claim he may imagine himself as possessing over you, while even the possibility of a shadow rests upon his name."

"The man who stole the bonds will be found," said Cicely.

And as if in echo to her words the parlor door opened, and a messenger from the bank stepped briskly up to Mr. Stuyvesant.

"A note from Mr. Folger," said he, with a quick glance at Mr. Sylvester.

===Chinese===
「令尊要说的，」西尔维斯特先生趁着这一时的停顿，替主人解围道，「无非是我的侄子太是个绅士，只要他的名姓上尚存一丝阴翳的可能，便不愿去强求任何他自以为对令嫐拥有的权利。」

「偷债券的人总会找到的。」西塞莉说。

像是应和她的这句话，客厅的门开了，一个银行的信差快步走到斯泰弗森特先生跟前。

「福尔杰先生的一封便笺。」他说着，朝西尔维斯特先生迅速瞥了一眼。

===Original===
Mr. Stuyvesant took the paper handed him, read it hastily through, and looked up with an air of some bewilderment.

"I can hardly believe it possible," cried he, "but Hopgood has absconded."

"Hopgood absconded?"

"Yes; is not that the talk at the bank?" inquired Mr. Stuyvesant, turning to the messenger.

"Yes sir. He has not been seen since yesterday afternoon when he left before the bank was closed for the night. His wife says she thinks he meant to run away, for before going, he came into the room where she was, kissed her and then kissed the child; besides it seems that he took with him some of his clothes."

===Chinese===
斯泰弗森特先生接过递来的那张纸，匆匆读罢，抬眼望去，满脸困惑。

「我简直难以置信，」他喊道，「可霍普古德（Hopgood）潜逃了。」

「霍普古德潜逃了？」

「是的；这岂不是银行里大家谈论的？」斯泰弗森特先生转向信差问。

「是的，先生。从昨日下午起就不见他的踪影了，他昨日在银行夜间落闸关门之前就离开了。他的妻子说她料想他是存心逃走的，因为临走之前，他到她所在的房里，先吻了她，又吻了孩子；此外，他似乎还带走了自己的一些衣物。」

===Original===
"Humph! and I had as much confidence in that man—"

"As I have now," came from Mr. Sylvester as the door closed upon the messenger. "If Hopgood has run away, it was from some generous but mistaken idea of sacrificing himself to the safety of another whom he may possibly believe guilty."

"No," rejoined Mr. Stuyvesant, "for here is a note from him that refutes that supposition. It is addressed to me and runs thus:

===Chinese===
「哼！我对那人本是一百个放心的——」

「正如我现在对他一样。」信差走出、房门关上之际，西尔维斯特先生的声音传来。「霍普古德若是逃走的，那必是出于某种慷慨却错误的想法，要牺牲自己以保全另一个他也许信其为有罪的人。」

「不然，」斯泰弗森特先生接道，「因为这里正有他的一封便笺，足以驳倒这一揣度。这信是写给我的，内容如下：

===Original===
> **Dear Sir.**—I beg your pardon and that of Mr. Sylvester for leaving my duties in this abrupt manner. But I have betrayed my trust and am no longer worthy of confidence. I am a wretched man and find it impossible to face those who have believed in my honesty and discretion. If I can bring the money back, you shall see me again, but if not, be kind to my wife and little one, for the sake of the three years when I served the bank faithfully.
> **John Hopgood**

===Chinese===
> **敬启者：**——我以这般仓促的方式擅离职守，恳请您与西尔维斯特先生宽宥。然而我已辜负所托，再不配受人信赖。我是一个可悲的人，再也无法面对那些曾信我诚实谨慎的人。倘若我能把钱带回来，您必能再见到我；倘若不能，请念在我为银行忠心效力三年的份上，善待我的妻儿。
> **约翰·霍普古德**

===Original===
"I don't understand it," cried Mr. Sylvester, "that looks—"

"As if he knew where the money was."

"I begin to hope," breathed Cicely.

Her father turned and surveyed her. "This puts a new aspect on matters," said he.

She glanced up beaming. "Oh, will you, do you say, that you think the shadow of this crime has at last found the spot upon which it can rightfully rest?"

"It would not be common sense in me to deny that it has most certainly shifted its position."

===Chinese===
「我不明白，」西尔维斯特先生喊道，「这瞧着——」

「好像他知道钱在哪儿似的。」

「我开始有希望了。」西塞莉轻轻吐出一句。

她父亲转过身来打量她。「这使事情有了新的面貌。」他说。

她容光焕发地抬起头来。「哦，您可会——您是说，您以为这桩罪行的阴影，总算找到了它当真可以栖身的那一处？」

「若说它确已挪动了位置，我若再加以否认，那便不合常理了。」

===Original===
With a radiant look at Cicely, Paula crossed to Mr. Stuyvesant's side, and laying her hand on his sleeve, whispered a word or two in his ear. He immediately glanced out of the window at the carriage standing before the door, then looked back at her and nodded with something like a smile. In another moment he stood at the front door.

"Be prepared," cried Paula to Cicely.

It was well she spoke, for when in an instant later Mr. Stuyvesant reentered the parlor with Bertram at his side, the rapidly changing cheek of the gentle girl showed that the surprise, even though thus tempered, was almost too much for her self-possession.

===Chinese===
宝拉朝西塞莉投去灿烂的一瞥，便走到斯泰弗森特先生身旁，把手搭在他袖上，在他耳边低声说了句把话。他立刻朝窗外望了望停在门前的那辆马车，又回过头看她，带着一丝近乎微笑的神情点了点头。再一转眼，他已经站在了临街的大门边。

「准备好。」宝拉朝西塞莉喊了一声。

幸亏她说了这话，因为转眼之间，斯泰弗森特先生便带着伯特兰重新走进客厅，这位温柔姑娘那变幻不定的脸色表明，这一惊，纵然如此预先打过招呼，也几乎令她难以自持。

===Original===
Mr. Stuyvesant did not wait for the inevitable embarrassment of the moment to betray itself in words. "Mr. Sylvester," said he, to the young cashier, "we have just received a piece of news from the bank, that throws unexpected light upon the robbery we were discussing yesterday. Hopgood has absconded, and acknowledges here in writing that he had something to do with the theft!"

"Hopgood, the janitor!" The exclamation was directed not to Mr. Stuyvesant but to Mr. Sylvester, towards whom Bertram turned with looks of amazement.

"Yes, it is the greatest surprise I ever received," returned that gentleman.

===Chinese===
斯泰弗森特先生并未等到此刻不可避免的尴尬在言语中流露出来。「西尔维斯特先生，」他对这位年轻的出纳主任说，「我们刚刚从银行接到一则消息，对我们昨日所议的那桩盗窃投下了一道意想不到的光。霍普古德潜逃了，并且在此亲笔承认他与这桩盗窃有所牵连！」

「霍普古德，那个门房！」这一声惊叹并非对斯泰弗森特先生而发，而是冲着西尔维斯特先生——伯特兰满脸惊异地转向了他。

「不错，这是我有生以来受到的最大一惊。」那位先生答道。

===Original===
"And Mr. Sylvester," continued Mr. Stuyvesant, with nervous rapidity and a generous attempt to speak lightly, "there is a little lady here who is so shaken by the news, that nothing short of a word of reassurance on your part will comfort her."

Bertram's eye followed that of Mr. Stuyvesant, and fell upon the blushing cheek of Cicely. With a flushing of his own brow, he stepped hastily forward.

"Miss Stuyvesant!" he cried, and looking down in her face, forgot everything else in his infinite joy and satisfaction.

===Chinese===
「还有，西尔维斯特先生，」斯泰弗森特先生继续道，语速紧张而急促，宽厚地竭力把话说得轻松些，「这里有一位小姑娘，因这消息震动得厉害，非得您亲自出言安抚，才能宽慰她。」

伯特兰的目光循着斯泰弗森特先生的看去，落在西塞莉绯红的脸颊上。他自己的额头也腾地一红，匆匆抢步上前。

「斯泰弗森特小姐！」他喊道，俯身望着她的脸，在无尽的欢喜与满足里，把其余一切都忘到了脑后。

===Original===
"Yes," announced the father with abrupt decision, "she is yours; you have fairly earned her."

Bertram bowed his head with irrepressible emotion, and for a moment the silence of perfect peace if not of awe, reigned over the apartment; but suddenly a low, determined "No!" was heard, and Bertram turning towards Mr. Stuyvesant, exclaimed, "You are very good, and the joy of this moment atones for many an hour of grief and impatience; but I have not earned her yet. The fact that Hopgood admits to having had something to do with the robbery, does not sufficiently exonerate the officers of the bank from all connection with the affair, to make it safe or honorable in me to unqualifiedly accept the inestimable boon of your daughter's regard. Till the real culprit is in custody and the mystery entirely cleared away, my impatience must continue to curb itself. I love your daughter too dearly to bring her anything but the purest of reputations. Am I not right, Miss Stuyvesant?"

===Chinese===
「是的，」父亲以一种突兀的决断宣布道，「她是你的了；这是你光明正大赢来的。」

伯特兰情不能自禁地低下了头，有一瞬间，整个房间里弥漫着一种尽善尽美的宁静，若非敬畏，便是近乎敬畏的静默；可忽然，一声低沉而坚决的「不！」传来，伯特兰转向斯泰弗森特先生，喊道：「您太好了，而这一刻的欢欣，足以抵偿许许多多个钟头的忧伤与焦灼；可我尚未赢得她。霍普古德既承认与这桩盗窃有牵连，这一事实尚不足以将银行的诸位职员与本案的一切瓜葛洗刷干净，使我可以安然、光彩地，无条件领受令嫐垂青这一无可估量的恩赐。真正的罪犯一日未曾归案、这重重疑团一日不曾彻底廓清，我的焦灼便只得继续自抑。我太爱您的女儿，除了最清白的名誉，不能带给她任何别的东西。我说得可对，斯泰弗森特小姐？」

===Original===
She cast a glance at her father, and bowed her head. "You are right," she repeated.

And Mr. Stuyvesant, with a visible lightening of his whole aspect, took the young man by the hand, and with as much geniality as his nature would allow, informed him that he was at last convinced that his daughter had made no mistake when she expressed her trust in Bertram Sylvester.

And in other eyes than Cicely's, shone the light of satisfied love and unswerving faith.

===Chinese===
她朝父亲看了一眼，低下了头。「你说得对。」她应道。

斯泰弗森特先生整个神情明显地松快下来，握住这年轻人的手，尽自己的性情所许，带着尽可能多的热忱告诉他：他终于信服，自己的女儿在表达对伯特兰·西尔维斯特的信赖时，并未看错人。

而在西塞莉之外的眼睛里，也闪烁着爱得满足、信得坚定不移的光。

## XVIII In the Night Watches / 十八 夜阑守更时

===Original===
> "Shall I not take mine ease in mine inn?"

> "What doth gravity out of his bed at midnight?"

===Chinese===
> 「我岂不能在自己的客栈里安享自在么？」

> 「庄重之人何以午夜便离了床？」

===Original===
"It has been the most delightful evening I have ever passed," said Mrs. Sylvester, as she threw aside her rich white mantle in her ample boudoir. "Sarah, two loops on that dolman tomorrow; do you hear? I thought my arms would freeze. Such an elegant gentleman as the Count de Frassac is! He absolutely went wild over you, Paula, but not understanding a word of English—O there, if that horrid little wretch didn't drop his spoon on my dress after all! He swore it never touched a thread of it, but just look at that spot, right in the middle of a pleating too. Paula, your opinion in regard to the lavendar was correct. I heard Mrs. Forsyth Jones whisper behind my back that lavendar always made blondes look *fade*. Of course I needed no further evidence to convince me that I had entirely succeeded in eclipsing her pale-faced daughter. Her daughter!" and the lazy gurgle echoed softly through the room, "As if every white-haired girl in the city considered herself entitled to be called a blonde!" She stopped to listen, examining herself in the glass near by. "I thought I heard Edward. It was very provoking in him to leave us in the cavalier manner in which he did. I was just going to introduce him to the count, not that he would have esteemed it much of an honor, Edward I mean, but when one has a good-looking husband—Sarah, that curtain over there hangs crooked, pull it straight this instant. Did you try the oysters, Paula? They were perfection, I shall have to dismiss Lorenzo without ceremony and procure me a cook that can make an oyster fricassee. By the way did you notice—" and so on and on for five minutes additional. Presently she burst forth with—"I do believe I know what it is to be thoroughly satisfied at last. The consideration which one receives as the wife of the president of the Madison bank is certainly very gratifying. If I had known I would feel such a change in the social atmosphere, I would have advocated Edward's dropping speculation long ago. Beauty and wealth may help one up the social ladder, but only a settled position such as he has now obtained, can carry you safely over the top. I feel at last as if we had reached the pinnacle of my ambition and had seen the ladder by which we mounted thrown down behind us. If I get my costume from Worth in time, I shall give a German next month."

===Chinese===
「这是我有生以来过得最惬意的一个晚上。」西尔维斯特夫人一边说，一边在她那间宽敞的闺房里把那件贵重的白色斗篷随手甩开。「莎拉（Sarah），明儿那件多尔曼外套要扣两道襻儿；听见没有？我这双胳膊都快冻僵了。德·弗拉萨克伯爵（Count de Frassac）真是位风度翩翩的先生！他简直为你神魂颠倒呢，宝拉，只可惜一句英文也听不懂——哎呀，瞧，那个可恶的小东西到底还是把他的调羹掉在我衣裳上了！他还赌咒说连一根纱都没碰着，可你瞧那一块污渍，偏偏落在褶裥正中。宝拉，你对那件淡紫色衣裳的见解果然不错。我听见福赛斯·琼斯夫人（Mrs. Forsyth Jones）在我背后咬耳朵，说淡紫色总叫金发人显*得暗淡*。这自然无须再有别的佐证，我便确信自己已把那个面色苍白的女儿彻底比下去了。她的女儿！」那懒洋洋的一串咯咯笑声在屋里轻轻地回荡着，「倒好像全城每个白头发的姑娘都自以为有资格被叫作金发美人似的！」她住了口侧耳一听，在近旁的镜前打量自己。「我方才好像听见爱德华（Edward）了。他那样把我们一丢、扬长而去，真是气人。我正要把他介绍给伯爵——虽说那也不见得能给他多大脸面，我说的是爱德华——可一个人既有个相貌堂堂的丈夫——莎拉，那边的帘子挂歪了，这便给我扯直。宝拉，那些牡蛎你尝了吗？做得无可挑剔，我只好不客气地把洛伦佐（Lorenzo）辞了，另觅一个会做奶汁牡蛎的厨子给我。对了，你可留意到——」如此这般又滔滔不绝地说了五分钟。忽然她又迸出一句——「我相信我这回可当真明白什么叫彻底心满意足了。身为麦迪逊银行（Madison bank）行长之妻所受的尊崇，实在叫人十分受用。早知道社交场上的气氛会起这么大的变化，我早就劝爱德华把那投机买卖丢开了。美貌和财富或许能助人爬上社交的梯子，可唯有像他眼下所得的这样稳固的地位，才能稳稳当当地把你送过顶去。我如今只觉得，我们到底攀上了我野心所求的绝顶，眼看着我们一路登上去的那架梯子已在身后被一脚踢倒。若是我那身从沃斯（Worth）那里订的衣裳能如期到手，下个月我便要办一场德国舞会（German）。」

===Original===
Paula from her stand at the door—for some minutes she had been endeavoring to escape to her room—surveyed her cousin in wonder. She had never seen her look as she did at that moment. Anyone who speaks from the heart, acquires a certain eloquence, and Ona for once was speaking from her heart. The unwonted emotion made her cheeks burn, and even her diamonds, ten thousand dollars worth as we have heard declared, were less brilliant than her eyes. Paula left her station on the doorsill and glided rapidly back to her side. "O Ona," said she, "if you would only look like that when—" she paused, what right had she to venture upon giving lessons to her benefactor.

===Chinese===
宝拉立在门口——方才这几分钟里，她一直想抽身回自己房里去——满眼惊奇地打量着表姐。她从未见过她像此刻这般模样。一个人但凡发自肺腑地说话，便自有一番雄辩；而这一回，奥娜（Ona）正是在发自肺腑地说话。这份不寻常的激动烧得她双颊通红，便连她那一身——据人所宣称值一万元之巨的——钻石，也不及她那双眼来得明亮。宝拉离开门槛处，又快步悄然地滑回她身边。「啊，奥娜，」她说，「你要是能一直这样神采——」她顿住了，自己有什么资格，竟胆敢给她的恩人说教呢。

===Original===
"When what?" inquired the other, subsiding at once into her naturally languid manner. Then with a total forgetfulness of the momentary curiosity that had prompted the question, held out her head to the attendant Sarah, with a command to be relieved of her ornaments. Paula sighed and hastened to her room. She could not bring herself to mention her anxiety in regard to the still absent master of the house, to this lazily-smiling thoroughly satisfied woman.

===Chinese===
「什么时候？」那一位问，立时又落回她那天生慵懒的做派里去了。接着，她竟把方才那一闪而过的、引出此问的好奇心忘得一干二净，只把头朝侍女莎拉伸过去，吩咐她替自己把首饰卸下来。宝拉叹了口气，急忙回自己房里去。对于这家那位仍旧未归的主人，她心头那一股焦虑，终究对着这个懒洋洋微笑、心满意足的女人，是吐露不出口的。

===Original===
But nonetheless did she herself sit up in the moonlight, listening with bended head for the sound of his step on the walk beneath. She could not sleep while he was absent; and yet the thoughts that disturbed her and kept her from her virgin pillow could not have been entirely for him, or why those wandering smiles that ever and anon passed flitting over her cheek, awakening the dimples that slumbered there, until she looked more like a dreamy picture of delight than a wakeful vision of apprehension. Not entirely for him—yet when somewhere towards three o'clock, she heard the long delayed step upon the stoop, she started up with eager eyes and a nervous gesture that sufficiently betrayed how intense was her interest in her benefactor's welfare and happiness. "If he goes to Ona's room it is all right," thought she; "but if he keeps on upstairs, I shall know that something is wrong and that he needs a comforter."

===Chinese===
可她自己却照样在月光里坐着，俯着侧耳倾听，听他的脚步声在楼下的石阶走道上响起。他不在家，她便睡不稳；然而扰乱她、叫她在这少女的枕上辗转的种种念头，又不见得全然是为了他——否则，怎会那些游移的笑意不时在她脸颊上掠过，惊醒了在那儿沉睡的笑靥，直叫她看上去更像一幅如梦的欢愉图，而不像一个辗转忧思的醒着的人儿呢。不见得全然为了他——可约莫三点钟光景，她终于听见那一向迟迟未至的脚步声踏上台阶时，她还是猛地一惊而起，眼里满是殷切，手里一个神经质的动作，已足够表明她对那位恩人的安宁与幸福，是怀着何等深切的挂念。「他若是往奥娜房里去，便无事了。」她心想，「可他若径直上楼，我便知道出了岔子，他需要有人宽慰。」

===Original===
He did not stop at Ona's room; and struck with alarm, Paula opened wide her door and was about to step out to meet him, when she caught a sight of his face, and started back. Here was no anxiety, that she could palliate! The very fact that he did not observe her slight form standing before him in the brilliant moonlight, proved that a woman's look or touch was not what he was in search of; and shrinking sensitively to one side, she sat down on the edge of her dainty bed, dropping her cheek into her hand with a weary troubled gesture from which all the delight had fled and only the apprehension remained. Suddenly she started alertly up; he was coming down again, this time with a gliding muffled tread. Sliding past her door, he descended to the floor below. She could hear the one weak stair in the heavy staircase creak, and—What! he has passed Ona's room, passed the bronze figure of Luxury on the platform beneath, is on his way to the front door, has opened it, shut it softly behind him and gone out again into the blank midnight streets. What did it mean? For a moment she thought she would run down and awaken Ona, but an involuntary remembrance of how those lazy eyes would open, stare peevishly and then shut again, stopped her on the threshold of her door; and sitting down again upon the side of her bed, she waited, this time with opened eyes eagerly staring before her, and quivering form that started at each and every sound that disturbed the silence of the great echoing house. At six o'clock she again rose; he had just reentered and this time he stopped at Ona's room.

===Chinese===
他并没有在奥娜的房门前停下；宝拉心头一惊，把房门整个推开，正要迈出去迎他，却一眼瞧见他的脸，又吓得退了回来。这一脸的神情，可不是她所能宽解的了！他竟没发觉她那单薄的身形，就在皎洁的月光里立在跟前——仅这一点，便足见他所要寻觅的，并非一个女人的一瞥或一抚；她敏感地往一旁缩了缩，在那张精致的小床边沿坐下，把手撑住脸颊，做了一个倦怠而忧愁的动作——其中所有的欢喜都已飞散，只剩下了那一份忧惧。忽然她机警地一跃而起；他又下来了，这一回是拖着一种悄无声息的、滑行似的脚步。他贴着她的房门掠过去，下到了下一层楼。她听得见那座沉重楼梯中那一级松动的楼梯吱呀一响，接着——什么！他已走过了奥娜的房间，走过了下面平台上那尊「奢华」的铜像，正朝大门走去，已经开了门，又把它在身后轻轻带上，再又走进了那空荡荡的午夜街头去了。这是怎么回事？有一瞬她恨不得奔下楼去叫醒奥娜，可一想到那双懒眼将怎样睁开、怎样气恼地瞪一下、又怎样重新合上，便不由自主地在自家门槛前停住了脚；于是她重新在床沿坐下，等着，这一回是睁大双眼急切地朝前直瞪，整个身形不住地颤动，每一声搅扰这空旷回响的大宅的寂静的声响，都叫她一激灵一激灵地。到了六点钟，她才又起身；他刚刚重新进门，这一回，他在奥娜的房门前停下了。

## XXV Jacqueline / 二十五 雅克琳

===Original===
> "The cold in clime are cold in blood,

 And love as scarce deserves the name,

 But mine is like the lava flood

 That burns in Etna's breast of flame."

===Chinese===
> 「生于寒带的人，血也冷，
> 他们的爱几乎不配这个名字，
> 可我的爱却像熔岩的洪流，
> 在埃特纳（Etna）烈焰的胸膛里燃烧。」

===Original===
"There are some men that have the appearance of being devoid of family affection, who in reality cherish it in the deepest and most passionate degree. Such a man was Colonel Japha. You have doubtless heard from your cradle what the neighbors thought of this stately, old fashioned gentleman. He was too handsome in his youth, too proudly reticent in his manhood, too self-contained and unrelenting in his age, not to be the talk of any town that numbered him among its inhabitants. But only from myself, a relative of the family and his housekeeper for years, can you learn with what undeviating faith and love he clung to the few upon whom he allowed his heart to fasten in affection. When he married Miss Carey, the world said, ‘He has chosen a beauty, because fine manners and a pretty face look well behind the Japha coffee-urn!’ But we, that is, this same young wife and myself, knew that in marrying her he had taken unto himself his other half, the one sweet woman for whom his proud heart could beat and before whom his stately head could bow. When she died, the world exclaimed, ‘He will soon fill her place!’ But I who watched the last look that passed between them in the valley of the shadow of that death, knew that the years would come and the years would go without seeing Colonel Japha marry again.

===Chinese===
「世上有那样一些男子，看去仿佛毫无骨肉之情，实则心里头把它藏得最深、爱得最烈。杰法上校（Colonel Japha）正是这样一个男子。这位庄重、守旧的老绅士，街坊邻里怎样看他，你一定自襁褓里便听人说过。他少时太英俊，壮年时太倨傲寡言，老来又太自持、太不肯通融，凡是收他做居民的小镇，没有不把他当作谈资的。可他究竟怀着怎样坚定不移的忠心与深情，依恋着那几个他容许自己的心去爱的人——这只有从我嘴里你才听得到；我是这家人的亲戚，又在他家做了多年的管家。他娶凯里小姐（Miss Carey）的那天，外头的人都说：『他挑了个美人，无非是因为仪态体面、脸蛋俏丽，衬得起雅法家那只咖啡壶罢！』可我们——也就是这位年轻夫人同我——心里明白：娶她，便是为自己娶来了另一半，那独一无二、叫他这颗骄傲的心肯为之跳动、叫他这颗高昂的头肯为之低下的女子。她死的时候，世人又叫起来：『他很快就会续弦的！』可我亲眼见过在那死亡的幽谷里，他们两人之间交换的最后那一眼；我知道，岁月来来去去，都再见不到杰法上校另娶了。

===Original===
“The little babe whom she left to his care, took all the love which he had left. From the moment it began to speak, he centered in its tiny life all the hope and all the pride of his solitary heart. And the Japha pride was nearly as great as the Japha heart. She was a pretty child; not a beauty like her mother or like you, my dear, who however so nearly resemble her. But for all that, pretty enough to satisfy the eyes of her secretly doting father, and her openly doting nurse and cousin. I say secretly doting father. I do not mean by that that he regarded her with an affection which he never displayed, but that it was his way to lavish his caresses at home and in the privacy of her little nursery. He never made a parade of anything but his pride. If he loved her, it was enough for her to know it. In the street and the houses of their friends, he was the strict, somewhat severe father, to whom her childish eyes lifted at first with awe, but afterwards with a quiet defiance, that when I first saw it, made my heart stand still with unreasoning alarm.

===Chinese===
「她撒手人寰，留给他的那个小婴儿，便把他所剩的爱一股脑儿全夺了去。从这孩子牙牙学语那天起，他便把那颗孤独之心里的全部希望、全部骄傲，都聚拢到她这条小小的命上来。而雅法家的骄傲，差不多和雅法家的心一样大。她是个俊俏的孩子；不像她母亲那样是个美人，也不像你，亲爱的——虽说你和她长得那么相像。可话虽如此，她已够俏丽，足以叫她那暗自溺爱的父亲、与她那毫不掩饰地疼她的保姆兼表姐看在眼里心满意足了。我说她父亲是暗自溺爱，并不是说他把这份情意藏在心底从不流露，而是说他的做派是：只在自家里头、只在她那间小小的育儿室里，才肯把满腔疼爱尽情倾吐。他从来不向人夸耀什么，除了他的骄傲。他若爱她，她自己知道便够了。到了街上、到了朋友家中，他便是那个严厉、甚至有些苛刻的父亲，孩子最初带着敬畏仰望他，后来却换成了一种静静的抗逆之色——我头一回瞧见的时候，一颗心直吓得定了住，涌起一阵毫无来由的惊慌。

===Original===
“She was so reserved a child and yet so deeply passionate. From the beginning I felt that I did not understand her. I loved her; I have never loved any mortal as I did her—and do; but I could not follow her impulses or judge of her feelings by her looks.

“When she grew older it was still worse. She never contradicted her father, or appeared in any open way to disobey his commands, or thwart him in his plans. Yet she always did what she pleased, and that so quietly, he frequently did not observe that matters had taken any other direction, than that which he had himself ordained. ‘It is her mother’s tact,’ he used to say. Alas it was something more than that; it was her father’s will united to the unscrupulousness of some forgotten ancestor.

===Chinese===
「她是那样一个内向的孩子，却又那样情深如火。打一开始我便觉得，自己摸不透她。我爱她；这世上我从未像爱她那样爱过任何生灵——如今仍然爱她；可我追不上她那一闪而过的念头，也凭她的神色判断不出她的心思。

「等她再大些，事情更糟了。她从不顶撞父亲，也不曾有任何公然违命、破坏他打算的行径。可她向来想做什么便做什么，而且做得那样悄无声息，他往往全然不曾察觉事情已偏离了他亲自定下的方向，拐到别处去了。『这是她母亲那份分寸感。』他从前爱这么说。唉，岂止是分寸感那么简单；那是她父亲的执拗，加上了某位早已被人遗忘的祖上那种不择手段的性子。

===Original===
“But with the glamour of her eighteen years upon me, I did not recognize this then, any more than he. I saw her through the magic glasses of my own absorbing love, and tremble as I frequently would in the still scorn of her unfathomable passion, I never dreamed she could do anything that would seriously offend her father’s affection or mortify his pride. The truth is, that Jacqueline did not love us. Say what you will of the claims of kindred, and the right of every father to his childrens’ regard, Jacqueline Japha accepted the devotion that was lavished upon her, but she gave none in return. She could not, perhaps. Her father was too cold in public and too warm in his home-bursts of affection. I was plain and a widow; no mate for her in age, condition or estate. She could neither look up to me nor lean upon me. I had been her nurse in childhood and though a relative, was still a dependent; what was there in all that to love! If her mother had lived—But we will not dwell on possibilities. Jacqueline had no mother and no friend that was dear enough to her, to teach her unwilling soul the great lesson of self-control and sacrifice.

===Chinese===
「可她十八岁那年的光彩蒙住了我的眼，那时我同他一样，都看不出这一点。我透过自己那副忘我痴爱的魔镜看着她，纵使时时在她那深不可测的、静静带着轻蔑的炽情面前发抖，也从未梦到她会做出什么当真触怒父亲、伤他骄傲的事来。真相是——雅克琳并不爱我们。任你怎样讲血脉亲情的羁绊，任你怎样讲每一个父亲理应享有子女的敬爱，雅克琳·雅法（Jacqueline Japha）照单全收了别人倾注在她身上的那一片痴情，自己却丝毫不肯还报。也许她是不能罢。她父亲在外头过于冷淡，而在家中情之所至时又过于炽热。我相貌平平，又是个寡妇；论年纪、身份、家底，都配不上做她的伴。她既无从仰望我，也无从倚靠我。我自幼是她的保姆，虽说是亲戚，到底是个仰人鼻息的人；这一切里头，有什么可爱之处呢！倘若她的母亲还在——可我们不去说那些『倘若』了。雅克琳没有母亲，也没有哪个朋友能亲热到把她这颗不肯就范的灵魂，教会那门克制与牺牲的大功课。

===Original===
“You will say that is strange. That situated as she was, she ought to have found friends both dear and congenial; but that would be to declare that Jacqueline was like others of her age and class, whereas she was single and alone; a dark-browed girl, who allured the gaze of both men and women, but who cared but little for anyone till—But wait, child. I shall have to speak of matters that will cause your cheeks to blush. Lay your head down on my knee, for I cannot bear the sight of blushes upon a cheek more innocent than hers.”

With a gentle movement she urged Paula to sit upon a little stool at her feet, pressed the young girl’s head down upon her lap, and burying the lovely brow beneath her aged hands, went hurriedly on.

===Chinese===
「你定要说这未免古怪。以她的处境，本该交得着又亲近又投契的朋友才是；可这话无异于说雅克琳与她那个年纪、那个阶层别的姑娘并无不同——而她是独一无二的，是孤独无伴的；一个眉目浓黑的少女，惹得男女两性都忍不住要看她，可她自个儿对谁都几乎不上心，直到——可且慢，孩子。接下来我要讲的事，会让你脸红。把你这颗小脑袋搁在我膝上吧，我可不忍心看见一张比她的脸清白得多的脸颊上，泛起那红晕。」

她轻轻一动，劝宝拉（Paula）在她脚边的一张小凳子上坐下，把那少女的头按在她腿上，用自己那双苍老的手把那可爱的额头整个掩住，便匆匆地往下讲。

===Original===
“You are young, dear, and may not know what it is to love a man. Jacqueline was young also, but from the moment she returned home to us from a visit she had been making in Boston, I perceived that something had entered her life that was destined to make a great change in her; and when a few weeks later, young Robert Holt from Boston, came to pay his respects to her in her father’s house, I knew, or thought I did, what that something was. We were sitting in this room I remember, when the servant-girl came in, and announced that Mr. Holt was in the parlor. Jacqueline was lying on the sofa, and her father was in his usual chair by the table. At the name, Holt, the girl rose as if it had suddenly thundered, or the lightning had flashed. I see her now. She was dressed in white—though it was early fall she still clung to her summer dresses—her dark hair was piled high, and caught here and there with old-fashioned gold pins, a splendid red rose burned on her bosom, and another flashed crimson as blood from her folded hands.

===Chinese===
「你还小啊，亲爱的，怕还不知道爱上一个男人是怎样一回事。雅克琳那时也年轻；可从她去波士顿（Boston）走了一遭、回到我们家里的那一刻起，我便察觉有一桩东西闯进了她的命里，注定要叫她大变模样。过了几个礼拜，年轻的罗伯特·霍尔特（Robert Holt）从波士顿来到她父亲家中拜访她，我便知道了——或者自以为知道了——那桩东西是什么。我记得清清楚楚，我们正坐在这间屋子里，那个女佣走进来，通报说霍尔特先生（Mr. Holt）在客厅里。雅克琳正躺在沙发上，她父亲照例坐在桌旁他那把椅子里。一听『霍尔特』这个名字，那姑娘便立时站了起来，仿佛天上忽然打了雷、或是闪了电。那情景至今还像在我眼前。她穿着一身白——虽已入初秋，她却还舍不下她那些夏装——她那乌黑的头发高高堆起，四处用老式的金钗别住，一朵艳丽的红玫瑰在她胸前像火一般燃烧，另一朵则从她交握的双手间闪烁出血一样深红的颜色。

===Original===
“‘Holt?’ repeated the Colonel without turning his head, ‘I know no such man.’

“‘He said he wished to see Miss Jacqueline,’ simpered the servant.

“‘Oh,’ returned the Colonel indifferently. He never showed surprise before the servants—and went on with his book, still without turning his head.

===Chinese===
「『霍尔特？』上校头也不回地重复了一句，『我不认得这样一个人。』

「『他说他想见雅克琳小姐。』那女佣拿腔作调地笑着说。

「『哦。』上校漫不经心地应了一声。他从不在下人面前露出惊讶之色——便又接着看他的书，依旧不曾回头。

===Original===
“I thought if he had turned it, he would scarcely sit there reading so quietly; for Jacqueline who had not stirred from her alert and upright position, was looking at him in a way no father, least of all a father who loved his child as he did her, could have beheld without agitation. It was the glance of a tigress waiting for the sight of an inconsiderate move, in order to spring. It was wild unconstrainable joy, eying a possible check and madly defying it. I shuddered as I looked at her eye, and sickened as I perceived a huge drop of blood ooze from her white fingers, where they unconsciously clutched a thorn, and drop dark and disfiguring upon her virgin garments. At the indifferent exclamation of her father, her features relaxed, and she turned haughtily towards the girl, with a veiling of her secret delight that already bespoke the woman of the world.

===Chinese===
「我心想，他若是回了头，怕就不能那样安安静静地坐在那儿看书了；雅克琳依然保持着那警觉、挺直的姿势一动未动，正望着他——那是任何一位父亲、尤其是像他这般爱女儿的父亲，看了都不可能不失措的一种目光。那是一头母虎的眼神，正等着看对方一个不留神的动作，便要扑上去。那是不可遏制的狂喜，盯着一个可能的障碍，疯狂地加以蔑视。我瞧着她的眼睛，不由得一阵寒颤；又看见一滴大大的血从她苍白的手指间渗出来——她不知不觉地捏着一根玫瑰花刺——那血滴漆黑而刺眼，落在了她那洁白无瑕的衣裙上，叫我一阵恶心。听到她父亲那声漫不经心的应答，她的神情松弛下来，傲慢地转向那个女佣，把她心底那份欢喜遮掩起来的那份功夫，已然显出一个久经世故的女子的做派。

===Original===
“‘Tell Mr. Holt that I will see him presently,’ said she, and was about to follow the girl from the room when I caught her by the sleeve.

“‘You will have to change your dress,’ said I, and I pointed to the ominous blot disfiguring its otherwise spotless white.

“She started and gave me a quick glance.

“‘I have a skin like a spider’s web,’” cried she. ‘I should never meddle with roses.’ But I noticed she did not toss the blossom away.

===Chinese===
「『去告诉霍尔特先生，我就出来。』她说，正要随那女佣出屋，我一把抓住了她的袖子。

「『你得换一身衣裳，』我说，一面指给她看那块不祥的污渍，正破坏着那一身原本一尘不染的白。

「她一惊，飞快地瞥了我一眼。

「『我这一身皮就像蛛丝那么薄，』她叫道，『我本就不该碰玫瑰。』可我留意到，她并没有把那朵花随手丢开。

===Original===
“‘Who is this Mr. Holt?’ now asked the Colonel suddenly turning, the servant having left the room.

“‘He is a gentleman I met in Boston,’ came from his daughter’s lips, in her usual light and easy tones. ‘He is probably passing through our town on his way to Providence, where I was told he did business. His call is no more than a formality, I presume.’ And with an indifferent little smile and nod, she vanished from the room, that a moment before had been filled with the threat of her silent passion. The Colonel gave a short sigh but returned undisturbed to his book.

===Chinese===
「『这位霍尔特先生是谁？』这时上校忽然回头问道——那女佣已经出了屋子。

「『是我在波士顿结识的一位先生，』他女儿用她平常那种轻盈随意的口吻答道，『他大概是路过我们镇上，往普罗维登斯（Providence）去，我听说他在那儿做生意。他这回来访，想必不过是循个礼数罢了。』说着，她漫不经心地微微一笑、点了点头，便从屋里消失了——方才这间屋子还满满当当地充塞着她那无声炽情的威胁。上校短短地叹了一口气，却不动声色地接着看他的书。

===Original===
“In the course of a few minutes Jacqueline came back. She had changed her dress for one as summerlike as the other, but still finer and more elaborate. She looked elegant, imperious, but the joy had died out from her eyes, and in its place was another expression incomprehensible to me, but fully as alarming as any that had gone before. ‘Mr. Holt finds himself obliged to remain in town over night, and would like to pay his respects to you,’ said she to her father.

“The Colonel immediately rose, looking very grand as he turned and surveyed his daughter with his clear penetrating eye.”

===Chinese===
