「过了几分钟，雅克琳回来了。她换了一身衣裙，同方才那身一样是夏装，却更为讲究、更为精致。她看上去雍容、威严，可她眼里那股欢欣已经熄了，取而代之的是另一种叫我捉摸不透的神情，却和先前任何一种一样叫人发憷。『霍尔特先生发觉自己不得不在镇上过夜，想过来向您致意。』她对父亲说。

「上校立时站起身来，转身用那双清亮锐利的眼睛打量着他的女儿，神情威严之至。」

===Original===
“‘You have a lover, have you not?’ he asked, laying his hand on her bare and beautifully polished shoulder.

“An odd little smile crossed her lip. She looked at her hands on which never a ring shone, and coquettishly tossed her head. ‘Let the gentleman speak for himself,’ said she, ‘I give no man his title until he has earned it.’

“Her father laughed. A lover was not such a dreadful thing in his eyes provided he were worthy. And Jacqueline would not choose unworthily of course—a Japha and his daughter! ‘Well then,’ said he, ‘let us see if he can make good his title; Holt is not a bad name and Boston is not a poor place to hail from.’ And without more ado, they hurried from the room. But the light had all died out from her face! What did it mean?

===Chinese===
「『你有了情人，是吗？』他问道，把一只手搁在她那裸露、光洁如玉的肩头。

「一丝古怪的浅笑掠过她的唇边。她看了看自己手上——没有一枚戒指在闪光——便卖弄风情地把头一扬。『让那位先生自己替自己说话罢，』她说，『哪个男子挣不来这头衔，我便不把这称呼给他。』

「她的父亲笑了。在他眼里，有情人并不是什么可怕的事，只要那人是当得起的。而雅克琳自然不会挑一个配不上的人——一个雅法家的人、他的女儿！『那好，』他说，『我们就瞧瞧他能不能挣来这头衔罢；霍尔特这名字不算难听，波士顿这地方也不是什么寒酸的来处。』说罢不再多话，他们便匆匆出了屋子。可她脸上的光彩已全然熄灭了！这是什么意思呢？

===Original===
“At tea time I met the gentleman. He had evidently made his title good. I was not only favorably impressed with him but actually struck. Of all the high-bred, clear-eyed, polished and kindly gentlemen who had sat about the board since I first came into the family in Mrs. Japha’s lifetime, here was surely the finest, the handsomest and the best; and surprised in more ways than one, I was giving full play to my relief and exhilaration, when I caught sight of Jacqueline’s eye, and felt again the cold shudders of secret doubt and apprehension. Smile upon him as she would, coquet with him as she did, the flame and the glory that drew her like an inspiration to her feet when his name was announced, had fled, and left not a shadow behind. Had he failed in his expressions of devotion? Was he hard or cold or severe, under all that pleasant and charming manner? Had the hot soul of our motherless child rushed upon ice, and in the shock of the dreadful chill, fallen inert? No, his looks bespake no coldness; they dwelt upon Jacqueline’s lovely but inscrutable face, with honest fervor and boundless regard. He evidently loved her most passionately, but she—if it had not been for that first moment of unconscious betrayal, I should have decided that she cared for him no more than she did for the few others who had adored her, in the short space of her incomprehensible life.

===Chinese===
「喝茶的时候，我见到了那位先生。他显然已经把那头衔挣到手了。我对他的印象不仅是好而已，简直是被打动了。自打雅法夫人（Mrs. Japha）在世时我初入这个家以来，围在这张桌旁坐过的高贵、明眸、温文、和善的先生们也算得不少，可这一位无疑是其中最出色、最英俊、最上等的；我在不止一方面暗暗惊讶，正尽情地任自己宽心、欣慰，却一眼撞见了雅克琳的目光，于是又觉出了那阵暗暗怀疑、暗暗忧虑的冷颤。任她怎样对他微笑，任她怎样同他调笑，那像神启一般把她吸起来、叫她一听他名字便站起身的火焰与光彩，都已逃得无影无踪，连一丝痕迹也没留下。是他表达爱意时失了分寸？是他在那一副和悦迷人的风度之下，内里原是冷酷、严峻？是我们这无母的孩子那颗火热的心魂扑到了冰上，在那可怕的寒意里一撞，便委顿了？不，他的神色并无半分冷漠；他停留在雅克琳那张可爱却莫测的脸上，目光里满是恳切的炽情与无尽的顾惜。他显然是用了整副心魂在爱她，可她——若不是有方才那一瞬间的无心泄露，我定会断定：她对他的在意，并不比她在这短短一段叫人摸不透的生涯里，对那几个也曾倾慕过她的人多上分毫。

===Original===
“The mystery was not cleared up when she came to me that night with a short, ‘How do you like my lover, Margery?’ I was forty years her senior, but she always called me Margery.

“‘I think he is the finest, most agreeable man I ever met,’ said I. ‘Is he your lover, Jacqueline? Are you going to marry him?’

“She turned about from the vase which she was denuding of its flowers, and gave me one of her sphinx-like looks. ‘You must ask papa,’ said she. ‘He holds the destinies of the Japhas in his hand, does he not?’

===Chinese===
「当天夜里她来我房里，短短地问一句：『你觉得我的情人如何，玛乔丽（Margery）？』——这桩谜团仍未解开。我比她年长四十岁，可她一向管我叫玛乔丽。

「『我觉得他是我所见过的最出色、最和悦的男子，』我说，『他是你的情人吗，雅克琳？你要嫁给他吗？』

「她正把一只花瓶里的花一朵朵揪出来，听到这话便转过身，给了我一记斯芬克斯式的眼神。『你得去问爸爸，』她说，『雅法家人的命数都捏在他手里，不是吗？』

===Original===
“‘Does he?’ I involuntarily whispered to myself; following the steady poise of her head and the assured movements of her graceful form, with a glance of doubt, but loving her all the same, O loving her all and ever the same!

“‘Your father is not the man to cross you when the object of your affections is as worthy as this gentleman. He loved your mother too fondly.’

“‘He did?’ She had turned quick as a flash and was looking me straight in the eyes.

“‘I never saw such union!’ I exclaimed, vaguely remembering that her mother’s name had always seemed to have power to move her. ‘There was no parade of it before the world; but here at their own fireside, it was heart to heart and soul to soul. It was not love it was assimilation.’

===Chinese===
「『是吗？』我不自觉地低声自语；目光追随着她那稳稳昂着的头、她那婀娜身姿里从容笃定的动作，满眼狐疑，却依然爱她，唉，照样地、永远地爱她！

「『你所钟情之人既像这位先生这般配得上，你父亲便不是那种会横加阻挠的人。他当年太爱你的母亲了。』

「『是吗？』她像闪电一样转过身来，直勾勾地盯着我的眼睛。

「『我从未见过那样的契合！』我失声喊道，隐隐记起，她母亲的名字似乎一向有种打动她的力量。『在外人面前他们并不张扬；可是在自家炉火旁，那是心连心、魂连魂。那不是爱，那是合而为一。』

===Original===
“The young girl rose upon me like a flame; her very eyes seemed to dart fire; her lips looked like living coals; she was almost appalling in her terrible beauty and superhuman passion. ‘Not love!’ she exclaimed, her every word falling like a burning spark, ‘not love but assimilation! Yet do you suppose if I told my father that my soul had found its mate; my heart its other half; that this, *this* nature,’ here she struck her breast as she would a stone, ‘had at last found its master; that the wayward spirit of which you have sometimes been afraid, was become a part of another’s life, another’s soul, another’s hope, do you suppose he would listen? Hush!’ she cried, seeing me about to speak. ‘You talk of love, what do you know of it, what does he know of it, who saw his young wife die, yet himself consented to live? Is love a sitting by the fire with hand locked in hand while the winter winds rage and the droning kettle sings? Love is a going through the fire, a braving of the winter winds, a scattering of the soul in sparks that the night and the tempest lick up without putting out the germ of the eternal flame. Love!’ she half laughed; ‘O, it takes a soul that has never squandered its treasure upon every passing beggar, to know how to love! Do you see that star?’ It was night as I have said and we were standing near an open window. ‘It has lost its moorings and is falling; when it descries the ocean it will plunge into it; so with some natures, they soar high and keep their orbit well, till an invisible hand turns them from their course and they fall, to be swallowed up, aye swallowed up, lost and buried in the great sea that has awaited them so long.’

===Chinese===
「那少女像一团火焰般在我面前升起来；她那双眼睛简直要射出火来；她的双唇像烧红的炭；她那可怕的美、那超乎凡人的炽情，几乎叫人心惊胆战。『不是爱！』她叫道，每一个字都像一颗燃烧的火星砸下来，『不是爱，而是合而为一！可你以为，我若去告诉父亲：我的灵魂已寻见它的配偶；我的心已寻见它的另一半；这——*这*天性，』她说到这里，像捶一堵石墙一般捶着自己的胸口，『到底寻见了它的主人；那叫你有时害怕的任性魂灵，已成了另一个人的生命、另一个人的灵魂、另一个人的希望的一部分——你以为他会听得进去吗？嘘！』她见我要开口，便喊道，『你们开口闭口都是爱，你又懂得什么爱，他又懂得什么爱——他眼睁睁看着自己年轻的妻子死去，自己却还肯活着？难道爱便是冬风怒号、茶壶嗡嗡作响之时，两个人手牵着手坐在炉边吗？爱是投身烈火，是迎击冬风，是把灵魂化作漫天火星抛散，任那长夜与风暴将它舔噬——却扑不灭那永恒火苗的胚芽。爱！』她半笑了一声，『唉，得是一颗从未把自己的宝藏随手施舍给每一个过路乞丐的灵魂，才懂得怎样去爱！你瞧见那颗星吗？』其时已是夜里——如我方才所说——我们正站在一扇敞开的窗前。『它脱了锚，正在往下坠；等它望见大海，便会一头扎进去；有些人的天性也是如此，他们高飞入云，把自个儿的轨道守得好好的，直到一只看不见的手把他们拨离了航道，他们便坠落，被吞噬，唉，被吞噬，遗失、埋葬在那片等候了他们许久的大海里。』

===Original===
“‘And you love—like this—’ I murmured, quailing before the power of her passion.

“‘Would it not be strange if I did not,’ she asked in an altered voice. ‘You say he is everything noble, handsome and attractive.’

“‘Yes, yes,’ I murmured, ‘but—’

“She did not wait to hear what lay behind that but. Picking up her flowers, she hastily crossed the room. ‘Did my young mother shriek from joy, when my father’s horses ran away with them along that deadly precipice at the side of the Southmore road? To lie for a few maddening moments on the breast of the man you love, earth reeling beneath you, heaven swimming above you, and then with a cry of bliss to fall heart to heart, down the hideous gap of some awful gulf, and be dashed into eternity with the cry still on your lips, that is what I call love and that is what I—’

“She paused, turned upon me the whole splendor of her face, seemed to realize to what an extent her impetuosity had lifted the veil with which she usually shrouded her bitterly suppressed nature, and calming herself with a sudden quick movement, gave me a short mocking courtesy and left the room.

===Chinese===
『那么你是这样——去爱的——』我低声说，在她那炽情的力量面前瑟缩。

『我若不这样爱，岂不反倒奇怪，』她换了一种声调反问道，『你自己说他又高贵、又英俊、又迷人。』

『是，是，』我喃喃道，『可是——』

她不等听那『可是』背后的话。捡起她那些花，她匆匆穿过屋子。『当年我父亲那几匹马沿着绍斯莫尔路（Southmore road）旁那道要命的悬崖失控狂奔时，我那年轻的母亲可曾因狂喜而尖叫过？能倚在所爱之人的胸膛上，挨过那几阵令人发狂的片刻——脚下的大地在打旋，头顶的天在打转——然后随着一声狂喜的呼喊，心贴心地坠入某道可怕深渊那可怖的裂口，唇边尚衔着那一声呼喊便被摔进了永恒——这，才叫我爱；而这，也正是我——』

她顿住，把她整张脸的全部光彩转向我，似乎这才猛然察觉，方才那股急切已把那一向用来裹紧她苦苦压抑的天性的帷幕，掀开了多深；她一个急促的动作镇静下来，朝我草草一膝一屈，行了个嘲弄的礼，便出了屋子。

===Original===
“Do you wonder that for half the night I sat up brooding and alive to the faintest sounds!

“Next day Mr. Holt called again, and a couple of weeks after—long enough to enable Colonel Japha to make whatever inquiries he chose as to his claims as a gentleman of means and position—sent a formal entreaty for Jacqueline’s hand. I had never seen Colonel Japha more moved. His admiration for the young man was hearty and sincere. From a worldly point of view, as well as from all higher standpoints, the match was one of which he could be proud; and yet to speak the word that would separate from him the only creature that he loved, was hard as the cutting off an arm or the plucking out of an eye. ‘Do you think she loves him?’ asked he of me with a rare condescension of which he was not often guilty. ‘You are a woman and ought to understand her better than I. Do you think she loves him?’

===Chinese===
「你便不奇怪，我大半个夜里坐着沉思，连最细微的声响都醒着耳朵！

「第二天霍尔特先生又来访；过了两个礼拜——这段时日足够杰法上校随意去打听他想打听的一切，核实这位先生作为有身家有地位之人的资格——便正式来函，恳求雅克琳的婚事。我从未见过杰法上校如此动容。他对这年轻人的赞赏是发乎真心、实心实意的。无论从世俗之见来看，还是从一切更高的立场来看，这桩婚事都足以让他引以为傲；可真要说出那句话、从此便要与他这世上唯一所爱之人相离，却像砍去一条胳膊、剜去一只眼睛那样难。『你看她是爱他的吗？』他破天荒地屈尊问我，这种纡尊他是不大肯做的。『你是个女人，理应比我更懂得她。你看她是爱他的吗？』

===Original===
“After the words I had heard her speak, what could I reply but, ‘Yes, sir; she is of a reserved nature and controls her feelings in his presence, but she loves him for all that, with the intensest fervor and passion.’

“He repeated again, ‘You are a woman and you ought to know.’ And then called his daughter to him.

“I cannot tell what passed between them, but the upshot of it was, that the Colonel despatched an answer to the effect that the father’s consent would not be lacking, provided the daughter’s could be obtained. I learned this from Jacqueline herself who brought me the letter to post.

===Chinese===
「听过了我亲耳听她说的那些话，我除了这样答，还能怎样答呢：『是的，先生；她天性内向，在他面前收敛着自己的情意，可她到底还是爱他的，爱得最炽烈、最如火如荼。』

「他又重复了一遍：『你是个女人，你理应知道。』说罢便把他女儿叫到跟前。

「他们父女之间说了些什么，我不得而知；但结局是，上校回了一封信，大意说：做父亲的这头不会从中作梗，只看女儿那头肯不肯。这事我是从雅克琳嘴里听说的——那封信正是她拿来叫我寄的。

===Original===
“‘You see then, that your father understands,’ said I.

“Her rich red lip curled mockingly, but she did not reply.

“Naturally Mr. Holt answered to this communication in person. Jacqueline received him with a fitful coquetry that evidently puzzled him, for all the distinguishing charm which it added to a beauty apt to be too reserved and statue-like. She however took his ring which blazed on her finger like a drop of ice on congealed snow. ‘I am engaged,’ she murmured as she passed by my door, ‘and to a Holt!’ The words rang long in my ears; why?

===Chinese===
『你看，你父亲是明白的。』我说。

「她那饱满红润的嘴唇嘲弄地一撇，却没作声。

「霍尔特先生自然亲自来作答。雅克琳接待他时，带着一阵忽冷忽热的卖弄风情，显然把他弄得摸不着头脑——纵使这种种情态为她那原本未免过于矜持、近乎雕像的美，添上了别一种格外动人的风韵。可她到底还是接了他的戒指——那戒指在她手指上熠熠生辉，像一滴冰落在凝结的雪上。『我订婚了，』她路过我门口时低声道，『许的是一位霍尔特！』这话在我耳边久久回响；为什么呢？

===Original===
“She desired no congratulations; she permitted nothing to be said about her engagement, among the neighbors. She had even taken off her ring which I found lying loose in one of her bureau drawers. And no one dared to remonstrate, not even her father, punctillious as he was in all matters of social etiquette. The fact is, Jacqueline was not the same girl she had been before she gave her promise to Mr. Holt. From the moment he bade her goodbye, with the remark that he was going away to get a golden cage for his bride, she began to reveal a change. The cold reserve gave way to feverish expectancy. She trod these rooms as if there were burning steels in the floors, she looked from the windows as if they were prison bars; night and day she gazed from them yet she never went out. The letters she received from him were barely read and tossed aside; it was his coming for which she hungered. Her father noticed her restless and eager gaze, and frequently sighed. I felt her strange removed manner and secretly wept. ‘If he does not amply return this passion,’ thought I, ‘my darling will find her life a hell!’

“But he did return it; of that I felt sure. It was my only comfort.

===Chinese===
「她不要任何人道贺；她不准邻里间有人提起她的婚约半个字。她甚至连戒指都摘了下来——后来我在她五斗橱的一个抽屉里看见它松松地搁着。谁也不敢去劝她一句，连她父亲也不——尽管他向来在一切社交礼数上最是讲究。事实是，自打她对霍尔特先生许下诺言那一刻起，雅克琳便不再是原来那个姑娘了。从他向她道别、说自己这就去为新娘备一只金笼子的那一刻起，她身上便开始显出一种变化。那冷冷的矜持，让位给了发烧一般的焦盼。她在这些屋里走来走去，仿佛地板上铺着烧红的烙铁；她从这些窗户朝外望，仿佛那是些铁窗棂；她日日夜夜地从这些窗户凝神外望，却从不肯出门半步。她接到他的信，几乎看也不看便扔在一边；她如饥似渴等候着的，是他本人前来。她父亲留意到了她那焦灼急切的目光，时常叹息。我觉出她那种古怪的、心不在焉的神气，背地里偷偷落泪。『他若不把这番情意完完整整地还报回来，』我心想，『我这块心头肉，怕要把这一辈子过成一座地狱！』

「可他到底是还报了的；这一点我拿得稳。这是我唯一的安慰。

===Original===
“Suddenly one day the restlessness vanished. Her beauty burst like a flame from smoke; she trod like a spirit that hears invisible airs. I watched her with amazement till she said ‘Mr. Holt comes tonight,’ then I thought all was explained and went smiling about my work. She came down in the afternoon clad as I had never seen her before. She wore one of her Boston dresses and she looked superb in it. From the crown of her head to the sole of her foot, she dazzled like a moving picture; but she lacked one adornment; there was no ring on her finger. ‘Jacqueline!’ cried I, ‘you have forgotten something.’ And I pointed towards her hand.

“She glanced at it, blushed a trifle as I thought, and pulled it out of her pocket. ‘I have it,’ said she, ‘but it is too large,’ and she thrust it carelessly back.

===Chinese===
「忽然有那么一天，那股焦躁消失了。她的美像火焰从烟雾里蹿出来一般迸发而出；她走路的样子，像一个听见了人所听不见的天籁的精灵。我惊讶地瞧着她，直到她说出一句『霍尔特先生今夜到』，我才恍然以为一切都明白了，便含笑去做自己的活计。下午她下楼来，打扮得我前所未见。她穿着一件波士顿带回来的衣裙，穿在身上真是华美之至。从头顶到脚底，她像一幅会移动的画那样耀眼夺目；可她少了一样装饰——她手指上没有戒指。『雅克琳！』我叫道，『你忘了什么东西。』我便朝她的手一指。

「她瞥了一眼那手，依我看来微微红了一红，便从口袋里把戒指掏了出来。『带着呢，』她说，『就是太大了。』说着便漫不经心地把它又塞了回去。

===Original===
“At three o’clock the train came in. Then I saw her eye flash and her lip burn. In a few minutes later two gentlemen appeared at the gate.

“‘Mr. Holt and his brother!’ were the words I heard whispered through the house. But I did not need that announcement to understand Jacqueline at last.”

===Chinese===
「三点钟，火车进站了。那时我便看见她眼里一亮、唇上一热。过了几分钟，两位先生出现在院门口。

「『霍尔特先生同他的兄弟！』——这是我听见整座宅子里此起彼伏的低语。可我并不需要这道通报，才终于在那一刻读懂了雅克琳。」

## Book II Life and Death / 卷二 生与死

## XIV Miss Belinda Has a Question to Decide / 十四 贝琳达小姐有一桩问题要决断

===Original===
> "I pray you in your letters,

 Speak of me as I am; nothing extenuate,

 Nor set down aught in malice."

===Chinese===
> 「我求你在你的信里，

 如实谈论我；不要有所粉饰，

 也不要怀着恶意记下任何事。」

===Original===
Miss Belinda sitting before her bedroom fire on a certain windy night in January, presented a picture of the most profound thought. A year had elapsed since, with heavy heart and moistened eye, she had bidden goodbye to the child of her care, and beheld her drift away with her new friend into a strange and untried life. And now a letter had come from that friend, in which with the truest appreciation for the feelings of herself and sister, he requested their final permission to adopt Paula as his own child and the future occupant of his house and heart.

===Chinese===
一月里一个风声呼啸的夜晚，贝琳达小姐坐在卧室的炉火前，呈现出一副陷入最深沉思索的模样。距她怀着沉重的心情、含着湿润的双眼，向自己一手照料的那个孩子道别，看着她随她的新朋友漂向一种陌生而未经尝试的生活，已过去了一年。如今那位朋友来了一封信，信中以对她和姐姐的心意最为周到的体谅，请求她们最终允准他将宝拉（Paula）收为亲生女儿，使之日后成为他宅邸与心田的女主人。

===Original===
Yes, after a year of increased comfort, Mrs. Sylvester, who would never have consented to receive as her own any child demanding care or attention, had decided it was quite a different matter to give place and position to a lovely girl already grown, whose beauty was sufficiently pronounced to do credit to the family while at the same time it was of a character to heighten by contrast her own very manifest attractions. So the letter, destined to create such a disturbance in the stern and powerful mind of Miss Belinda, had been written and dispatched.

===Chinese===
是的，在愈发宽裕地过了一年之后，西尔维斯特夫人——她本绝不肯把任何一个需要照料、需要费心的孩子当作自己的来接纳——已认定，把地位与身份让给一位已经长成的可爱姑娘，情形便截然不同了；那姑娘的美貌已足够出众，足以为这个家族增光，同时又恰好能与她自己那一身颇为显眼的魅力相映衬、愈发凸显。于是，那封注定要在贝琳达小姐刚毅而有力的心头搅起这般波澜的信，就这样写就、寄出了。

===Original===
And indeed it was matter for the gravest reflection. To accede to this important request was to yield up all control over the dear young girl whose affection had constituted the brightness of this somewhat disappointed life, while to refuse an offer made with such evident love and anxiety, was to bring a pang of regret to a heart she hesitated to wound. The question of advantage which might have swayed others in their decision, did not in the least affect Miss Belinda. Now that Paula had seen the world and gained an insight into certain studies beyond the reach of her own attainments, any wishes in which she might have indulged on that score were satisfied, and mere wealth with its concomitant of luxuriant living, she regarded with distrust, and rather in the light of a stumbling-block to the great and grand end of all existence.

===Chinese===
这的确是件最该郑重思量的事。应下这桩重要的请求，便是放弃对那位亲爱少女的一切掌控——正是她的爱，构成了这略带失意的一生的光彩；而拒绝一份怀着如此明显的爱与焦灼而提出的好意，又会给一颗她不忍伤害的心带来悔恨的刺痛。那些本可左右旁人决断的利益之念，对贝琳达小姐却毫无影响。宝拉既已见过世面，又在若干远非她贝琳达所能传授的学问上开了眼界，那么她在这上头本可抱有的任何心愿也都满足了；至于单凭财富及其带来的奢靡生活，她素来心存戒备，倒更愿把它看作横亘在一切生存之崇高终极目标前的一块绊脚石。

===Original===
Suddenly with that energy which characterized all her movements, she rose from her seat, and first casting a look of somewhat cautious inquiry at the recumbent figure of her sister, asleep in the heavy old fashioned bed that occupied one corner of the room, she proceeded to a bureau drawer and took out a small box which she unlocked on the table. It was full of letters; those same honest epistles, which, as empowered by Mr. Sylvester, she had requested Paula to send her from week to week. Some of them were a year old, but she read them all carefully through, while the clock ticked on the shelf and the wind soughed in the chimney. Certain passages she marked, and when she had finished the pile, she took up the letters again and reread those passages. They were necessarily desultory in their character, but they all had, in her mind at least, a bearing upon the question on hand, and as such, I give them to my readers.

===Chinese===
忽然，带着她一举一动中所特有的那股果决，她从座上站起，先朝卧在房间一隅那张笨重的老式床上熟睡的姐姐的身影，投去一道颇为审慎探询的目光，随即便走向五斗橱的抽屉，取出一个小匣子，在桌上开了锁。匣中满满都是信；正是那些坦率的信札——西尔维斯特先生授意之下，她曾请宝拉每周寄给她的那些。有些已是一年前的旧物了，她却仍把它们一封封细细读完，任由座钟在架上滴答作响、风在烟囱里呜咽。读到某些段落她便做上记号；待整堆读完，她又把那些信重新拿起，将做过记号的段落再读一遍。这些段落其性质难免显得零散，但至少在她心中，无一不与手头这桩问题有所牵连；我且把它们原样呈给我的读者。

===Original===
"O aunty, I have made a friend, a sweet girl friend who I have reason to hope will henceforth be to me as my other eye and hand. Her name is Stuyvesant—a name by the way that always calls up a certain complacent smile on Cousin Ona's countenance—and she is the daughter of one of the directors of Mr. Sylvester's bank. I met her in a rather curious way. For some reason Ona had expressed a wish for me to ride horseback. She is rather too large for the exercise herself, but thought it looked well, she said, to see a lady and groom ride from the front of the house; moreover it would keep me in color by establishing my health. So Mr. Sylvester who denies her nothing, promised us horses and the groom, and as a preparation for acquitting myself with credit, has sent me to one of the finest riding academies in the city. It was here I met Miss Stuyvesant. She is a small interesting-looking girl whose chief beauty lies in her expression which is certainly very charming. I was conscious of a calm and satisfied feeling the moment I saw her. Her eyes which are raised with a certain appeal to your face, are blue, while her lips that break into smiles only at rare moments, are rosy and delicately curved. In her riding-habit she looks like a child, but when dressed for the street she surprises you with the reserved and womanly air with which she carries her proud head. Altogether she is a sweet study to me, alluring me with her glance yet awing me by her dainty ladyhood, a ladyhood too unconscious to be affected and yet so completely a part of her whole delicate being, that you could as soon dissociate the bloom from the rose, as the air of highborn reserve, from this sweet scion of one of New York's oldest families.

===Chinese===
「噢，姨母，我交到了一位朋友，一位甜美的女友，我有理由盼着她从此于我便如我的另一只眼、另一只手。她姓斯泰弗森特（Stuyvesant）——说来也怪，这个名字每每在奥娜（Ona）表姐脸上勾起一抹自得似的微笑——她是西尔维斯特先生那家银行的一位董事的女儿。我和她相识颇有点离奇。不知何故，奥娜表露过想让我骑马的心愿。她自己身形略嫌丰腴，不便从事这项运动，却说有位太太带着马夫从宅子正门出发骑马，看着很是体面；再说这也能让我身体康健、面上添些血色。于是对她百依百顺的西尔维斯特先生，便应承下马匹和马夫；而为了让我能体面地应付下来，又把我送进了城里一家最上乘的骑术学堂。正是在这里，我遇见了斯泰弗森特小姐。她是个身量娇小、模样耐看的姑娘，最美的乃是她那神情，那神情实在迷人得很。一见她，我便觉出一种平静而满足的心绪。她那双眼睛带着几分祈求之意抬向你，是蓝色的；她那双难得才绽出笑意的唇，则嫣红而曲线纤秀。身着骑装时她像个孩子，可一旦换上出门的装束，她那端庄成熟的女子气度、她那高高昂起的头颅，便会叫你吃上一惊。总而言之，于我她是一道甜美的研习之题，她的目光引诱着我，她那娇贵的大家闺秀之气又叫我心生敬畏——这闺秀之气天然得毫无做作之态，却又与她整个纤秀的人那样浑然一体，正如你无法将那一层粉光从玫瑰上剥离，你也无法将这一种生而高贵、矜持自持的气度，从这纽约最古老世家之一的一位甜美后裔身上剥离。

===Original===
"I was mounting my horse when our eyes first met, and I never shall forget her look of delighted surprise. Did she recognize in me the friend I now hope to become? Later we were introduced by Mr. Sylvester who had been so kind as to accompany me that day. The way in which he said to her, 'This is Paula,' proved that I was no new topic of conversation between them, and indeed she afterwards explained to me that she had been forewarned of my arrival during an afternoon call at his house. There was in this first interview none of the unnecessary gush which you have so often reprobated as childish; indeed Miss Stuyvesant is not a person with whom one would presume to be familiar, nor was it till we had met several times that any acknowledgement was made of the mutual interest with which we found ourselves inspired. Cousin Ona to whom I had naturally spoken of the little lady, wished me to cultivate her acquaintance more assiduously, but I knew that if I had excited in her the same interest she had awakened in me, this would not be necessary; our friendship would grow of itself and blossom without any hothouse forcing. And so it did. One day she came to the riding-school with her eyes like stars and her cheeks like the oleanders in your sitting-room. Her brightness was so contagious, I stepped up to her. But she greeted me with almost formal reserve, and mounting her horse, proceeded to engage in her usual exercise. I was not hurt; I recognized the presence of some thought or feeling which made a barrier around her sensitive nature, and duly respected it. Mounting my own horse, I rode around the ring which is the somewhat limited field of my present equestrian efforts, and waited. For I knew from the looks which she cast me every now and then, that the flower of our friendship was outgrowing its sheath and would soon burst into the bud of perfect understanding. At the end of the lesson we approached each other. I do not know how it was done, but we walked home together, or rather I accompanied her to the stoop of her house, and before we parted we had exchanged those words which give emphasis to a sentiment long cherished but now for the first time avowed. Miss Stuyvesant and I are friends, and I feel as though a new stream of enjoyment had opened in my breast.

===Chinese===
「我俩的目光初次相遇时，我正要上马，我永远忘不了她那一脸又惊又喜的神情。她可是从我身上认出了我现在盼望成为的那位朋友吗？后来，承蒙那天好意陪我同行的西尔维斯特先生，把我们作了介绍。他对她说『这位是宝拉』时的那种语气，便证明我在他俩之间早已不是个新鲜的话题了；她也确实事后向我解释过，说是某日下午去他家拜访时，已预先得知我要到来的消息。这头一次见面，丝毫没有那种你不止一次斥为稚气的、多余的狂热；斯泰弗森特小姐本就不是那种可以贸然亲近的人，直到我们见过好几面之后，彼此才有所表示，承认我们心中互生的那份兴致。我自然向奥娜表姐提起过这位小女子，她盼着我更勤地去结交她；可我明白，倘若我在她心里激起了与她在我的心里所激起的相同的兴致，这一切便大可不必；我们的友谊自会自行生长、自行绽放，无须任何温室里的催逼。果然如此。有一日她来到骑术学堂，双目如星，双颊像你起居室里的夹竹桃。她那明媚那样地感染人，我便走向她。可她却以近乎正式的矜持招呼了我，随即上马，照常练她的功课。我并不伤心；我辨得出有某种心绪或情愫在她敏感的天性周遭筑起了一道屏障，便恰如其分地予以尊重。我也上了自己的马，绕着那个圈场——那是我眼下骑术施展的颇为有限的天地——缓缓而行，静候着。因为我从她不时投来的目光里便知道，我们友谊的那朵花已长得冲出了花萼，很快便要结成完满默契的花蕾。课程结束时，我们彼此走近。我不知道那是怎样发生的，可我们竟一同走回了家，或者说我陪她走到了她家门前台阶，临别之前，我们交换了那几句使一份久已珍藏在心、而今头一回吐露出来的情意得以分明的话。斯泰弗森特小姐和我成了朋友，我只觉得胸中仿佛新开了一道欢愉的溪流。

===Original===
"The fact that I still call her by this formal title instead of her very pretty name of Cicely, proves the nature of the respect she inspires even in the breasts of her girlish associates."

===Chinese===
「我至今仍以这正式的称谓称呼她，而不用她那个十分动听的名字西塞莉（Cicely），便足见她所唤起的那份敬意，连她那些少女同伴也未能例外。」

===Original===
"Why is it that I frequently hesitate as I go up the stairs and look about me with a vague feeling of apprehension? The bronze figure of Luxury that adorns the landing, wears no semblance of terror to the wildest imagination, and yet I often find myself seized by an inexplicable shudder as I hurry past it; and once I actually looked behind me with the same sensation as if someone had plucked me by the sleeve.

"It is a folly; for recording which, I make my excuses."

===Chinese===
「为何我上楼时常常踌躇，还带着一种说不出的惴惴不安四下张望？装点着楼梯转角的那尊『奢华』铜像，任凭最天马行空的想象也看不出一丝骇人之处，可我每每匆匆从它身边经过，却常被一阵无从解释的战栗攫住；有一次我竟真真切切地回头望了一眼，那种感觉，就仿佛有人扯了扯我的衣袖。

「这自然是痴念；记下这等痴事，谨此告罪。」

===Original===
"Cousin Ona has decided that I must never wear colors. 'Soft grays, my dear, dead blacks and opaque whites are all that you need to bring out the fine contrast of your hair and complexion; the least hint of blue or pink would destroy it.' So she says and so I must believe, for who else has made such a study of the all important subject of dress. Behold me, then, arrayed for my first reception in a colorless robe of rich silk to which Ona after long consideration allowed me to add some ornaments of plain gold with which Mr. Sylvester has kindly presented me. But I think more of the people I am going to meet than of anything else, though I enjoy the home-feeling which a pretty dress gives me, as well as a violet does its bright blue coat."

===Chinese===
「奥娜表姐已断定我永远不可穿带颜色的衣裳。『柔和的灰色，亲爱的，死沉的黑和不透光的白，这就尽够衬出你发色与肤色之间那精妙的对比了；哪怕一丝蓝、一丝粉都会毁了它。』她这样说，我也只得这样信，因为除了她，还有谁在衣着这门头等重要的事上做过这般钻研。那么，请看我为了头一次出席招待会的一身装扮吧：一袭素色的华绸长裙，奥娜表姐斟酌良久之后，才允我在其上加几件素金的饰物——那是西尔维斯特先生好意送我的。可我更惦记的，乃是我将要遇见的那些人，尽管我也享受一袭漂亮衣裙带给我的那种居家之感，一如一朵紫罗兰享受它那件鲜亮的蓝外套。」

===Original===
"I have heard a great preacher! What shall I say? At first it seems as if nothing could express my joy and satisfaction. The sapling that is shaken to its root by the winds of heaven, keeps silence I imagine. But O Aunty, if my smallness makes me quake, it also makes me feel. What gates of thought have been opened to me! What shining tracks of inquiry pointed out! I feel as if I had been shown a path where angels walked. Can it be that such words have been uttered every week of my life and I in ignorance of them? It is like the revelation of the ocean to unaccustomed eyes. Henceforth small things must seem like pebble stones above which stretch innumerable heavenly vistas. It is not so much that new things have been revealed to me as that old things have been made strangely eloquent. The voice of a daisy on the hill side, the breath of thunder in the mountain gorges, the blossoming of a child's smile under its mother's eye, the fact that golden portals are opened in every life for the coming and going of the messengers of God, all have been made real to me, real as the voice of the Saviour to his disciples as they walked in the fields or started back awestricken from the stupendous vision of the cross. It is a solemn thing to see one's humble thoughts caught by the imagination of a great mind and carried on and up into regions you never realized existed.

===Chinese===
「我听了一位了不起的布道者！我该说什么呢？起先似乎没有任何言辞能表达我的欣喜与满足。一株被天风撼到根上的幼苗，我想，是默然无声的。可是噢，姨母，倘若我的渺小令我战栗，它也令我有所感。有多少思想之门向我敞开了！有多少发人深省的闪亮路径向我指出了！我只觉得自己仿佛被领到了一条天使曾走过的小径上。难道这样的言语我生命中的每个礼拜都在被人宣讲，而我竟一无所知吗？这正如初见的眼目头一回望见大海。从此之后，渺小之物在我眼中必将不过像一颗颗卵石，而卵石之上延展着无数的天国之景。与其说是新的事物向我显露了，不如说是旧的事物变得奇异地能言善辩。山坡上一朵雏菊的声音，山间峡谷里雷的呼吸，孩子微笑在母亲眼皮底下绽放的那一瞬，每一个生命都为着上帝使者的来往而敞开金门这一桩事实——这一切于我都变得真切了，真切得一如救主对门徒说话的声音，真切得一如他们行走田野时所闻、又如他们从那十字架的赫赫异象前敬畏倒退时所闻。一个人谦卑的思绪被一颗伟大心灵的想象力所捕捉，被一路托举、一路引向你从未意识到其存在的境域，这是一桩庄严的事。

===Original===
"I was so burdened with joy that I could not forbear asking Mr. Sylvester if he did not feel as if the whole face of the world had changed since we entered those holy doors. He did not respond with the glad 'Yes' for which I hoped, and though his smile was very kind, I could not help wondering what it was that sometimes fell between us like a veil."

===Chinese===
「我被这份欢欣压得那样满，忍不住问西尔维斯特先生，自从我们踏进那扇圣洁的门之后，他是否也觉得仿佛这世界的整个面貌都变了。他并没有用我所盼望的那一声欣然的『是的』来回答我；尽管他笑得很是和蔼，我却不禁暗暗纳闷，有时落在我们之间、像一层轻纱一般隔开我们的，究竟是什么。」

===Original===
"O Aunty, how my heart does yearn towards Mr. Sylvester at times! As I see him sitting with clouded brow in the midst of so much that ought to charm and enliven him, I ask myself if the advantages of wealth compensate for all this care and anxiety. But I notice he is much more cheerful now than when I first came. Ona says he is in danger of losing the air of melancholy reserve which made him look so distinguished, but I think we can spare a little of such doubtful distinguishment for the sake of the smiles with which he now and then indulges us."

===Chinese===
「噢，姨母，我的心有时是那样地眷恋着西尔维斯特先生！每见他在本该令他欣悦、令他振奋的种种美好之中，眉头深锁地坐着，我便暗自追问，财富带来的种种好处，是否当真抵得过这般忧烦焦虑。可我也看出，他比我初来时快活多了。奥娜表姐说他大有失去那股忧郁矜持之气的危险——正是那股气让他看上去那般卓尔不群；可我想，为了他偶尔赏给我们的那几个微笑，我们大可少要一点这等可疑的卓然之气。」

===Original===
"I feel as if a hand had gripped my throat. Cousin Ona spoke to Mr. Sylvester this morning in a way that made my very heart stand still. And yet it was only a simple, 'Follow your own judgment, Mr. Sylvester.' But how she said it! Do these languid women carry venom in their tongues? I had always thought she was of too easy a disposition to feel anger or display it; but the spring of a serpent is all the deadlier for his long silent basking in the sun. O pardon me for making such a frightful allusion. But if you had seen her and heard Mr. Sylvester's sigh as he turned and left the room!"

===Chinese===
「我只觉得仿佛有一只手攥住了我的喉咙。今晨奥娜表姐对西尔维斯特先生说话的语气，叫我的心几乎都停了。可那其实不过是一句平平淡淡的：『西尔维斯特先生，您自个儿拿主意便是。』可她说这话的那个腔调！这些慵懒的女人，舌头上莫非带着毒？我向来以为她的性子散淡，不会动怒，也不会流露出来；可一条蛇长久地、无声地在太阳底下晒着，它那一扑反愈发致命。噢，原谅我做了这样一个骇人的比方。可您若见过她那副神色，听过西尔维斯特先生转身离去的那一声叹息！」

===Original===
"Mr. Bertram Sylvester has awakened my deepest interest. His uncle has told me his story, which alone of all the things I have heard in this house, I do not feel at liberty to repeat, and it has aroused in me strange thoughts and very peculiar emotions. He is devoted to someone we do not know, and the idea surrounds him in my eyes with a sort of halo that you would perhaps call fanciful, but which I am nevertheless bound to reverence. He does not know that I am acquainted with his story. I wish he did and would let me speak the words that rise to my lips whenever I see him or hear him play."

===Chinese===
「伯特兰·西尔维斯特先生（Mr. Bertram Sylvester）唤起了我最深的关切。他的叔父把他的故事告诉了我，这故事是我在这宅子里所听见的种种之中，唯一不便转述的一桩；它在我心里唤起了奇怪的心绪和十分特别的感情。他心有所属，钟情的乃是一个我们不认识的人，这一个念头在我眼中为他笼上了一圈光晕——您也许会称之为想入非非，可我仍不能不对此心怀敬意。他并不晓得我已得知他的故事。我但愿他晓得，但愿他能容我把那些话——那些每每见到他、或听见他弹琴时便涌到我唇边的话——说出口。」

===Original===
"There are moments when I long to flee back to Grotewell. It is when Cousin Ona comes in from shopping with a dozen packages to be opened and commented upon, or when Mrs. Fitzgerald has been here or some other of her ultra-fashionable acquaintances. The atmosphere of the house for hours after either of the above occurrences is too heavy for breathing. I have to go away and clear my brain by a brisk walk or a look into Knœdler's or Schaus'."

===Chinese===
「有些时刻我恨不得逃回格罗特韦尔（Grotewell）去。那便是奥娜表姐买了大包小包进门、要一件件拆开品评的时候；或是菲茨杰拉德夫人（Mrs. Fitzgerald）来过、或她那班极时髦的友人中某一位来过的时候。上述任一事发生后，这宅子里的空气一连几个钟头都沉重得叫人难以呼吸。我只好躲出去，借一阵疾行，或者去克诺德勒（Knoedler）画廊、绍斯（Schaus）画廊里看一看，好清醒清醒脑子。」

===Original===
"The panel where Cousin Ona's picture used to hang, has been filled by one of Meissonier's most interesting studies; and though I never thought Mr. Sylvester particularly fond of the French style of art, he seems very well satisfied with the result. I cannot understand how Cousin Ona can regard the misfortune to her portrait so calmly. I think it would break my heart to see a husband look with complacency on any picture, no matter how exquisite, that took the place of my own, especially if like hers, it was painted in my bridal days. I sometimes wonder if those days are as sacred to the memory of husband and wife as I have always imagined them to be."

===Chinese===
「原本挂着奥娜表姐画像的那块画板，如今被一幅梅索尼埃（Meissonier）最有趣味的研究之作填上了；虽说西尔维斯特先生从前在我眼里并算不得特别钟爱法兰西画风，这一回他似乎对这结果十分满意。我真不懂奥娜表姐怎能对自己画像的不幸遭际这般安之若素。我想，倘若一个丈夫能心平气和地对着任何一幅取代了我的画像端详——无论那画何等精妙，尤其若是像我这样、画于新婚之日的画像——我的心一定都要碎了。我有时不禁怀疑，那些日子在夫妻两人的记忆里，是否当真如我一直所以为的那般神圣。」

===Original===
"Why does Cousin Ona never speak of Grotewell, and why, if by chance I mention the name, does she drop her eyes and a shadow cross the countenance of Mr. Sylvester?"

===Chinese===
「为何奥娜表姐从不提起格罗特韦尔？为何我若无意间提到这名字，她便会垂下眼帘，而一片阴霾便会掠过西尔维斯特先生的脸？」

===Original===
"There is a word Mr. Sylvester uses in the most curious way; it is *fuss*. He calls everything a fuss that while insignificant in size or character has power either to irritate or please. A fly is a fuss; so is a dimple in a girl's cheek or a figure that goes wrong in accounts. I have even heard him call a child, 'That dear little fuss.' Bertram unconsciously imitates his uncle in this peculiar mannerism and is often heard alluding to this or that as a *fuss of fusses*. Indeed they say this use of the word is a peculiarity of the Sylvester family."

===Chinese===
「有个词西尔维斯特先生用得奇巧得很，那便是 *fuss*（小折腾）。但凡一件东西，个头虽小、性质虽轻，却或能惹恼人、或能讨人欢心，他一概称之为一个 fuss。一只苍蝇是一个 fuss；姑娘颊上的一个酒涡是一个 fuss；账上一笔对不上的数也是一个 fuss。我甚至听他把一个孩子唤作『那个可爱的小 fuss』。伯特兰在这一古怪的习癖上不自觉地学他叔父，常听见他把这啦那啦地说成 *fuss of fusses*（折腾里的折腾）。据说他们西尔维斯特家把这个词这样用法，乃是这一族特有的做派。」

===Original===
"I think from the way Mr. Sylvester spoke yesterday, that he must have experienced some dreadful trouble in his life. We were walking in the wards of a hospital—that is, Miss Stuyvesant, Mr. Sylvester and myself—when someone near us gave utterance to the trite expression, 'O it will heal, but the scar will always remain.' 'That is a common saying,' remarked Mr. Sylvester, 'but how true a one no one realizes but he who carries the scar.'"

===Chinese===
「从西尔维斯特先生昨日说话的口气，我想他这一生中一定经历过某种可怕的苦楚。当时我们——也就是斯泰弗森特小姐、西尔维斯特先生和我——正在一家医院的病房里走着，身旁有人顺口说了那句老话：『噢，会好的，只是那道疤要留一辈子。』『这是一句常言，』西尔维斯特先生说道，『可除了那带着伤疤的人，没人知道这话有多真。』」

===Original===
"It may be imagination or simply the effect of increased appreciation on my part, but it does seem as if Miss Stuyvesant grew lovelier and more companionable each time that I meet her. She makes me think of a temple in which a holy lamp is burning. Her very silences are eloquent, and yet she is never distraite but always cheerful and frequently the brightest of the company. But it is a brightness without glitter, a gentle lustre that delights you but never astonishes. I meet many sweet girls in the so-called heartless circles of society, but none like her. She is my white lily on which a moonbeam rests."

===Chinese===
「这也许是我想当然，或者只是我愈来愈懂得欣赏的缘故，可斯泰弗森特小姐似乎每次相见都愈发可爱、愈发可亲。她让我想到一座燃着一盏圣灯的庙宇。她那沉默本身就能言善辩，可她从不走神，总是开开朗朗的，常常还是一席人里最明亮的一位。但她那是一种不刺眼的明亮，一缕柔和的光华，使你欢欣，却从不叫你惊异。在所谓冷酷无情的社交圈子里，我遇见过不少甜美的姑娘，却没有一个像她。她是我那一朵月华流照的白百合。」

===Original===
"This house contains a mystery, as Ona is pleased to designate the room at the top of the house to which Mr. Sylvester withdraws when he desires to be alone. And indeed it is a sort of Bluebeard's chamber, in that he keeps it rigidly under lock and key, allowing no one to enter it, not even his wife. The servants declare that no one but himself has ever crossed its threshold, but I can scarcely believe that. Ona has not, but there must surely be some trusty person to whom he allots the care of its furniture. Am I only proving myself to be a true member of my sex when I allow that I cannot hinder my own curiosity from hovering about a spot so religiously guarded? Yet what should we see if its doors were thrown open? A study surrounded with books it displeases him to see misplaced, or a luxurious apartment fitted with every appointment necessary to rest and comfort him when he comes home tired from business."

===Chinese===
「这座宅子里藏着一桩秘密——奥娜表姐便是如此戏称屋子顶层那间房的，每逢西尔维斯特先生想独处，便退到那里去。那确也堪称一间蓝胡子（Bluebeard）的密室，因为他把它严严实实地锁着，不让任何人进去，连他的妻子也不例外。仆人们都说除了他本人，再没人迈过那道门槛，可我实在难以置信。奥娜表姐不曾进去过，可那儿总该有某个他信得过的人，由他分派去照管那房里的陈设吧？当我说到自己按捺不住那份好奇、不住在那般被虔诚守护的所在周围打转时，是不是只不过证明了我乃是我们这个性别里一名再地道不过的成员？可那扇门若真敞开了，我们又能看见什么呢？一间被书围簇、他不乐见一册放错位置的书房？或是一间陈设考究、应有尽有、好让他在外办事归来疲倦时得以歇息的奢华屋子？」

===Original===
"I never saw Mr. Sylvester angry till today. By some inadvertence he went downtown without locking the door of his private room, and though he returned immediately upon missing the key from his pocket, he was barely in time to prevent Cousin Ona from invading the spot he has always kept so sacred from intrusion. I was not present and of course did not hear what was said, but I caught a glimpse of his face as he left the house, and found it quite sufficient to assure me of his dissatisfaction. As for Ona, she declares he pulled her back as if she had been daring the plague. 'I do not expect to find five beautiful wives hanging up there by their necks,' concluded she with a forced laugh, 'but I shall yet see the interior of that room, if only to establish my prerogative as the mistress of this house.'

"I do not now feel as if I wished to see it."

===Chinese===
「直到今日我才头一次见西尔维斯特先生动怒。他一时疏忽，没锁好自己那间私室的门便去了下城；待到他从兜里摸不着钥匙、立刻折回，也险些来不及阻止奥娜表姐闯进那处他向来视若禁地、不容惊扰的所在。当时我不在场，自然也未听见说了些什么，可他离宅时我瞥见了一眼他的脸色，仅这一眼便足以向我证明他的不快。至于奥娜表姐，她说他把她一把拽了回去，那架势就当她要去招惹瘟疫似的。『我也不指望在那上头看见五位美艳的太太吊着脖子挂成一排，』她勉强地一笑作结，『可我迟早要看一看那间屋子的里头，哪怕只是为了立一立我作为这宅子女主人的规矩。』

「可如今，我倒不觉得自己还想看它了。」

===Original===
"There is one thing that strikes me as peculiar in Miss Stuyvesant, and that is, that as much pleasure as she seems to take in my society when we meet, she never comes to see me in Mr. Sylvester's house. For a long time I wondered over this but said nothing, but one day upon receiving a second invitation to visit her, I mentioned the fact as delicately as I could, and was quite distressed to observe how seriously she took the rebuke, if rebuke it could be called. 'I cannot explain myself,' she murmured in some embarrassment; 'but Mr. Sylvester's house is closed against me. You must not ask me to seek you there or expect me to do myself the pleasure of attending Mrs. Sylvester's receptions. I cannot. Is that enough for me to say to my dearest friend?' I hardly knew what to reply, but finally ventured to inquire if she was restrained by any fact that would make it undignified in me to seek her society and enjoy the pleasures she is continually offering me. And she answered with such a cheerful negative I was quite reassured. And so the matter is settled. Our friendship is to be emancipated from the bonds of etiquette and I am to enjoy her company whenever I can. Tomorrow we are going to take our first ride in the park. The horses have been bought, and much to Cousin Ona's satisfaction, the groom has been hired."

===Chinese===
「有一件事在我看来颇为古怪，那是关于斯泰弗森特小姐的：尽管我们相见时她似乎格外乐于与我作伴，她却从不踏进西尔维斯特先生的家来看我。许久以来我都暗暗纳罕，却什么也没说；直到有一日，在第二次接到她邀我相访的请柬之后，我方才把这事尽可能委婉地提了出来；见她竟把这话——倘若这也算得上责备的话——看得那样重，我着实难过。『我没法把话说明白，』她颇为窘迫地低声道；『只是西尔维斯特先生的家对我关着门。您不可约我到那里找您，也不可指望我赏光出席西尔维斯特夫人（Mrs. Sylvester）的招待会。我做不到。这话，对我最最要好的朋友说，可算够了么？』我几乎不知如何作答，末了才大着胆子问她：将她绊住的，是不是某一桩会使我去结交她、去领受她不断殷勤相待的种种乐趣有失我身份的事实？她那样欣然地予以否认，我也就放了心。于是这事便就此定下。我们的友谊将摆脱礼数的羁绊，我只在能够之时便去与她为伴。明日我们就要头一遭在公园里骑一回马了。马已经买下，最令奥娜表姐满意的是，马夫也已雇下了。」

===Original===
"I was told something the other day, of a nature so unpleasant that I should not think of repeating it, if you had not expressly commanded me to confide to you everything that for any reason produced an effect upon me in my new home. My informant was Sarah, the somewhat gossiping woman whom Ona has about her as seamstress and maid. She said—and she had spoken before I could prevent her—that the way Mrs. Sylvester took on about her mourning at the time of little Geraldine's death was enough to wear out the patience of Job. She even went so far as to tell the dressmaker that if she could not have her dress made to suit her she would not put on mourning at all! Aunty, can you wonder that Mr. Sylvester looks so bitterly sombre whenever mention is made of his child? He loved it, and its own mother could worry over the fit of a dress while his bereaved heart was breaking! I confess I can never feel the same indulgence towards what I considered the idiosyncrasies of a fashionable beauty again. Her smooth white skin makes me tremble; it has never flushed with delight over the innocent smiles of her firstborn."

===Chinese===
「前几日有人对我讲了一桩事，性质甚是不堪，若非您曾明明白白地吩咐过我，凡在这新家之中因任何缘故对我有所触动的事，都要向您和盘托出，我原是不想转述的。讲给我听的，是萨拉（Sarah）——奥娜表姐跟前那位颇爱嚼舌的缝纫兼贴身女仆。她说——话已出口，我拦也拦不及——小杰拉尔丁（Geraldine）夭折之时，西尔维斯特夫人为自己那身丧服闹的那一场，足能把约伯（Job）那般的耐性都磨光。她甚至对裁缝说，若是她那身衣裳做的不称她的心，她索性不穿丧服！姨母，您还怪西尔维斯特先生每每一提到他的孩子便面容那样悲苦阴沉吗？他是爱那孩子的，而那孩子的亲生母亲，竟在他那颗丧亲的心正在破碎之时，为一件衣裳合不合身而犯愁！我承认，我再也不能像从前那样，宽容地看待我所谓的时髦美人的种种怪癖了。她那光洁白皙的皮肤叫我战栗；那皮肤从未因她头生骨肉那天真无邪的笑靥而喜悦地泛红过。」

===Original===
"Mr. Sylvester is very polite to Cousin Ona and seems to yield to her wishes in everything. But if I were she I think my heart would break over that very politeness. But then she is one who demands formality even from the persons of her household. I have never seen him stoop for a kiss or beheld her even so much as lay her hand on his shoulder. But I have observed him wait on her at moments when he was pale from weariness and she flushed with long twilight reclinings before her sleepy boudoir fire."

===Chinese===
「西尔维斯特先生对奥娜表姐彬彬有礼，凡事似乎都顺着她的意。可我若是她，单是那份彬彬有礼便要叫我心碎了。可话说回来，她本就是那种连家里上下人等都要求以礼数相待的人。我从未见过他俯身去吻她，也未见过她哪怕把手搭上他的肩头。可我却见他在因疲倦而面无人色之时仍要伺候她，而彼时她正因为在那慵懒的闺房炉火前长长地斜倚了一个黄昏而双颊泛红。」

===Original===
"There are times when I would not exchange my present opportunities for any others which might be afforded me. General ——— dined here today, and what a vision of a great struggle was raised up before me by his few simple words in regard to Gettysburg. I did not know which to admire most, the military bearing and vivid conversation of the great soldier, or the ease and dignity with which Mr. Sylvester met his remarks and answered each glowing sentence. General ——— spoke a few words to me. How gentle these lion-like men can be when they stoop their tall heads to address little children or young women!"

===Chinese===
「有些时刻，我不会拿眼下的种种际遇去换任何别的际遇。今日 ——— 将军（General ———）在此用膳，他几句平平淡淡关于葛底斯堡（Gettysburg）的话，便在我眼前唤起了一场伟大鏖战的整幅图景。我真不知该最钦佩哪一样——是这位大将军那军人风度与他那生动的言谈，还是西尔维斯特先生应答他的话、回他每一句灼灼之言时那份从容与气度。——— 将军也同我讲了几句话。这些如狮般的男人，当他们低下那高大的头颅去对小孩子或年轻女子说话时，竟是这般温文！」

===Original===
"What a noble-hearted man Mr. Sylvester is! Mr. Turner in speaking of him the other night, declared there is no one in his congregation who in a quiet way does so much for the poor. 'He is especially interested in young men,' said he, 'and will leave his own affairs at any time to aid or advise them.' I knew Mr. Sylvester was kind, but Mr. Turner's enthusiasm was uncommon. He evidently admires Mr. Sylvester as much as everyone else loves him. And he is not alone in this. Almost every day I hear some remark made of a nature complimentary to my benefactor's character or ability. Even Mr. Stuyvesant who so seldom appears to notice us girls, once interrupted a conversation between Cicely and myself to inquire if Mr. Sylvester was quite well. 'I thought he looked pale today,' remarked he, in his dry but not unkindly way, and then added, 'He must not get sick; he is too valuable to us.' This was a great deal for Mr. Stuyvesant to say, and it caused a visible gratification to Mr. Sylvester when I related it to him in the evening. 'I had rather satisfy that man than any other I know,' declared he. 'He is of the stern old-fashioned sort, and it is an honor to anyone to merit his approval. I did not tell him that I had also heard Mr. Stuyvesant observe in a conversation with some business friend of his, that Edward Sylvester was the only speculator he knew in whom he felt implicit confidence. Somehow it always gives me an uncomfortable feeling to hear Mr. Sylvester alluded to as a speculator. Besides since he has entered the Bank, he has I am told, entirely restricted himself to what are called legitimate operations.'"

===Chinese===
「西尔维斯特先生是何等一副仁厚心肠啊！特纳先生（Mr. Turner）前几日晚上说起他，宣称在他那座教区的会众里，再没人能在不动声色之中为穷人做这许多事。『他对年轻人尤其上心，』他说，『随时都会撂下自己的事去帮助他们、给他们出主意。』我原知西尔维斯特先生为人厚道，可特纳先生的热忱还是非同寻常。他显然钦佩西尔维斯特先生，一如旁人皆爱戴他一般。而他这样并非孤例。我几乎每日都能听见一两句赞美我这位恩主品性或才干的话。连斯泰弗森特先生（Mr. Stuyvesant）——他那样难得留意到我们这些姑娘——也曾打断了西塞莉与我之间的一场谈话，探问西尔维斯特先生身子是否安好。『我看他今日脸色有些发白。』他以他那干巴却不失和气的口吻说道，随即又补了一句：『他不能病倒，他于我们太要紧了。』这话出自斯泰弗森特先生之口已属难得；当晚我转述给西尔维斯特先生听时，显然令他十分快慰。『我宁可讨这一位的满意，也不愿讨我所认识的任何别的人的满意，』他说，『他是那种刚毅的老派人，能博得他的赞许，对任何人都是一桩体面。』我没告诉他，我还听见过斯泰弗森特先生在与某位生意上的朋友谈话时说：爱德华·西尔维斯特（Edward Sylvester）是他所认识的唯一一位令他完全信得过的投机客。不知怎的，每听见人把西尔维斯特先生称作投机客，我心里总有些不自在。况且自从他进了银行，听说他已完全把自己限制在所谓正当营生之列了。」

===Original===
"Mr. Sylvester came home with a dreadful look on his face today. We were standing in the hall at the time the door opened, and he went by us without a nod, almost as if he did not see us. Even Ona was startled and stood gazing after him with an anxiety such as I had never observed in her before, while I was conscious of that sick feeling I have sometimes experienced when he came upon me suddenly from his small room above, or paused in the midst of the gayest talk, to ask me some question that was wholly irrelevant and most frequently sad.

===Chinese===
「今日西尔维斯特先生回家时，脸上那副神情可怕极了。门开之时我们正立在门厅里，他从我们身旁走过，连一点头都没有，简直像没有看见我们。连奥娜表姐都吃了一惊，带着那样焦灼的神色望着他的背影——我从未在她身上见过那种焦灼；而我则感觉到那阵叫我作呕的心绪，那种我有时在他从楼上那间小屋骤然来到我跟前、或在最热闹的谈笑中途顿住、问我一句全然不着边际、又多半沉痛欲绝的话时，所感觉到的心绪。

===Original===
" 'He has met with some heavy loss,' murmured his wife, glancing down the handsome parlors with a look such as a mother might bestow upon the face of a sick child. But I was sure she had not sounded his trouble, and in my impetuosity was about to fly to his side when we saw him pause before the image of Luxury that stands on the stair, look at it for a moment with a strange intentness, then suddenly and with a gesture of irrepressible passion, lift his arm as if he would fell it from its place. The action was so startling, Ona clutched my sleeve in terror, but he passed on and in another moment we heard him shut the door of his room.

===Chinese===
『他遭了什么大损失了，』他的妻子低声道，朝那几间华美的客厅瞥了一眼，那种眼神，一如母亲投在病孩脸上的那种眼神。可我断定她并未探到他烦忧的底里；我一时冲动，正要奔到他身边去，却见他在立于楼梯上的那尊『奢华』像前停了下来，以一种古怪的专注盯了它片刻，随即突然地、按捺不住似地以一种激愤之态抬起手臂，仿佛要把那像从原处一掌击落。这一举动那样骇人，奥娜表姐吓得一把攥住我的衣袖；可他径自走过去，再过一刻，我们便听见他把自己那间屋子的门关上了。

===Original===
"Would he be down to dinner? that was the next question. Ona thought not; I did not dare to think. Nevertheless it was a great relief to me when I saw him enter the dining-room with that set immovable look he sometimes wears when Ona begins one of her long and rambling streams of fashionable gossip. 'It is nothing,' flashed from his wife's eyes to mine, and she lapsed at once into her most graceful self, but she nevertheless hastened her meal and I was quite prepared to observe her follow him, as with the polite excuse of weariness, he left the table before desert. I could not hear what she asked him, but his answer came distinctly to my ears from the midst of the library to which they had withdrawn. 'It is nothing in which you have an interest, Ona. Thank heaven you do not always know the price with which the splendors you so love are bought.' And she did not cry out, 'O never pay such a price for any joy of mine! Sooner than cost you so dear I would live on crusts and dwell in a garret.' No, she kept silence, and when in a few minutes later I joined her in the library, it was to find on her usually placid lips, a thin cool smile that struck like ice to my heart, and made it impossible for me to speak.

===Chinese===
「他会下来用饭么？这便是下一个问题。奥娜表姐以为不会；我却连想都不敢想。然而，当我看见他带着那一脸凝固不动、有时在奥娜表姐开始她那一长串东拉西扯的时髦闲话时所惯有的神情走进餐厅，我大大松了一口气。『没事的。』这一句从她妻子的眼里一闪传到我眼里，她随即又恢复了那最为优雅从容的自己；可她仍旧加快了用饭，而他先于甜点之前、以疲倦为由客气地离席之时，我一点也不意外地看见她跟了出去。我没听见她问了他什么，可他的答话从他们退入的那间书房里清清楚楚传到我耳中：『这事与你无干，奥娜。谢天谢地，你并不总能知道，你所钟爱的这些荣华，是以怎样的代价换来的。』而她竟没有喊出：『噢，切莫为我任何一点欢愉付这样的代价！与其叫你出这样大的代价，我宁愿啃干面包、住阁楼！』不，她默不作声；待几分钟后我走进书房与她同处，只见她那一向平和的唇上，挂着一丝薄薄的、冷冷的微笑，那笑像冰一样击中我的心，叫我再也说不出话来。

===Original===
"But the hardest trial of the day was to hear Mr. Sylvester come in at eleven o'clock—he went out again immediately after dinner—and go upstairs without giving me my usual good night. It was such a grief to me I could not keep still, but hurried to the foot of the stairs in the hopes he would yet remember me and come back. But instead of that, he no sooner saw me than he threw out his hand almost as if he would push me back, and hastened on up the whole winding flight till he reached the refuge of that mysterious room of his at the top of the house.

===Chinese===
「可这一日最难捱的一桩，乃是听见西尔维斯特先生十一点钟回来——他饭罢立刻又出门去了——径直上楼，连平日那一句晚安也没有给我。这叫我那样难过，我坐立不住，急忙奔到楼梯脚下，盼着他还能记起我、转回来。可谁知他一见我，便伸出手来，那架势简直要把我推回去，随即加快步子，一口气登上整段蜿蜒的楼梯，直到他躲进屋子顶层那间神秘的房间。

===Original===
"I could not go back to Ona after that—she had been to make a call somewhere with a young gentleman friend of hers;—yes on this very night had been to make a call—but I took advantage of the late hour to retire to my own room where for a long time I lay awake listening for his descending step and seeing, as in a vision, the startling picture of his lifted arm raised against the unconscious piece of bronze on the stair. Henceforth that statue will possess for me a still more dreadful significance."

===Chinese===
「此后我无法回到奥娜表姐那里去——她跟着一位年轻的绅士朋友到某处做客去了；——是的，恰恰是在这一夜，她出门做客去了——我倒借着夜深之故回到自己房里，许久许久躺着不能成眠，听他的脚步会不会下楼，眼前如见幻象一般，反复浮现那骇人的一幕：他抬起手臂，朝楼梯上那一尊浑然不觉的铜像挥去。从此之后，那一尊像于我，将带着更为可怖的意味。」

===Original===
"It is the twenty-fifth of February. Why should I feel as if I must be sure of the exact date before I slept?"

===Chinese===
「这是二月二十五日。为何我会有这样一种感觉——仿佛非要在入睡之前把这一确切的日子牢牢记住不可？」

===Original===
The next extract followed close on this and was the last which Miss Belinda read.

===Chinese===
下一段摘录紧接在这之后，也是贝琳达小姐所读的最后一段。

===Original===
"Mr. Sylvester seems to have recovered from his late anxiety. He does not shrink from me any more with that half bitter, half sad expression that has so long troubled and bewildered me, but draws me to his side and sits listening to my talk until I feel as if I were really of some comfort to this great and able man. Ona does not notice the change; she is all absorbed in preparing for the visit to Washington, which Mr. Sylvester has promised her."

===Chinese===
「西尔维斯特先生似乎已从近来的焦虑之中缓过来了。他不再带着那一副久来令我困扰、令我迷惑的半是苦涩、半是悲戚的神情，见我便躲，反而把我拉到他身旁，坐着听我说话，直到我觉得自己仿佛当真能给这位伟大而能干的人一点慰藉。奥娜表姐不曾留意这一变化；她全副心思都扑在为西尔维斯特先生应承下的那趟华盛顿（Washington）之行做打点上了。」

===Original===
Miss Belinda calmly folded up the letters and locked them again in the little mahogany box, after which she covered up the embers and quietly went to bed. But next morning a letter was despatched to Mr. Sylvester which ran thus:

===Chinese===
贝琳达小姐不慌不忙地把信折好，重新锁回那小红木小匣子里，随后将余烬掩上，悄然就寝。可次日清晨，一封信便寄给了西尔维斯特先生，信上写道：

## XII Miss Belinda Makes Conditions / 十二 贝琳达小姐讲条件

===Original===
> "For of the soul the body form doth take,
 
 For soul is form, and doth the body make."

===Chinese===
> 「盖身体乃灵魂所取之形，
> 因灵魂即是形相，方才成就此身。」

===Original===
Miss Belinda was somewhat taken aback at the proposal of Mr. Sylvester to receive Paula into his own house. She had not anticipated any such result to her efforts; the utmost she had expected was a couple of years or so of instruction in some state Academy. Nor did she know whether she was altogether pleased at the turn affairs were taking. From all she had heard, her niece Ona was, to say the least, a frivolous woman, and Paula had a mind too noble to be subjected to the deteriorating influence of a shallow and puerile companionship. Then the child had great beauty; Mr. Sylvester who ought to be a judge in such matters had declared it so, and what might not the adulation of the thoughtless and the envy of the jealous, do towards belittling a nature as yet uncontaminated.

===Chinese===
对于西尔维斯特先生要把宝拉接到自己家中抚养这一提议，贝琳达小姐多少有些猝不及防。她并未曾指望自己一番奔走能换来这样的结果；她所盼望的，至多不过是在某所州立学院里读上一两年书罢了。她甚至说不准，事情这般转折，自己心里是否全然欢喜。据她所闻，她的外甥女奥娜，往轻里说，也是个浮浅轻佻的女子；而宝拉的心性何等高贵，怎能让她受那浅薄幼稚的交往日日侵蚀。况且这孩子生得一副绝世的容貌；西尔维斯特先生在这上头原该是行家，既是他亲口这样说，那么那些无思无虑之人的阿谀、那些心怀妒意之人的嫉恨，又会把这颗尚且一尘不染的心，侵蚀到何等地步，实难预料。

===Original===
"We ought to think twice," she said to Miss Abby with some bitterness, who on the contrary never having thought once was full of the most childish hopes concerning a result which she considered with a certain secret complacency she would not have acknowledged for the world, had been very much furthered by her own wise recommendations to Mr. Sylvester in the beginning of his visit. Yet notwithstanding her doubts Miss Belinda allowed such preparations to be made as she considered necessary, and even lent her hand which was deft enough in its way, to the task of enlarging the child's small wardrobe. As for Paula, the thought of visiting the great city with the dear friend whose image had stood in her mind from early childhood as the impersonation of all that was noble, generous and protecting, was more than joyful; it was an inspiration. Not that she did not cling to the affectionate if somewhat quaint couple who had befriended her childhood and sacrificed their comfort to her culture and happiness. But the chord that lies deeper than gratitude had been struck, and fond as were her memories of the dear old home, the charm of that deep "My child," with its hint of fatherly affection, was more than her heart could stand; and no spot, no not the realms of fairyland itself, looked so attractive to her fancy as that far fireside in an unknown home where she might sit with cousin Ona and alternately with her exert her wit to beguile the smile to his melancholy lips.

===Chinese===
「我们该三思而后行才是。」她带着几分苦涩对阿比小姐（Miss Abby）说道。偏生阿比小姐恰恰相反，素来不曾思量过一回，这会儿满心都是最孩子气的盼头；她怀着一种打死也不肯承认的、暗自得意的盘算，认定这桩结局之所以有今日，全仗她当初在西尔维斯特先生刚到访时那一番明智的进言所促成。然而贝琳达小姐尽管心存疑虑，还是依着自己认为妥当的方式，让该做的准备一一办了起来，甚至还亲自动手——她那一双手在这上头是颇有些灵巧的——帮着为那孩子少得可怜的几件衣裳添补扩充。至于宝拉，一想到要随那位亲爱的友人同赴那座大都会，而这位友人的形象，自她幼年记事起便在她心中立着，是高贵、慷慨与呵护的化身，她心中的欢喜已不止于欢喜；那简直是一种感召、一种启迪。这并非说她不舍得那一对慈爱却略带古怪的夫妻——是她童年的恩人，为了教养她、成全她的幸福，甘愿牺牲了自家的安逸。然而，那一根比感恩更深的心弦已被拨动；她对那可爱的旧家的记忆虽深，那深情的「我的孩子」三个字，以及字里行间隐然可辨的那一份如父之爱，却叫她的心再也无法招架。于是再没有一处地方——不，便是仙境本身也不行——在她眼中能如那一方远在异乡、尚未相识的炉火旁这般叫人心驰；在那里，她可以与奥娜表姐并肩而坐，与她轮番施展巧思，只为博得那个愁眉不展之人唇边的一笑。

===Original===
When therefore upon the stated day, Mr. Sylvester made his second appearance at the little cottage in Grotewell, it was to find Paula radiant, Miss Abby tearfully exultant and Miss Belinda—O anomaly of human nature—silent and severe. Attributing this however to her very natural regret at parting with Paula, he entered into all the arrangements for their departure on the following morning without a suspicion of the real state of her mind, nor was he undeceived until the day was nearly over and they sat down to have a few minutes of social conversation before the early tea.

===Chinese===
及至约定的那一日，西尔维斯特先生再度出现在格罗特韦尔那座小屋时，所见却是：宝拉容光焕发，阿比小姐喜极而泣，而贝琳达小姐——啊，人性之难解啊——竟沉默寡言、神色凛然。他只当这是她与宝拉临别在即、自然而生的不舍之情，便毫无疑心地一同筹划次日起程的种种事宜，对她真实的心绪毫无察觉。直到那一日将尽，众人坐下要在早茶之前闲谈片刻，方才真相大白。

===Original===
They had been speaking on some local topic involving a question of right and wrong, and Mr. Sylvester's ears were yet thrilling to the deep ringing tones with which Paula uttered the words, "I do not see how any man can hesitate an instant when the voice of his conscience says no. I should think the very sunlight would daunt him at the first step of his foot across the forbidden line," when Miss Belinda suddenly spoke up and sending Paula out of the room on some trivial pretext, addressed Mr. Sylvester without reserve.

===Chinese===
方才众人正谈论着一桩关乎是非曲直的乡里之事，西尔维斯特先生的耳畔犹自震颤着宝拉方才说出那几句话时深沉而嘹亮的嗓音：「我实在不明白，一个人既听见良心在心头断然说『不』，又怎还能有半分迟疑。依我想，单是那头顶的日光，便该在他违禁迈出的第一步上将他镇住。」就在这时，贝琳达小姐忽然开了口，随便寻个由头把宝拉支出屋去，便对西尔维斯特先生毫无保留地直言起来。

===Original===
"I have something to say to you, sir, before you take from my home the child of my care and affection."

===Chinese===
「先生，在你把我亲手照料、视若己出的孩子从我家中带走之前，我有几句话要跟你说。」

===Original===
Could he have guessed what that something was that he should turn with such a flush of sudden anxiety to meet her determined gaze.

===Chinese===
倘若他能猜到那「几句话」究竟是什么，他又怎会带着那样一抹骤然焦虑的红潮，转过身去迎上她那坚定不移的目光。

===Original===
"The rules of our life here have been simple," continued she in a tone of voice which those who knew her well recognized as belonging to her uncompromising moods. "To do our duty, love God and serve our neighbor. Paula has been brought up to reverence those rules in simplicity and honor; what will your gay city life with its hollow devices for pleasure and its loose hold on the firm principles of life, do for this innocent soul, Mr. Sylvester?"

===Chinese===
「我们此地的日子，所循的规矩原是极简单的。」她以一种熟知她的人一望便知的、属于她寸步不让之时的语气接着说道，「尽己之责，爱主我们的神，服事我们的邻舍。宝拉是守着这几条规矩长大的，在质朴与恭敬中尊奉它们至今；可你那繁华的都市生活，那些徒有其表的寻欢作乐之术，那对人生坚固原则的松懈把持，西尔维斯特先生，又能为这一颗纯洁的灵魂做些什么呢？」

===Original===
"The city," he said firmly but with a troubled undertone in his voice that was not unnoted by the watchful woman, "is a vast cauldron of mingled good and evil. She will hear of more wrong doing, and be within the reach of more self-denying virtue, than if she had remained in this village alone with the nature that she so much loves. The tree of knowledge bears two kinds of fruit, Miss Belinda; would you therefore hinder the child from approaching its branches?"

===Chinese===
「城市，」他语气坚定地说道，声音里却压着一缕不安——这一缕不安不曾逃过这位留心妇人的耳目，「是一口硕大的鼎锅，善恶在其中一并煎熬。她将听见的恶行，她将触手可及的克己之德，都要比她独自留在这座小村里、与她所深爱的大自然相伴时为多。知识之树所结的果子有两般滋味，贝琳达小姐；难道您便因此要拦住这孩子，不让她靠近那枝头么？」

===Original===
"No, sir; I am not so weak as to keep a child in swaddling-clothes after the period of infancy is past, neither am I so reckless as to set her adrift on an unknown sea without a pilot to guide her. Your wife—" she paused and fixed an intent look upon the flames leaping before her. "Ona is my niece," she resumed in a lower tone of voice, "and I feel entitled to speak with freedom concerning her. Is she such a guide as I would choose for a young girl just entering a new sphere in life? From all I have heard, I should judge she was somewhat over-devoted to this world and its fashions."

===Chinese===
「不，先生；我还不至于糊涂到孩子都过了襁褓之龄，仍把她裹在襁褓里；可也不至于鲁莽到连个领港的引路人都没有，便把她撇在一无所知的大海上去随波逐流。你的夫人——」她顿了顿，目不转睛地盯着面前跳动的火苗。「奥娜是我的外甥女，」她放低了声音接着说，「我自觉有权对她畅所欲言。她可还算得上我心目中那种能为一个初入新天地的少女所选的引路人么？据我所闻，我只怕她是过于沉溺此世与这世上的浮华了。」

===Original===
Mr. Sylvester flushed painfully, but seeing that any softening of the truth would be wholly ineffectual with this woman, replied in a candid tone, "Ona is the same now as she was in the days of her girlhood. If she loves the world too well she is not without her excuse; from her birth it has strewn nothing but roses in her path."

===Chinese===
西尔维斯特先生痛苦地涨红了脸，但他也看出，对这位妇人，把真相说得软和半分都是全然无用的，便以坦率的口吻答道：「奥娜如今还是她少女时代的那个样子。她若是太爱慕这浮华世界，那也并非全无因由；自她降生之日起，这世界便只在她脚下撒满了玫瑰。」

===Original===
"Humph!" came from the lips of the energetic spinster. Then with a second stern glance at the fire, continued, "Another question, Mr. Sylvester. Does your wife consent to receive my niece into her house, for the indefinite length of time which you mention, from interest in the girl herself or indeed from any motive I should judge worthy of Paula? It is a leading question I know, but this is no time for niceties of speech."

===Chinese===
「哼！」从这位精明强干的老小姐唇间迸出这么一声。接着她又冷峻地瞥了火堆一眼，继续说道：「还有一问，西尔维斯特先生。尊夫人答应把这孩子接到她屋里、照你所讲的一住便是那等遥遥无期的一程，是出于她本人对这孩子的关切，抑或——说老实话——出于哪一种我看得上、配得上宝拉的因由？我知道我这是在刨根问底，可眼下不是说客气话的时候。」

===Original===
"Miss Belinda," replied he, and his voice was firm though his fingers slightly trembled where they rested upon the arms of his chair, "I will try and forget for a moment that Ona is my wife, and frankly confide to you that any such motive on her part, as would meet with your entire approval, must not be expected from a woman who has never fully recognized the solemn responsibilities of life. That she will be kind to Paula I have no doubt, that she may even learn to take an interest in her for her own sake, is also very possible, but that she will ever take your place towards her as guide or instructor, I neither anticipate nor would feel myself justified in leading you to."

===Chinese===
「贝琳达小姐，」他答道，声音虽坚定，搭在椅臂上的手指却微微发颤，「我愿意暂且把奥娜是我的妻子这件事搁过一旁，坦白地相告：她那一方，您所期望的那种全然合您心意的动机，原也不该指望一个从不曾真正体认人生庄严责任的女人能拿得出来。她会对宝拉和善，我毫不怀疑；她甚至可能学着因为这孩子本身的缘故而对她生出兴趣，这也大有可能；可要说她终有一日能取代您、做这孩子的引路人或教诲者，我既不存此指望，也自觉不该这样引您去指望。」

===Original===
The look which Miss Belinda cast him was anything but reassuring. "And yet," said she, "you will take away my darling and give her up to an influence that can not be for good, or your glance would not be so troubled or your lip so uncertain. You would set her young feet in a path where the very flowers are so thick they conceal its tendency and obscure its dangers. Mr. Sylvester you are a man who has seen life with naked eyes, and must recognize its responsibilities; dare you take this Paula, whom you have seen, out of the atmosphere of truth and purity in which she has been raised, and give her over to the enervating influences of folly and fashion? Will you assume the risk and brave the consequences?"

===Chinese===
贝琳达小姐投给他的那一眼，毫无令人宽慰之处。「然而，」她说，「你却要带走我的心头肉，把她交付给一种断不是为善的影响力——若是为善，你的目光又怎会这般忧烦，你的嘴唇又怎会这般犹疑？你要让她那双小小的脚踏上一条小径，那条路上的花朵开得这样密，密得盖住了它通向何方，也遮住了暗藏的凶险。西尔维斯特先生，你是个以赤裸双目直视过人生的人，理当认清它所附带的责任；你可敢，把这样一个你已亲眼见过的宝拉，从她自幼所长的真诚与纯洁的氛围中带出去，把她交到那足以消磨心志的浮华与愚行的影响之下？你可愿担下这风险，承受一切后果？」

===Original===
As though an electric shock had touched the nerve of his nature, Mr. Sylvester hastily rose and moved in a restless manner to the window. It was his favorite refuge in any time of sudden perplexity or doubt, and this was surely an occasion for both.

===Chinese===
仿佛一道电流触及了他天性深处某一根神经，西尔维斯特先生霍然起身，烦躁不安地踱到窗前。每逢猝然陷入困惑或犹疑之际，这窗前总是他最惯于退避的去处，而此刻，正是二者兼具之时。

===Original===
"Miss Belinda," he began and then paused, looking out on the hills of his boyhood, every one of which spoke to him at that moment with a force that almost sickened his heart and benumbed the faculties of his mind; "I recognize the love which leads you to speak in this way, and I bow before it, but—" here his tongue faltered again, that ready tongue whose quick and persuasive eloquence on public occasions had won for him the name of Silver-speech among his friends and admirers—"but there are others who love your Paula also, love her with a yearning that only the childless can feel or the disappointed appreciate. I had hoped—" here he left the window and approached her side, "to do more for Paula than to give her the temporal benefit of a luxurious home and such instruction as her extraordinary talents demand. If Ona upon seeing and knowing the child had found she could love her, I had intended to ask you to yield her to us unreservedly and forever, in short to make her my child in place of the daughter I have lost. But now—" with a quick gesture he began pacing the floor and left the sentence unfinished.

===Chinese===
「贝琳达小姐，」他开了口，又顿住，目光投向窗外那一片他度过童年的山峦——每一座山丘此刻都在对他说话，那力量之大，几令他的心作呕、令他的神智发木；「我明白引您这般说话的那份爱，我对它心怀敬意，可是——」说到此处他那根舌头又打了磕巴，那素来口齿伶俐、每逢公众场合便辞令敏捷、说服力极强的舌头，那曾为他赢得朋友与景仰者口中「银舌」之名的舌头——「可是还有旁人，也爱着您的宝拉；那一份爱里所含的渴慕，只有无儿无女之人才感受得到，只有失所望之人才懂得衡量。我原本指望——」他离开窗前，走到她身侧，「为宝拉所做的，不止是给她一所华美宅第所能带来的尘世之利，不止是依她那过人天赋所应受的教诲。倘若奥娜一见这孩子、一识这孩子，发觉自己当真能爱她，我原本打算求您把她毫无保留、永永远远地交与我们；简而言之，让她做我的孩子，顶替我所失去的那个女儿。可是如今——」他打了个急促的手势，开始在屋里来回踱步，把话留在了半截。

===Original===
Miss Belinda's eyes which were of a light grey, wholly without beauty but with strange flashes of expression in them, left the fire and fell upon his face, and a tear of real feeling gathered beneath her lids.

===Chinese===
贝琳达小姐的那双眼——一双浅灰色的、毫无美貌可言、却时而奇异闪烁出神情的眼——从炉火上移开，落到了他脸上；一滴真情实感的泪，在她眼睑之下沁了出来。

===Original===
"I had no idea," said he, "that you cherished any such intention as that. If I had I might have worded my apprehensions differently. The yearning feeling of which you speak, I can easily understand, also the strength of the determination it must take on the part of a man like yourself, to give up a hope of this nature. Yet—" Seeing him pause in his hurried pacing and open his lips as if to speak, she deferentially stopped.

===Chinese===
「我全然不知，」他说，「您心里竟藏着这样一番心意。若早知道，我的那些忧惧或会换一种说法。您所说的那一股渴慕之情，我自是容易体会；而像您这样一位男子，要舍弃这一类希望，又须拿出何等的决断，我也能想见。只是——」见他停下那匆匆的踱步、张口似要说话，她便知趣地止住了话头。

===Original===
"Miss Belinda," said he, in the firm and steadfast way more in keeping with his features than his agitated manner of a moment before, "I cannot give it up. The injury it would do me is greater than the harm, which one of Paula's lofty nature would be apt to acquire in any atmosphere into which she might chance to be introduced. She is not a child, Miss Belinda, though we allude to her as such. The texture of those principles which you have instilled into her breast, is of no such weak material as to give way to the first petty breeze that blows. Paula's house will stand, while mine—"

===Chinese===
「贝琳达小姐，」他开了口，语气又变得坚定沉稳，这种气度与他五官的轮廓更为相称，方才那一阵激动反倒显得不合；「我割舍不下。这件事对我所造成的损伤，要比宝拉这样心性高洁的孩子，无论置身何种氛围都容易沾染的那点坏处，更为深重。贝琳达小姐，她已不是个孩子了，纵然我们口口声声这般称呼她。您所植入她胸中的那一整套准则，其质料决不至于这般薄弱，一阵区区微风便吹得倒。宝拉那所房子会立得住，而我的——」

===Original===
He paused and gave way to a momentary struggle, but that over, he set his lips firmly together and the last vestige of irresolution vanished. Sitting down by her side, he turned his face upon her, and for the first time she realized the power which with one exception he had always exerted over the minds of others. "Miss Belinda," said he, "I am going to give you an evidence of my trust; I am going to leave with you the responsibility of Paula's future. She shall go with me, and learn, if she can, to love me and mine, but she shall also be under obligations to open her heart to you on all matters that concern her life and happiness in my house, and the day you see any falling off in her pure and upright spirit, you shall demand her return, and though it tears the heart from my breast, I will yield her up without question or parley as I am a gentleman and a Christian. Does that content you?"

===Chinese===
他停下，任由自己经历了一阵短暂的挣扎；但那阵挣扎一过，他便紧紧抿住了双唇，最后一丝犹疑也消散殆尽。他在她身旁坐下，转过脸来对着她；这是她头一回真切地感受到，他一向施加于旁人心智之上的那股力量——除却一人之外。此人的力量，此刻正向她全然显出。「贝琳达小姐，」他说，「我要给您一个我信得过的凭据；我要把宝拉将来的那份责任，交托到您手里。她会随我同去，倘若她能，让她学着爱我、爱我的家人；但她同时也得受一重约束：凡是在我家中关乎她一生幸福的事，都要向您敞开心扉。哪一日您见她那纯洁正直的心性有了半点折损，您只管开口要她回去；便是这一要求如剜心一般，我也决不讨价还价，必把她交还给您——以一个君子、一个基督徒之名起誓。这样，您可满意？」

===Original===
"It certainly ought to, sir. No one could ask more, I am sure," returned the other in a voice somewhat unsteady for her.

===Chinese===
「先生，这当然该叫人满意了。再没有谁能做得比这更多，我深信不疑。」对方答道，声音在她而言已算颇为不稳。

===Original===
"It is opening my house to the gaze of a stranger," said he, "for I desire you to command Paula to withhold nothing that seriously affects her; but my confidence in you is unbounded and I am sure that whatever you may learn in this way, will be held as sacred by you as though it were buried in a tomb."

===Chinese===
「这无异于把我的家向一个陌生人的审视敞开，」他说，「因为我所求于您的，是命宝拉凡有严重影响于她的事，一概不得向您隐瞒；但我对您的信赖是无边无际的，我也深信，凡您由此知晓的一切，您必视之如圣物、如埋于坟墓之中那般守口如瓶。」

===Original===
"It certainly will, sir."

===Chinese===
「自是当然，先生。」

===Original===
"As for the dearer hope which I have mentioned, time and the condition of things must decide for us. Meanwhile I shall strive to win a father's place in her heart, if only to build myself a refuge for the days that are to come. You see I speak frankly, Miss Belinda; will you give me some token that you are not altogether dissatisfied with the result of this conversation?"

===Chinese===
「至于我所提到的那个更为深切的心愿，便只好交由时光、交由事态来替我们定夺了。这其间，我会竭力在她心中争得一个父亲的位置，纵然只为着那将来的日子，给自己营一处栖身的避风之所。您瞧，我说话可谓坦白了，贝琳达小姐；您可愿给我一个信号，叫我得知您对今日这一席话的结果，并非全然不满？」

===Original===
With the straightforward if somewhat blunt action that characterized all her movements, she stretched out her hand, which he took with something more than his usual high-bred courtesy. "With you at the wheel," said she, "I think I may trust my darling, even to the whirl and follies of such a society as I know Ona loves. A man who can so command himself, ought to be a safe guide to pioneer others."

===Chinese===
她以那种直来直去、虽略嫌生硬却贯穿她一举一动的姿态，伸出手来；他握住这只手时所表现的，比他平日那种出身高雅的礼数还要更深一层。「有你掌舵，」她说，「我想我大可放心把我的心头肉托付出去，便是送进奥娜所钟爱的那一种喧嚣与浮华的社交圈里，也还信得过。一个这般能把持得住自己的人，理该是一位能替旁人开路的安全向导。」

===Original===
And the considerate gentleman bowed; but the frank smile that hailed her genial clasp had somehow vanished, and from the sudden cloud that at that moment swept over the roseate heavens, fell a shadow that left its impress on his lip long after the cloud itself had departed.

===Chinese===
这位体贴的先生躬身为礼；然而，迎接她那温厚一握的那一抹坦率微笑，不知怎地已悄然隐去。正当此刻，一朵乌云骤然掠过那玫瑰色的天际，投下一道阴影；云散之后许久，那阴影仍印在他的唇边，久久不退。

===Original===
An hour or so had passed. The fire was burning brightly on the hearthstone, illumining with a steady glow the array of stuffed birds, worsted samplers and old-fashioned portraits with which the walls were adorned, but reserving its richest glow and fullest irradiation for the bended head of Paula, who seated on a little stool in the corner of the hearth, was watching the rise and fall of the flickering flames.

===Chinese===
约莫一个钟头过去了。炉床上的火烧得正旺，以一道稳定的红光照亮了满墙陈列的鸟雀标本、毛线绣样和一张张旧式画像；可它把最浓烈的暖光、最圆满的辉照，都留给了宝拉那低垂的头颅——她正坐在炉角的一张矮凳上，凝望着那一明一暗、忽高忽低的火苗。

===Original===
She had packed her little trunk, had said goodbye to all her neighboring friends and was now sitting on the old hearthstone, musing upon the new life that was about to open before her. It was a happy musing, as the smile that vaguely dimpled her cheeks and brightened her eyes beneath their long lashes, amply testified. As Mr. Sylvester watched her from the opposite side of the hearth where he was sitting alone with his thoughts, he felt his heart sink with apprehension at the fervor of anticipation with which she evidently looked forward to the life in the new home. "The young wings think to gain freedom," thought he, "when they are only destined to the confinement of a gilded cage."

===Chinese===
她那只小箱子已经收拾停当，左邻右舍的朋友也都一一辞过了，此刻她便坐在那张旧炉床前，遐想着即将在她眼前展开的新生活。那是一段快乐的遐想，她脸颊上隐隐现出的笑靥、长睫下双眸里漾起的亮光，都足以为证。西尔维斯特先生独自抱着自己的思绪坐在炉火对面望着她，眼见她显然以一种何等炽烈的憧憬盼望着新家中的生活，心头不禁因忧虑而一沉。「这对年轻的翅膀，自以为就要博得自由了，」他暗想，「殊不知它们注定的，不过是一只镀金笼中的困居罢了。」

===Original===
He was so silent and looked so sad, Paula with a certain sort of sensitiveness to any change in the emotional atmosphere surrounding her, which was one of her chief characteristics, hastily looked up and meeting his eye fixed on her with that foreboding glance, softly arose and came and sat down by his side. "You look tired," murmured she; "the long ride after a day of business care has been too much for you."

===Chinese===
他这般沉默，神情又这般哀戚，宝拉——她对周身情志氛围的任何变化都有一种特殊的敏感，而这正是她最显著的天性之一——便匆匆抬起头来；一触上他那带着不祥预兆、定定凝在她身上的目光，她便轻轻起身，走过去坐在他身旁。「您看上去倦了，」她低声道，「忙碌了一整日，又赶了这么远的路，对您而言是太过了。」

===Original===
It was the first word of sympathy with his often over-wearied mind and body, that had greeted his ears for years. It made his eyes moisten.

===Chinese===
这是多年来头一句对他那常被劳顿所困的身心发出的体恤之语，落入他耳中。一时之间，他的双眼湿润了。

===Original===
"I have been a little overworked," said he, "for the last two months, but I shall soon be myself again. What were you thinking of, Paula?"

===Chinese===
「这两个月来我确实有些操劳过度，」他说，「不过我不久便会恢复如常。宝拉，你方才在想什么？」

===Original===
"What was I thinking of?" repeated she, drawing her chair nearer to his in her loving confidence. "I was thinking what wonders of beauty and art lay in that great kernel which you call the city. I shall see lovely faces and noble forms. I shall wander through halls of music, the echo of whose songs may have come to me in the sob of the river or the sigh of the pines, but whose notes in all their beauty and power have never been heard by me even in my dreams. I shall look on great men and touch the garments of thoughtful women. I shall see life in its fullness as I have felt nature in its mightiness, and my heart will be satisfied at last."

===Chinese===
「我在想什么？」她重复着，满怀依恋地把椅子朝他挪得更近些。「我在想，您称之为城市的那一枚硕大果核里，究竟藏着多少美与艺术的奇迹。我将见到可爱的容颜、高贵的身影。我将信步穿过一座座乐声缭绕的厅堂——那些厅堂里的歌声，或许早已化作河水的呜咽、松林的叹息传到我耳边过，可那曲调的真美与全部力量，却连在梦里我也不曾领略过。我将亲眼见到伟大的人物，亲手触到那些心思深沉的女子衣袂的一角。我将如体悟过大自然的雄浑那般，得见人生之圆满，而我的心，终将得到餍足。」

===Original===
Mr. Sylvester drew a deep breath and his eyes burned strangely in the glow of the firelight. "You expect high things," said he; "did you ever consider that the life in a great city, with its ceaseless rush and constant rivalries, must be often strangely petty in despite of its artistic and social advantages?"

===Chinese===
西尔维斯特先生深吸了一口气，双眼在炉火的红光里异样地灼亮。「你所期盼的，太高了。」他说，「你可曾想过，大都市里的生活——那无休无止的奔忙、永不停歇的争逐——纵然有它的种种艺术与社交之利，却往往出奇地琐碎？」

===Original===
"All life has its petty side," said she, with a sweet arch look. "The eagle that cleaves the thundercloud, must sometimes stop to plume its wings. I should be sorry to lose the small things out of existence. Even we in the face of that great sunset appealing to us from the west, have to pile up the firewood on the hearth and set the table for supper."

===Chinese===
「一切生活都有它琐碎的一面。」她说，带着一抹俏皮而甜美的神情。「便是那劈开雷云的雄鹰，有时也不得不停下来梳理一下羽翼。若把生活中那些细小的事物都剔除净尽，我会很觉惋惜。便是我俩此刻，面对着那一轮从西方向我们动人心魄的壮丽落日，也还是得往炉膛里添柴、得摆桌子摆晚饭呢。」

===Original===
"But fashion, Paula," he pursued, concealing his wonder at the maturity of mind evinced by this simple child of nature, "that inexorable power that rules the very souls of women who once step within the magic circle of her realm! have you never thought of her and the demands that she makes on the time and attention even of the worshippers of the good and the true?"

===Chinese===
「可是时尚呢，宝拉，」他接着说，暗自压下心头对这一个质朴自然之子所流露出的心智成熟所感到的惊奇，「那一种毫不通融的势力——但凡女人一旦踏进它那魔圈似的疆域，便连灵魂都要受它辖制！你难道从不曾想到过它，想到过它对那些即便一心敬仰真与善之人的时间与心神，所提出的种种索取么？」

===Original===
"Yes, sometimes," she returned with a repetition of her arch little smile, "when I put on a certain bonnet I have, which Aunt Abby modeled over from one of my grandmother's. Fashion is a sort of obstinate step-dame I imagine, whom it is less trouble to obey than to oppose. I don't believe I shall quarrel with Fashion if she will only promise to keep her hands off my soul."

===Chinese===
「有时也想过的。」她答道，又绽开那俏皮的小小一笑，「那是我戴上一顶我现有的帽子的时候——那是阿比姨母用我外祖母的一顶旧帽改制的。依我想，时尚大抵算得上一位置气固执的继母，顺从它比违拗它要省事得多。只要它肯应允一件事——不伸手来碰我的灵魂——我瞧我与时尚是吵不起架来的。」

===Original===
"But if—" with a pause, "she asks your all, what then?"

===Chinese===
「可若是——」他顿了一顿，「它要索取你的全部呢？那时又当如何？」

===Original===
"I shall consider that I am in a country of democratic principles," she laughed, "and beg to be excused from acceding to the tyrannical demands of any autocrat male or female."

===Chinese===
「我便权当自己置身于一个奉行民主原则的国度，」她笑道，「并恭请原谅，恕我无法应允任何暴君——无论男女——所提的专横要求。」

===Original===
"You have been listening to Miss Belinda," said he; "she is also opposed to all and any tyrannical measures." Then with a grave look from which all levity had fled, he leaned toward the young girl and gently asked, "Do you know that you are a very beautiful girl, Paula?"

===Chinese===
「你这都是听贝琳达小姐说的。」他道，「她也是反对一切暴政手段的。」随即，他换上一副凝重的神色——先前那点轻松之意已一扫而空——朝这少女倾过身去，轻声问道：「宝拉，你可知道，你是一个十分美丽的姑娘？」

===Original===
She flushed, looked at him in some surprise and slowly drooped her head. "I have been told I looked like my father," said she, "and I know that means something very kind."

===Chinese===
她红了脸，略带惊讶地看了他一眼，又缓缓垂下了头。「有人说过，我长得像我的父亲，」她说，「我明白，这是一句很亲切的话。」

===Original===
"My child," said he, with gentle insistence, "God has given you a great and wonderful gift, a treasure-casket of whose worth you scarcely realize the value. I tell you this myself, first because I prize your beauty as something quite sacred and pure, and secondly because you are going where you will hear words of adulation, whose folly and bluntness will often offend your ears, unless you carry in your soul some talisman to counteract their effect."

===Chinese===
「我的孩子，」他以一种温柔的郑重说道，「上天赋了你一份奇妙伟大的礼物，一只珍宝之匣，其价值你自己都几乎不曾察觉。这话我亲口告诉你，其一，是因为我把你的美视为一种近乎神圣纯洁之物；其二，是因为你将去往一个处所，在那儿你会听到种种阿谀之辞，其愚蠢、其莽撞，会时常冒犯你的双耳——除非你灵魂里揣着一样护身符，足以抵消它们的作用。」

===Original===
"I understand," said she, "I know what you mean. I will remember that the most engaging beauty is nothing without a pure mind and a good heart."

===Chinese===
「我明白，」她说，「我懂得您的意思。我会记住：若没有一颗纯洁的心思、一副善良的心肠，那最动人的美貌也算不得什么。」

===Original===
"And you will remember too," continued he, "that I blessed your innocent head tonight, not because it is circled by the roses of a youthful and fresh loveliness, but because of the pure mind and good heart I see shining in your eyes." And with a fond but solemn aspect he reached out his hand and laid it on her ebon locks.

===Chinese===
「你也要记着，」他接着说，「今夜我祝福你这天真无邪的头颅，并非因为它被一圈青春鲜妍的可爱玫瑰所环绕，而是因为我在你眼中看见了一颗纯洁心思、一副善良心肠在闪闪发光。」说罢，他带着一种慈爱而肃穆的神情，伸出手来，按在她那一头乌黑的鬈发上。

===Original===
She bowed her head upon her breast. "I will never forget," said she, and the firelight fell with a softening glow on the tears that trembled from her eyelashes.

===Chinese===
她把头低到了胸前。「我永世不忘。」她说，炉火以一道柔润的光，落在她睫毛上颤动欲坠的泪珠上。

## XXX Miss Belinda Presents Mr. Sylvester with a Christmas Gift / 三十 贝琳达小姐送给西尔维斯特先生一件圣诞礼物

===Original===
> "For, O; for, O the hobby horse is forgot."

It was a clear winter evening. Mr. Sylvester sat in his library, musing before a bright coal fire, whose superabundant heat and blaze seemed to make the loneliness of the great empty room more apparent. He had just said to himself that it was Christmas eve, and that he, of all men in the world, had the least reason to realize it, when the doorbell rang. He was expecting Bertram, whose advancement to the position of cashier in place of Mr. Wheelock, now thoroughly broken down in health, had that day been fully determined upon in a late meeting of the Board of Directors. He therefore did not disturb himself. It was consequently a startling surprise, when a deep, pleasant voice uttered from the threshold of the door, "I have brought you a Christmas present;" and looking up, he saw Miss Belinda standing before him, with Paula at her side.

"My child!" was his involuntary exclamation, and before the young girl knew it, she was folded against his breast with a passionate fervor that more than words, convinced her of the depth of the sacrifice which had held them separate for so long. "My darling! my little Paula!"

She felt her heart stand still. Gently disengaging herself, she looked in his face. She found it thin and wan, but lit by such a pleasure she could not keep back her smile. "You are glad, then, of your little Christmas present?" said she.

He smiled and shook his head; he had no words with which to express a joy like this.

===Chinese===
> 「因为，啊；因为，啊，那木马竟被忘却了。」

那是一个晴朗的冬夜。西尔维斯特先生坐在自己的书房里，对着明亮的煤炉火出神；炉火那过于丰盈的热度与光焰，倒似乎把这间空旷大宅的孤寂衬得更显分明了。他正自思忖今夜是圣诞前夜，而普天之下，再没有谁比他更没有资格来体味这个夜晚了——就在这时，门铃响了。他正盼着伯特兰；那一天稍晚时候召开的董事会上刚刚议定，由伯特兰接替如今身子骨已彻底垮掉的威洛克先生出任出纳员一职。因此他并没有动弹。于是，当一道低沉而悦耳的嗓音从门口传来——「我给您带来了一件圣诞礼物」——他不禁吃了一惊；抬起头来，只见贝琳达小姐（Miss Belinda）正立在他面前，宝拉陪在她身侧。

「我的孩子！」他情不自禁地喊了出来，那少女还来不及反应，便已被他紧紧拥在胸前；那一腔炽烈的深情胜过千言万语，使她真切地体会到：那桩曾使他们长久分离的牺牲，是何等深重。「我的心肝！我的小宝拉！」

她只觉自己的心都停住了。她轻轻地从他怀里挣出身来，望着他的脸。她见那脸庞消瘦而憔悴，却被一种喜悦照得通明，教她忍不住也漾起了笑意。「这么说，您是喜欢您这件小小的圣诞礼物了？」她说道。

他笑着摇了摇头；这般一份欢喜，他已找不出什么话来表达。

===Original===
Miss Belinda meanwhile stood with a set expression on her face, that, to one who did not know her, would immediately have proclaimed her to be an ogress of the very worst type. Not a glance did she give to the unusual splendor about her, not a wavering of her eye betokened that she was in any way conscious that she had just stepped from the threshold of a very humble cottage, into a home little short of a palace in size and the splendor of its appointments. All her attention was concentrated on the two faces before her.

"The ride on the cars has made Paula feverish," cried she, in sharp clear tones that rang with unexpected brusqueness through the curtained alcoves of that lordly apartment.

They both started at this sudden introduction of the prosaic into the hush of their happy meeting, but remembering themselves, drew Miss Belinda forward to the fire and made her welcome in this house of many memories.

===Chinese===
贝琳达小姐这时却板着脸站在一旁，那副神情，落在不知她底细的人眼里，准会立刻断定她是个顶顶凶恶的吃人妖婆。对于周遭那份不寻常的华美，她一眼也不曾去瞧；她目光丝毫不动，全无半点察觉自己方才才从一间极为寒素的村舍门槛跨出，便踏入了一处在气派与陈设的华美上几乎不逊于宫殿的宅邸。她全部的心思，都凝注在眼前那两张脸上。

「坐了一路火车，宝拉都发热了。」她嚷道，那尖锐清亮的嗓音带着一种出人意料的生硬，回响在那间华屋垂着帷幔的凹室之间。
