「闲话！我可从没把它当作闲话。」她答道，这是头一回察觉他神色里的变化。「那都是好久好久以前的事了，比起邻里间的一段传闻，倒更像一篇古拙的旧时故事。再说，一个任性的姑娘，跟着她自己所选中的人，从父亲家里私奔了——这事实本身总不见得有那么可怕吧，虽说她再没同丈夫回到过那宅子的墙里头来，她父亲又因这一桩打击而一蹶不振，从此再没人见他笑过。」

「是啊，」他匆匆瞥了她一眼，像是松了口气，「我所奇怪的，不过是这些陈年旧事竟能这样长久地缠住众人的耳朵罢了。我原以为，连雅克琳·雅法（Jacqueline Japha）这名字，也会在那一次忤逆之后漫长的沉寂里，被人们一并忘却。」

「也本会如此，倘若不是那所紧闭着的宅子、和它正门上那一道阴森森的横木——它一边招惹着人们的好奇，一边又把一切探究都实实在在挡在门外。既有这一件死者那不共戴天之仇的物证，日日摆在我们眼前，我们又怎能不有时去揣想那位成了这仇念所指之人的下场呢。」

===Original===
"And no intimations of that fate have been ever received in Grotewell. For all that is known to the contrary, Jacqueline Japha may have preceded her father to the tomb."

Paula bowed her head, amazed at the gloomy tone in which this emphatic assertion was made by one whose supposed ignorance she had been endeavoring to enlighten. "You knew her history before, then," observed she, "I beg your pardon."

"And it is granted," said he with a sudden throwing off of the shadow that had enveloped him. "You must not mind my sudden lapses into gloom. I was never a cheerful man, that is, not since I—since my early youth I should say. And the shadows which are short at your time of life grow long and chilly at mine. One thing can illumine them though, and that is a child's happy smile. You are a child to me; do not deny me a smile, then, before I go."

===Chinese===
「而在格罗特韦尔（Grotewell），关于她那下场，从来未曾有过半点音信。就人们所知而言，雅克琳·雅法说不定早已先她父亲一步入了土。」

宝拉低下了头，她原是要把所谓自己所不知的事讲给对方听，不料这一位竟用这般阴沉的语气，说出这般斩钉截铁的话来，她一时好生诧异。「那么说，您从前就知道她的故事了，」她说，「是我失敬了。」

「恕你无罪。」他说着，猛地把笼罩着他的那片阴影甩脱了。「我这一时一时的忽然沉下脸来，你可千万别放在心上。我从来不是个快活的人——或者不如说，自从我——自从我早年的青年时代以来，便不是了。那些在你这般年纪短得很的影子，到了我这般年纪，便拖得又长又冷。不过有一样东西能照亮它们，那便是一个孩子那快活的笑。你在我眼里还是个孩子；那么，在我走之前，别舍不得给我一个笑。」

===Original===
"Not one nor a dozen," cried she, giving him her hands in goodbye for they had arrived at the depot by this time and the sound of the approaching train was heard in the distance.

"God bless you!" said he, clasping those hands with a father's heartfelt tenderness. "God bless my little Paula and make her pillow soft till we meet again!" Then as the train came sweeping up the track, put on his brightest look and added, "If the fairy-godmother chances to visit you during my departure, don't hesitate to obey her commands, if you want to hear the famous organ peal."

"No, no," she cried. And with a final look and smile he stepped upon the train and in another moment was whirled away from that place of many memories and a solitary hope.

===Chinese===
「别说一个，便是一打也依您。」她喊道，把双手伸给他作别——这时他们已经走到了车站，远处已能听见火车驶近的声音。

「愿上帝赐福给你！」他说，以一种父亲般由衷的温柔紧握住那双手。「愿上帝赐福给我这个小宝拉，叫她的枕头软软的，直等到我们再相见！」说罢，当那列车沿着铁轨疾驶过来时，他装出他最明快的一副脸色，又道，「若是我不在家时，那位仙女教母（fairy-godmother）恰巧来看你，你想听那架出了名的大风琴奏起来，可就别迟疑，只管听她的吩咐。」

「不，不。」她喊道。他给了她最后的一瞥、一笑，便踏上了列车；转眼的工夫，他便被载离了那个有着许多回忆、和一桩孤零零的盼望的地方。

## XX The Dregs in the Cup / 二十 杯中残滓

===Original===
> “O eloquent, just and mightie death! whom none could advise, thou hast persuaded; what none hath dared, thou hast done; and whom all the world hath flattered, thou only hast cast out of the world and despised: thou hast drawn together all the farre stretched greatnesses; all the pride, crueltie and ambition of man and covered it all over with these two narrow words, ‘Hic jacet’ ”

===Chinese===
> 「啊，雄辩、公义而全能的死亡啊！无人能进言的，你却已将其劝服；无人敢为之的，你却已将其做成；普天之下人人所逢迎的，唯你将他抛出尘世、弃之如敝屣：你把一切纵极极远的尊荣，把人所有的骄傲、残忍与野心，一并收拢，又用『长眠于此』这两个局促的字眼，悉数掩盖。」

===Original===
Bertram’s hurried ring at his uncle’s door was answered by Samuel the butler.

“What is this I hear?” cried the young man, entering with considerable agitation, “Mrs. Sylvester dead?”

“Yes sir,” returned the old and trusty servant, with something like a sob in his voice. “She went out riding this morning behind a pair of borrowed horses—and being unused to Michael’s way of driving, they ran away and she was thrown from the carriage and instantly killed.”

“And Miss Fairchild?”

“She didn’t go with her. Mrs. Sylvester was alone.”

“Horrible, horrible! Where is my uncle, can I see him?”

“I don’t know, sir,” the man returned with a strange look of anxiety. “Mr. Sylvester is feeling very bad, sir. He has shut himself up in his room and none of his servants dare disturb him, sir.”

“I should, however, like him to know I am here. In what room shall I find him?”

“In the little one, sir, at the top of the house. It has a curious lock on the door; you will know it by that.”

“Very well. Please be in the hall when I come down; I may want to give you some orders.”

===Chinese===
伯特兰急匆匆按响叔父家的门铃，来开门的是管家塞缪尔（Samuel）。

「我听说的那是怎么回事？」年轻人嚷着，神色十分激动地跨进门来，「西尔维斯特夫人去世了？」

「是的，先生。」这位忠心耿耿的老仆答道，嗓音里带着一声近似呜咽。「她今早出门坐马车，驾的是一对借来的马——那两口子不习惯迈克尔的赶车法子，便撒蹄狂奔起来，她从车上摔了下去，当场就没了命。」

「费尔柴尔德小姐（Miss Fairchild）呢？」

「没有跟她同去。西尔维斯特夫人是一个人出门的。」

「可怕，太可怕了！我叔父在哪儿，我能见他吗？」

「我说不准，先生。」那仆人答道，神情有一种异样的焦灼。「西尔维斯特先生心里难受得很，先生。他把自己关在房里，底下的仆人没一个敢去惊动他，先生。」

「可我总得让他知道我来了。在哪间屋里能找到他？」

「顶层那间小屋子，先生。屋门上有一把古怪的锁；您一看那锁便认得了。」

「好。等我下来时，请你在门厅里候着；我或许有事要吩咐你。」

===Original===
The old servant bowed and Bertram hastened with hushed steps to ascend the stairs. At the first platform he paused. What is there in a house of death, of sudden death especially, that draws a veil of spectral unreality over each familiar object! Behind that door now inexorably closed before him, lay without doubt the shrouded form of her who but a few short hours before, had dazzled the eyes of men and made envious the hearts of women with her imposing beauty! No such quiet then reigned over the spot filled by her presence. As the vision of a dream returns, he saw her again in all her splendor. Never a brow in all the great hall shone more brightly beneath its sparkling diamonds; never a lip in the whole vast throng curled with more self-complacent pride, or melted into a more alluring smile, than that of her who now lay here, a marble image beneath the eye of day. It was as if a flowery field had split beneath the dancing foot of some laughing siren. One moment your gaze is upon the swaying voluptuous form, the half-shut beguiling eye, the white out-reaching arms upon whose satin surface a thousand loves seem perching; the next you stare horror-stricken upon the closing jaws of an awful pit, with the flash of something bright in your eyes, and the sense of a hideous noiseless rush in which earth and heaven appear to join, sink and be swallowed! Bertram felt his heart grow sick. Moving on, he passed the bronze image of Luxury lying half asleep on its bed of crumpled roses. Hideous mockery! What has luxury to do with death? She who was luxury itself has vanished from these halls. Shall the mute bronze go on smiling over its wine cup while she who was its prototype is carried by without a smile on the lips once so vermeil with pride and tropical languors!

===Chinese===
老仆人一躬身，伯特兰便蹑着脚步，赶忙往楼上走去。上了第一段楼梯的平台，他停住了脚步。一所死过人的宅子——尤其是猝然丧命之所——究竟有什么魔力，竟能给每一样眼熟的物事都蒙上一层鬼魅般的虚幻！此刻，在那扇对他无情紧闭的房门背后，毫无疑义地躺着那个裹了尸衣的人；而不过短短几个钟头之前，正是她以那雍容的美貌，叫男人的眼睛为之目眩，叫女人的心为之嫉妒！彼时她所立之处，绝非如今这般沉寂。梦境般的幻象重又浮现，他仿佛又看见了她盛装时的全副光华。整座大厅里，再没有哪一尊额头能在那闪烁的钻石之下放出更亮的光来；在那济济一堂的人海里，再没有哪一张嘴唇，能比此刻躺在这里、化身为白日之下大理石像的她，卷起过更自满自得的骄矜，或是化作过更迷人的微笑。这情景，恰似一片繁花盛放的草野，在某一个欢笑的塞壬（siren）那踏着舞步的脚下訇然裂开。方才你目光所及的，还是那摇曳生姿、妖冶动人的身段，那半阖着、勾人魂魄的眼，那一双白皙伸出的胳膊——在那缎子般的肌肤上，仿佛栖着千千万万个小爱神；转眼之间，你便惊恐万状地瞪着一口正在合拢的骇人深渊的巨颚，眼里闪过一抹什么发亮的东西，耳际涌起一种可怖的、无声的坠落之感——天与地仿佛一齐在这坠落里合拢、下沉、被吞没！伯特兰只觉心里一阵发怵。他往前走，经过那尊青铜的「奢靡」之像——它半睡半醒地卧在它那铺满皱皱巴巴玫瑰花的榻上。可憎的嘲讽！奢靡与死亡何干？奢靡的化身本人，不是已从这些厅堂里消失无踪了吗。那本尊既已被人抬了出去——那一双嘴唇，曾因骄矜与热带般的慵懒而红艳无比，如今却再挂不上一丝笑意——难道这尊哑口无言的青铜，还能对着它的酒杯继续微笑下去吗！

===Original===
Arrived at the top of the house, Bertram knocked at the door with the strange lock, and uttering his own name, asked if there was anything he could do here or elsewhere to show his sympathy and desire to be of use in this great and sudden bereavement. There was no immediate reply and he began to fear he would be obliged to retire without seeing his uncle, when the door was slowly opened and Mr. Sylvester came out. Instantly Bertram understood the anxiety of the servant. Not only did Mr. Sylvester’s countenance exhibit the usual traces of grief and horror incident to a sudden and awful calamity, but there were visible upon it the tokens of another and still more unfathomable emotion, a wild and paralyzed look that altered the very contour of his features, and made his face almost like that of a stranger.

“Uncle, what is it?” sprang involuntarily to his lips. But Mr. Sylvester betraying by a sudden backward movement an instinctive desire to escape scrutiny, he bethought himself, and with hasty utterance offered some words of consolation that sounded strangely hollow and superficial in that dim and silent corridor. “Is there nothing I can do for you?” he finally asked.

“Everything is being done,” exclaimed his uncle in a strained and altered voice; “Robert is here.” And a silence fell over the hall, that Bertram dared not break.

===Chinese===
伯特兰攀到了宅子顶层，在那扇锁头古怪的门前叩了几下，报上自己的姓名，问可有什么事是他能在此处、或是到别处去办的，好借此表一表他的关切与在这样一场猝不及防的大丧里效劳的心意。一时无人作答，他正担心自己不得不不见叔父一面便退下来，门却缓缓打开了，西尔维斯特先生走了出来。伯特兰立时就明白了那仆人何以如此忧心忡忡。原来西尔维斯特先生的面色上，不仅有一场飞来横祸所常带的那种悲戚与骇愕的痕迹，更看得见另一种、更深不可测的情绪的形迹——一种狂乱而呆木的神情，竟把五官的轮廓都改了样，叫他的脸几乎像是个陌生人。

「叔父，您怎么了？」这句话不自觉地冲到了嘴边。可西尔维斯特先生猛地往后一缩，那动作泄露了他一种本能的、想躲开旁人审视的念头；伯特兰便醒悟过来，匆忙间说出了几句宽慰的话——在那昏暗寂静的走廊里，这几句话听来空泛而浅薄得近乎古怪。「您当真没有什么要我做的吗？」他终于问道。

「该办的，都在办了。」叔父用一种紧绷而走了样的嗓音说道，「罗伯特在这儿。」于是一片寂静落满了门厅，伯特兰不敢去打破它。

===Original===
“I have help for everything but—” He did not say what, it seemed as if something rose up in his throat that choked him.

“Bertram,” said he at last in a more natural tone, “come with me.”

He led him into an adjoining room and shut the door. It was a room from which the sunshine had not been excluded and it seemed as if they could both breathe more easily.

“Sit down,” said his uncle, pointing to a chair. The young man did so, but Mr. Sylvester remained standing. Then without preamble, “Have you seen her?”

There was no grief in the question, only a quiet respect. Death clothes the most volatile with a garment of awe. Bertram slowly shook his head. “No,” said he, “I came at once upstairs.”

“There is no mark on her white body, save the least little discolored dent here,” continued his uncle, pointing calmly to his temple. “She had one moment of fear while the horses ran, and then—” He gave a quick shudder and advancing towards Bertram, laid his hand on his nephew’s shoulder in such a way as to prevent him from turning his head. “Bertram,” said he, “I have no son. If I were to call upon you to perform a son’s work for me; to obey and ask no questions, would you comply?”

===Chinese===
「样样事我都有人帮衬，只除了一件——」他没有说那一件是什么，仿佛有什么东西顶上了喉头，把他噎住了。

「伯特兰，」他终于用较为自然的口吻说道，「跟我来。」

他把侄儿领进隔壁一间屋子，关上了门。那是一间没有挡住日光的屋子，两个人进了里面，仿佛都能喘得畅快些了。

「坐下。」叔父指着一把椅子说。年轻人坐下了，可西尔维斯特先生依旧站着。接着他单刀直入地问：「你可见过她了？」

这一问里没有悲戚，只有一种肃然的恭敬。死亡给最轻浮躁动的人，也披上一件令人敬畏的外衣。伯特兰缓缓摇了摇头。「没有，」他说，「我径直上了楼。」

「她那洁白的身上没有半点伤痕，只除了这儿，一个几乎看不出的、带点青紫的小凹痕。」叔父接着说，平静地指了指自己的太阳穴。「惊马狂奔的那一会儿，她怕是有一刹那的恐惧，再然后——」他猛地打了个寒噤，朝伯特兰走近一步，把一只手搭在侄儿的肩上，搭得叫他不能回头。「伯特兰，」他说，「我没有儿子。倘若我要你替我做一桩儿子分内的事；要你唯命是从、不问缘由，你可肯依？」

===Original===
“Can you ask?” sprang from the young man’s lips; “you know that you have only to command for me to be proud to obey. Anything you can require will find me ready.”

The hand on his shoulder weighed heavier. “It seems a strange time to talk about business, Bertram, but necessity knows no law. There is a matter in which you can afford me great assistance if you will undertake to do immediately what I ask.”

“Can you doubt—”

“Hush, it is this. On this paper you will find a name; below it a number of addresses. They are all of places downtown and some of them not very reputable I fear. What I desire is for you to seek out the man whose name you here see, going to these very places after him, beginning with the first, and continuing down the list until you find him. When you come upon him, he will ask you for a card. Give him one on which you will scrawl before his eyes, a circle, so. It is a token which he should instantly understand. If he does, address him with freedom and tell him that your employer—you need make use of no names—re-demands the papers made over to him this morning. If he manifests surprise or is seen to hesitate, tell him your orders are imperative. If he declares ruin will follow, inform him that you are not to be frightened by words; that your employer is as fully aware of the position of affairs as he. Whatever he says, bring the papers.”

===Chinese===
「这还用问吗？」这话脱口而出，从年轻人嘴边迸了出来，「您该明白，您只管下令就是，我奉命而行，乃是引以为荣的。您但凡有所吩咐，我无有不从。」

搭在他肩头的那只手，越发沉了下去。「伯特兰，眼下谈这种事，未免不合时宜，可事急从权，顾不得许多了。有一桩事，你若肯立刻照我所嘱去办，便是帮我一个大忙了。」

「您还能疑心我——」

「嘘，是这样的。这张纸上你会看见一个名字，名字底下是一串地址。都是下城（downtown）一带的去处，其中几处，我怕还不大体面。我所要你做的，是去寻出那纸上所写的这个人——照着这些地址一处一处地去找他，从第一个起，顺着单子往下，直到找着为止。你撞见他时，他会向你要一张名片。你给他一张，当着他的面，在上面潦草地画上一个圆圈，像这样。这是个暗号，他一见便该明白。他若明白了，你就大大方方地同他说话，告诉他，你的东家——不必提任何人的名姓——要追回今早转交到他手里的那几份文件。他若是露出惊讶，或是见他有犹豫之色，你便告诉他，你所奉的令是不容打折扣的。他若是扬言这样一来要大祸临头，你就回他，几句空话吓你不倒；你的东家对这事的原委，与他一样心里有数。无论他说什么，务必把那文件带回来。」

===Original===
Bertram nodded his head and endeavored to rise, but his uncle’s hand rested upon him too heavily.

“He is a small man; you need have no dread of him physically. The sooner you find him and acquit yourself of your task, the better I shall be pleased.” And then the hand lifted.

On his way downstairs Bertram encountered Paula. She was standing in the hall and accosted him with a very trembling tone in her voice. All her questions were in regard to Mr. Sylvester.

“Have you seen him?” she asked. “Does he speak—say anything? No one has heard him utter a word since he came in from downtown and saw her lying there.”

“Yes, certainly; he spoke to me; he has been giving me some commissions to perform. I am on my way now to attend to them.”

She drew a deep breath. “O!” she cried, “would that he had a son, a daughter, a child, someone!”

===Chinese===
伯特兰点了点头，想站起来，可叔父那只手仍重重地按着他。

「他是个身量不大的人；论气力你全不必怕他。你越早寻着他、把这件事办妥，我便越高兴。」说罢，那只手才抬了起来。

伯特兰下楼时，正撞见宝拉。她站在门厅里，一开口，嗓音里满是颤。她问的句句都关乎西尔维斯特先生。

「你可见着他了？」她问，「他说话吗——讲什么没有？自打他从下城回来、瞧见她躺在那儿，谁也没听见他吐过一个字。」

「见了，自然是见了；他同我说话来着；交了几桩差使给我去办。我这就要去办了。」

她深深地倒抽了一口气。「啊！」她失声道，「他要是有个儿子、有个女儿、有个孩子、有个人在身边，该多好！」

===Original===
This exclamation following what had taken place above struck Bertram forcibly. “He has a son in me, Paula. Love as well as duty binds me to him. All that a child could do will I perform with pleasure. You can trust me for that.”

She threw him a glance of searching inquiry. “His need is greater than it seems,” whispered she. “He was deeply troubled before this terrible accident occurred. I am afraid the arrow is poisoned that has made this dreadful wound. I cannot explain myself,” she went on hurriedly, “but if you indeed regard him as a father, be ready with any comfort, any help, that affection can bestow, or his necessities require. Let me feel that he has near him some stay that will not yield to pressure.”

There was so much passion in this appeal that Bertram involuntarily bowed his head. “He has two friends,” said he, “and here is my hand that I will never forsake him.”

“I do not need to offer mine,” she returned. “He is great and good enough to do without my assistance.” But nevertheless she gave her hand to Bertram and with a glow of her lip and eye that made her beauty, supreme at all times, something almost supernatural in its character.

“I dared not tell him,” she whispered to herself as the front door closed with the dull slow thud proper to a house of mourning. “I dare not tell anyone, but—”

What lay beyond that but?

===Chinese===
这声惊呼，紧随方才楼上所发生的一切而来，重重地叩在伯特兰心上。「他便有我这么一个儿子呢，宝拉。是情分，也是本分，把我拴在他身边。凡是做儿女的所能做的，我都乐意去做。这一点，你尽可相信我。」

她朝他投来一道探询而锐利的一眼。「他的难处，比表面上要大得多。」她低声说，「在这场可怕的事故发生之前，他心里早已盛着极大的烦恼了。我怕，射出这道可怖伤口的那支箭，是淬过毒的。我说不清楚，」她急急地往下说，「可你若当真把他当作父亲看待，那就无论什么样的慰藉、什么样的援手——只要是情分所能给的、或是他所急切需要的——你都预备着拿出来。让我也安心：知道他身边好歹有根顶得住事儿的柱子。」

这一番话里含着那样多的深情，伯特兰不由得低下了头。「他有两个朋友。」他说，「这一只手，我绝不会舍了他。」

「我的手便不必伸出来了。」她答道，「他又伟大、又善良，原用不着我来相助。」可话虽如此，她还是把自己的手伸给了伯特兰，唇边眼里都燃起一抹光——那光使她那原本便无出其右的美貌，此刻几乎添上了一层超凡脱俗的意味。

「我不敢告诉他。」前门合上时，她独自喃喃着——那一声沉闷、迟缓的关门声，正合一所居丧之宅该有的分量。「我不敢告诉任何人，可是——」

那一个「可是」后头，究竟藏着什么？

===Original===
When Mr. Sylvester came in at six o’clock in the morning, Paula had risen from the bed on which she had been sitting, but not to make preparation for rest, for she could not rest. The vague shadow of some surrounding evil or threatened catastrophe was upon her, and though she forced herself to change her dress for a warmer and more suitable one, she did not otherwise break her vigil, though the necessity for it seemed to be at an end. It was a midwinter morning and the sun had not yet risen, so being chilly as well as restless, she began to pace the floor, stopping now and then to glance out of the window, in the hopes of detecting some signs of awakening day in the blank and solemn east. Suddenly as she was thus consulting the horizon, a light flashed up from below, and looking down upon the face of the extension that ran along at right angles to her window, she perceived that the shades were up in Mrs. Sylvester’s boudoir. They had doubtless been left so the evening before, and Mr. Sylvester upon turning up the gas had failed to observe the fact. Instantly she felt her heart stand still, for the house being wide and the extension narrow, all that went on in that boudoir, or at least in that portion of it which Mr. Sylvester at present occupied, was easily observable from the window at which she stood; and that something was going on of a serious and important nature, was sufficiently evident from the expression of Mr. Sylvester’s countenance. He was standing with his face bent towards someone seated out of sight, his wife undoubtedly, though what could have called her from her dreams—and was busily engaged in talking. The subject whatever it was, absorbed him completely. If Paula had allowed herself the thought, she would have described him as pleading and that with no ordinary vehemence. But suddenly while she gazed half fascinated and but little realizing what she was doing, he started back and a fierce change swept over his face, a certain incredulity, that presently gave way to a glance of horror and repugnance, which the quick action of his out-thrown palm sufficiently emphasized. He was pushing something from him, but what? A suggestion or a remembrance? It was impossible to determine.

===Chinese===
清晨六点钟，西尔维斯特先生进门时，宝拉正从她一直坐着的那张床上站起身来——可她并不是要去安置歇息，因为她根本歇息不下。一种说不清的、四围逼近的祸祟、一种仿佛大难将至的阴影，正罩在她心头；她虽然强打着精神换上了一身更暖和、更合时宜的衣裙，却并未就此打断她的守夜——虽说这守夜的必要，看样子已经到头了。那是个隆冬的清晨，太阳尚未升起，她身上发冷，心里又不宁，便开始在屋里来回踱步，时不时停下步子，朝窗外张一眼，盼着能在那一片空白而肃穆的东方，辨出几分破晓的迹象来。正当她这样望着天边出神，忽然，下头闪起一缕光；她朝那与她的窗户成直角伸出去的厢房屋顶上一望，发觉西尔维斯特夫人那间小起居室的窗帘竟没有放下。想来是前一夜便那样撂着的，西尔维斯特先生扭亮煤气灯时，未曾留意这一层。她当下只觉心都停住了不跳——因为宅子面阔、那厢房又窄，那间起居室里——至少是西尔维斯特先生此刻所占的那一隅里——所发生的种种，站在她这扇窗前，是一目了然的；而此刻分明正有一桩极其要紧的事在进行，单看西尔维斯特先生脸上的神情，便再清楚不过。他正低着脸，朝着一位坐在他视线之外的人——毫无疑问是他的妻子——尽管是什么事把她从梦里唤了起来——他自己正忙着说话。那话题，不论是什么，已把他整个人都吸了进去。倘若宝拉容许自己有这个念头，她简直会形容他是在恳求，而且恳求得绝非常见的激烈。可就在她这样半被摄住心魄、又几乎未觉察自己在做什么的当口，他猛地往后一退，脸上掠过一阵凶狠的变化——一种不可置信的神色，旋即化作一种惊恐与厌恶的一瞥，而他猛然伸出的那一掌，把这份惊恐与厌恶强调得分外分明。他是在把什么东西从他面前推开，可那是什么？一个提议？还是一段回忆？实在无从判断。

===Original===
The countenance of Mrs. Sylvester who that moment appeared in sight sailing across the floor in her azure wrapper, offered but little assistance in the way of explanation. Immovable under most circumstances, it was simply at this juncture a trifle more calm and cold than usual, presenting to Paula’s mind the thought of a white and icy barrier, against which the most glowing of arrows must fall chilled and powerless.

“O for a woman’s soul to inform that breast if but for a moment!” cried Paula, lost in the passion of this scene, while so little understanding its import. When as if in mockery to this invocation, the haughty form upon which she was gazing started rigidly erect, while the lip acquired a scorn and the eye a menace that betrayed the serpent ever in hiding under this white rose.

===Chinese===
西尔维斯特夫人这时刚好出现在视野里，一身天蓝色的晨衣，像一只雍容的天鹅般从地板上掠过——可她那张脸，在解释这事上却帮不了什么忙。那张脸在多数情形下本就不动声色，此刻只不过比寻常更冷峻、更寒淡了几分，落到宝拉心里，便如同一道白皑皑、冰森森的障壁——最灼热的箭，射到它上面，也不免变冷、跌落，再也使不出气力。

「啊，但愿有一个女人的灵魂，能在这胸膛里活过那怕是一瞬！」宝拉失声呼道，她已为这一幕所攫，却又几乎全然不懂它的含义。谁知，仿佛是有意嘲笑这一声祝祷似的，她所凝望的那傲岸身影倏地挺得笔直，唇角浮起一缕轻蔑，眼里聚起一缕威吓——那威吓与轻蔑，把这朵白玫瑰底下素来藏着的那条毒蛇，给露了出来。

===Original===
Paula could look no longer. This last revelation had awakened her to the fact that she was gazing upon a scene sacred to the husband and wife engaged in it. With a sense of shame she rushed to the bed and threw herself upon it, but the vision of what she had beheld would not leave her so easily. Like letters of fire upon a black ground, the panorama of looks and gestures to which she had just been witness, floated before her mind’s eye, awakening a train of thought so intense that she did not know which was worse, to be there in the awful dawn dreaming over this episode of the night, or to rise and face again the reality. The fascination which all forbidden sights insensibly exert over the minds of the best of us, finally prevailed, and she slowly crept to the window to catch a parting glimpse of Mr. Sylvester’s tall form hurrying blindly from the boudoir followed by his wife’s cold glance. The next minute the exposed condition of the room seemed to catch that lady’s attention, and with an anxious look into the dull gray morn, Mrs. Sylvester drew down the shades, and the episode was over.

===Chinese===
宝拉再不敢看下去了。这最后一幕的揭示，叫她猛然醒悟：她方才所窥见的，是一对夫妻之间一段不容旁观的隐秘。她怀着羞愧冲到床边，一头扑倒在床上，可方才所见的那一幕，却不肯这么轻易地放过她。宛如漆黑底色上一行行火焰般的字，她刚才所目睹的那一连串神情与手势，仍一幕幕浮在她心眼之前，勾起一串如此强烈的思绪，叫她都说不清究竟是哪一样更难熬——是就这样待在这可怖的晨光里，把昨夜这一段当作梦魇般反复咀嚼；还是爬起身来，再去面对那冰冷的现实。一切被禁制的景象，纵是最有定力的人，也不知不觉要被它摄住——这股魔力到底占了上风，她又慢慢地爬到窗前，想偷着看最后一眼：只见西尔维斯特先生那高高的身影正失魂落魄地从那间小起居室里奔出来，背后跟着他妻子一道冷冷的目光。再过一分钟，那屋子这般毫无遮拦的样子，似乎引起了那位夫人的注意——她朝那灰蒙蒙的清晨焦虑地望了一眼，便把窗帘放了下来。这一段插曲，到此便算终了。

===Original===
Or so Paula thought; but when she was returning upstairs after her solitary breakfast—Mrs. Sylvester was too tired and Mr. Sylvester too much engaged to eat, as the attentive Samuel informed her—the door of Ona’s room swung ajar, and she distinctly heard her give utterance to the following exclamation:

“What! give up this elegant home, my horses and carriage, the friends I have had such difficulty in obtaining, and the position which I was born to adorn? I had rather die!” And Paula feeling as if she had received the key to the enigma of the last night’s unaccountable manifestations, was about to rush away to her own apartment, when the door swayed open again and she heard his voice respond with hard and bitter emphasis,

“And it might be better that you should. But since you will probably live, let it be according to your mind. I have not the courage—”

There the door swung to.

===Chinese===
至少宝拉是这样以为的。可待她独自用过早饭往楼上走时——西尔维斯特夫人太累了，西尔维斯特先生又有太多事缠身，都顾不上用饭，这是那留心的塞缪尔告诉她的——奥娜那间屋子的门正半开半掩，她清清楚楚听见她迸出了下面这一句：

「什么！要我放弃这座体面的宅子，放弃我的马和马车，放弃我好不容易才结交下的那些朋友，还有我生来就配享有的地位？我宁可去死！」宝拉觉得自己仿佛拿到了昨夜那一连串莫名其妙举动的谜底，正要奔回自己的房间去，那门却又被推开了，她听见他的声音，带着一种生硬而辛酸的强调，应了一句：

「你若当真死了，或许倒好些。可既然你多半还要活下去，那就随你的便罢。我没有那个勇气——」

说到这儿，门又合上了。

===Original===
An hour from that Mr. Sylvester left the house with a small valise in his hand, and Mrs. Sylvester dressed in her showiest costume, entered her carriage for an early shopping excursion.

And so when Paula whispered to herself, “I did not dare to tell him; I did not dare to tell anyone, but—” she thought of those terrible words, “Die? It might be better, perhaps, that you should!” and then remembered the ghastly look of immeasurable horror with which a few hours later, he staggered away from that awful burden, whose rigid lines would never again melt into mocking curves, and to whom the morning’s wide soaring hopes, high reaching ambitions and boundless luxuries were now no more than the shadows of a vanished world; life, love, longing, with all their demands, having dwindled to a noisome rest between four close planks, with darkness for its present portion and beyond—what?

===Chinese===
一个钟头之后，西尔维斯特先生手里拎着一只小旅行袋出了门；而西尔维斯特夫人则换上了她最惹眼的一身装束，登上了自家的马车，趁一大早出门购物去了。

是以，当宝拉独自低语着「我不敢告诉他；我不敢告诉任何人，可是——」的时候，她心里想着的，正是那几句可怕的话：「去死？你若当真死了，或许倒好些！」继而她又记起，几个钟头之后，当他踉跄着从那一具可怖的累赘旁退开时，脸上那种不可丈量的、煞白如死人的惊恐之色——那一具身躯，那些僵硬的线条，再不会化作嘲弄人的曲线了；而对它而言，清晨里那志在云天的希冀、那高不可攀的雄图、那漫无止境的奢华，此刻都不过是另一个业已消逝的世界投下的影子罢了；生命、爱情、渴望，连同它们一切的索求，都已萎缩成四块紧窄的木板之间一场恶臭的安息，眼前这一份是黑暗，而黑暗那头——又是什么？

## XIII The End of My Lady's Picture / 十三 夫人画像的终结

===Original===
> "Heaven from all creatures hides the book of Fate."

Mrs. Sylvester was spending an evening at home. This was something so unusual for this august lady of fashion to indulge in, that she found it difficult not to fall asleep in the huge crimson-backed chair in which she had chosen to ensconce herself. Not that she had desisted from making every effort known to mortal woman to keep herself awake and if possible amused till the expected travellers should arrive. She had played with her bird till the spoiled pet had himself protested, ducking his head under his wing and proceeding without ceremony to make up his little feather bed, as cunning Geraldine used to call the round, fluffy ball into which he rolled himself at night. More than that, she had looked over her ornaments and taken out such articles as she thought could be spared for Paula, to say nothing of playing a bar or so from the last operatic sensation, and laboriously cutting open the leaves of the new magazine. But it was all of no use, and the heavy white lids were slowly falling, when the bell rang and Mr. Bertram Mandeville was announced, or rather Bertram Sylvester as he now chose to be called.

===Chinese===
> 「苍天对一切造物，都掩上了命运之书。」

西尔维斯特夫人这一晚竟在家消磨。这般时髦雍容的贵妇人肯在家度夜，实在是稀罕至极的事，以至于她觉着要想不在自己挑中安身的那张硕大的红缎靠背椅里睡过去，都颇为困难。倒不是她不曾使出凡属女子所能知晓的一切法子，来撑住自己不睡、若可能还要寻点消遣，好捱到那几位翘盼中的旅人到来。她逗弄过她的鸟儿，直逗到那只被宠坏了的小东西自己都抗议起来，把头往翅膀底下一缩，也不讲什么客气，径自去打理它那张小小的羽床——机灵的杰拉尔丁（Geraldine）从前就爱这么称呼它夜里蜷作的那一团毛茸茸的圆球。不止如此，她还检视过自己的首饰，把那些她觉得可以让与宝拉（Paula）的物件一一取出；更不消说她又随手弹了一两小节最近轰动乐坛的歌剧段子，又费力地裁开了那本新到的杂志书页。可这一切全无用处，那沉重的白眼皮正慢慢地耷拉下来——就在这时，门铃响了，有人通报伯特兰·曼德维尔先生（Bertram Mandeville）到——或者照他如今情愿被称呼的那样，伯特兰·西尔维斯特。

===Original===
It was a godsend to her as she politely informed him upon his entrance; and though in his secret heart he felt anything but God sent—he was not of a make to appreciate his uncle's wife at her very evident value—he consented to remain and assist her in disposing of the evening till Mr. Sylvester should return.

"He is going to bring a pretty girl with him," remarked she, in a tone of some interest, "a cousin of mine from Grotewell. I should like to have you see her."

===Chinese===
他一进门，她便客客气气地告诉他，他这一来真是天赐之福；可他心里头却半点没有受天之赐的感觉——他这种人，原本就无从赏识他这位婶母那明摆着的价值——不过他还是答应留下来，帮她把这一晚打发过去，直捱到西尔维斯特先生归来。

「他打算带一个俊俏的姑娘一道回来，」她颇有些兴味地说道，「是我格罗特韦尔（Grotewell）的一位表妹。我倒是愿意让你见见她。」

===Original===
"Thank you," replied he, his mind roaming off at the suggestion, into the region of a certain plain little music-room where the clock on the mantel ticked to the beating of his own heart. And for ten minutes Mrs. Sylvester had the pleasure of filling the room with a stream of easy talk, in which Grotewell, dark beauties, the coming Seventh Regiment reception, the last bit of gossip from London, and the exact situation of the Madison Bank formed the principal topics.

To the one last mentioned, it having taken the form of a question, he was forced to reply; but the simple locality having been learned, she rambled easily on, this time indulging him with a criticism upon the personal appearance of certain business gentlemen who visited the house, ending with the somewhat startling declaration:

"If Edward were not the fine appearing gentleman that he undoubtedly is, I should feel utterly out of place in these handsome parlors. Anything but to see an elegant and modern home, decorated with the costliest works of art, and filled with bijouterie of the most exquisite delicacy, presided over by a plain and commonplace woman or a bald-headed and inferior-looking man. The contrast is too vivid; works of the highest art do not need such a startling comparison to bring out their beauty. Now if Edward stood in the throne-room of a palace, he would somehow make it seem to others as a handsome set off to his own face and figure."

===Chinese===
「多谢。」他答道，心思却随这一句话飘了开去，飘到了那间朴素的小小琴室里——那屋里壁炉架上的钟一下一下地滴答着，正与他自家的心跳合拍。于是足足十分钟，西尔维斯特夫人便得以在这间屋子里，用一串从容不迫的闲谈将四下灌满；那闲谈里头，格罗特韦尔、黑眼睛的美人、即将到来的第七团招待会、伦敦最新一段闲话，以及麦迪逊银行（Madison Bank）眼下的确切情势，便是其中的几桩主要话题。

最后一桩既是以问题的形式提出，他不得不作答；可待这简单的方位一弄清楚，她便又信口扯了开去，这一回竟还不辞辛劳地对他品评起几位常来宅中走动的商界先生们的仪表风度来，末了抛出一句颇叫人吃惊的论断：

「若不是爱德华这副相貌气度，无可争辩地是位仪表堂堂的君子，我在这般华美的客厅里，怕要觉得自己格格不入到极点了。最怕的就是瞧着一户雅致的、时新的宅子，陈设着最昂贵的艺术品，满摆着最精巧绝伦的珠宝小件，却由一个相貌平庸、毫不打眼的女人，或一个秃头秃脑、瞧着低人一等的男人来做它的主人。那对照未免太刺眼了；最高等的艺术品原不必借这般刺目的反衬，来显出它们的美。可若是爱德华立在宫殿的觐见室里，他总有法子，叫旁人觉着那地方倒是给他自家的容貌身姿做了一处相当漂亮的衬映。」

===Original===
This was all very wife-like if somewhat unnecessary, and Bertram could have listened to it with pleasure, if she had not cast the frequent and sidelong glances at the mirror, which sufficiently betrayed the fact that she included herself in this complacent conclusion; as indeed she may have considered herself justified in doing, husband and wife being undoubtedly of one flesh. As it was, he maintained an immovable countenance, though he admired his uncle as much as she did, and the conversation gradually languished till the white somnolent lids of the lady again began to show certain premonitory signs of drooping, when suddenly they were both aroused by the well known click of a latchkey in the door, and in another moment Mr. Sylvester's voice was heard in the hall, saying, in tones whose cheery accents made his wife's eyes open in surprise—

"Welcome home, my dear."

===Chinese===
这番话做妻子的说来原也颇为得体，虽说稍稍有些多余；伯特兰本可以听得很惬意——倘若她不曾频频朝那面镜子斜斜地瞟上几眼的话。那几瞟已足够泄露天机：她分明把自己也算进了这桩自得的结论里；而这一点，她大约也觉得自己名正言顺——夫妻原是一体嘛。话虽如此，他脸上仍是一副纹丝不动的神情，尽管他之钦佩叔父，并不亚于她之钦佩丈夫；谈话渐渐地也就懒散下来，直到夫人那双白皙犯困的眼皮又开始显出几分校下垂的先兆——忽然之间，门上一把弹簧钥匙那熟识的咔哒一声，把两人一同惊醒了；不一会儿，门厅里便传来了西尔维斯特先生的声音，那语调轻快而欢悦，叫他的妻子都吃惊地睁大了眼——

「欢迎回家，亲爱的。」

===Original===
"They have come," murmured Mrs. Sylvester rising with a look of undeniable expectation. Had Paula not been a beauty she would have remained seated.

"Yes, we have come," was heard in hearty tones from the doorway, and Mr. Sylvester with a proud look which Bertram long remembered, ushered into their presence a young girl whose simple cloak and bonnet in no wise prevented Mrs. Sylvester from recognizing the somewhat uncommon beauty she had been led to expect.

"Paula, this is your cousin Ona, and—Ah, Bertram, glad to see you—this is my only nephew, Mr. Sylvester."

===Chinese===
「他们到了。」西尔维斯特夫人喃喃地说，站起身来，脸上是一副不容置疑的期盼之色。倘若宝拉不是个美人，她原会照旧坐着不动。

「是的，我们到了。」门口传来一声爽朗的话音；西尔维斯特先生带着一副自豪的神气——伯特兰久久记得那神气——把一个年轻姑娘引到他们跟前。姑娘那一身朴素的斗篷和软帽，丝毫不妨碍西尔维斯特夫人辨认出她意料之中的那种略显不凡的美。

「宝拉，这是你表姐奥娜（Ona）；还有——啊，伯特兰，很高兴见到你——这是我唯一的侄子，西尔维斯特先生。」

===Original===
The young girl, lost in the sudden glamour of numerous lights, shining upon splendors such as she may have dreamed of over the pages of Irving's Alhambra, but certainly had never before seen, blushed with very natural embarrassment, but yet managed to bestow a pretty enough greeting upon the elegant woman and handsome youth, while Ona after the first moment of almost involuntary hesitation, took in hers the two trembling hands of her youthful cousin and actually kissed her cheek.

"I am not given to caresses as you know," she afterwards explained in a somewhat apologetic tone to her husband; "and anything like an appeal for one on the part of a child or an inferior, I detest; but her simple way of holding out her hand disarmed me, and then such a face demands a certain amount of homage, does it not?" And her husband in his surprise, was forced to acknowledge to himself, that as closely as he had studied his wife's nature for ten years, there were certain crooks and turns in it which even he had never penetrated.

===Chinese===
小姑娘一时被那骤然亮起的无数灯火耀眼的辉煌弄得失了神——这般辉煌，她或许只在欧文（Irving）的《阿尔罕伯拉》（Alhambra）的字里行间梦见过，却断然未曾亲眼见过——不由得十分自然地窘红了脸，可到底还是把一声颇为得体的问候，送给了那位雍容的妇人和那位英俊的少年；而奥娜在一开头那近乎不由自主的一怔之后，便握住了这位小表妹那两只微微发抖的手，竟还当真亲了亲她的脸颊。

「我向来不惯于这种亲热，你是知道的，」事后她以一种略带歉意的口吻向丈夫解释道，「小孩子或下属那一类求人爱抚的样子，我是顶厌恶的；可她那一种大大方方把手伸出来的模样，倒把我这一层武装解了去；况且那样一张脸，总该有它一份相当的敬意才是，不是么？」她丈夫吃了一惊，不禁暗自承认：自己虽说把这十年来把妻子的脾性揣摩得不能再细，其中竟也还有这样几处曲折拐角，是他连他都未曾窥透的。

===Original===
"You look dazzled," that lady exclaimed, gazing not unkindly into the young girl's face; "the sudden glare of so much gaslight has bewildered you."

"I do not think it is that," returned Paula with a frank and admiring look at the gorgeous room and the circle of pleasant faces about her. "Sudden lights I can bear, but I have come from a little cottage on the hillside and the magnificence of nature does not prepare you for the first sudden view of the splendors of art."

Mrs. Sylvester smiled and cast a side glance of amusement at Bertram. "You admire our new hangings I see," remarked she with an indulgence of the other's naivete that greatly relieved her husband.

===Chinese===
「你看上去被晃花了眼，」那位夫人大声道，目光并不含恶意地打量着小姑娘的脸，「这一下子亮起这么些煤气灯，强光直射，把你弄糊涂了吧。」

「我想不是那个缘故。」宝拉答道，坦然且带着几分赞赏地环顾了一下这间华丽的屋子、围在她身边的那一圈和悦的脸。「突如其来的灯光我倒受得住；可我一路是从山坡上的一座小屋来的，大自然的那种壮美，可没法叫人事先有了底，去承当这头一遭骤然撞见的艺术的华美。」

西尔维斯特夫人笑了笑，朝伯特兰投去一道觉得有趣的眼风。「我瞧你是很赏脸，夸了我们新换的帷幔呢。」她说，对这姑娘的天真所流露的那份宽纵，叫她丈夫大大地松了一口气。

===Original===
But in that instant a change had come across Paula; the simple country maid had assimilated herself with the surroundings, and with a sudden grace and dignity that were unstudied as they were charming, dropped her eyes from her cousin's portrait—that for some reason seemed to shine with more than its usual insistence—and calmly replied, "I admire all beautiful color; it is my birthright as a Walton, to do so, I suppose."

Mrs. Sylvester was a Walton also and therefore smiled; but her husband, who had marked with inward distrust, the sudden transformation in Paula, now stepped forward with a word or two of remark concerning his appetite, a prosaic allusion that led to the rapid disappearance of the ladies upstairs and a short but hurried conversation between the two gentlemen.

===Chinese===
可就在这一刹那间，宝拉已起了变化；这个朴素的乡下姑娘已然把自己与周遭融作了浑然一片，带着一种突如其来、既不造作又极可人的端庄仪态，把自己的目光从表姐的画像上——那画像不知怎的，像比平日更显殷勤地熠熠逼人地发着光——收了下来，从容答道：「凡是美的颜色，我一概都爱；我想，作为沃尔顿家（Walton）的一员，这原是我的天赋权利。」

西尔维斯特夫人也是沃尔顿家的人，于是便笑了一笑；可她丈夫方才一直暗自戒备地注视着宝拉这突然的转变，此刻便上前搭了两句话，说的是自己胃口如何——这一句家常之谈，引得两位夫人飞快地往楼上避去了；叔侄两位之间，于是有了一段简短而匆匆的交谈。

===Original===
"I have brought you a sealed envelope from the office," said Bertram, who, in accordance with his uncle's advice, had already initiated himself into business by assuming the position of clerk in the office of the wealthy speculator.

"Ah," returned his uncle hastily opening it. "As I expected, a meeting has been held this day by the board of Directors of the Madison Bank, a vote was cast, my proxy did his duty and I am duly elected President. Bertram, we know what that means," smiled he, holding out his hand with an affectionate warmth greatly in advance of the emotion displayed by him on a former occasion.

===Chinese===
「我从行里给您带来了一封封口的信。」伯特兰说。他听从叔父之劝，已经到这位富有的投机商人的行里就了职，充当一名办事员，以此初涉这门营生。

「啊。」叔父急急地拆开它答道。「不出我所料——麦迪逊银行的董事会今日开了一次会，投了一次票，我的代理人尽了他的职，我便正式当选了行长。伯特兰，咱们明白这意味着什么。」他微笑着伸出手来，那一份亲热温煦之情，已远胜前次相见时所流露的。

===Original===
"I hope so indeed," young Bertram responded. "An increase of fortune and honor for you, though you seem to have both in the fullest measure already, and a start in the new life for me to whom fortune and honor mean happiness."

A smile younger and more full of hope than any he had seen on his uncle's face for years, responded to this burst. "Bertram," said he, "since our conversation of a couple of weeks ago something has occurred which somewhat alters the opinions I then expressed. If you have patience equal to your energy, and a self-control that will not put to shame your unbounded trust in women, I think I can say Godspeed to your serious undertaking, with something like a good heart. Women are not all frivolous and foolish-minded; there are some jewels of simple goodness and faith yet left in the world."

===Chinese===
「我也当真这样盼着。」年轻的伯特兰答道，「于您是财帛与名位的更上一层楼——虽说您这两样看起来早已绰绰有余；于我则是这新生活的一个开端，财帛和名位于我这样的人，可就是幸福本身了。」

一缕比他多年来在叔父脸上所见都要年轻、都更满怀希望的微笑，回应了这一番热烈的倾吐。「伯特兰，」他说，「自打咱们两礼拜前那次谈话之后，出了一些事，叫我当时所表达的那一些见解，多少得有所改动了。你若能与自己的精力相称的那一份耐心，再有那一份不至于叫你对女人那毫无保留的信托蒙羞的自制之力，我想我便可以以一种颇为热切的心情，祝你这一桩正经的抱负，一路顺风了。女子并非尽是些轻浮糊涂之辈；这世上毕竟还留有几颗质朴的良善与信实的明珠。」

===Original===
"Thank God for your conversion," returned his nephew smiling, "and if this lovely girl whom you have just introduced to me, is the cause of it, then thank God for her also."

His uncle bowed with a gravity almost solemn, but the ladies returning at this moment, he refrained from further reply. After supper, to which unusual meal Mr. Sylvester insisted upon his nephew remaining, the two gentlemen again drew apart.

"If you have decided upon buying the shares I have mentioned," said the former, "you had better get your money in a position to handle at once. I shall wish to present you to Mr. Stuyvesant tomorrow, and I should like to be able to mention you as a future stockholder in the bank."

===Chinese===
「多谢上天叫您转了这一念。」侄子笑着答道，「若您方才引我见到的这位可人儿，便是这转变的缘由，那么也多谢上天赐了她来。」

叔父以一种近乎肃穆的庄重颔首为礼；可几位夫人正在此刻回到屋里，他便不再往下说了。用罢晚饭——这一顿异乎寻常的晚饭，西尔维斯特先生执意留侄子一同入席——叔侄两位又另退到一处。

「你若已决意买下我前番提到的那几股，」前者说道，「便最好把你那笔钱先调到一个随手可取的地位。我明日要引你去见斯泰弗森特先生（Mr. Stuyvesant），我盼望能把你作为银行日后的股东举荐于他。」

===Original===
"Mr. Stuyvesant!" exclaimed Bertram, ignoring the rest of the sentence.

"Yes," returned his uncle with a smile, "Thaddeus Stuyvesant is the next largest stockholder to myself in the Madison Bank, and his patronage is not an undesirable one."

"Indeed—I was not aware—excuse me, I should be happy," stammered the young man. "As for the money, it is all in Governments and is at your command whenever you please."

===Chinese===
「斯泰弗森特先生！」伯特兰失声呼道，把那句话的其余部分撇在了一边。

「是的，」叔父微笑着答道，「撒迪厄斯·斯泰弗森特（Thaddeus Stuyvesant）是麦迪逊银行里仅次于我本人的最大的股东；他肯提携照应，倒也不失为一件美事。」

「哎呀——我竟不曾知道——失敬失敬，我是十分乐意的。」年轻人结结巴巴地说。「至于那笔钱，全在国债（Governments）里头，随时听凭您吩咐便是。」

===Original===
"That is good, I'll notify you when I'm ready for the transfer. And now come," said he, with a change from his deep business tone to the lighter one of ordinary social converse, "forget for a half hour that you have discarded the name of Mandeville, and give us an aria or a sonata from Mendelssohn before those hands have quite lost their cunning."

"But the ladies," inquired the youth glancing towards the drawing-room where Mrs. Sylvester was giving Paula her first lesson in ceramics.

"Ah, it is to see how the charm will act upon my shy country lassie, that I request such a favor."

"Has she never heard Mendelssohn?"

"Not with your interpretation."

===Chinese===
「那很好，待我预备妥当了转移手续，便着人知会你。这会儿来吧，」他说着，从方才那低沉的办事腔调一转而为寻常闲谈的轻快腔调，「就这半个钟头，权当你没把曼德维尔这个姓弃之不用，趁那一双手还没把它的精巧全丢光，给我们来一支门德尔松（Mendelssohn）的咏叹调，或者奏鸣曲罢。」

「可几位夫人呢？」少年问道，朝那间起居室里瞟了一眼——西尔维斯特夫人正在那里给宝拉上头一课，讲的是陶瓷。

「啊，正是要瞧这一份魅力，会对我这害羞的乡下小丫头起怎样的作用，我才讨你这一桩情。」

「她从未听过门德尔松么？」

「不曾听过用你这般诠释的门德尔松。」

===Original===
Without further hesitation the young musician proceeded to the piano, which occupied a position opposite to my lady's picture in this anomalous room denominated by courtesy the library. In another instant, a chord delicate and ringing, disturbed the silence of the long vista, and one of Mendelssohn's most exquisite songs trembled in all its delicious harmony through these apartments of sensuous luxury.

Mr. Sylvester had seated himself where he could see the distant figure of Paula, and leaning back in his chair, watched for the first startled response on her part. He was not disappointed. At the first note, he beheld her spirited head turn in a certain wondering surprise, followed presently by her whole quivering form, till he could perceive her face, upon which were the dawnings of a great delight, flush and pale by turns, until the climax of the melody being reached, she came slowly down the room, stretching out her hands like a child, and breathing heavily as if her ecstacy of joy in its impotence to adequately express itself, had caught an expression from pain.

===Chinese===
年轻的音乐家不再迟疑，径自走到钢琴前——这架琴正占着这间不伦不类、承情称作「书斋」的屋子里、与夫人画像遥遥相对的位置。下一刻，一个纤巧而清亮的和弦，划破了这一道长长视廊里的寂静；一首门德尔松最精妙的歌，便以它那令人沉醉的全部和声，颤颤地流过这一处处奢靡旖旎的内室。

西尔维斯特先生拣了一个能望见远处宝拉身影的位子坐下，背靠椅背，只等瞧她头一刹那惊动的反应。他并未失望。第一个音符起处，他便瞧见她那神采飞扬的头带着几分惊诧地转了过来，紧接着便是她整个微微战栗的身子，直到他可以看见她的脸——那脸上正有大欢喜的曙色初现——一阵红一阵白地变着颜色，直到那旋律抵到顶点，她才慢慢地穿过屋子走来，像孩童一般把两只手伸得长长的，喘息沉沉，仿佛她那无从尽情倾诉的狂喜，在倾吐无门之际，竟从苦痛那里借来了一副神情。

===Original===
"O Mr. Sylvester!" was all she said as she reached that gentleman's side; but Bertram Mandeville recognized the accents of an unfathomable appreciation in that simple exclamation, and struck into a grand old battle-song that had always made his own heart beat with something of the fire of ancient chivalry under its breastplate of modern broadcloth.

"It is the voice of the thunder clouds when they marshal for battle!" exclaimed she at the conclusion. "I can hear the cry of a righteous struggle all through the sublime harmony."

"You are right; it is a war-song ancient as the time of battle-axes and spears," quoth Bertram from his seat at the piano.

"I thought I detected the flashing of steel," returned she. "O what a world lies in those simple bits of ivory!"

"Say rather in the fingers that sweep them," uttered Mr. Sylvester. "You will not hear such music often."

===Chinese===
「啊，西尔维斯特先生！」她走到那位先生身旁时，所说的话只这一句；可伯特兰·曼德维尔已在这一声短短的惊叹里，听出了一种深不可测的鉴赏的口吻，便径直转入一支恢宏的古战歌——这支歌每每叫他自家那颗藏在今日呢绒礼服胸衣之下的心，也多少带着几分古昔骑士的火气而跳动起来。

「这是雷云列阵出战时的声音！」一曲既终，她失声呼道，「这一整片崇高的和声里，我都听得见一场正义之争的呐喊。」

「你说得不错；这是一支战歌，古老得一如战斧和长枪的时代。」伯特兰从钢琴前的座上说道。

「我方才也恍惚瞧见了钢铁的闪光呢。」她答道，「啊，这区区几片小小的象牙里，竟藏着怎样一个世界！」

「倒不如说，是藏在抚过它们的那几根手指里。」西尔维斯特先生开口道，「这样的音乐，你是不会常常听得到的。」

===Original===
"I am glad of that," she cried simply, then in a quick conscious tone explained, "I mean that the hearing of such music makes an era in our life, a starting-point for thoughts that reach away into eternity; we could not bear such experiences often, it would confuse the spirit if not deaden its enjoyment. Or so it seems to me," she added naively, glancing at her cousin who now came sweeping in from the further room, where she had been trying the effect of a change in the arrangement of two little pet monstrosities of Japanese ware.

"What seems to you?" that lady inquired. "O, Mr. Mandeville's playing? I beg pardon, Sylvester is the name by which you now wish to be addressed I suppose. Fine, isn't it?" she rambled on all in the same tone while she cautiously hid an unfortunate gape of her rosy mouth behind the folds of her airy handkerchief. "Mr. Turner says the hiatus you have made in the musical world by leaving the concert room for the desk, can never be repaired," she went on, supposedly to her nephew though she did not look his way, being at that instant engaged in sinking into her favorite chair.

===Chinese===
「那我倒高兴。」她天真地喊道，随即又用一种忙不迭自觉的口吻解释道，「我是说，听到这样的音乐，是咱们一生里头一桩划得着时代的大事，是一片起点，从这儿发出来的念头，能一路远远地伸到永恒里去；这一类的经历，咱们原受不了常常有，它若不叫一颗心麻木了感受，便要叫它乱了方寸。至少我是这样觉着的。」她又天真地补了一句，一面瞟了一眼她的表姐——她这会儿正从那一头的屋里一阵风似的卷进来，方才她在那里试换着两只她宠爱的日本小怪物摆设的位置，看看效果如何。

「你怎么觉着来着？」那位夫人问，「啊，是曼德维尔先生弹琴？对不住，你如今愿人叫你西尔维斯特，我猜是吧。好得很呐，是不是？」她一路信口说下去，全然是那一种腔调，一面又小心翼翼地把她那张樱桃小口一个煞风景的哈欠掩到了那方轻罗手帕的褶子背后。「特纳先生（Mr. Turner）说，你丢下音乐厅坐到写字台前，给乐坛留下的那道缺憾，是再也无法填补的了。」她又往下说，这话照理是对她侄子说的，可她眼睛并不朝他那边瞧——她那会儿正忙着把自己沉进那张她最心爱的椅子里去。

===Original===
"I am glad," Bertram politely returned with a frank smile, "to have enjoyed the approval of so cultivated a critic as Mr. Turner. I own it occasions me a pang now and then," he remarked to his uncle over his shoulder, "to think I shall never again call up those looks of self-forgetful delight, which I have sometimes detected on the faces of certain ones in my audience."

And he relapsed without pause into a solemn anthem, the very reverse of the stirring tones which he had previously accorded them.

"Now we are in a temple!" whispered Paula, subduing the sudden interest and curiosity which this young man's last words had awakened. And the awe which crept over her countenance was the fittest interpretation to those noble sounds, which the one weary-hearted man in that room could have found.

===Chinese===
「我能得到像特纳先生这般有修养的鉴赏家的赞许，」伯特兰彬彬有礼地答道，坦率地笑了笑，「实在荣幸。我承认，」他越过肩膀对叔父说道，「一想到我此后再也唤不起那种忘我的欣悦之色——我从前有时能从我听众里几位脸上瞧出的那种神色——我倒也间或感到一阵心痛。」

说着他便不停歇地滑入了一支肃穆的颂歌，与方才给他们的那一支激昂之曲恰恰相反。

「这会儿我们可算是进了座神庙啦！」宝拉悄声说，把这位年轻人末了那几句话在她心头勾起的突发的兴味和好奇按捺下去。爬上她脸容的那种敬畏之色，正是这一派崇高之音所能寻得的最相称的诠释了——这一份诠释，正是那屋里那唯一的一颗疲惫的心所能寻得的。

===Original===
"I have something to tell you, Ona," remarked Mr. Sylvester shortly after this, as the music being over, they all sat down for a final chat about the fireside. "I have received notice that the directors of the Madison Bank have this day elected me their president. I thought you might like to know it tonight."

"It is a very gratifying piece of news certainly. President of the Madison Bank sounds very well, does it not, Paula?"

The young girl with her soul yet ringing with the grand and solemn harmonies of Mendelssohn and Chopin, turned at this with her brightest smile. "It certainly does and a little awe-inspiring too;" she added with her arch glance.

===Chinese===
「我有件事要告诉你，奥娜。」过了一会儿，西尔维斯特先生说道——此时曲已终，众人皆围炉坐下，作最后一番夜话。「我接到通知，麦迪逊银行的董事们今日已举我做他们的行长。我想你今夜便愿意知道这事。」

「这自然是十分叫人欣慰的消息。麦迪逊银行的行长，听上去蛮不错，可不是么，宝拉？」

这姑娘那一颗心还在门德尔松和肖邦那宏大肃穆的和声里震荡着，闻言便转过脸来，露出她最明媚的笑。「的确是的，而且听着还有几分叫人敬畏呢。」她那一道调皮的眼色又补了一句。

===Original===
"Your congratulations are also requested for our new assistant cashier. Arise, Bertram, and greet the ladies."

With a blush his young nephew arose to his feet.

"What! are you going into the banking business?" queried Mrs. Sylvester. "Mr. Turner will be more shocked than ever: he chooses to say that bankers, merchants and such are the solid rock of his church, while the lighter fry such as artists, musicians, and let us hope he includes us ladies, are its minarets, and steeples. Now to make a foundation out of a steeple will quite overturn his methodical mind I fear."

Mr. Sylvester looked genially at his wife; she was not accustomed to attempt the facetious; but Paula seemed to have the power of bringing out unexpected lights and shadows from all with whom she came in contact.

===Chinese===
「咱们这位新任的助理出纳员，也有份讨你道喜呢。起来，伯特兰，给夫人们见个礼。」

年轻的侄子红着脸站起身来。

「怎么！你要进银行做事啦？」西尔维斯特夫人问道。「特纳先生可要更吃惊了：他最爱说，银行家、商人这一干人等，是他那座教会的坚石磐基；至于艺术家、音乐家这一类轻飘飘的人物——但愿他也把咱们这些太太小姐们算在这一类里——便是那教会的细塔尖顶。如今竟要把一座塔尖拿来作基，我瞧他那颗讲求条理的脑袋，可要大大地被搅翻了。」

西尔维斯特先生和颜悦色地望着妻子；她素不惯于尝试诙谐这一道；可宝拉身上，似乎天生便有一种本事，能从所有与她接触的人身上，激出些意想不到的光影明暗来。

===Original===
"A clergyman who rears his church on the basis of wealth must expect some overturning now and then," laughed he.

"If by means of it he turns a fresh side to the sun, it will do him no harm," chimed in Paula.

Seldom had there been so much simple gaiety round that fireside; the very atmosphere grew lighter, and the brilliance of my lady's picture became less oppressive.

"We ought to have a happy winter of it," spoke up Mr. Sylvester with a glance around him. "Life never looked more cheerful for us all, I think; what do you say, Bertram my boy."

"It certainly looks promising for me."

"And for me," murmured Paula.

The complacent way with which Mrs. Sylvester smoothed out the feathers of her fan with her jewelled right hand—she always carried a fan winter and summer, some said for the purpose of displaying those same jewelled fingers—was sufficient answer for her.

===Chinese===
「一位牧师若把他的教会立在财帛这一层根脚上，自然就得预备着偶尔被搅翻一搅翻。」他笑道。

「若借此搅他一搅，叫他把另一面朝向太阳晒一晒，那倒也于他无损。」宝拉接了上去。

炉边许久不曾有过这许多质朴的欢悦了；连这一屋子空气仿佛都轻快了些许，夫人那幅画像上耀目的光彩，也不那么叫人喘不过气来了。

「我们这一冬该过得挺快活的。」西尔维斯特先生开口道，目光环顾了一下四周，「我想，咱们一家的日子，从来没有瞧着比此刻更叫人开怀的了；你说呢，我的孩子伯特兰？」

「我这边瞧着，前景的确大好。」

「我也是。」宝拉低声道。

至于西尔维斯特夫人——她用那只戴满珠宝的右手，自得地把折扇上的羽毛一翎一翎地理顺——她一年到头冬夏都携着一柄扇子，有人说那原是为炫示她这双戴满珠宝的手指——她这一副神情，便尽够替她作答了。

===Original===
At that moment there was a hush, when suddenly the small clock on the mantelpiece struck eleven, and instantly as if awaiting the signal, there came a rush and a heavy crash which drew everyone to their feet, and the brilliant portrait of my lady fell from the wall, and toppling over the cabinet beneath, slid with the various articles of bronze and china thereon, almost to the very chair in which its handsome prototype had been sitting.

It was a startling interruption and for an instant no one spoke, then Paula with a look towards her cousin breathed to herself rather than said, "Pray God it be not an omen!" And the pale countenances of the two gentlemen standing face to face on either side of that fallen picture, showed that the shadow of the same superstition had insensibly crossed their own minds.

===Chinese===
正在这一刻，四下里忽然一静——忽然之间，壁炉架上那只小钟敲起了十一下；霎时间，仿佛就单等着这个信号似的，传来一阵呼啸与一声重重的轰然巨响，把众人都惊得站了起来——夫人那幅光彩夺目的画像从墙上摔了下来，越过下方那只橱柜的顶一路翻倒，连同上面那几件铜器瓷器一起，几乎滑到了那位美貌的原型本人方才端坐的那张椅子跟前。

这一声惊扰实在非同小可，有一刹那谁都没作声；随后宝拉朝她表姐那边望了一眼，与其说是说出口，不如说是自言自语地吐出了那么一句：「求上帝保佑这不是个凶兆！」而那两位相对立在画像两侧的先生苍白的脸色，分明表示出，同一缕迷信的阴影，也已不知不觉掠过了他俩的心头。

===Original===
Mrs. Sylvester was the only one who remained unmoved. "Lift if up," cried she, "and let us see if it has sustained any injury."

Instantly Bertram and her husband sprang forward, and in a moment its glowing surface was turned upward. Who could read the meaning of the look that crossed her husband's face as he perceived that the sharp spear of the bronze horseman, which had been overturned in the fall, had penetrated the rosy countenance of the portrait and destroyed that importunate smile forever.

"I suppose it is a judgment upon me for putting all the money you had allowed me for charitable purposes, into that exquisite bit of bronze," observed Mrs. Sylvester, stooping above the overturned horseman with an expression of regret she had not chosen to bestow on her own ruined picture. "Ah he is less of a champion than I imagined; he has lost his spear in the struggle."

===Chinese===
西尔维斯特夫人是唯一不为所动的一位。「把它抬起来，」她喊道，「咱们瞧瞧它可损伤了没有。」

伯特兰和她的丈夫立时抢上前去，顷刻之间，那幅画像光彩熠熠的正面便被翻转朝上。谁能读出她丈夫脸上此时掠过的那一丝神情是什么意思呢——他发觉，方才那一跤里被推翻的那位青铜骑手的尖利长矛，竟自刺穿了画像上那张红润的脸容，把那副咄咄逼人的笑靥，永远地毁掉了。

「我想这倒是对我的一项报应呢——谁叫我把你给我的那笔慈善款项，全花在了那一件精致的铜器上。」西尔维斯特夫人说道，俯身在那位翻倒的骑手之上，那种惋惜的神情，她方才可没肯施舍给她自家那幅被毁的画像。「啊，他这做护花的英雄，可比我想象的差远了；这一番较量里，他连自家的长矛都丢了。」

===Original===
Paula glanced at her cousin in surprise. Was this pleasantry only a veil assumed by this courtly lady to hide her very natural regret over the more serious accident? Even her husband turned toward her with a certain puzzled inquiry in his troubled countenance. But her expression of unconcern was too natural; evidently the destruction of the picture had awakened but small regret in her volatile mind.

"She is less vain than I thought," was the inward comment of Paula.

Ah simple child of the woods and streams, it is the extent of her vanity not the lack of it, that has produced this effect. She has begun to realize that ten years have elapsed since this picture was painted, and that people are beginning to say as they examine it, "Mrs. Sylvester has not yet lost her complexion, I see."

===Chinese===
宝拉诧异地瞥了表姐一眼。这一番戏谑，难道只是这位雍容夫人用来遮掩她对这一桩更严重的事故所自然生出的惋惜的一层面纱么？连她的丈夫也带着一脸困惑探询的神色转向她。可她那副毫不在意的神情实在太过自然；显然，这幅画的毁灭，并不曾叫她那颗浮薄的心生出多少惋惜。

「她的虚荣心倒比我想的少呢。」宝拉心里这样暗评了一句。

啊，你这山林溪泉间长大的单纯孩子，叫她这般淡然的，并非她虚荣之少，倒是她虚荣之多啊。她已经开始意识到，自这幅画像画成以来，已整整过了十年；而人们端详这幅画像时，已开始说：「瞧，西尔维斯特夫人的容颜竟还未褪色呢。」

===Original===
A break necessarily followed this disturbance, and before long Bertram took his leave, not without a cordial pressure from his uncle's hand and a look of kindly interest from the stranger lassie, upon whose sympathetic and imaginative mind the hints let fall as to his former profession, had produced a deep impression. With his departure Mrs. Sylvester's weariness returned, and ere long she led the way to her apartments upstairs. As Paula was hastening to follow Mr. Sylvester stopped her.

"You will not allow this unfortunate occurrence," he said, with a slight gesture towards the picture now standing with its face against the wall, "to mar your first sleep under my roof, will you Paula, my child?"

"No, not if you say that you think Cousin Ona will not be likely to connect it with my appearance here."

"I do not think she will; she is not superstitious and besides does not seem to greatly regret the misfortune."

"Then I will forget it all and only remember the music."

"It was all you anticipated?"

"It was more."

"Sometime I will tell you about the player and the sweet young girl he loves."

"Does he—" she paused, blushing; love was a subject upon which she had never yet spoken to anyone.

"Yes he does," Mr. Sylvester returned smiling.

===Chinese===
出了这一桩骚乱，自然免不了一番收拾；不久伯特兰便告辞了，行时既得了叔父一记热忱的握手，又得了那位素昧平生的小姑娘一道关切的、善意的眼色——她那一颗富于同情、富于想象的心，已为他方才漏下的、关于他从前那门职业的几句口风，深深地打上了印记。他一走，西尔维斯特夫人的倦意又涌了上来，不多时她便领头往楼上的寝室去了。宝拉正急急地跟着要走，西尔维斯特先生把她叫住了。

「你这头一夜睡在我家屋檐底下，总不至于让这一桩不幸的意外，」他说着，朝那幅此刻脸朝墙立着的画像微微一抬手，「扫了你的兴罢，会吗，我的孩子宝拉？」

「不会的；只要您说，您瞧着表姐奥娜未必会把这事跟我来这里这件事牵到一块儿。」

「我想她不会；她并不迷信，况且她看上去对这桩不幸也并不怎样惋惜。」

「那我便把这事整个儿忘了，只记着今夜的音乐好了。」

「它一如你所盼望的么？」

「有过之。」

「改日我再同你说，那位弹琴的人，以及他所爱的那一位温柔的少女。」

「他可——」她顿住了，红起脸来；爱情这一桩题目，她从前还不曾与任何人谈起过。

「是的，他是的。」西尔维斯特先生微笑着答道。

===Original===
"I thought there was a meaning in the music I did not quite understand. Good night, uncle,"—he had requested her to address him thus though he was in truth her cousin, "and many, many thanks."

But he stopped her again. "You think you will be happy in these rooms," said he; "you love splendor."

She was not yet sufficiently acquainted with his voice to detect the regret underlying its kindly tone, and answered without suspicion. "I did not know it before, but I fear that I do. It dazzled at first, but now it seems as if I had reached a home towards which I had always been journeying. I shall dream away hours of joy before each little ornament that adorns your parlors. The very tiles that surround the fireplace will demand a week of attention at least."

She ended with a smile, but unlike formerly he did not seem to catch the infection. "I had rather you had cared less," said he, but instantly regretted the seeming reproach, for her eyes filled with tears and the tones of her voice trembled as she replied,

"Do you think the beauty I have seen has made me forget the kindness that has brought me here? I love fine and noble objects, glory of color and harmony of shape, but more than all these do I love a generous soul without a blot on its purity, or a flaw in its integrity."

===Chinese===
「我就觉着，那音乐里头还藏着一层意思，我不大懂得。晚安，伯父，」——他虽其实是她表兄一辈，却曾要她这般称呼他——「多谢、多谢您了。」

可他又把她叫住了。「你想，你在这几间屋子里会过得快活，」他说，「你是爱热闹、爱排场的。」

她对他那嗓音还不够熟，听不出那和善之下所掩的一缕惋惜，便一无戒心地答道：「我从前倒不晓得自己是这样，可我怕是当真爱排场的。这头一眼是晃得我眼花，可这会儿我倒觉着，自己仿佛是到了一处我素来趱路要去的地方——可算到了家了。您那几间起居室里每一件小摆设跟前，我都够痴痴地消磨上好几个时辰。光是壁炉四周的那一圈花砖，少说也得叫我端详上一个礼拜。」

她说着末了抿嘴一笑；可这一回他却像从前那样未能被她感染。「我倒宁愿你爱的少些。」他说，可话一出口便懊悔这像是责备了；因为她两眼立时盈满了泪水，话音也颤了起来，答道：

「您难道以为，我所瞧见的这番华美，已叫我忘怀了把我领到这里来的那一片好意？我是爱那些精美高贵之物，爱颜色之辉煌、形制之和谐；可这一概，我都远不及爱一颗宽宏的心来得深——一颗灵魂，其纯洁上无半点瑕疵，其正直上亦无一丝破绽。」

===Original===
She had meant to utter something that would show her appreciation of his goodness and the universal esteem in which he was held, but was quite unprepared for the start that he gave and the unmistakable deepening of the shadow on his sombre face. But before she could express her regret at the offence, whatever it was, he had recovered himself, and it was with a fatherly tenderness that he laid his hand upon hers while he said, "Such a soul may yours ever continue, my child," and then stood watching her as she glided up the stairs, her charming face showing every now and then as she leaned on her winding way to the top, to bestow upon him the tender little smile she had already learned was his solace and delight.

It was the beginning of happier days for him.

===Chinese===
她原想说几句话，既表自家的感激，也称颂那天下人对他一致的敬爱；可他猛地一惊、那张阴郁的脸上一道阴影无可错认地加深——这两桩，却是她始料未及的。还不等她把那份冒犯——无论那是怎么一桩冒犯——的歉意说出口，他已然镇定下来；他以一种慈父般的温柔，把自己的手覆在她的手上，说道：「愿你这一颗灵魂，能永远如此，我的孩子。」说罢便立在那里，目送她上楼去；她那可爱的脸，在那一段蜿蜒而上的楼梯转角处，不时探出来朝他投下温柔的小小一笑——她已经学得，这一笑是他的一份安慰，一份喜悦。

这于他，是一段更快乐的日子开端。

## XLV “The Hour of Six Is Sacred” / 四十五 「六点钟这一刻是神圣的」

===Original===
> "Mightier far

 Than strength of nerve or sinew, or the sway

 Of magic potent over sun and star,

 Is love, though oft to agony distrest,
> And though its favorite seat be feeble woman's breast."

===Chinese===
> 「远为强大的，
> 胜过筋骨之力，胜过那
> 统御日月星辰的魔法之力，
> 是爱——纵然它常常苦痛到极处，
> 纵然它最爱的栖所，是柔弱女子的胸怀。」

===Original===
It was at the close of a winter afternoon. Paula who had returned to Grotewell for the few weeks preceding her marriage, sat musing in the window of her aunt's quaint little parlor. Her eyes were on the fields before her all rosy with the departing rays of the sun, but her thoughts were far away. They were with him she best loved—with Cicely, waiting in patience for the solution of the mystery of the stolen bonds; with Bertram, eagerly, but as yet vainly, engaged in searching for the vanished janitor; and last but not least, with that poor, wretched specimen of humanity moaning away her life in a New York hospital;—for the sight of the Japha house, in a walk that day, had reawakened her most vivid remembrances of Jacqueline. All that had ever been done and suffered by this forsaken creature, lay on her heart like a weight; and the question which had disturbed her since her return to Grotewell, viz., whether or not she ought to acquaint Mrs. Hamlin with the fact that she had seen and spoken to the object of her love and prayers, pressed upon her mind with an insistence that required an answer. There was so much to be said for and against it. Mrs. Hamlin was not well, and though still able to continue her vigil, showed signs of weakening, day by day. It might be a comfort to her to know that another's eyes had rested on the haggard form for whose approach she daily watched; that another's kiss had touched the scarred and pallid forehead she longed to fold against her breast; that the woman she loved and of whose fate she had no intimation, was living and well cared for, though her shelter was that of a hospital, and her prospects those of the grave.

On the other hand, the awful nature of the circumstances which had brought her to her present condition, were such as to make any generous heart pause before shocking the love and trust of such a woman as Mrs. Hamlin, by a relation of the criminal act by which Jacqueline had slain her child and endangered her own existence. Better let the poor old lady go on hoping against hope till she sinks into her grave, than destroy life and hope at once by a revelation of her darling's reckless depravity.

And yet if the poor creature in the hospital might be moved to repentance by some word from Mrs. Hamlin, would it not be a kindness to the latter to allow her, though even at the risk of her life, to accomplish the end for which she indeed professed to live?

===Chinese===
那是一个冬日下午的傍晚时分。宝拉（Paula）回到格罗特韦尔（Grotewell）准备过这几周就要成婚了，此刻正坐在她姑母那间古雅小客厅的窗前出神。她的目光落在眼前一片田野上，那田野被夕阳的余晖染得通红一片，可她的心思却飞到了远方。她的心飞向了她最爱的那个人；飞向了西塞莉（Cicely），她正耐心等待着那桩失窃债券之谜能够水落石出；飞向了伯特兰（Bertram），他正热切地——却至今徒劳地——四处寻找那个失踪的看门人；最后，也同样要紧的，飞向了那个可怜的、悲惨的人，那个正在纽约一家医院里哀吟着熬过余生的女子——因为那天散步时瞥见雅法家的宅子，又把她对雅克琳最为鲜活的记忆一并勾了起来。这个被遗弃之人所做过、所承受过的一切，像一块重石压在宝拉的心头。而自她回到格罗特韦尔以来，一直有一桩事在她心头萦绕不去——那便是：她究竟该不该把她已经见过、也曾与之说过话这件事，告知哈姆林夫人（Mrs. Hamlin）——这个她所爱、所日夜祈求的人。这个问题以一种非要得到一个答案的执拗，压迫着她的心思。这事说起来，赞成与反对的理由都有许多。哈姆林夫人身子不大爽快，虽说还能勉强继续她的守候，却已一日一日显出衰弱的样子。倘若让她知道，另有一双眼睛也曾凝视过她日日盼望其归来的那个憔悴身影；另一双嘴唇也曾吻过她渴望搂进怀里的那道疤痕斑斑、苍白惨淡的额头；她所爱、又对其命运一无所知的那个人，如今还活着，也有人好好照应着——尽管她栖身之处不过是一家医院，她的前景不过是坟墓——倘若让她知道这些，或许于她也是一种慰藉罢。

可在另一方面，把雅克琳弄到今日这般地步的那桩变故，其性质之可怕，又足以叫任何一个宽厚的心肠，在三思之后，仍不敢贸然用那一桩罪行的述说，去惊扰像哈姆林夫人这样一个人的爱心与信赖——须知正是那桩罪行，雅克琳才亲手害死了自己的孩子，也险些送了自己的性命。倒不如让这可怜的老太太怀着那一线渺茫的希望继续等下去，直到她沉沉地躺进坟墓里，也好过用一番披露，道出她那心头肉是怎样一意孤行、自甘堕落，从而一下子把她的性命和指望都一并毁掉。

然而，倘若医院里那可怜人能被哈姆林夫人的一句话所感动，从而幡然悔悟，那么允许她——哪怕要冒着自己性命的危险——去完成她口口声声说是她活着所为的那桩心愿，这于她岂不反倒是一种恩慈么？

===Original===
The mind of Paula was as yet undecided, when a child from the village passed the window, and seeing her sitting there, handed her a small package with the simple message that Mrs. Hamlin was very ill. It contained, as she anticipated, the great key to the Japha mansion, and understanding without further words, what was demanded of her, Paula prepared to keep the promise she had long ago made to this devoted woman. For though she knew the uselessness of the vigil proposed to her, she nonetheless determined to complete it. Easier to sit an hour in that dark old house, than to explain herself to Mrs. Hamlin. Besides, the time was good for prayer, and God knows the wretched object of all this care and anxiety, stood in need of all the petitions that might be raised for her.

Telling her aunts that she had a call to make in the village, she glided hurriedly away, and ere she realized all to which she was committed, found herself standing in the now darkened streets, before the grim door of that dread and mysterious mansion. Never had it looked more forbidding; never had the two gruesome poplars cast a deeper shadow, or rustled with a more woeful sound in the chill evening air. The very windows seemed to repel her with their darkened panes, behind which she could easily imagine the spirits of the dead, moving and peering. A chill not unlike that of terror, assailed her limbs, and it was with a really heroic action that she finally opened the gate and glided up the path made by the daily steps of her aged friend. To thrust the big key into the lock required another effort, but that once accomplished, she stilled every tumultuous beating of her heart, by crying under her breath, "She has done this for one whom she has not seen for fifteen years; shall I then hesitate, who know the real necessity of her for whom this hour is made sacred?"

===Chinese===
宝拉的心思尚未拿定，村里一个孩童正打窗前过，一眼瞧见她坐在那儿，便递给她一个小包，只附了简简单单一句话：哈姆林夫人病得很重。包里装的，果如她所料，是那把雅法大宅的大钥匙。宝拉不必再要多言，便已明白要她做的是什么，于是着手去兑现她早先许给这位痴心之人的诺言。因为她虽然明知这桩守夜于事无补，却仍旧决意把它做完。到那昏暗的旧宅里坐上一个钟头，总比向哈姆林夫人分说缘由要容易些。况且这个时辰正宜祷告，而天知道，这一切牵挂与焦虑所系的那个可怜人，正需要有人为她献上一切所能献上的祈求。

她告诉几位姑母，说是村里有一处礼要拜访，便匆匆地溜了出去。等她恍然意识到自己已应承下的是怎样一件事时，她已立在如今已黑下来的街上了——正立在那座阴森可怖、神秘莫测的宅子那扇严峻的大门前。那宅子从来不曾显得这般拒人于千里之外；那两棵阴森的白杨树从来不曾投下这般浓重的阴影，也从来不曾在寒夜的冷风里簌簌作响得这般凄凉。便是那一扇扇窗户，也仿佛用它们那漆黑的玻璃在排斥她——在那黑玻璃背后，她很容易就想象出亡魂的鬼影在游移窥探。一阵近乎恐惧般的寒意袭上她的四肢，而她终于推开院门、沿着那条由她这位老友日日脚步踏出的小径走上去时，确乎是一种真正的英勇之举。要把那把大钥匙塞进锁孔，还须再使一把劲；可这一旦做成，她便用一句压在喉咙底下的低呼，按下了心头每一阵狂乱的跳动：「她为一个十五年来不曾见过的人尚且如此；我既深知这一个为她而定为神圣的时辰里，藏着怎样的迫切，难道反倒要犹豫么？」

===Original===
The slow swinging open of the door was like an ushering into the abode of ghosts, but she struck a light at once, and soon had the satisfaction of beholding the dismal room with its weird shadows, resolve into its old and well remembered aspect. The ancient cabinet and stiff haircloth sofa, Colonel Japha's chair by the table, together with all the other objects that had attracted her attention in her former visit, confronted her again with the same appearance of standing ready and waiting, which had previously so thrilled her. Only she was alone this time, and terror mingled with her awe. She scarcely dared to glance at the doors that led to other portions of the house. In her present mood it would seem so natural for them to swing open, and let upon her horrified gaze the stately phantom of the proud old colonel or the gentler shade of Jacqueline's mother. The moan of the wind in the chimney was dreadful to her, and the faint rumbling sounds of mice scampering in the walls, made her start as though a voice had spoken.

But presently the noise of a sleigh careering by the house recalled her to herself, and remembering it was but early nightfall, she sat down in a chair by the door, and prepared to keep her vigil with suitable patience and equanimity. Suddenly she recollected the clock on the mantelpiece and how she had seen Mrs. Hamlin wind it, and rising up, she followed her example, sighing unconsciously to find how many of the sixty minutes had yet to tick themselves away, "Can I endure it!" she thought, and shuddered as she pictured to herself the dim old staircase behind those doors, and the empty rooms above, and the little Bible lying thicker than ever with dust, on the yellowed pillows of Jacqueline's bed.

===Chinese===
门扇缓缓地朝里荡开，像是由人领进了鬼魂的居所，但她立刻打了个火，不久便欣慰地看见，那间阴沉沉的屋子连同它那些诡异的阴影，一点点还原成它旧日那副她记忆犹新的模样。那只古老的橱柜、那张硬邦邦的马毛布面沙发，杰法上校（Colonel Japha）放在桌旁的那把椅子，以及她上次来访时曾引起她注意的种种物件，又一齐摆在她面前，仍是那副「早已备好、正等着什么」的神气——正是这副神气，上回曾叫她心头为之一震。只是这一回她是独自一人，恐惧便和她的敬畏掺在了一起。她几乎不敢朝通向宅子其余各处的几扇门瞥上一眼。以她此刻的心境，那些门仿佛很自然地便要朝里荡开，把她惊恐的目光迎上那位傲骨铮铮的老上校的庄严鬼影，或是雅克琳母亲那较为柔和的幽魂。风在烟囱里的呜咽，在她听来可怖极了；老鼠在墙壁里奔跑时发出的窸窸窣窣的细响，也叫她猛地一惊，仿佛有一道嗓音在她耳畔开口说话。

但不一会儿，一辆雪橇从宅前疾驶而过的声响，又把她唤回到自己身上来。她想起此刻不过天刚黑，便在门边的一把椅子上坐下来，预备以与之相称的耐心与镇定，守完这一夜。忽然，她记起了壁炉台上的那座钟，记起她曾见哈姆林夫人怎样给它上发条；于是她站起身，学着她的样儿，也照做了一遍，一边不知不觉地叹了口气，只见那六十分钟里还有多少未走完。「我挨得过么！」她心想，一想到那几扇门背后那座昏暗的旧楼梯，楼上那一间间空屋子，还有那本小小的《圣经》——此刻积满了比从前更厚的灰尘，正摊在雅克琳那张床的泛黄枕头上——她便不寒而栗。

===Original===
Suddenly she stood still; the noise she had just heard, was not made by the pattering of mice along the rafters, or even the creaking of the withered vines that clung against the walls! It was a human sound, a clicking as of the gate without, a crunching as of feet dragging slowly over the snow. Was Mrs. Hamlin coming after all, or—she could not formulate her fear; a real and palpable danger from the outside world had never crossed her fancy till now. What if some stranger should enter, some tramp, some—a step on the porch without made her hair rise on her forehead; she clasped her hands and stood trembling, when a sudden moan startled her ears, followed by the sound of a heavy fall on the threshold, and throwing aside all hesitation, she flung herself forward, and tearing open the door, saw—oh, angels that rejoice in heaven over one sinner that repenteth, let your voices go up in praise this night, for Jacqueline Japha has returned to the home of her fathers!

===Chinese===
忽然她定住了脚步；她方才听见的那个声响，绝不是老鼠顺着椽子奔跑的窸窣声，也不是攀附在墙上的枯藤所发出的吱嘎声！那是人的声响，像是外头院门的搭扣响了一声，又像是脚拖着步子在雪地上慢慢碾过的咯吱声。莫非哈姆林夫人终究还是来了，抑或——她不敢把自己的恐惧想个明白；从外头世界而来的、真真切切的危险，直到此刻，竟从未掠过她的脑际。倘若有个陌生人闯进来，倘若是个流浪汉，倘若——门外廊上一记脚步声，惊得她额前的头发都竖了起来；她紧攥着双手，浑身颤抖地立在那里。忽然一声呻吟刺入她耳中，紧接着便是门槛上一声沉沉的倒地的声响。她一把抛开所有的犹豫，抢步上前，猛地拉开那扇门，只见——啊，在天上为着一个悔罪的罪人而欢喜的天使啊，让你们的歌声今夜都化作赞美罢，因为雅克琳·雅法（Jacqueline Japha）已经回到了她祖父亲的家中！

===Original===
She had fainted, and lay quite still on the threshold, but Paula, who was all energy now, soon had her in the centre of the sitting-room, and was applying to her such restoratives as had been provided against this very emergency. She was holding the poor weary head on her knee, when the wan eyes opened, and looking up, grew wild with a disappointment which Paula was quick to appreciate.

"You are looking for Margery," said she. "Margery will come by-and-by; she is not well tonight and I am taking her place, but when she hears you have returned, it will take more than sickness to keep her to her bed. I am Paula, and I love you, too, and welcome you—oh, welcome you so gladly."

The yearning look which had crept into the woman's bleared and faded eyes, deepened and softened strangely.

"You are the one who told me about Margery," said she, "and bade me bring my baby here to be buried. I remember, though I seemed to pay no heed then. Night and day through all my pain, I have remembered, and as soon as I could walk, stole away from the hospital. It has killed me, but I shall at least die in my father's house."

Paula stooped and kissed her. "I am going to get your bed ready," said she. And without any hesitation now, she opened the door that led into those dim inner regions that but a few minutes before had inspired her with such dread.

===Chinese===
她已经晕了过去，一动不动地躺在门槛上。可此刻浑身是劲的宝拉，不多时便把她挪到了起居室正中，正为她施用那些专为这一桩意外而预备好的提神之物。她正把那颗可怜的、疲惫不堪的头捧在自己膝上，那双黯淡的眼睛忽然睁了开来，仰面望上去，随即因一股失望而变得狂乱——这失望，宝拉立刻便心领神会。

「你在找玛吉丽（Margery），」她说。「玛吉丽随后就到；她今夜身上不好，我便是来替她的。可她一听说你回来了，要她躺在床上可就难了，再重的病也拴不住她。我是宝拉，我也爱你，也欢迎你——啊，这样高高兴兴地欢迎你回来。」

那女子那双浑浊黯淡的眼里悄悄爬上来的那股渴慕之色，奇怪地变深了，也变柔了。

「你便是那个告诉我玛吉丽之事的人，」她说，「便是那个叫我把我那孩子带到这儿来安葬的人。我记得的，虽说那时候我好像全没在意。日日夜夜里，穿过我所有的苦痛，我都记着；等我一旦能够下地走路了，我便从医院里偷偷溜了出来。这一来是要了我的命了，可我总算能死在我父亲家里了。」

宝拉俯下身去吻了她。「我去给你把床铺好。」她说。这一回她再不犹豫了，推开那扇通往那几处昏暗内室去的门——而几分钟之前，那里头还叫她怕得要命。

===Original===
She went straight to Jacqueline's room. "It must all be according to Mrs. Hamlin's wishes," she cried, and lit the fire on the hearth, and pulled back the curtains yet farther from the bed, and gave the benefit of her womanly touch to the various objects about her, till cheerfulness seemed to reign in a spot once so peopled with hideous memories. Going back to Jacqueline, she helped her to rise, and throwing her arm about her waist, led her into the hall. But here memory, ghastly accusing memory, stepped in, and catching the wretched woman in its grasp, shook her, body and soul, till her shrieks reverberated through that desolate house. But Paula with gentle persistence urged her on, and smiling upon her like an angel of peace and mercy, led her up step after step of that dreadful staircase, till at last she saw her safely in the room of her early girlhood.

The sight of it seemed at first to horrify but afterwards to soothe the forlorn being thus brought face to face with her own past. She moved over to the fire and held out her two cramped hands to the blaze, as if she saw an altar of mercy in its welcoming glow. From these she passed tottering and weak to the embroidery-frame, which she looked at for a moment with something almost like a smile; but she hurried by the mirror, and scarcely glanced at a portrait of herself which hung on the wall over her head. To sink on the bed seemed to be her object, and thither Paula accompanied her. But when she came to where it stood, and saw the clothes turned down and the pillows heaped at the head, and the little Bible lying open for her in the midst, she gave a great and mighty sob, and flinging herself down upon her knees, wept with a breaking up of her whole nature, in which her sins, red though they were as crimson, seemed to feel the touch of the Divine love, and vanish away in the oblivion He prepares for all His penitent ones.

===Chinese===
她径直朝雅克琳的房间走去。「这一切都须得照着哈姆林夫人的心意来。」她喊道，便在炉膛里点起了火，把床帐从床边又拉开了一些，又以她那女人家的细心，把周围种种物件一一理了个妥帖，直弄得这处曾经满是可怖记忆的地方，竟像有了一股欢快的气象。她回到雅克琳身边，扶她站起来，一只胳膊搂住她的腰，引她走进过厅。可就在这儿，记忆——那阴惨惨、声声指控的记忆——横身拦了进来，一把攫住这可怜的女子，摇撼着她的身子与灵魂，直到她的尖叫声回荡在那座空荡荡的宅子里。可宝拉只是柔声地、不肯放松地催她往前，像一位和平与怜悯的天使那样朝她微笑着，领她一级一级地登上那段可怖的楼梯，直到终于亲眼看着她平平安安地进了她少女时代住过的那间屋子。

这屋子的模样，起初似乎反倒叫这孤立无援的人心惊，随后却又抚慰了她——她就这样被带到自己过往的面前，与之面面相觑。她挪到炉火跟前，把两只痉挛的手伸向那一炉熊熊的火，仿佛在它那迎人的红光里，看见了一座慈悲的祭坛。她从那里又踉踉跄跄、虚弱无力地走到那架绣花绷子跟前，对着它端详了片刻，嘴角几乎浮起一丝像是微笑的神气；可她匆匆地走过那面镜子，对悬在自己头顶墙上的一幅本人画像，几乎不曾瞥一眼。她的目的仿佛是扑到床上去，宝拉便也陪着她走到那里。可当她走到床边，看见被褥已经掀开、枕头高高地堆在床头，那本小小的《圣经》正摊开摆在当中等着她——她猛地发出一声又大又沉的呜咽，扑通一声跪倒在地，哭了出来，哭得像整个人都要裂开似的；在这一场痛哭里，她那些虽红如朱红的罪，仿佛也触到了神那慈爱的手，便在那为一切悔罪之人所预备的遗忘里，烟消云散了。

===Original===
When everything was prepared and Jacqueline was laid quiet in bed, Paula stole out and down the stairs and wended her way to Mrs. Hamlin's cottage. She found her sitting up, but far from well, and very feeble. At the first sight of Paula's face, she started erect and seem to forget her weakness in a moment.

"What is it?" she asked; "you look as though you had been gazing on the faces of angels. Has—has my hope come true at last? Has Jacqueline returned? Oh, has my poor, lost, erring child come back?"

Paula drew near and gently steadied Mrs. Hamlin's swaying form. "Yes," she smiled; and with the calmness of one who has entered the gates of peace, whispered in low and reverent tones: "She lies in the bed that you spread for her, with the Bible held close to her breast."

===Chinese===
待一切都备齐、雅克琳也安安静静地躺在床上之后，宝拉悄悄溜出门，下了楼，一路朝哈姆林夫人那所小屋走去。她见她坐了起来，可气色很不好，身子也虚极了。哈姆林夫人一见宝拉的脸色，猛地直起身来，那一刻似乎把自己身上的虚弱全忘了。

「怎么了？」她问，「你看上去像是刚望过天使的脸。莫非——莫非我的盼望终于成真了？雅克琳回来了？啊，我那可怜的、失落的、走错了路的孩子，回来了么？」

宝拉走上前去，轻轻地扶住了哈姆林夫人摇晃的身子。「是的。」她微笑着；以一个已经踏入和平之门的人所有的那种镇定，用低低的、虔敬的声气悄声道：「她躺在那张你为她铺好的床上，把那本《圣经》紧紧抱在胸前。」

===Original===
There are moments when the world about us seems to pause; when the hopes, fears and experiences of all humanity appear to sway away and leave us standing alone in the presence of our own great hope or scarcely comprehended fear. Such a moment was that which saw Paula reenter Jacqueline's presence with Mrs. Hamlin at her side.

Leaving the latter near the door, she went towards the bed. Why did she recoil and glance back at Mrs. Hamlin with that startled and apprehensive look? The face of Jacqueline was changed—changed as only one presence could change it, though the eyes were clearer than when she left her a few minutes before, and the lips were not without the shadow of a smile.

"She is dying," whispered Paula, coming back to Mrs. Hamlin; "dying, and you have waited so long!"

But the look that met hers from that aged face, was not one of grief; and startled, she knew not why, Paula drew aside, while Mrs. Hamlin crossed the room and quietly knelt down by her darling's side.

"Margery!"

"Jacqueline!"

The two cries rang through the room, then all was quiet again.

"You have come back!" were the next words Paula heard. "How could I ever have doubted that you would!"

"I have been driven back by awful suffering," was the answer; and another silence fell. Suddenly Jacqueline's voice was heard. "Love slew me, and now love has saved me!" exclaimed she. And there came no answer to that cry, and Paula felt the shadow of a great awe settle down upon her, and moving nearer to where the aged woman knelt by her darling's bedside, she looked in her bended face and then in the one upturned on the pillow, and knew that of all the hearts that but an instant before had beat with earth's deepest emotion in that quiet room, one alone throbbed on to thank God and take courage.

And the fire which had been kindled to welcome the prodigal back, burned on; and from the hollow depths of the great room below, came the sound of a clock as it struck the hour, seven!

===Chinese===
世上有那样一些时刻，我们周围的世界仿佛停顿了；全人类的种种希望、恐惧与经历，仿佛都纷纷退去，只留下我们独自站在那里，面对着自己心头那极大的盼望，或那几乎还不能领悟的恐惧。宝拉重新走进雅克琳的房间、身边伴着哈姆林夫人的那一刻，便是这样的一个时刻。

她把哈姆林夫人留在门边，自己朝床边走去。她为什么猛地一缩，回过头朝哈姆林夫人投去那样一道惊惶而忧虑的目光？雅克琳的脸变了——变得只有一种人的到来才能使它发生的那种变化，虽说那双眼比方才宝拉离开她时还要清亮几分，那两片嘴唇上也并非全无一丝微笑的影儿。

「她要去了。」宝拉回到哈姆林夫人身边，悄声说，「要去了，而你等了这么久！」

可那张苍老的脸迎上她的目光，却不是悲伤之色；宝拉不知为何猛地一惊，便侧身让开，哈姆林夫人穿过屋子，在心肝儿的床边静静地跪了下来。

「玛吉丽！」

「雅克琳！」

这两声呼唤响彻了整间屋子，随后一切又归于寂静。

「你到底回来了！」宝拉接着听见的话便是这几句。「我怎会一度疑心你不回来呢！」

「是可怕的苦痛把我赶了回来。」对方答道；又是一阵沉默。忽然，雅克琳的声音又响了起来。「爱杀了我，如今爱又救了我！」她喊道。这一声喊却再无回答，宝拉只觉一层巨大的敬畏之影落到了自己身上，她朝那位跪在心肝儿床边的老人身边挪近了一些，看了看她低垂的脸，又看了看枕上那张仰起的脸，便明白了：方才在那间静屋子里，本来有几颗心以人世间最深的情感一齐跳动着，而如今，只有一颗还在跳着，去感谢上帝、重新振作。

那炉为迎接这浪子回家而点起来的火，仍在烧着；从楼下那间大屋子空旷的深处，传来一座钟报时的声响——七点了！

## XXIV The Japha Mansion / 二十四 雅法宅邸

===Original===
> "Ah what a warning for a thoughtless man,
> Could field or grove, could any spot on earth
> Show to his eye an image of the pangs
> Which it has witnessed; render back an echo
> Of the sad steps by which it hath been trod."

===Chinese===
> 「啊，对于一个漫不经心的人，这是何等的警示，
> 倘若田野或丛树，倘若世间任一寸土地
> 能向他眼底映出它所目睹的种种苦痛之相，
> 能以回声送还
> 那曾踏过其上的悲伤足音。」

===Original===
Unexplained actions if long continued, lose after awhile their interest if not their mystery. The aged lady who now for many years had been seen at every nightfall to leave her home, traverse the village streets, enter the Japha mansion, remain there an hour and then reissue with tremulous steps and bowed head, had become so common a sight to the village eye, that even the children forgot to ask what her errand was, or why she held her head so hopefully when she entered, or looked so despondent when she came forth.

===Chinese===
难以解释的举动若长久持续下去，久而久之便会失掉人们的兴致——纵然失不掉那份神秘。那位上了年纪的夫人，多年来人们每见她在薄暮时分离开家门，穿过村中街巷，走进那座雅法宅邸（Japha mansion），在那里盘桓一个钟头，再以颤抖的脚步、低垂的头颅重新走出来——这一幕在村人眼中早已成了司空见惯的光景，连孩子们都忘了去问她究竟所为何事，忘了问她何以进门时把头昂得那样满怀期冀，而出 来时却又那般垂头丧气。

===Original===
But to Paula, for reasons already mentioned, this secret and persistent vigil in a forsaken and mysterious dwelling, was fraught with a significance which had never lost its power either to excite her curiosity or to arouse her imagination. Many a time had she gone home from some late encounter with the aged lady, to brood by the hour upon the expression of that restless eye which in its wanderings never failed to turn upon her own youthful face and linger there in the manner I have already noted. She thought of it by night, she thought of it by day. She felt herself drawn to that woman's suffering heart as by invisible cords. To understand the feelings of this desolate being, she had even studied the face of that old house, until she knew it under its every aspect. Often in shutting her eyes at night, she would perceive as in a mirror a vision of its long gray front, barred door and sealed windows shining in the moon, save where the deep impenetrable shadows of its two guardian poplars lay black and dismal upon its ghostly surface. Again she would behold it as it reared itself dark and dripping in a blinding storm, its walls plastered with leaves from the immovable poplars, and its neglected garden lying sodden and forlorn under the flail of the ceaseless storm. Then its early morning face would strike her fancy. The slow looming of its chimney-tops against a brightening sky; the gradual coming out of its forsaken windows and solemn looking doors from the mystery of darkness into the no less mystery of day; the hint of roselight on its barren boards; the gleam of sunshine on its untrodden threshold; a sunshine as pure and sweet as if a bride stood there in her beauty, waiting for admission into the deserted halls beyond. All and everything that could tend to invest the house and its constant visitor with an atmosphere of awe and interest, had occurred to this young girl in her daily reveries and nightly dreams. It was therefore with a thrill deep as her expectation and vivid as her sympathy, that she recognized in her eager interlocutor and proposed confident, the woman about whose life and actions rested for her such a veil of impenetrable mystery. The thought moved her, excited her, and made the rest of the evening pass like a dream. She was anxious for the next day to come, that she might seek this Mrs. Hamlin in her home, and hear from her lips the tale of devotion that should mate her own simple but enthusiastic poem.

===Chinese===
可对宝拉而言——出于前文已经提及的种种缘由——这场在一所被人遗弃、神秘莫测的宅子里暗暗地、执拗地守下去的夜夜守望，却始终承载着一种意义，那意义从未失去撩拨她好奇、触动她想象的力量。有许多回，她与那位老夫人不期而遇之后回到家中，便要整时整时地冥想那双不安的眼睛里的神情——那双眼睛在四处游移之时，总不会忘记转向她年轻的脸庞，并在那上面停留，正是我用前文已记述过的那一种停留方式。她夜里想着它，白天也想着它。她觉得自己像是被一条条看不见的绳索牵引着，走向那女人那颗受苦的心。为了能理解这个孤寂之人的情怀，她甚至研习过那座老宅的脸色，直到它每一种神情她都了如指掌。夜里常常一闭上眼，她便如对明镜般看见它那一长条灰色的正面、钉死的门和封死的窗在月光里闪闪发亮——唯有那两棵守护它的白杨树投下的深不可测的阴影，阴沉漆黑地压在它那鬼气森森的墙面上。她又看见它在一场叫人睁不开眼的暴风雨中黑压压、湿淋淋地矗立着，墙皮上贴满了从那两棵一动不动的白杨树上打落的树叶，那无人照管的园子在无休无止的风雨鞭笞之下，瘫软着、凄凉地伏在那里。再后来，它在清晨的那一副神情又会攫住她的想象：烟囱顶端在渐渐明亮的天空背景下缓缓显现；那些被弃的窗户、神情肃穆的门，从黑暗的神秘里一点点露出来，走进白日里那份同样深不可测的神秘；它光秃秃的木板上那一抹玫瑰色的晨曦的暗示；无人踏足的门槛上那一缕阳光的闪烁——那阳光纯净而甘美，仿佛有位新娘正以她的美貌立在那里，等着被迎进身后那些早已无人居住的厅堂。凡是一切能给这座宅子和它那位常客披上一层敬畏与兴味之氛围的事，都曾在这少女白日的遐想与夜里的梦境中一一浮现。正因如此，当她认出眼前那位热切的对话者、那位主动要来做她知己的人，便是那个其生平行事在她心头始终蒙着一层不可透视的神秘面纱的女人时，她心中那一阵震颤，便与她的期望一般深沉，与她的同情一般鲜明。这个念头打动她、激荡她，使那一晚余下的时光如一场梦般溜过。她巴不得次日立即到来，好去这位哈姆林夫人（Mrs. Hamlin）家中寻她，亲口听她讲出那份能与我这首质朴而热烈的诗作相匹敌的、奉献的故事。

===Original===
When the next day did come, it rained, rained bitterly, persistent and with a steady drive from the north east, that made her going out impossible. The day following she was indisposed, and upon the succeeding afternoon, she was engaged in duties that precluded all thought of visiting. The next day was Sunday, and Monday had its own demands which she could not slight. It was therefore well nigh a week from the night of the entertainment, before the opportunity offered for which she was so anxious. Her curiosity and expectation had thus time to grow, and it was with a determination to allow nothing to stand in her way, that she set out from home in a flood of mild September sunshine, to visit Mrs. Hamlin. But alas, for resolutions made in a country village prior to the opening of a church fair! She had scarcely gone a dozen steps before she was accosted by one of the managers, a woman who neither observes your haste, nor pays any attention to your possible preoccupation. Do what she could, she found it impossible to escape from this persistent individual until she had satisfied her upon matters which it took a full half hour to discuss, and when at last she succeeded in doing so, it was only to fall into the hands of an aged deacon of the church, whose protecting friendship it were a sin to wound, while his garrulous tongue made it no ordinary trial of patience to stand and listen. In short the best part of the afternoon was gone before she found herself at the door of Mrs. Hamlin's house. But she was not to be deterred by further hesitation from the pursuit of her object. Rapping smartly on the door, she listened. No stir came from within. Again she rapped and again she listened. No response came to assure her that her summons had been heard.
