Surprised at this, for she had been told Mrs. Hamlin was always at home during the afternoon, she glanced up at the church clock in plain view from the doorstep, and blushed to observe that it was six o'clock, the hour at which this mysterious woman always left her house, to accomplish her vigil at the Japha mansion.

===Chinese===
可次日真到来了，天却下起了雨，下得苦苦地、绵绵地，从东北方一阵稳劲地扑打着，叫她全无出门的可能。再下一天她又身体不适，到了再下一日的下午，她又忙于几桩脱不开身的差使，拜会一事全无暇念及。再下一天是礼拜天，而礼拜一又有它自家推不开的计较，她也不能等闲怠慢。如此一来，距离那场游艺会的那个晚上，竟已将近整整一个礼拜，方才等来了她苦盼的那个机会。她的好奇与期冀也因此有了滋长的时候；正是怀着一种不容任何事阻挡自己的决心，她踏出家门，浸在一派九月的暖阳里，去拜访哈姆林夫人。可叹呐，在乡间村里、在教堂游艺会（church fair）开办之前所下的决心！她走出去还不到十来步，便被一位主持人拦住了——那种女人既瞧不出你的匆忙，也不理会你心里可能装着的事。她费尽气力，竟也甩不开这位黏人的角色，非得把她那桩足足要花半个钟头来商议的事料理妥帖才成；好容易脱了身，却又落入了一位教堂老执事的手里——这位长者那一腔庇护之谊伤之有罪，可他那张絮叨的嘴，又教立着听完成了一桩非同小可的耐性试炼。简而言之，等她终于站到哈姆林夫人家的门前，一下午大好的辰光已去了大半。但她不肯再因迟疑而退出自己追寻的目标。她在门上清脆地敲了几下，侧耳倾听。屋里毫无动静。她又敲了一回，又听了一回。没有任何回应叫她确知她这召唤已被人听见。她不免诧异——因她曾听人说，哈姆林夫人下午总在家——便抬头望了望从门前一目了然的那座教堂钟，一看竟已是六点钟，登时臊红了脸：这个钟点，正是这位神秘女子每日离家、到雅法宅邸去完成她那一夕守望的时辰。

===Original===
"What have I done?" thought Paula, and felt a strange thrill as she realized that even at that moment, the woman with the eager but restless eyes, was shut within the precincts of that deserted dwelling, engaged in prayer, perhaps wet with tears, who knows? The secret of what she did in that long and quiet twilight hour had never been revealed. Leaving the little brown house behind, Paula found herself insensibly taking the road to the Japha mansion. If she could not enter it and share the watch of the devoted woman who had promised her her confidence, she could at least observe if the windows were open or the blinds raised. To be sure she ought to be at home, but Miss Belinda was indulgent and did not question her comings and goings too closely. An irresistible force drew her down the street, and she did not hesitate to follow the lead of her impulse. No one accosted her now, it was the tea hour in most of these houses and the streets were comparatively deserted. The only house whose chimneys lacked the rising smoke, was the one towards which her footsteps were tending. She could descry it from afar. Its gaunt walls from which the paint had long ago faded, stared uncompromisingly upon her in the autumn sunshine. There was no welcome in its close shutters with their broken slats from which hung tangled strips of old rags—the remnants of some boy's kite. The stiff and solemn poplars rose grim and forbidding at the gate once swung wide to the fashion and gallantry of proud ladies and stalwart gentlemen, but now pushed aside solely by the hand of a tremulous old woman, or the irreverent palm of some daring schoolboy. From the tangled garden looked forth neither flower nor blossoming shrub. Beauty and grace could not thrive in this wilderness of decay. A dandelion would have felt itself out of place beneath the eye of that ghostly door, with the sinister plank nailed across it, like the separating line between light and darkness, right and wrong, life and death. What loneliness! what a monument of buried passions outliving death itself!

===Chinese===
「我这是做了什么？」宝拉心想，只觉心头掠过一阵奇异的震颤——她恍然意识到，便在此时此刻，那个眼里燃烧着殷切而又不安神色的女人，正把自己关在那座空宅的院墙之内，或正跪着祈祷，或已被泪水打湿，谁知道呢？在那漫长而寂静的暮色时辰里她究竟做些什么，这秘密从未被揭开过。宝拉把那栋棕色的小屋抛在身后，发觉自己不知不觉间已走上了通往雅法宅邸的那条路。她既不能走进去与那位应许了她一片信赖的痴心女子共守一夜，至少也能远远瞧瞧那些窗户是否开着、那些百叶是否吊起。论理她此刻原该在家，可贝琳达小姐（Miss Belinda）素来宽纵，并不曾把她的来去盯得太紧。一股不可抗拒的力量把她顺着街牵了过去，她也便毫不犹豫地顺从了这股冲动。这会儿再没有人来搭讪她了——这条街上的人家多半是用茶的时候，街上相当地空寂。唯一一座烟囱里不见炊烟升起的房子，便是她的脚步正趋向的那一座。她从老远便能望见它。它那一身瘦削的墙，油漆早已褪尽，在秋日的阳光下一毫不让地瞪着她。它那些紧闭的百叶窗毫无欢迎之意，破裂的窗板上挂着一绺绺纠缠不清的旧布条——是哪个男孩的风筝留下的残骸。那两棵笔挺肃穆的白杨，阴森而凛然地守在门口——这道门，曾经向那些骄傲淑女和魁梧绅士的排场与华丽大敞着，如今却只被一位颤巍巍的老妇人的手、或某个胆大包天的学童那只不敬的手掌推开了。从那一片蓬乱的园子里，望不见一朵花、一丛开花的灌木。美与雅是不能在这片衰败的荒野里滋长的。便是一棵蒲公英，在那扇鬼气森森、被一块阴森木板横钉死了的门下——那木板像一道分割明与暗、是与非、生与死的界线——也会觉得自己格格不入。何其孤寂啊！何等一座比死亡本身更经久、埋葬着一腔腔激情的丰碑！

===Original===
Paula paused as she reached the gate; but remembering that Mrs. Hamlin was accustomed to enter the house by a side door, hurried around the corner and carefully surveyed the windows from that quarter. One of the shutters was open, allowing the flame of the setting sun to gild the panes like gold. She did not know then nor has she been able to explain since, what it was that came over her at the sight, but almost before she realized it, she had returned to the gate, opened it, threaded the overgrown garden, reached the door which she had so frequently beheld the aged woman enter and knocked.

===Chinese===
宝拉走到门口便停下了脚步；可她记起哈姆林夫人一向是从一扇侧门进屋的，便绕过墙角，从那一面把那几扇窗子仔仔细细地打量了一番。其中一扇百叶窗正开着，任那一轮将落的太阳的火光把窗玻璃镀得如金。她那时不知——至今也无法解释——一见了这景象，她究竟是被什么摄住了，只是几乎未等自己回过神来，她已经折回了门口，推开栅门，穿过那片荒草没胫的园子，走到了那一扇她曾多少次目睹那位老夫人走进去的门前，敲响了它。

===Original===
Instantly she was seized with a consciousness of what she had done, and frightened at her temerity, meditated an immediate escape. Drawing the folds of her mantle about her form and face, she prepared to fly, when she remembered the look of entreaty with which this woman had said on that night of their conversation, "Do not disappoint me! Do not keep me long in suspense!" and moved by a fresh impulse, turned and inflicted another resounding knock on the door.

===Chinese===
顷刻之间，她猛然意识到自己做了什么，被自己的胆大妄为吓了一跳，便盘算着即刻脱身。她把斗篷的褶裥拢紧了身子和脸，正要逃走，却记起了那一夜她们交谈时，这女人说那句「别叫我失望！别让我久悬着心！」时脸上那一副恳求的神情——于是被一股新的冲动所推动，她转过身，又在门上敲了一记响亮的叩击。

===Original===
The result was unlooked-for and surprising. To the sound from within of a quick passionate cry, there came a hurried movement, followed by a deep silence, then another hasty stir succeeded by a longer silence, then a rush which seemed to bring all things with it, and the door opened and Mrs. Hamlin appeared before her with a countenance so pallid with expectancy, that Paula instinctively felt that in some unconscious way, she had loosened the bonds of an uncontrollable emotion, and was drawing back, when the woman with a quick look in her shrouded face, exultantly caught her hand in hers, and drawing her over the threshold, gasped out in a delirium of incomprehensible joy:

===Chinese===
随之而来的反应出乎意料，令人吃惊。屋内先传出一声急促而激动的惊呼，接着是一阵匆忙的脚步声，随之是一片沉沉的死寂；然后又是一阵慌乱的动静，接着是一段更长的沉默；继而是仿佛把一切一并卷来的一阵疾奔——门开了，哈姆林夫人出现在她面前，那一张脸因期待而惨白得——宝拉本能地感到，自己是在某种无意识之间，解开了一股无法驾驭的情感的缰绳，正想退后，那女人却朝她那张掩在斗篷里的脸飞快地投来一瞥，狂喜地一把抓住了她的手，把她拉过门槛，在一阵难解的欢悦的狂乱里喘息着说：

===Original===
"I knew you would come! I knew that God would not let you forget! Fifteen years have I waited, Jacqueline! fifteen long, tedious, suffering years! But they all seem like nothing now! You have come, you have come, and all that I ask, is that God will not let me die till I realize my joy!"

===Chinese===
「我就知道你会回来！我就知道上帝不会让你忘掉！我等了十五年啦，雅克琳（Jacqueline）！十五个漫长、沉闷、受苦的年头啊！可如今这一切都算不得什么了！你回来了，你回来了，我所求的只有一桩——愿上帝别叫我闭眼，直等我亲口尝一尝这喜悦的滋味！」

===Original===
The emotion with which she uttered these strange words was so overpowering, and her body seemed so weak to stand the strain, that Paula instinctively put forth her hand to sustain her. The action loosened her cloak. Instantly the eyes that had been fixed upon her with such delirious rapture grew blank with dismay, a frightful shudder ran through the woman's aged frame; she tore at the cloak that still enveloped the young girl's shoulders, and pulling it off, took one view of the fresh and beautiful countenance before her, and without uttering a word, fell back in a deep and deadly swoon upon the floor.

===Chinese===
她说出这一番奇怪话语时的那股情绪是如此排山倒海，她那副身板看上去又如此难以撑持，宝拉本能地伸手去扶她。这一动却松开了她的斗篷。立时，那一双方才还带着如许狂喜盯住她的眼睛，因惊惶而变得一片茫然；一阵可怕的战栗穿过老夫人衰朽的身躯；她扯着仍裹在少女肩头上的那件斗篷，把它一把扯下，朝眼前那张鲜妍美丽的脸看了一眼，便一言不发，往后直直晕倒在地，昏得不省人事。

===Original===
"O what have I done?" cried Paula, flinging herself down beside that pale and rigid figure; but instantly remembering herself she leaped to her feet and looked about for some means to resuscitate the sufferer. There was a goblet of water on a table near by. Seizing it, she bathed the face and hands of the woman before her, moaning aloud in her grief and dismay, "Have I killed her! O what is this mystery that brings such a doom of anguish to this poor heart?"

===Chinese===
「啊，我做了什么呀？」宝拉失声喊道，扑倒在那一具苍白僵硬的身躯旁边；可她马上记起自己该做什么，纵身跃起，四下里张望寻思着有什么法子能救醒这个昏过去的人。近旁一张桌上摆着一玻璃杯水。她一把抓过来，浸湿了面前的女人家的脸和手，一边痛心疾首、慌乱不已地高声哀号：「莫不是我害死了她！啊，这究竟是怎样一桩秘事，竟给这一颗可怜的心带来这样的一场苦劫？」

===Original===
But from those pallid lips came no response, and feeling greatly alarmed, Paula was about to rush from the house for assistance, when she felt a tremulous pull upon her skirt, and turning, saw that the glassy eyes had opened at last and were now gazing upon her with mute but eloquent appeal.

===Chinese===
可那一对惨白的嘴唇毫无回应。宝拉心下大慌，正要冲出门去呼援，却觉着自己的裙裾被人颤巍巍地一拉，一回头，看见那双浑浊的眼终于张开了，正以一种无言却动人心魄的恳求望着她。

===Original===
She instantly returned. "O I am so sorry," she murmured, sinking again upon her knees beside the suffering woman. "I did not know, could not realize that my presence here would affect you so deeply. Forgive me and tell me what I can do to make you forget my presumption."

===Chinese===
她立时返了回去。「啊，我真对不住，」她低语着，重新跪倒在这位受苦的女人身边。「我先前不知道，也想象不到，我竟会在这里出现，竟会这样深地搅扰了您。原谅我吧，告诉我，我能为您做点什么，好让您忘掉我的唐突。」

===Original===
The woman shook her head, her lips moved and she struggled vainly to rise. Paula immediately lent her the aid of her strong young hand and in a few minutes, Mrs. Hamlin was on her feet. "O God!" were her first words as she sank into the chair which Paula hastily drew forward, "that I should taste the joy and she be still unsaved!"

===Chinese===
那女人摇了摇头，嘴唇翕动着，挣扎着想要起身却不能够。宝拉即刻伸出她年轻有力的手去搀扶；不消几分钟，哈姆林夫人已经站了起来。「啊，上帝！」她跌进宝拉匆忙拉过来的那张椅子里时，吐出来的头一句话便是，「我竟得以尝到这喜悦，而她竟仍不得拯救！」

===Original===
Seeing her so absorbed, Paula ventured to glance around her. She found herself in a large square room sparsely but comfortably furnished in a style that bespake it as the former sitting-room of the dead and buried Japhas. From the walls above hung a few ancient pictures. A large haircloth sofa of a heavy antique shape, confronted the eye from one side of the room, an equally ancient bookcase from the other. The carpet was faded and so were the curtains, but they had once been of an attractive hue and pattern. Conspicuous in the midst stood a large table with a well-trimmed lamp upon it, and close against it an easy chair with an upright back. This last as well as everything else in the room, was in a condition of neatness that would have surprised Paula if she had not been acquainted with the love and devotion of this woman, who in her daily visits to this house, probably took every pains to keep things freshened and in order.

===Chinese===
见她如此出神，宝拉便大着胆子朝四下里扫了一眼。她发觉自己身处一间大方形屋子里，陈设虽简，却颇为舒坦，那一种式样显见得说明这原是那已长眠地下的雅法一家人的旧日起坐间。墙上方挂着几幅古画。屋子的这一面正对着一只笨重古旧的大马毛呢沙发，那一面则是一只同样古旧的书橱。地毯已经褪了色，窗帘也是一样，可它们一度也曾有过悦目的颜色与花式。屋子正中显眼地摆着一张大桌子，上面搁着一盏修剪得齐齐整整的灯，紧挨着它的是一张高背的安乐椅。这最后一件，也同屋里其余的一切物件一样，整洁得一丝不苟——若不是宝拉早已深知这女人的一片痴心与热忱，她每日到这座宅子里来，大概是煞费苦心地把这一切都收拾得清爽齐整，这份整洁本会叫她吃一惊的。

===Original===
Satisfied with her survey, she again directed her attention to Mrs. Hamlin, and started to find that person's eyes fixed upon her own with an expression of deep, demanding interest.

===Chinese===
她把这番巡视看得心满意足，便又把心思转回了哈姆林夫人身上——却吓了一跳，只见对方那一双眼正牢牢盯着自己，神色里含着一种深沉而急切的关注。

===Original===
"You are looking at the shadows of things that were," exclaimed the old lady in thrilling tones. "It is a fearful thought to be shut up with the ghost of a vanished past, is it not? That chair by your side has not been sat in since Colonel Japha rose from it twelve years ago to totter to the bed where he breathed his last. It is waiting, everything is waiting. I thought the end had come tonight, that the vigil was over, the watch finished, but God in his wisdom says, 'No,' and I must wait a little longer. Alas in a little while longer the end will be here indeed!"

===Chinese===
「您正在看的，是那些已逝之物的影子，」老夫人用一种叫人战栗的声调开口道。「与一段消逝的往日之幽灵一同锁在屋里——这是一个叫人不寒而栗的念头，是不是？您身边那张椅子，自十二年前杰法上校（Colonel Japha）从上头站起来、踉跄着走向他咽气的那张床之后，便再没有人坐过。它在等，样样东西都在等。我原以为今夜尽头到了，以为守望完了，守夜尽了，可上帝凭他的智慧说『还不』，于是我还得再等些时。唉，再过不久，尽头当真就要到啦！」

===Original===
The despondency with which she uttered these last words showed where her thoughts were tending, and to comfort her, Paula drew up a chair and sat down by her side. "You were going to tell me the story of a great love and a great devotion. Cannot you do so now?"

===Chinese===
她说出这末了几句话时所带的那份颓丧，已显见得说明她的心绪正朝哪一处去；为了宽慰她，宝拉拉过一张椅子，在她身边坐下。「您先前要给我讲一段大爱与大虔诚的故事。您此刻不能讲了吗？」

===Original===
The woman started, glanced hastily around, and let her eyes travel to Paula's face where they rested with something of their old look of secret longing and doubt.

===Chinese===
那女人一激灵，匆忙四下里一瞥，然后任她的目光游到宝拉的脸上，在那里停住，带着几分旧日那一种隐密的渴望与犹疑。

===Original===
"You are the one who wrote the poem," she murmured; "I remember." Then with a sudden feverish impulse, leaned forward, and stroking back the waving locks from Paula's brow, exclaimed hurriedly, "You look like her, you have the same dark hair and wonderful eyes, more beautiful perhaps, but like her, O so like her! That is why I made such a mistake." She shuddered, with a quick low sob, but instantly subdued her emotion and taking Paula's hand in hers continued, "You are young, my daughter; youth does not enjoy carrying burdens; can I, a stranger ask you to assist me with mine?"

===Chinese===
「您便是写那首诗的人，」她喃喃道；「我记得。」接着，她被一股突如其来的狂热的冲动所驱使，倾身向前，把宝拉额前那几绺波浪般的卷发掠开，急急地喊道：「您长得像她，您有她那样乌黑的头发、那样一双奇妙的眼，或许还更美一些，可像她，啊，真像她！正因如此，我才犯了这么个错。」她打了个寒噤，发出一声短而低的呜咽，但立刻又按捺住自己，握住宝拉的手，接着说：「您年轻啊，我的孩子；年轻人是不爱挑担子的；我这么个陌生人，能请您帮我分担我这一副么？」

===Original===
"You may," returned Paula. "If it will give you any relief I will help you bear it willingly."

===Chinese===
「您能。」宝拉答道。「若这能给您带去一丝宽解，我便乐意帮您分担它。」

===Original===
"You will! Has heaven then sent me the aid my failing spirits demand? Can I count on you, child? But I will ask for no promise till you have heard my story. To no one have I ever imparted the secret of my life, but from the first moment I saw your fair young face, I felt that through you would come my help, if help ever came to make my final moments easier and my last days less bitter." And rising up, she led Paula to a door which she solemnly opened. "I am glad that you are here," said she. "I could never have asked you to come, but since you have braved the dead and crossed this threshold, you must see and know the whole. You will understand my story better."

===Chinese===
「您肯！那么上天当真派来了我这衰颓之心所求的援手了？我能指望您吗，孩子？可是在您听完我的故事之前，我不会向您索要任何允诺。我一生的秘密，从未对任何人吐露过；可从我瞧见您这张姣好年轻的脸的第一刻起，我便感觉到——倘若会有什么援助降临，叫我的临终之时轻松些、末了的日子少苦些——那援助是要从您这里来的。」说着她站起身，把宝拉领到一扇门前，神色凝重地把它打开了。「您在这里，我很高兴，」她说。「我绝没有胆量开口请您来；可既然您已向这些亡魂壮了胆、跨过了这道门槛，您便非得眼看、非得知晓这一切不可。这样您就会更明白我的故事。」

===Original===
Taking her through a dark passage, she threw wide another door, and the parlors of the vanished Japhas opened before them. It was a ghostly vision. A weird twilight scene of clustered shadows brooding above articles of musty grandeur. In spite of the self-command learned by her late experiences, Paula recoiled, saying,

===Chinese===
她引她穿过一道黑暗的过道，把另一扇门大大地推开——那已逝的雅法一家人的客厅便在他们眼前展开了。这是一幅鬼气森森的景象。一种怪异的暮色之景：成簇的阴影盘踞在那些发霉的华丽物件之上。尽管宝拉已从近来的种种经历中学得几分自持，她仍不禁往后一缩，说道：

===Original===
"It is too sad, too lonesome!" But the woman without heeding her, hurried her on over the worm-eaten carpet and between the timeworn chairs and heavy-browed cabinets, to the hall beyond.

===Chinese===
「这太凄凉、太孤寂了！」可那女人并不理会她，只催着她往前，越过那虫蛀的地毯，从那些被岁月磨旧的椅子、那些眉宇沉重的橱柜之间穿过去，走进了那一头的门厅。

===Original===
"I have not been here, myself, for a year," said Mrs. Hamlin, glancing fearfully up and down the dusky corridor. "It is not often I can brave the memories of this spot." And she pointed with one hand towards the darkened door at its end, whose spacious if not stately panels gave no hint to the eye of the dread bar that crossed it like a line of doom upon the outside, and then turning, let her eye fall with still heavier significance upon the broad and imposing staircase that rose from the centre of the hall to the duskier and more dismal regions above.

===Chinese===
「我自己也有一年没到这里来过了，」哈姆林夫人说着，怯怯地朝那昏暗的走廊两头望了望。「这地方所唤起的种种记忆，我不是常常敢于招惹的。」她一只手指着走廊尽头那一扇被遮暗的门——它那一片宽阔、纵非气派也颇可观的门板，丝毫看不出外头那一根像一道厄运之线般横钉穿过它的那根可怕的横木；接着她转过身，把目光投到那座从门厅正中拔地而起、通向上头那些更幽暗、更阴森之处的一道宽阔气派的楼梯上，神色越发沉重。

===Original===
"A brave, old fashioned flight of steps is it not! But the scene of a curse, my child." And unheeding Paula's shudder, she drew her up the stairs.

===Chinese===
「一道气派的、老式的楼梯，是不是！可它是一道诅咒的发生地啊，我的孩子。」她不顾宝拉的战栗，把她拉上了楼。

===Original===
"See," continued her panting guide as they reached a square platform near the top, from which some half dozen or more steps branched up on either side. "They do not build like this nowadays. But Colonel Japha believed in nothing new, and thought more of his grand old hall and staircase, than he did of all the rest of his house. He little dreamed of what a scene it would be the witness. But come, it is getting late and you must see her room."

===Chinese===
「您瞧，」气喘吁吁的引路人到了离顶端不远的一处方形平台时，接着说——那平台左右两边各有六七级台阶岔开往上。「如今的人可不这么盖房子了。可杰法上校什么都不信新的，对他那座气派的老门厅和楼梯看得比他全宅其余各处都重。他做梦也没想到，这里竟会成为那样一场惨剧的见证。可来吧，时候不早了，您得看一看她的房间。」

===Original===
It was near the top of the staircase and was fully as musty, faded and dismal as the rest. Yet there was an air of expectancy about it, too, that touched Paula deeply. From between the dingy hangings of the bed, looked forth a pair of downy pillows, edged with yellowed lace, and beneath them a neatly spread counterpane carefully turned back over comfortable-looking blankets, as one sees in a bed that only awaits its occupant; while on the ancient hearth, a pile of logs stood heaped and ready for the kindling match.

===Chinese===
那房间就在楼梯近顶处，与别处一般地发着霉、褪了色、阴沉沉的。然而它也透着一种等候着什么的气息，深深触动了宝拉。从床顶那帐子的暗色帷挂之间，探出一对毛绒绒的枕头，镶着已泛黄的蕾丝边；枕头下面铺着一块齐齐整整的床罩，床罩被仔细地翻开着，搭在几条看着就暖和的毯子上，正如人在一张只等住客入住的床上所见的那般；而在那古旧的壁炉前，一堆木柴也已码好，只等着一点引火的火苗。

===Original===
"It is all waiting you see," said the old lady in a trembling voice, "like everything else, just waiting."

===Chinese===
「这一切都在等着呢，您瞧，」老夫人颤声说道，「同别的东西一样，只是在等着。」

===Original===
There was an embroidery frame in one corner of the room, from which looked a piece of faded and half completed work. The needle was hanging from it by a thread, and a skein of green worsted hung over the top, Paula glanced at it inquiringly.

===Chinese===
屋子的一角立着一副绣花架子，上头绷着一块褪了色、绣了一半的活计。一根针还由一根线连在绷子上，一绞绿色的绒线从架顶垂下来。宝拉询问似的瞥了它一眼。

===Original===
"It is just as she left it! He never entered the room after she went and I would never let it be touched. It is just the same with the piano below. The last piece she played is still standing open on the rack. I loved her so, and I thought then that a few months would bring her back! See, here is her bible. She never used to read it, but she prized it because it was her mother's. I have placed it on the pillow where she will see it when she comes to lay her poor tired head down to rest." And with a reverent hand the aged matron drew the curtains back from the open bed, and disclosed the little bible lying thick with dust in the centre of the nearest pillow.

===Chinese===
「这都还是她走时留下的样子！她走后他再没踏进过这间屋子，而我也从不许人动它一指头。楼下的钢琴也是一样。她弹过的最后一首曲子，至今还翻开搁在谱架上。我是那样爱她，那时还以为过不上几个月她就会回来！您瞧，这儿是她的圣经。她向来不读它的，可她把它看得很重，因为是母亲的遗物。我把它搁在枕头上，等她回来把她那可怜倦乏的头搁下歇息时，一眼便能瞧见。」这位老夫人怀着虔敬的手，把那张未挂帐子的床的帐子拉开，露出那一本积了厚厚一层灰的小圣经，正搁在离自己最近的那只枕头的正中央。

===Original===
"O who was this you loved so well? And why did she leave you?" cried Paula with the tears in her eyes, at sight of this humble token.

===Chinese===
「啊，您这般深爱的究竟是谁？她又是为何离开了您？」宝拉眼中噙着泪，一见这件朴素的纪念物便失声喊道。

===Original===
The aged lady seized her hand and hurried her back into the room below. "I will tell you where I have waited and watched so long. Only be patient till I light the lamp. It is getting late and any chance wanderer going by and seeing all dark, might think I had forgotten my promise and was not here."

===Chinese===
那位老夫人一把抓住她的手，匆匆把她带回楼下的屋子。「我这就告诉您，我在何处守了、望了这么长久。只是您稍耐着性子，容我先把灯点上。时候不早了，万一有过路的闲人走过，看见屋里漆黑一片，只当我忘了自己的誓约，没有到这里来呢。」

## Book III The Japha Mystery / 卷三 贾法之谜

## XXVII The Lone Watcher / 二十七 孤独的守望者

===Original===
> "Hark! to the hurried question of Despair,

 Where is my child?—and Echo answers—Where?"

"Colonel Japha recovered from his shock, but was never the same man again. All that was genial, affectionate and confiding in his nature, had been turned as by a lightning's stroke, to all that was hard, bitter and suspicious. He would not allow the name of Jacqueline to be spoken in his presence; he would listen to no allusion made to those days when she was the care and perplexity, but also the light and pleasure of the house. Men are not like women, my child; when they turn, it is at an angle, the whole direction of their nature changes.

===Chinese===
> 「听啊！那绝望者匆促的叩问——
> 我的孩子在哪里？——回声答道——在哪里？」

「杰法上校（Colonel Japha）那一场打击总算熬了过来，可他从此再也不是原先那个人了。他天性里一切和蔼、深情、容易信赖他人的东西，都像被一道闪电劈过似的，尽数化作了冷酷、刻毒与猜忌。他不许任何人在他面前提起雅克琳（Jacqueline）这个名字；也不肯听人暗示半句那些曾把她视作全家操心与烦恼、却也是全家的亮光与欢乐的日子。男人不比女人，我的孩子；他们一旦变起来，是转成直角的，整个性情的方向都随之改了。

===Original===
"Perhaps the news that presently came to us from Boston may have had something to do with this. It was surely dreadful enough; Jacqueline's perfidy had slain her lover. Mr. Robert Holt, the cultured, noble, high-souled gentleman, had been found lying dead on the floor of his room, a few days after the events I have just related, with a lady's diamond ring in his hand and the remnants of a hastily burned letter in the grate before him. He had burst a blood-vessel, and had expired instantly.

===Chinese===
「也许过不久从波士顿（Boston）传来的那个消息，与此不无关系。那消息实在够骇人的了：雅克琳的背信弃义害死了她的情人。就在我方才所述的那几桩事过后没几天，罗伯特·霍尔特先生（Mr. Robert Holt）——那位有教养、高尚、灵魂崇高的绅士——被人发现僵卧在自己房间的地板上，断了气，手里握着一只女式的钻石戒指，面前的壁炉里是一封匆匆烧去的信的残烬。他是一条血管迸裂，当即咽了气。

===Original===
"This sudden and tragic ending of a man of energy and will, was also the reason, perhaps, why Grotewell never arrived at the truth of Jacqueline's history. Boston was a long way from here in those days, and the story of her lover's death was not generally known, while the fact of her elopement was. Consequently she was supposed to have fled with the man who had been seen to visit her most frequently; a report which neither the Colonel nor myself had the courage to deny.

===Chinese===
「一个精力充沛、意志坚强的人竟这样骤然惨死，这或许也就是格罗特韦尔（Grotewell）这地方始终无从得知雅克琳那段往事真相的缘故。那些年头，波士顿（Boston）离这里远得很，她情人死去的消息并不为世人所知，而她私奔的事却尽人皆晓。于是人们便以为她是跟那个被人瞧见最常上门访她的男人一同逃走的；这一种说法，无论上校还是我，都没有勇气去辩驳。

===Original===
"My child, you have a brow like snow, and a cheek like roses; you know little of life's sorrows and little of life's sins. To you the skies are blue, the woods vernal, the air balmy; the sad looks upon men's and women's faces, tell but shallow tales of the ceaseless grinding of grief in their pent up souls. But you are gentle, and you have an imagination that goes beyond your experience; perhaps if you pause and think, you can understand what a tale could be told of the weeks and months and years that now followed, without hint or whisper of the fate of her who had gone out from amongst us with the brand of her father's curse upon her brow. At first we hoped, yes, *he* hoped—I could see it in his eyes when there came a sudden ring at the bell—that some sign of her penitence, or some proof of her existence, would come to relieve the torture of our fears, if not the shame of our memories. But the door that closed upon her on that fatal eve, had shut without an echo. While we vainly waited, time had ample leisure to carve the furrows of age as well as of suffering on the Colonel's once smooth brow, and to change my daily vigil into a custom of despair, rather than of hope. Time had also leisure to rob us of much of our worldly goods and to make our continued living in this grand old house, an act that involved constant care and the closest economy. That we were enabled to preserve appearances to the day that beheld the Colonel laid low by the final stroke of his dread disease, was only due to the secret charity of a certain gentleman, who, declaring he was indebted to us, secretly supplied me with means of support.

===Chinese===
「我的孩子，你的额头洁白如雪，你的两颊红得像玫瑰；人生的忧患你知之甚少，人生的罪孽你也知之甚少。在你眼里，天是蓝的，树林是一片新绿，空气和煦宜人；男男女女脸上那一缕忧色，也只道出他们那郁结灵魂里无休无止的悲苦磨碾之浅浅一端。可你生性温厚，又有一份越出你阅历之外的想像力；也许你若停下来想一想，便能领会：在那随后的几周、几月、几年里，可以讲述出怎样一个故事——而对她那个额上烙着父亲诅咒的印记、从我们中间出走的人，关于她的下落，竟无半点暗示、半声传言。起初我们抱有希望，是的，连*他*也抱有希望——门铃猛地一响时，我从他眼里看得出这份希望——总以为她悔意的些许端倪，或她尚在人世的某种凭据，总会传来，好缓解我们那番恐惧的煎熬，哪怕不能消解记忆中的羞耻。然而在那个要命的前夜在她身后合拢的那扇门，合上之后竟没有回响半声。我们徒然地等候着，岁月却有的是闲暇，在上校那原本光洁的额上，刻下衰老与苦难的沟壑；又把我日复一日的守望，一点点变成了一种绝望的惯例，而不再是希望的惯例。岁月也有闲暇夺去我们大量世间的财物，使我们继续住在这座古老宏大的宅子里这件事，成了一桩需要处处留心、精打细算到极点的事。我们之所以能够维持体面，一直撑到看见上校被那可怖恶疾的最后一击击倒的那一天，全靠某位先生的暗中周济——他自称受过我们的恩惠，便暗中接济我度日的银钱。

===Original===
"But of all this you care little.

===Chinese===
「可这些事，你都不大关心。

===Original===
"You had rather hear about the evening watch with its hopeful assurance, 'Yet another day and she will be here,' to be followed so soon by the despairing acknowledgement, 'Yet another day and she has not come!' or of those dark hours when the Colonel lay blank and white upon his pillow, with his eyes fixed on the door which would never open to the beating of a daughter's heart, while the gray shadow of an awful resolution deepened upon his immovable face. What that resolution was I could not know, but I feared it, when I saw what a sternness it gave to his eye, what a fixedness to his set and implacable lip; and when in the waning light of a certain December afternoon, the circle of neighbors about his bed gave way to the stiff and forbidding form of Mr. Phelps, I felt a thrill of mortal apprehension and only waited to hear the short, 'It shall be done,' of the lawyer to some slowly whispered command of the colonel, to rise from my far off corner and stand ready to accost Mr. Phelps as he came from the bedside of the dying man.

===Chinese===
「你宁愿听我说那些黄昏的守候——那守候带着满怀希冀的笃定：『再过一天，她就要回来了』，可这么快便接上那绝望的承认：『再过一天，她竟还是没有回来！』；或者你想听我说那些黑暗的时辰——上校苍白而毫无血色地躺在枕上，两眼死死盯着那扇永远不会再为一个女儿心跳而开启的门，而他那张纹丝不动的脸上，一种可怖决心的灰色阴影越积越深。那决心究竟是什么，我无从知晓，可我惧怕它；当我看见这决心给了他的眼神怎样一股严厉，给了他那抿紧而不饶人的嘴唇怎样一种僵定，我便惧怕它；当十二月的某个下午，天光渐暗，围在他床边的几位邻里让开位置，让费尔普斯先生（Mr. Phelps）那副僵硬而生硬的身形走上前来时，我只觉一阵入骨的预惧猛地窜过全身，只等着听见那律师对上校某句缓慢低语的吩咐，短短答一句『一定办到』——我便要从自己那个远远的角落里站起来，守在这位临终者床边，准备在费尔普斯先生一出来时就拦住他。

===Original===
" 'What is it?' I asked, rushing up to him as he issued forth into the hall, and seizing him by the arm, with a woman's unreasoning impetuosity. 'I have nursed his daughter on my knee; tell me, then, what it is he has ordered you to do in this final moment?'

===Chinese===
『是怎么回事？』他一走到门厅里，我便冲上前去，带着女人那种不加思索的急切，一把抓住他的胳膊问他。『我曾在膝上抱过他的女儿；那么，你告诉我，他在这临终的一刻究竟吩咐你去做什么？』

===Original===
"Mr. Phelps for all his ungainly bearing, is not a hard-hearted man, as you know, and he doubtless saw the depth of the misery that made me forget myself. Giving me a look that was not without its touch of sarcasm, he replied, 'The colonel has made me promise, to see that a plank is nailed across the front door of this house, after his body has been carried out to burial.'

===Chinese===
「费尔普斯先生尽管举止笨拙，却不是个心硬的人，这一点你是知道的；他想必也看出了使我忘形的那份苦痛有多深。他朝我看了一眼——那眼神里并不是全无讥讽——答道：『上校叫我应承下一件事：等他的遗体被抬出去安葬之后，要亲眼看人用一块木板，把这宅子的正门钉死封上。』

===Original===
"A board across the front door! His anger then was implacable. The withering curse that had rung in my ears for ten years, was to outlive his death! With a horrified groan, I pressed my hands over my eyes and rushed back. My first glimpse of the Colonel's face showed me that the end was at hand, but that fact only made more imperative my consuming desire to see that curse removed, even though it were done with his final breath. Drawing near his bedside, I leaned down, and waiting till his eye wandered to my face, asked him if there was nothing he wished amended before his strength failed. He understood me. We had not sat for so long, face to face across the chasm of a hideous memory, without knowing something of the workings of each other's mind. Glancing up at his wife's portrait which ever faced him as he lay upon his pillow, his mouth grew severe and he essayed to shake his head. I at once pointed to the portrait.

===Chinese===
「正门上钉一块木板！这么说，他的怒气是不肯和解的了。在我耳边响了十年的那道刻毒诅咒，竟要活过他的死！我发出一声惊骇的呻吟，双手捂住眼睛，冲了回去。我第一眼瞥见上校的脸，便知大限已到；可这一桩事实，反倒叫我心头那股火烧般的渴望愈发不可遏制——我非得看见那道诅咒被收回不可，哪怕是用他最后一口气来收回。我走到他床边，俯下身去，等着他的眼神游移到我脸上，才问他：趁气力还未散尽，可有什么想加以更改的。他懂得我的意思。我们隔着那段可怖记忆的深渊，相对而坐了这么久，彼此心思如何运转，多少是知道一点的。他抬眼朝他妻子的画像望了一眼——他躺在床上，那画像终日正对着他——他的嘴严厉地抿紧了，他想摇一摇头。我立刻指向那画像。

===Original===
" 'What will you say to her when she meets you on the borders of heaven?' I demanded with the courage of despair.' She will ask, 'Where is my child?' And what will you reply?'

===Chinese===
『等她在天堂的边境迎上你时，你打算对她说什么？』我凭着绝望带来的那股勇气追问。『她要问：「我的孩子在哪儿？」你将怎么回答她？』

===Original===
"The fingers that lay upon the coverlid moved spasmodically; he eyed me with a steady deepening stare, awful to meet, fearful to remember. I went on steadily; 'She has gone out of this house with your curse; tell me that if she comes back, she may be greeted with your forgiveness.' Still that awful stare which changed not. 'I have watched and waited for her every day since her departure,' I whispered, 'and shall watch and wait for her, every day until I die. Shall a stranger's love be greater than a father's?' This time his lips twitched and the grey shadow shifted, but it did not rise. 'I had sworn to do it,' I went on. 'When you lay there at the top of the stairs, smitten down by your first shock, I told her, come sickness, come health, I should keep a daily vigil at that door of the house which your severity had not closed upon her; and I have kept my word till now and shall keep it to the end. What will you do for this miserable child of whose being you are the author?'

===Chinese===
「搭在被上的那几根手指痉挛般地动了一动；他目不转睛地盯着我，那凝视越深越紧，叫人对视时心惊，事后回想起来胆寒。我镇定地接着说下去：『她是带着你的诅咒走出这宅子的；你告诉我，若是她回来，她将得到你的宽恕相迎。』那可怖的凝视依旧不改。『自她走后，我每日都在守望她、等候她，』我低声说，『直到我死的那一天，我都会日日守着、等着她。一个外人的爱，难道能大过一个父亲的爱吗？』这一回他的嘴唇抽动了一下，那层灰色阴影也动了动，却不曾升起。『我早已发誓要这样做，』我接着说，『当初你躺在楼梯顶那儿，被头一场打击撂倒的时候，我就对她说过，无论疾病、无论康健，我都要每日在这宅子门口守候——你的严苛不曾把这门对她关上；从那以后我信守至今，也将一直信守到最后。这个可怜的孩子，她的生命是你给的，你打算为她做些什么？』

===Original===
"With indescribable anxiety I paused and watched him, for his lips were moving. 'Do for her?' he repeated.

===Chinese===
「我怀着无法言喻的焦虑停下，注视着他，因为他的嘴唇在动。『为她做些什么？』他重复道。

===Original===
"How awful is the voice of the dying! I shivered as I listened, but drew near and nearer, that I might lose no word that came from his stony lips.

===Chinese===
「将死之人的声音何等可怖！我听着，浑身打了个冷战，却仍凑得越来越近，唯恐漏掉他那双石像般的嘴唇里吐出的任何一个字。

===Original===
" 'She will not come,' gasped he, with an effort that raised him up in bed, and deepened that horrible stare, 'but—'

===Chinese===
『她不会回来了。』他喘着气说，那一阵用力使他竟在床上撑起身子来，也更深了那叫人毛骨悚然的凝视，『可是——』

===Original===
"Who shall say what he might have uttered if Death's hand had delayed a single instant, but the inexorable shadow fell, and he never finished the sentence.

===Chinese===
「倘若死神的手迟上半刻，他还会说出什么来，谁能知道呢？然而那道无情无转圜的阴影落下去了，他这句话终究没能说完。

===Original===
"My child, these are frightful things for you to hear. God knows I would not assail your pure ears with a tale like this, if it were not for the help and sympathy I hope to gain from you. Sin is a hideous thing; the gulf it opens is wide and deep; well may it be said to swallow those who trust themselves above its flower-hung brink. But we who are human, owe something to humanity. Love stops not because of the gulf; love follows the sinner with wilder and more heartbreaking longing, the deeper and deeper he sinks into the illimitable darkness. Ten years have passed since we laid the Colonel away in the burying-place of all the Japhas, and dutiful to his last request, nailed up the front door of his speedily to be forsaken mansion. In all that time my watch has remained unbroken in this house, which by will he had left to me, but which I secretly hold in trust for her. The hour of six has found me at my post, sometimes elate with hope, sometimes depressed with repeated disappointments, but whether hopeful or sad, always trustful that the great God who Himself so loved all sinners, that He gave the life of His Son to rescue them, would ultimately grant me the desire of my heart. But the decrepitude of age is coming upon me, and each morning I leave my bed, with growing fear lest my infirmities will increase until they finally overcome my resolution. Child, if this should happen, if lying in my bed I should some day hear that she had come back, and failing to find the lamp burning and the welcome ready, had gone away again—But the thought is madness. I cannot bear it. A sinner, lost, degraded, suffering, starving, perhaps, is wandering this way. She is hardened and old in guilt; she has drunk the cup of life's passions and found them corrupting poison; all that was lovely and pure and good has withdrawn from her; she stands alone, shut off by her sin, like a wild thing in a circle of flame. What shall touch this soul? The preacher's voice has no charm for her; good men's advice is but empty air. God's love must be mirrored in human love, to strike an eye so unused to looking up. Where shall she find such love? It is all that can rescue her; love as great as her sin, as boundless as her degradation, as persistent as her suffering. Child—"

===Chinese===
「我的孩子，这些事叫你听了未免骇人。上帝知道，若不是盼望从你这里得到帮助与同情，我绝不肯拿这样一个故事来惊扰你纯洁的双耳。罪是可憎的东西；它所撕开的深渊又宽又深；人们说，那些敢在那缀满鲜花的深渊边上信步的人，被它一口吞去，这话是一点不错的。可我们既然是人，对人世便还欠着一份情分。爱并不因这深渊而却步；罪人越是沉入那无边无际的黑暗，爱反倒以一种更狂乱、更令人心碎的渴慕，追着他下去。自我们把上校安葬到杰法一族的墓地、又遵他临终之命，把他那座很快就要人去楼空的宅子的正门钉封起来，至今已过了十年。这十年里，我在这宅子中的守望一刻不曾间断——这宅子他遗嘱里留给了我，我却在暗中替她托管着。每日到了六点钟，我便守在自己的位子上，有时因希望而心喜，有时因一再的失望而低沉；然而无论怀着希望还是满怀忧伤，我始终相信：那位亲自如此爱了一切罪人，竟赐下自己独生子的性命来拯救他们的伟大上帝，终究会允我心愿。只是老年的衰朽正一日日追上我，每天早晨我从床上起身，便越发起一层怕——怕我这副孱弱会愈益加重，到头来压垮我的决心。孩子，倘若真有这一天，倘若我卧病在床，某一日听人说她回来了，却寻不见亮着的灯、寻不见备好的欢迎，又转身走了——可是这个念头就是发疯。我受不住。一个罪人——迷失的、堕落的、受苦的、也许正在挨饿的——正向这边走来。她在罪里已变得又麻木又老练；人生的种种情欲之杯她都已饮尽，发现它们尽是腐蚀人心的毒酒；一切可爱、纯洁、善良的东西都已从她身上退去；她孤零零地立着，被自己的罪所隔绝，像一只被一圈烈火围住的野兽。什么东西能触动这颗灵魂呢？传道人的声音对她再无魅力；好人的劝诫不过是空空的清风。上帝的爱必须映照在人的爱里，才能击中这样一双如此不习惯仰望的眼睛。她到哪里去寻找这样的爱呢？唯有这爱能救她：与她的罪同等浩大的爱，与她的堕落同等无边的爱，与她的苦难同等持久的爱。孩子——」

===Original===
"I know what you are going to say," suddenly exclaimed Paula, rising up and confronting Mrs. Hamlin with a steady high look of determination. "In the day of your weakness or illness you want someone to unlock the door and light the lamp. You have found her!"

===Chinese===
「我知道您要说什么。」宝拉（Paula）蓦地出声，站起身来，以一种沉稳而高贵的决断眼神，迎上了哈姆林夫人（Mrs. Hamlin）。「在您病弱的那一天，您要一个人来替您开门、替您点灯。这个人，您已经找到了！」

## XLVI The Man Cummins / 四十六 库明斯其人

===Original===
> "Oh day and night, but this is wondrous strange."

> "Shut up in measureless content."

The lights were yet shining in Mr. Stuyvesant's parlors, though the guests were gone, who but a short time before had assembled there to witness the marriage of Cicely's dear friend, Paula.

At one end of the room stood Mr. Sylvester and Bertram, the former gazing with the eyes of a bridegroom, at the delicate white-clad figure of Paula, just leaving the apartment with Cicely.

===Chinese===
> 「啊，日也夜也，这真是离奇得叫人难信。」

> 「幽居于无边的满足之中。」

斯泰弗森特先生客厅里的灯火犹自亮着，虽说方才宾客们都已散去——就在不久之前，他们还聚在此处，观礼西塞莉挚友宝拉的婚礼。

屋子一头站着西尔维斯特先生和伯特兰，前者以一个新郎的目光，凝望着宝拉那一袭素白、正与西塞莉一同退出房间的纤纤身影。

===Original===
"I have but one cause for regret," said Mr. Sylvester as the door closed. "I could have wished that you and Cicely had participated in our joy and received the minister's benediction at the same moment as ourselves."

"Yes," said Bertram with a short sigh. "But it will come in time. It cannot be but that our efforts must finally succeed. I have just had a new idea; that of putting the watchman on the hunt for Hopgood. They are old friends, and he ought to know all the other's haunts and possible hiding-places."

===Chinese===
「我只憾有一桩，」门关上时，西尔维斯特先生说道，「我本愿你和西塞莉也能与我们同享这份喜悦，与我们在同一时刻领受牧师的祝福。」

「是啊，」伯特兰短叹了一声，「但那一天终归会来的。我们这一番努力，不可能终究毫无结果。我刚想到一个新主意——让那个守夜人去追查霍普古德（Hopgood）的下落。他们是老交情了，他理当知道对方一切常去之处和可能的藏身之地。」

===Original===
"If Fanning could have helped us, he would have told us long ago. He knows that Hopgood is missing and that we are ready to pay well for any information concerning him."

"But they are old cronies, and possibly Fanning is keeping quiet out of consideration for his friend."

"No; I have had a talk with Fanning, and there was no mistaking his look of surprise when told the other had run away under suspicion of being connected with a robbery on the bank's effects. He knows no more of Hopgood than we do, or his wife does, or the police even. It is a strange mystery, and one to which I fear we shall never obtain the key. But don't let me discourage you; after a suitable time Mr. Stuyvesant will—"

He paused, for that gentleman was approaching him.

===Chinese===
「法宁（Fanning）要是能帮得上忙，他早就对我们说了。他清楚霍普古德失踪一事，也清楚我们愿意为任何有关他的消息重金酬谢。」

「可他们是老伙计，说不定法宁是出于对朋友的顾忌，才一直闷声不响。」

「不然；我同法宁谈过，当被告知那人因涉嫌与一桩银行财物盗案有牵连而潜逃时，他脸上那惊讶之色是错不了的。他对霍普古德的事并不比我们知道得多，也不比他妻子、甚至警方知道得多。这是一桩离奇的谜，我怕我们永远也寻不着谜底。不过，别叫我扫了你的兴；等过上一段相宜的时日，斯泰弗森特先生会——」

他打住了，因为那位先生正朝他走来。

===Original===
"There is a man outside who insists upon seeing me; says he knows there has just been a wedding here, but that the matter he has to communicate is very important, and won't bear putting off. The name on his card is Cummins; I am afraid I shall have to admit him, that is, if you have no objection?"

Mr. Sylvester and Bertram at once drew back with ready acquiescence. They had scarcely taken their stand at the other end of the apartment, when the man came in. He was of robust build, round, precise and businesslike. He had taken off his hat, but still wore his overcoat; his face in spite of a profusion of red whiskers and a decided pair of goggles, was earnest and straightforward. He walked at once up to Mr. Stuyvesant.

===Chinese===
「外头有个人，非要见我不可；他说他知道这里刚刚办过一场喜事，可他要通报的事十分要紧，耽搁不得。他名片上印的是库明斯（Cummins）这个名字；看来我不得不放他进来——这自然要看你们二位有没有异议？」

西尔维斯特先生和伯特兰立即爽快地依言退至一旁。他们才在屋子另一头站定，那人便走了进来。他体格壮实，身形敦圆，一举一动干脆利落，一副办事人的派头。他已脱下帽子，身上却还披着外套；一脸浓密的红色连鬓胡，鼻梁上架着一副颇为扎眼的大护目镜——纵然如此，那张脸仍是恳切而率直的。他径直朝斯泰弗森特先生走去。

===Original===
"Your pardon," said he, in a quick tone. "But I hear you have been somewhat exercised of late over the disappearance of certain bonds from one of the boxes in the Madison Bank. I am a detective, and in the course of my duty have come upon a few facts that may help to explain matters."

Mr. Sylvester and Bertram at once started forward; this was a topic that demanded their attention as well as that of the master of the house.

The man cast them a quick look from behind his goggles, and seeming to recognize them, included them in his next question.

===Chinese===
「恕我冒昧，」他语调急促地说，「但我听说，近来麦迪逊银行（Madison Bank）有一只保险箱里的若干债券不翼而飞，颇令各位焦心。我是个侦探，因公查访之间，撞见了几桩事实，或可有助于把事情说明白。」

西尔维斯特先生和伯特兰登时抢上一步——这一桩事，同这座宅子的主人一样，正也揪着他们的心。

那人从护目镜后面飞快地瞥了他们一眼，似乎认出了他们，便把下一句问话也一并算上了他们：

===Original===
"What do you think of the watchman, Fanning?"

"Think? we don't think," uttered Mr. Stuyvesant sharply. "He has been in the employ of the bank for twelve years, and we know him to be honest."

"Yet he is the man who stole your bonds."

"Impossible!"

"The very man."

===Chinese===
「你们觉得那个守夜人，法宁，怎么样？」

「觉得？我们谈不上什么觉得，」斯泰弗森特先生尖利地答道，「他在银行里做事已经十二年了，我们都知道他为人诚实。」

「可偷你们债券的，正是此人。」

「不可能！」

「正是此人。」

===Original===
Mr. Sylvester stepped up to him. "Who are you, and how do you know this?"

"I have said my name is Cummins, and I know this, because I have wormed myself into the man's confidence and have got the bonds, together with his confession, here in my pocket." And he drew out the long lost bonds, which he handed to their owner, with a bit of paper on which was inscribed in the handwriting of the watchman, an acknowledgment to the effect that he, alone and unassisted, had perpetrated the robbery which had raised such scandal in the bank and led to the disappearance of Hopgood.

===Chinese===
西尔维斯特先生走到他跟前。「你是何人？这又是从何得知的？」

「我说过敝姓库明斯，我之所以知道，是因为我已设法取得了那人的信任，把那些债券连同他的亲口供词都弄到了手——就在我口袋里。」说着，他掏出那久已丢失的债券，交还给它们的主人；同时还附了一张小纸片，上面以那守夜人的笔迹写着一纸认状，言明是他独自一人、并无旁人协助，犯下了这桩在银行里掀起如此轩然大波、并致使霍普古德失踪的盗案。

===Original===
"And the man himself?" cried Bertram, when they had all read this. "Where is he?"

"Oh, I allowed him to escape."

Mr. Sylvester frowned.

"There is something about this I don't understand," said he. "How came you to take such an interest in this matter; and why did you let the man escape after acknowledging his crime?"

===Chinese===
「那人本人呢？」众人读罢，伯特兰失声喊道，「他在哪儿？」

「哦，我放他逃了。」

西尔维斯特先生皱起了眉。

「这事里头有些蹊跷，我弄不明白，」他说，「你怎么会对这桩事这般上心？又为何在那人认罪之后，反倒放他逃走？」

===Original===
With a quick, not undignified action, Cummins stepped back. "Gentlemen," said he, "it is allowable in a detective in the course of his duty, to resort to means for eliciting the truth, that in any other cause and for any other purpose, would be denominated as unmanly, if not mean and contemptible. When I heard of this robbery, as I did the day after its perpetration, my mind flew immediately to the watchman as the possible culprit. I did not know that he had done the deed, and I did not see how he could have possessed the means of doing it, but I had been acquainted with him for some time, and certain expressions which I had overheard him use—expressions that had passed over me lightly at the time, now recurred to my mind with startling distinctness. 'If a man knew the combination of the vault door, how easily he could make himself rich from the contents of those boxes!' was one, I remember; and another, 'I have worked in the bank for twelve years and have not so much money laid up against a rainy day, as would furnish Mr. Sylvester in cigars for a month.' The fact that he had no opportunity to learn the combination, was the only stumbling-block in the way of my conclusions. But that obstacle was soon removed. In a talk with the janitor's wife—a good woman, sirs, but a trifle conceited—I learned that he had once had the very opportunity of which I speak, provided he was smart enough to recognize the fact. The way it came about was this. Hopgood, who always meant to do about the right thing, as I know, was one morning very sick, so sick that when the time came for him to go down and open the vaults for the day, he couldn't stir from his bed, or at least thought he couldn't. Twice had the watchman rung for him, and twice had he tried to get up, only to fall back again on his pillow. At last the call became imperative; the clerks would soon be in, and the books were not even in readiness for them. Calling his wife to him, he asked if she thought she could open the vault door provided she knew the combination. She returned a quite eager, 'yes,' being a naturally vain woman and moreover a little sore over the fact that her husband never entrusted her with any of his secrets. 'Then,' said he, 'listen to those three numbers that I give you; and turn the knob accordingly,' explaining the matter in a way best calculated to enlighten her as to what she had to do. She professed herself as understanding perfectly and went off in quite a flutter of satisfaction to accomplish her task. But though he did not know it at the time, it seems that her heart failed her when she got into the hall, and struck with fear lest she should forget the numbers before she got to the foot of the stairs, she came back, and carefully wrote them down on a piece of paper, armed with which she started for the second time to fulfil her task. The watchman was in the bank when she entered, and to his expressions of surprise, she answered that her husband was ill and that she was going to open the vaults. He offered to help her, but she stared at him with astonishment, and waiting till he had walked to the other end of the bank, proceeded to the vault door, and after carefully consulting the paper in her hand, was about to turn the knob as directed, when Hopgood himself came into the room. He was too anxious, he said, to keep in bed, and though he trembled at every step, came forward and accomplished the task himself. He did not see the paper in his wife's hand, nor notice her when she tore it up and threw the pieces in the wastebasket nearby, but the watchman may have observed her, and as it afterwards proved, did; and thus became acquainted with the combination that unlocked the outer vault doors."

===Chinese===
库明斯纵身往后一退，那动作虽急，倒并不失体面。「诸位先生，」他说，「一个侦探为履行职责，所采取的某些探求真相的手段，若换在别种事业、别种目的之下，便不免要被人称作不够光明正大，甚而卑劣可鄙了。我一听闻这桩盗案——事发翌日我便听说了——心里便当即疑到那守夜人，疑心他是那个可能的案犯。我并不敢断定此事必是其所为，也想不出他能有怎样的法子下手；可我与他相识已有一段时日，几句我曾偶尔听他随口说出的话——当时只当耳旁风轻轻掠过——此刻却以惊人的清晰重现于我脑际。我记得有一句是：『一个人若是知道那保险库门上的密码，要从这些箱匣的内容里把自己发家致富，岂不是易如反掌！』另一句是：『我在银行里做了十二年，攒下来以备不时之需的钱，还不够供西尔维斯特先生一个月抽雪茄的。』而他没有机会学到那个密码——这是我推论之上唯一的绊脚石。可这一重障碍，不久便除去了。我与那看门人的妻子谈了一回话——她是个好女人，诸位先生，只是略有些自命不凡——从她口中我得知，他确实曾有过我所说的那等机会，只看他够不够机灵，识得这一点。事情原是这样的。霍普古德——据我所知，他向来是个做事不出大格的人——一天早上病得不轻，病到每日里该下楼去开保险库的时辰到了，他竟下不了床，或者至少他自以为下不了。守夜人为这事已经按过两次铃，他也试着起身两次，每次都只能重新跌回枕上。可催唤终至到了不可再缓的地步；办事员们眼看就要进来，账册却还全未为他们备好。他把妻子叫到跟前，问她若是知道那组密码，可想自己能开得了那只库门。她极其爽快地应了一声『能』——她天性要强爱面子，何况心里还有点小小的不痛快，恼丈夫从不肯把任何机密交托给她。『那么，』他说，『你听好我报给你的那三个数字，照着去拧那旋钮便是，』说罢又细细交代了一番，好叫她明白自己当如何动手。她口口声声说全明白了，便满怀得意地一阵风似地去办她的事。可霍普古德当时并不知道的是——看来她一走进过道便打了退堂鼓，唯恐还没下到楼梯脚下，便把那几个数字忘个干净，于是又折回来，仔仔细细地把它们写在一张纸片上；握着这道护身符，她才第二度出发去履命。她进银行时，那守夜人正在里头；对她这副意外出现的样子表示惊讶，她答说丈夫病了，她来替他开库。他提出要帮忙，她却一脸诧异地瞪着他，等他走到银行那一头去，才径直走到库门前，仔细照着手中纸片上写的，正要依言去拧那旋钮——恰在这时，霍普古德本人走进了屋子。他说他实在放心不下，躺不住了，便颤巍巍地，一步一抖地走上前来，亲手把那桩事办了。他未曾看见妻子手中的纸片，也未留意她将它撕碎、丢进旁边的废纸篓——可那守夜人说不定看见了，而事后证明，他确是看见了；如此一来，那开启库门外层的密码，便叫他得了去。」

===Original===
"Humph!" broke in Mr. Sylvester, "if this is true, why didn't Hopgood inform me of the matter when I questioned him so closely?"

"Because he had forgotten the circumstance. He was in a fever at the time, and having eventually unlocked the vault himself, lost sight of the fact that he had previously sent his wife to do it. He went back to his bed after the clerks came in, and did not get up again till night. He may have thought the whole occurrence part of the delirium which more than once assailed him that day."

"I remember his being sick," said Bertram; "it was two or three days before the robbery."

"The very day before," corrected the man; "but let me tell my story in my own way. Having learned from Mrs. Hopgood of this opportunity which had been given to Fanning, I made up my mind to sift the matter. Being as I have said a friend of his, I didn't want to peach on him unless he was guilty. To blast an honest man's reputation, is, I think, one of the meanest tricks of which a fellow can be guilty: but the truth I had to know, and in order to learn it, a deep and delicate game was necessary. Gentlemen, when the police have strong suspicions against a person whose reputation is above reproach and whose conduct affords no opportunity for impeachment, they set a springe for him. One of their number disguises himself, and making the acquaintance of this person, insinuates himself by slow degrees—often at the cost of months of effort—into his friendship and if possible into his confidence. 'Tis a detestable piece of business, but it is all that will serve in some cases, and has at least the merit of being as dangerous as it is detestable. This plan, I undertook with Fanning. Changing my appearance to suit the necessities of the case, I took board in the small house in Brooklyn where he puts up, and being well acquainted with his tastes, knew how to adapt myself to his liking. He was a busy man, and being obliged by his duties to turn night into day, had not much time to bestow upon me or anyone else; but heedful of this, I managed to make the most of the spare moments that saw us together, and ere long we were very good comrades, and further on, very good friends. The day when I first ventured to suggest that honesty was all very well as long as it paid, was a memorable one to me. In that cast of the die I was either to win or lose the game I had undertaken. I won. After a feint or two, to see if I were in earnest, he fell into the net, and though he did not commit himself then, it was not long before he came to me, and deliberately requested my assistance in disposing of some bonds which he was smart enough to acquire, but not daring enough to attempt to sell. Of course the whole story came out, and I was sympathetic enough till I got the bonds into my hands, then—But I leave you to imagine what followed. Enough that I wrung this confession from him, and that in consideration of the doubtful game I had played upon him, let him go where he is by this time beyond the chance of pursuit."

===Chinese===
「哼！」西尔维斯特先生插话道，「这话若当真，那我当初那样紧紧地盘问霍普古德，他为何不把这事告诉我？」

「因为那件事他早已忘了。其时他正在发烧，后来终究是亲手开了那只库门，便把先前差遣妻子去开一事抛在了脑后。办事员们进来之后，他便回床歇息，直到入夜才再起身。那整件事，他说不定只当是自己那天不止一次发作的谵妄之中的一段。」

「我记得他病过一场，」伯特兰说，「是在出事之前两三天。」

「正是出事的前一日，」那人纠正道，「不过，且容我以自己的法子把话说完。我既从霍普古德太太口中得知法宁曾有过这等机会，便拿定主意要把事情探个分明。我如前所述与他乃是朋友，自不愿在未见真章之时便出卖他。毁坏一个清白人的名声，依我看，乃是一个人所能做的最卑劣的勾当之一：可真相我非知道不可，而要探出真相，便非得布下一局深谋慎行之棋不可。诸位先生，警方若对一个人起了强烈的疑心，而这人名声无瑕、行迹又无可指摘，他们便会为他设下一副陷阱。自己人中一个改了装束，去与那人结识，再一点一点地——往往要费上数月的工夫——打进去，进到他的友谊里，可能的话，进到他的信任里。这是桩叫人作呕的勾当，可在某些案子中却别无他途，至少它有这样一个好处：它与叫人作厌同等程度地危险。这套法子，我便用在了法宁身上。我依着案情的需要改了容貌，到布鲁克林（Brooklyn）他寄宿的那间小屋去包了伙住下，因我熟知他的口味，便晓得如何投其所好。他是个忙人，职责所在，不得不以夜作昼，没有多少工夫可花在我、或任何人身上；可我留心到这一点，便尽力利用我们相处的点滴空闲，不久我们便是极好的伙伴，再往后，便是极好的朋友。我头一回大着胆子，试探着说出『诚实原是好事，只要它划算得来』这样的话——那一天于我是难忘的一日。这一掷之下，我所担当的那局棋，或赢或输，便见分晓。我赢了。他虚晃一两招，试出我是当真的，便落入了网中；虽说当时他并未把话说死，可不久之后，他便来找我，从容不迫地请我帮忙脱手若干债券——这些债券他有本事弄到手，却没有胆子自己去脱手。事情的来龙去脉自然和盘托出，我也跟着同情怜悯，直至把债券弄到了手中，那时——不过其后之事，诸位自可想象。我只需说，我从他口中榨出了这纸供状，又念及我对他玩的这套手段到底不大地道，便放他走了——此刻他已到了追捕不及的地方。」

===Original===
"But your duty to your superior; your oath as a member of the force?"

"My superior is here!" said the man pointing to Mr. Sylvester; "an unconscious one I own, but still my superior; and as for my being a member of the force, that was true five years ago, but not today." And brushing off his whiskers with one hand and taking off his goggles with the other, Hopgood, the janitor, stood before them!

===Chinese===
「可你对上司的职责呢？你身为警员所立的誓呢？」

「我的上司便在这里！」那人指着西尔维斯特先生说道，「我承认，他虽不自知，可到底是我的上司；至于我身为警员一节——那是五年前的事，今日却不是了。」说时，他一手抹下那副连鬓胡，一手摘去那副护目镜——那看门人霍普古德，便赫然立于众人之前！

---

===Original===
It was a radiant figure that met Cicely, when she came downstairs with Paula, and a joyous group that soon surrounded the now blushing and embarrassed janitor, with questions and remarks concerning this great and unexpected development of affairs. But the fervor with which Mr. Stuyvesant clasped Bertram's hand, and the look with which Cicely turned from her young lover to bestow a final kiss upon the departing bride, was worth all the pains and self-denial of the last few weeks—or so the janitor thought, who with a quicker comprehension than usual, had divined the situation and rejoiced in the result. But the most curious thing of all was to observe how, with the taking off of his goggles, Hopgood had relapsed into his old shrinking, easily embarrassed self. The man who but a few minutes before had related in their hearing a clear and succinct narrative, now shrank if a question was put him, and stammered in quite his ancient fashion, when he answered Mr. Sylvester's shake of the hand, by a hurried:

===Chinese===
西塞莉陪宝拉下楼时，迎上她的是一幅喜气洋溢的光景；不多时，那一群人便围住了此刻正红着脸、手足无措的看门人，七嘴八舌地问着、议论着这桩重大而出人意表的变故。然而斯泰弗森特先生紧握伯特兰之手的那股热忱，西塞莉从她那年轻的爱人身上回过头来、给这临行新娘以最后一吻时的那一眼——这数周来的种种辛苦与克制，便都值回来了——至少那看门人是这般想的；他这一回比素日机敏了些，已揣度出了眼前的情势，并为这结局满心欢喜。然而最叫人好奇不过的是：霍普古德那副护目镜一摘下来，他便又缩回了原先那个畏缩、动辄窘迫的老样子。方才还当着众人之面，把一桩事的始末讲得条理分明、简明扼要的那个人，此刻若有人问他一句话，便又会矮了半截；他以与西尔维斯特先生握手之机，仓促地答了那么一句，口吃的样子，与从前竟毫无二致：

===Original===
"I am going to see my wife now, sir. She's a good woman, if a little flighty, and will be the last one in the future to beg me to put more confidence in her. Will you tell me where she is, sir?"

Mr. Sylvester informed him; then added, "But look here, Hopgood, answer me one thing before you go. Why is it that with such talents as you possess, you didn't stay in the police force? You are a regular genius in your way, and ought not to drone away your existence as a janitor."

===Chinese===
「我这就去看我妻子，先生。她是个好女人，纵然略微轻浮些；日后她是再不会催我把更多机密交托给她了。先生，您可否告诉我她在何处？」

西尔维斯特先生告知了他；接着又道：「可是，霍普古德，你临走之前，回答我一件事。你有这般才干，当年为何不留在警界？以你这般本事，真是难得的一位奇才，本不该做一辈子看门人、浑浑噩噩地混日子。」

===Original===
"Ah, sir," replied the other, shaking his head, "a man who is only capable of assuming one disguise, isn't good for much as a professional detective. Goggles and red whiskers will deceive one rogue, but not fifty. My eyes were my bane, sir, and ultimately cost me my place. While I could cover them up I was all right. It not only made a man of me, leaving me free to talk and freer to think, but disguised me so, my best friends couldn't recognize me; but after awhile my goggles were too well known for me to be considered of much further use to the department, and I was obliged to send in my resignation. It is too bad, but I have no versatility, sir. I'm either the clumsy, stammering creature you have always known, or else I am the man Cummins you saw here a few minutes ago."

"In either case an honest fellow," answered Mr. Sylvester, and allowed the janitor to depart.

===Chinese===
「唉，先生，」对方摇着头答道，「一个人一辈子只会一副化装的本事，做职业侦探是没多大出息的。一副护目镜、一把红胡须，能蒙得住一个坏人，却蒙不住五十个。我这双眼睛是我命里的克星，先生，到头来叫我为它们丢了差事。只要能把它们遮起来，我便万事大吉。这不但使我像个像样的人，叫我放胆说话、放胆思虑，更把我化装得连我最好的朋友都认不出来；可时日一久，我这副护目镜太出名了，警务上便觉得我再无可大用之处，我也就不得不递上辞呈。这实在可惜，可我毫无变通的余地，先生。我若不是诸位一向认得的那副笨拙、口吃的模样，便是方才诸位所见的那位库明斯其人。」

「无论哪一副模样，都是个诚实的人。」西尔维斯特先生答道，便放那看门人去了。

---

===Original===
One more scene, and this in the house which Paula is henceforth to make a home for herself and its once melancholy owner. They have come back from their wedding-journey, and are standing in their old fashion, he at the foot, and she halfway up the stairs. Suddenly she turns and descends to his side.

"No, I will not wait," said she. "Here, on this spot we both love so well, and in this the first hour of our return, I will unburden my mind of what I have to say. Edward, is there nothing of all the past that still rests upon you like a shadow? Not one little regret you could wish taken away?"

===Chinese===
再说一幕场景，这一幕发生在宝拉日后要为她和这宅子那位一度郁郁寡欢的主人安下的新家。他们已从婚礼之旅归来，仍照他们的老样子站着——他在楼梯脚下，她则在楼梯半途。忽然，她转过身，走下来到他身旁。

「不，我不能再等了，」她说，「就在这里，在这处我们都如此钟爱的地方，在我们归来的第一个时辰里，我要把心里的话一吐为快。爱德华，从前种种，当真没有一丝一毫还像阴影一样压在你心头？没有一点小小的憾事，是你愿它被一笔勾销的？」

===Original===
"No," said he, enfolding her in his arms with a solemn smile. "The great gift which I hold is the fruit of that past, perhaps; I cannot wish it changed."

"But the sense of obligation never fulfilled, would you not be happier if that were removed?"

"Perhaps," he said, "but it cannot be now. I shall have to live without being perfectly happy."

===Chinese===
「没有，」他说着，带着郑重的微笑将她拥入怀中，「我所握有的这份大礼，或许便是那往昔的果实；我不能愿它换一个模样。」

「可那一桩从未偿清的亏负之感——若能将它除去，你岂不更快活？」

「也许吧，」他说，「可如今已不能了。我只好就这么过下去，做一个并不十全十美地快乐的人。」

===Original===
She lifted her face and her smile shone like a star. "Oh God is good," she cried, "you shall not lack being perfectly happy;" and taking a little paper out of her pocket she put it in his hand. "We found that hidden in Jacqueline Japha's breast, when we went to lay her out for burial."

It was only a line; but it made Mr. Sylvester's brow flush and his voice tremble.

---

"Whatever I own, and I have been told that I am far from penniless, I desire to have given to the dear and disinterested girl that first told me of Margery Hamlin's vigil."

---

===Chinese===
她抬起脸来，那一笑灿若星辰。「啊，上帝是慈悲的，」她喊道，「你必不至于少了那份十全十美的快乐；」说着，她从口袋里掏出一张小纸片，放进他手里。「这是我们去为雅克琳·雅法（Jacqueline Japha）入殓时，在她贴胸之处找到的。」

那不过区区一行字；却叫西尔维斯特先生热潮涌上额头，声音也为之颤抖。

---

「凡我所有的——而我听说自己远非一贫如洗——我都愿捐与那位头一个向我讲起玛乔丽·哈姆林（Margery Hamlin）守夜之事的、可敬而无求的好姑娘。」

---

===Original===
"Paula, Paula, Paula, thou art indeed my good gift! May God make me worthy of your love and of this His last and most unexpected mercy!"

And the look which crossed her face, was that sweet and unearthly radiance which speaks of perfect peace.

===Chinese===
「宝拉，宝拉，宝拉，你当真是我命里所赐的好礼物！愿上帝叫我配得上你的爱，配得上他这临末、最出乎意料的怜悯！」

而她脸上掠过的那一抹神情，正是那种甜美而超凡的光辉——那种道出完完全全平安的光辉。

## XXXVII The Opinion of a Certain Noted Detective / 三十七 一位著名侦探的看法

===Original===
> "But still there clung
   
 One hope, like a keen sword on starting threads uphung."

> "Facts are stubborn things."

===Chinese===
> 「然而仍有一线希望萦系不去，
>  犹如一柄利剑，悬于将断未断的丝线之上。」

> 「事实乃是顽梗之物。」

===Original===
Meanwhile Mr. Stuyvesant hasted on his way downtown and ere long made his appearance at the bank. He found Mr. Sylvester and Bertram seated in the directors' room, with a portly smooth-faced man whose appearance was at once strange and vaguely familiar.

"A detective, sir," explained Mr. Sylvester rising with forced composure; "a man upon whose judgment I have been told we may rely. Mr. Gryce, Mr. Stuyvesant."

===Chinese===
与此同时，斯泰弗森特先生匆匆往城下赶去，不多时便出现在银行里。他看见西尔维斯特先生与伯特兰坐在董事会议室里，旁边还有一个体态丰盈、面庞光洁的男人，其面貌既觉陌生，又依稀叫人觉得在哪里见过。

「一位侦探，先生。」西尔维斯特先生强自镇定地站起身来解释道，「此人，据我所闻，其判断是可以信赖的。格莱斯先生（Mr. Gryce）——斯泰弗森特先生。」

===Original===
The latter gentleman nodded, cast a glance around the room, during which his eye rested for a moment on Bertram's somewhat pale countenance, and nervously took a seat.

"A mysterious piece of business, this," came from the detective's lips in an easy tone, calculated to relieve the tension of embarrassment into which the entrance of Mr. Stuyvesant seemed to have thrown all parties. "What were the numbers of the bonds found missing, if you please?"

Mr. Stuyvesant told him.

===Chinese===
后一位先生点了点头，朝屋内环视了一眼——其间他的目光在伯特兰那张略现苍白的脸上停留了片刻——便神情紧张地落了座。

「这件事可真够蹊跷的。」这句话从侦探口里吐出，语调从容，分明是有意要缓解一下斯泰弗森特先生进来时众人似乎都陷入的那股尴尬与紧张。「请问，发觉失窃的那些债券，号码是哪些？」

斯泰弗森特先生把号码报给了他。

===Original===
"You are positively assured these bonds were all in the box when you last locked it?"

"I am."

"When was that, sir? On what day and at what hour of the day, if you please?"

"Tuesday, at about three o'clock, I should say."

"The box was locked by you? There is no doubt about that fact?"

"None in the least."

"Where were you standing at the time?"

"In front of the vault door. I had taken out the box myself as I am in the habit of doing, and had stepped there to put it back."

"Was anyone near you then?"

"Yes. The cashier was at his desk and the teller had occasion to go to the safe while I stood there. I do not remember seeing anyone else in my immediate vicinity."

===Chinese===
「您敢肯定，您最后一次上锁时，这些债券都在匣子里么？」

「我敢肯定。」

「那是何时的事，先生？哪一日，一日里的哪个时辰，有劳见告？」

「星期二，下午三点钟光景，我估摸着。」

「是您亲手锁的匣子？此事确凿无疑？」

「毫无疑义。」

「当时您站在何处？」

「在保险库门前。我自己取出匣子——这是我素来的习惯——又走到那里，预备把它放回去。」

「那时您身畔还有旁人么？」

「有。出纳员坐在自己的案前；我立在那儿时，那位柜员又有事往保险柜那边走了一趟。至于紧挨着我身旁的，我记不得还看见过别的什么人。」

===Original===
"Do you remember ever going to the vaults and not finding someone near you at the time or at least in full view of your movements?"

"No."

"I have informed Mr. Gryce," interposed Mr. Sylvester, with a ring in his deep voice that made Mr. Stuyvesant start, "that our chief desire at present is to have his judgment upon the all important question, as to whether this theft was committed by a stranger, or one in the employ and consequently in the confidence of the bank."

===Chinese===
「您可曾记得，有哪一回往保险库去时，身畔既无人靠近，至少也无人能将您一举一动尽收眼底的？」

「记不得。」

「我已告知格莱斯先生，」西尔维斯特先生插话道，他低沉的嗓音里带着一种音调，惹得斯泰弗森特先生为之一怔，「我们眼下最盼望的，便是请他对那一桩至为紧要的问题作出裁断：这桩窃案，究竟是外人所为，还是银行雇用、因而也受银行信任之人所作。」

===Original===
Mr. Stuyvesant bowed, every wrinkle in his face manifesting itself with startling distinctness as he slowly moved his eyes and fixed them on the inscrutable countenance of the detective.

"You agree then with these gentlemen," continued the latter, who had a way of seeming more interested in everything and everybody present than the person he was addressing, "that it would be difficult if not impossible for anyone unconnected with the bank, to approach the vaults during business hours and abstract anything from them without detection?"

"And do these gentleman both assert that?" queried Mr. Stuyvesant, with a sharp look from uncle to nephew.

"I believe they do," replied the detective, as both the gentlemen bowed, Bertram with an uncontrollable quiver of his lip, and Mr. Sylvester with a deepening of the lines about his mouth, which may or may not have been noticed by this man who appeared to observe nothing.

===Chinese===
斯泰弗森特先生鞠了一躬，脸上的每一道皱纹都显了出来——那清晰竟到了叫人吃惊的地步——他缓缓转动目光，把它定在侦探那张莫测高深的脸上。

「那么，您与这几位先生意见一致，」对方接着说——他有一种做派，似乎对在场的每一个人、每一件事，都比对他正在攀谈的那位更感兴趣，「认为但凡与银行无干之人，欲在营业时间内靠近保险库、从里面窃取任何东西而不被察觉，纵非绝无可能，也是难上加难？」

「这两位先生都这样断言么？」斯泰弗森特先生质问道，目光锐利地从叔父身上扫到侄儿身上。

「我相信是的。」侦探答道。两位先生俱各鞠躬——伯特兰嘴唇一阵按捺不住的颤动，西尔维斯特先生则嘴角的纹路加深了几分——这一丝变化，这位仿佛什么也不曾留意的人，未必看见，也未必未曾看见。

===Original===
"I should be loth to conclude that the robbery was committed by anyone but a stranger," remarked Mr. Stuyvesant; "but if these gentlemen concur in the statement you have just made, I am bound to acknowledge that I do not myself see how the theft could have been perpetrated by an outsider. Had the box itself been missing, it would be different. I remember my old friend Mr. A—, the president of the police department, telling me of a case where a box containing securities to the amount of two hundred thousand dollars, was abstracted in full daylight from the vaults of one of our largest banks; an act requiring such daring, the directors for a long time refused to believe it possible, until a detective one day showed them another box of theirs which he had succeeded in abstracting in the same way.1 But the vaults in that instance were in a less conspicuous portion of the bank than ours, besides to approach an open vault, snatch a box from it and escape, is a much simpler matter than to remain long enough to open a box and choose from its contents such papers as appeared most marketable. If a regular thief could do such a thing, it does not seem probable that he would. Nevertheless the most acute judgment is often at fault in these matters, and I do not pretend to have formed an opinion."

===Chinese===
「我不愿遽然断定这桩窃案非外人所作。」斯泰弗森特先生说道，「可若这两位先生都赞同您方才所言，那我便不得不承认：我自己也看不出这窃案怎能由一个外人下手。倘或失窃的乃是匣子本身，自当别论。我记得老友警察局长 A—先生曾同我讲过一桩案子：一只装有二十万元有价证券的匣子，竟在大白天从本市一家最大银行的保险库里被取走；此举所需胆量之大，使诸位董事久久不信其可行，直到后来某日，一位侦探把另一只属于他们的匣子——他以同样手法成功窃出的匣子——摆到了他们眼前。1可那一桩案子里的保险库，所处位置原不似我们这间这般显眼；况且，走近一只大开的库、从里头抓走一只匣子再脱身，与久久停留、去打开一只匣子、再从其所盛中挑出最易脱手的票据——前者比之后者，实在是简单得多的事。纵然一个惯窃能做出这种事来，似也不致当真去做。然而此等事，再敏锐的判断也常常失手，我不敢妄称已有了定见。」

===Original===
The detective who had listened to these words with marked attention, bowed his concurrence and asked if the bonds mentioned by Mr. Stuyvesant were all that had been found missing from the bank. If any of the other boxes had been opened, or if the contents of the safe itself had ever been tampered with.

"The contents of the safe are all correct," came in deep tones from Mr. Sylvester. "Mr. Folger, my nephew and myself went through them this morning. As for the boxes I cannot say, many of them belong to persons travelling; some of them have been left here by trustees of estates, consequently often lie for weeks in the vaults untouched. If however any of them have been opened, we ought to be able to see it. Would you like an examination made of their condition?"

===Chinese===
那侦探方才全神贯注地听完这番话，此刻鞠了一躬，以示赞同，随而问起：斯泰弗森特先生所提及的那些债券，可就是从银行里查觉失窃的全部？其余匣子可曾有哪只被打开过，保险柜本身所盛之物可曾被人动过手脚？

「保险柜所盛一概无误。」西尔维斯特先生以深沉的嗓音发话。「福尔杰先生、舍侄与我今早逐一核对过了。至于匣子，我说不准——其中不少属于在外旅行之人；又有几只是遗产受托人存放于此的，故而常常在库里一连几周无人触动。然而倘有哪只曾被打开过，我们理应能看出端倪。您可愿让人查验一番它们的情形？」

===Original===
The detective nodded.

Mr. Sylvester at once turned to Mr. Stuyvesant. "May I ask you to mention what officer of the bank you would like to have go to the vaults?"

That gentleman started, looked uneasily about, but meeting Bertram's eye, nervously dropped his own and muttered the name of Folger.

Mr. Sylvester suppressed a sigh, sent for the paying-teller, and informed him of their wishes. He at once proceeded to the vaults. While he was gone, Mr. Gryce took the opportunity to make the following remark.

===Chinese===
侦探点了点头。

西尔维斯特先生立刻转向斯泰弗森特先生。「可否请您指定，您愿由行里哪一位职员下库去？」

那位先生为之一怔，不安地四下望了望，可一遇上伯特兰的目光，便紧张地垂下自己的眼睛，嘟囔着说出了福尔杰这个名字。

西尔维斯特先生强抑住一声叹息，着人去叫那位付款柜员，把他们的意思告知了他。福尔杰立刻下库去了。趁他不在，格莱斯先生抓住空隙发了如下一通议论。

===Original===
"Gentlemen," said he, "let us understand ourselves. What you want of me, is to tell you whether this robbery has been committed by a stranger or by someone in your employ. Now to decide this question it is necessary for me to ask first, whether you have ever had reason to doubt the honesty of any person connected with the bank?"

"No," came from Mr. Sylvester with sharp and shrill distinctness. "Since I have had the honor of conducting the affairs of this institution, I have made it my business to observe and note the bearing and character of each and every man employed under me, and I believe them all to be honest."

===Chinese===
「诸位先生，」他说，「我们之间先把话说清楚。你们要我做的，是告诉你们这桩窃案究竟是外人所为，还是你们所雇之人所作。那么，要决断这个问题，我必须先问一句：你们可曾有任何缘由，怀疑过与银行有涉之人的诚实？」

「没有。」西尔维斯特先生答道，那两个字又尖又亮，清晰异常。「自从我有幸主持这家机构的各项事务以来，我便把察看、记录麾下每一名雇员的举止行止与品性视为己任，我相信他们个个诚实。」

===Original===
The glance of the detective while it did not perceptibly move from the large screen drawn across the room at the back of Mr. Sylvester, seemed to request the opinions of the other two gentlemen on this point.

Bertram observing it, subdued the rapid beatings of his heart and spoke with like distinctness. "I have been in the bank the same length of time as my uncle," said he, "and most heartily endorse his good opinion of the various persons in our employ."

"And Mr. Stuyvesant?" the immovable glance seemed to say.

"Men are honest in my opinion till they are proved otherwise," came in short stern accents from the director's lips.

===Chinese===
侦探的目光——虽说并未明显地从西尔维斯特先生身后那面横亘屋内的大屏风上移开——却似乎在向另外两位先生就此一点征求意见。

伯特兰察觉到了，便按住心头急促的跳动，以同样清晰的口齿说道。「我在行里的时日与叔父一样长。」他说，「对于麾下各人，叔父所怀的善意评价，我衷心附和。」

「那么斯泰弗森特先生呢？」那一道纹丝不动的目光似乎在问。

「以我之见，人在未被证明为不诚实之前，皆是诚实的。」短短几句严峻的字句，从那位董事唇间吐出。

===Original===
The detective drew back in his chair as if he considered that point decided, and yet Bertram's eye which had clouded at Mr. Stuyvesant's too abrupt assertion, did not clear again as might have been expected.

"There is one more question I desire to settle," continued the detective, "and that is, whether this robbery could have been perpetrated after business hours, by someone in collusion with the person who is here left in charge?"

"No;" again came from Mr. Sylvester, with impartial justice. "The watchman—who by the way has been in the bank for twelve years—could not help a man to find entrance to the vaults. His simple duty is to watch over the bank and give alarm in case of fire or burglary. It would necessitate a knowledge of the combination by which the vault doors are opened, to do what you suggest, and that is possessed by but three persons in the bank."

"And those are?"

"The cashier, the janitor, and myself."

===Chinese===
侦探往椅背上一靠，仿佛认为那一点已无需再议，然而伯特兰那双眼——因斯泰弗森特先生过于生硬的断言而蒙上了一层云翳的——却不似预料那般重新澄澈起来。

「还有一个问题我想要敲定。」侦探接着说，「那就是：这桩窃案，可会是在非营业时间，由某位与留守此处之人串通一气者所作？」

「不会。」这话再次出自西尔维斯特先生之口，公允不偏。「那守夜人——顺便提一句，此人在行里已做了十二年——没法帮人进到保险库里去。他唯一的职责便是看守银行，遇火警或盗警时拉响警报。要做成您所揣度的那种事，必得知道开保险库门的那组暗码，而这暗码，行里只有三个人掌握。」

「那三位是？」

「出纳员、看门人，还有我自己。」

===Original===
He endeavored to speak calmly and without any betrayal of the effort it caused him to utter those simple words, but a detective's ear is nice and it is doubtful if he perfectly succeeded.

Mr. Gryce however limited himself to a muttered, humph! and a long and thoughtful look at a spot on the green baize of the table before which he sat.

"The janitor lives in the building, I suppose?"

"Yes, and is, as I am sure Mr. Stuyvesant will second me in asserting, honesty to the backbone."

"Janitors always are," observed the detective; then shortly, "How long has *he* been with you?"

"Three years."

Another "humph!" and an increased interest in the ink spot.

===Chinese===
他竭力平静地说出这几个简单的字眼，不露半分费力之态，然而侦探的耳朵是尖的，他是否当真做得天衣无缝，倒也难说。

不过格莱斯先生仅限于咕哝了一声「哼！」，又对着自己面前那块绿呢台布上的一处斑痕凝视良久。

「那看门人便住在这楼里，我猜？」

「正是。而且我确信，斯泰弗森特先生定会与我一同担保——此人诚实到了骨子里。」

「看门人向来如此。」侦探说道；接着又短促地补了一句，「*他*跟了你们多久了？」

「三年。」

又是一声「哼！」，对那处墨斑的兴趣又添了几分。

===Original===
"That is not long, considering the responsibility of his position."

"He was on the police force before he came to us," remarked Mr. Sylvester.

Mr. Gryce looked as if that was not much of a recommendation.

"As for the short time he has been with us," resumed the other, "he came into the bank the same winter as my nephew and myself, and has found the time sufficient to earn the respect of all who know him."

===Chinese===
「论及他所司之职的分量，这点时日不算长。」

「他来我们这里之前，曾在警察队里当过差。」西尔维斯特先生说道。

格莱斯先生的神情，似乎觉得这一点也算不上怎样的褒扬。

「至于他在我们这里时日之短，」对方接着说，「他来银行任职的那个冬天，正是舍侄与我进银行的同一个冬天；这些时日已足以使他博得所有认识他之人的敬重。」

===Original===
The detective bowed, seemingly awed by the dignity with which the last statement had been uttered; but anyone who knew him well, would have perceived that the film of uncertainty which had hitherto dimmed the brightness of his regard was gone, as if in the other's impressive manner, if not in the suggestion his words had unconsciously offered, the detective had received an answer to some question which had been puzzling him, or laid his hand upon some clue which had till now eluded his grasp. The inquiries which he made haste to pursue, betrayed, however, but little of the tendency of his thoughts.

"The janitor, you say, knows the combination by which the vault doors are opened?"

"The *vault doors*," emphasized Mr. Sylvester. "The safe is another matter; that stands inside the vault and is locked by a triple combination which as a whole is not known to any one man in this building, not even to myself."

===Chinese===
侦探鞠了一躬，似乎对那最后一番话所带出的庄严气度肃然起敬；但凡熟知此人的，都会察觉到，方才还罩在他目光之上的那一层犹疑的薄膜已经散去——仿佛从对方那撼人的气度里，纵非从其言语无意间透露的暗示里，这位侦探已得到了某个久困其心的问题的答案，又或攥住了某条至今与他失之交臂的线索。然而他紧接着发问的几个问题，却几乎全然看不出他心思所向。

「您是说，那看门人知道开保险库门的那组暗码？」

「*保险库门*。」西尔维斯特先生加重了语气。「保险柜是另一回事；它就立在保险库里头，由一组三重暗码锁住，整组暗码在这楼里没有哪一个人——连我自己在内——是统统知晓的。」

===Original===
"But the boxes are not kept in the safe?"

"No, they are piled up with the books in the vaults at the side of the safe, as you can see for yourself, if you choose to join Mr. Folger."

"Not necessary. The janitor, then, is the only man besides yourselves, who under any circumstances or for any reason, could get at those boxes after business hours?"

"He is."

"One question more. Who is the man to attend to those boxes? I mean to ask, which of the men in your employ is expected to procure a box out of the vaults when it is called for, and put it back in its place when its owner is through with it?"

"Hopgood usually does that business, the janitor of whom we have just been speaking. When he is upstairs or out of the way, anyone else whom it may be convenient to call."

===Chinese===
「可匣子并不放在保险柜里？」

「不；它们同账簿一道堆放在保险库里、保险柜的旁侧，您若肯随福尔杰先生下去一看便知。」

「倒也不必。那么除了诸位之外，那看门人是唯一一个——不论在何种情形下、为着何种缘故——能在非营业时间接触到那些匣子的人？」

「他是。」

「还有一个问题。平日里经管这些匣子的是谁？我是说，行里雇员之中，每当有人要取匣子，被指望下库去取、待主人用毕再放回原处的，是哪一位？」

「这种差事通常由霍普古德来做——就是我们方才说到的那位看门人。若他在楼上，或一时不在手边，便是哪位叫着方便，便由哪一位代劳。」

===Original===
"The janitor, then, has free access to the boxes at all times, night and day?"

"In one sense, yes, in another, no. Should he unlock the vaults at night, the watchman would report upon his proceedings."

"But there must be time between the closing and opening of the bank, when the janitor is alone with the vaults?"

"There is a space of two hours after seven in the morning, when he is likely to be the sole one in charge. The watchman goes home, and Hopgood employs himself in sweeping out the bank and preparing it for the business of the day."

"Are the watchman and the janitor on good terms with one another?"

"Very, I believe."

The detective looked thoughtful. "I should like to see this Hopgood," said he.

===Chinese===
「那么，日夜任何时候，看门人都能随意进出、接触那些匣子？」

「一面说是，一面说不是。倘若他在夜里开启保险库，守夜人便会就其行径上报。」

「可是在银行闭门与开门之间，必有那么一段时辰，看门人是独自与保险库相处的？」

「早上七点之后，有两小时的工夫，他大概便是唯一留守之人。守夜人回家去了，霍普古德便忙着打扫银行，为之开市那一日的营生做准备。」

「守夜人与看门人彼此交情如何？」

「我想是极好的。」

侦探面露思忖之色。「我想见一见这位霍普古德。」他说。

===Original===
But just then the door opened and Mr. Folger came in, looking somewhat pale and disturbed. "We are in a difficulty," cried he, stepping up to the table where they sat. "I have found two of the boxes unlocked; that belonging to Hicks, Saltzer and Co., and another with the name of Harrington upon it. The former has been wrenched apart, the latter opened with some sort of instrument. Would you like to see them, sir?" This to Mr. Sylvester.

With a start that gentleman rose, and as suddenly reseated himself. "Yes," returned he, carefully avoiding his nephew's eye; "bring them in."

"Hicks, Saltzer and Co., is a foreign house," remarked Mr. Stuyvesant to the detective, "and do not send for their box once a fortnight, as I have heard Mr. Sylvester declare. Mr. Harrington is on an exploring expedition and is at present in South America." Then in lower tones, whose sternness was not unmixed with gloom, "The thief seems to have known what boxes to go to."

Bertram flushed and made some passing rejoinder; Mr. Sylvester and the detective alone remained silent.

===Chinese===
可正在这时门开了，福尔杰先生走了进来，神情有些苍白、有些不安。「我们遇上难处了。」他嚷道，迈步走到他们围坐的那张桌前。「我发觉有两只匣子没上锁：一只是希克斯、萨尔泽公司（Hicks, Saltzer and Co.）的，另一只上面写着哈灵顿（Harrington）的名字。前一只是被硬撬开的，后一只是用什么家什给弄开的。您要不要瞧一瞧，先生？」这话是对西尔维斯特先生说的。

那位先生猛地站起身来，又同样突然地重新坐下。「好。」他答道，刻意避开侄儿的目光，「把它们拿进来。」

「希克斯、萨尔泽公司是一家洋行。」斯泰弗森特先生对侦探说道，「他们半月光景也未必叫人取一次匣子，我听西尔维斯特先生亲口说过。哈灵顿先生正在一支探险队里，眼下人在南美。」随后他又压低了嗓子，那严峻中不无阴郁之色：「这贼似乎知道该冲哪几只匣子下手。」

伯特兰涨红了脸，随口敷衍了几句作答；西尔维斯特先生与侦探则默然不语。

===Original===
The boxes being brought in, Mr. Gryce opened them without ceremony. Several papers met his eye in both, but as no one but the owners could know their rightful contents, it was of course impossible for him to determine whether anything had been stolen from them or not.

"Send for the New York agent of Hicks, Saltzer and Co.," came from Mr. Sylvester, in short, businesslike command.

Bertram at once rose. "I will see to it," said he. His agitation was too great for suppression, the expression of Mr. Stuyvesant's eye, that in its restlessness wandered in every direction but his own, troubled him beyond endurance. With a hasty move he left the room. The cold eye of the detective followed him.

"Looks bad," came in laconic tones from the paying teller.

"I had hoped the affair begun and ended with my individual loss," muttered Mr. Stuyvesant under his breath.

The stately president and the inscrutable detective still maintained their silence.

===Chinese===
匣子被拿进来后，格莱斯先生毫不客气地把它们一一打开。两只匣子里都有几份单据映入他的眼帘，可除了主人之外，谁也不知道匣中原应盛些什么，他当然无从判断里头是否少了什么。

「去把希克斯、萨尔泽公司驻纽约的代办请来。」西尔维斯特先生发话，短短一句，公事公办的口吻。

伯特兰立刻站起身来。「我去办。」他说。他的激动难以自抑——斯泰弗森特先生那一双目光，正躁动不安地朝四面八方游移，唯独不肯落到自己身上——这叫他难以忍受。他匆匆离了屋。侦探那双冷眼目送他出去。

「瞧着不妙。」付款柜员简短地说了一句。

「我原本指望这事从我一人之失起头，也到我一人之失收场。」斯泰弗森特先生压在喉咙底下咕哝着。

那位仪态庄重的行长与那位莫测高深的侦探，仍旧保持着各自的沉默。

===Original===
Suddenly the latter moved. Turning towards Mr. Sylvester, he requested him to step with him to the window. "I want to have a look at your several employees," whispered he, as they thus withdrew. "I want to see them without being seen by them. If you can manage to have them come in here one by one upon some pretext or other, I can so arrange that screen under the mantelpiece, that it shall not only hide me, but give me a very good view of their faces in the mirror overhead."

"There will be no difficulty about summoning the men," said Mr. Sylvester.

"And you consent to the scheme?"

"Certainly, if you think anything is to be gained by it."

===Chinese===
忽然，后一位动了起来。他转向西尔维斯特先生，请他随自己到窗子那边去。「我想瞧一瞧贵行几位雇员。」趁他们这样退到一旁时，他低声说道，「我要见他们，却不让他们见我。您若能设法找个什么由头，让他们一个一个到这里来，我便能把壁炉架下头那面屏风安排得不仅把我藏起，还能让我从头顶那面镜子里把他们的脸瞧得清清楚楚。」

「把人召来并不难。」西尔维斯特先生说。

「您应承这个法子？」

「自然应承，只要您觉着能从中有所获。」

===Original===
"I am sure that nothing will be lost. And sir, let the cashier be present if you please; and sir," squeezing his watch chain with a complacent air, as the other dropped his eyes, "talk to them about anything that you please, only let it be of a nature that will necessitate a sentence or more in reply. I judge a man as much by his voice as his expression."

Mr. Sylvester bowed, and without losing his self-command, though the short allusion to Bertram had greatly startled him, turned back to the table where Mr. Folger was still standing in conversation with the director.

"I will not detain you longer," said he to the paying teller. "Your discretion will prevent you from speaking of this matter, I trust." Then as the other bowed, added carelessly, "I have something to say to Jessup; will you see that he steps here for a moment?"

Mr. Folger again nodded and left the room. Instantly Mr. Gryce bustled forward, and pulling the screen into the position he thought best calculated to answer his requirements, slid rapidly behind it. Mr. Stuyvesant looked up in surprise.

===Chinese===
「我敢说，绝不会一无所获。还有，先生，劳您驾让出纳员也在场；再就是，先生，」他自得地捏着表链，趁对方垂下眼帘时说道，「您与他们随便谈什么都可以，只要所谈的事性质上须得他们回上一句或几句。我判人，看神情与听嗓音各占一半。」

西尔维斯特先生鞠了一躬，并未失了自持——尽管方才顺带提及伯特兰那一句叫他大为震惊——便转身回到福尔杰先生仍与那位董事站着攀谈的那张桌前。

「我不再留您了。」他对那位付款柜员说，「此事您自然慎于口舌，不会外传，我相信。」接着，趁对方鞠躬之际，他又漫不经心地添了一句：「我有话要同杰萨普（Jessup）说；劳您驾，叫他到这儿来一下成么？」

福尔杰先生又点了点头，离了屋。格莱斯先生立时忙活起来，把那面屏风拽到他认为最能合乎己用的位置，迅速闪到了屏风背后。斯泰弗森特先生诧异地抬起头来。

===Original===
"I am going to interview the clerks for Mr. Gryce's benefit," exclaimed Mr. Sylvester. "Will you in the meantime look over the morning paper?"

"Thank you," returned the other, edging nervously to one side, "my notebook will do just as well," and sitting down at the remote end of the table, he took out a book from his pocket, above which he bent with very well simulated preoccupation. Mr. Sylvester called in Bertram and then seated himself with a hopeless and unexpectant look, which he for the moment forgot would be reflected in the mirror before him, and so carried to the eye of the watchful detective. In another instant Jessup entered.

===Chinese===
「我要为格莱斯先生的缘故，把那几位办事员一一问过来。」西尔维斯特先生说道，「这工夫，您要不要翻翻晨报？」

「多谢。」对方答道，紧张地往边上挪了挪，「我的笔记本也就够了。」说着他便在桌子那最远的一头坐下，从口袋里掏出一册本子，俯身其上，装出一副十分入戏的专心模样。西尔维斯特先生把伯特兰叫进来，自己也随之落座，脸上是一副无望无待的神色——此刻他却忘了，这副神色会映在面前的镜子里，从而送入那位留心观望的侦探眼中。不一会儿，杰萨普走了进来。

===Original===
What was said in the short interview that followed, is unimportant. Mr. Jessup, the third teller, was one of those clear eyed, straightforward appearing men whose countenance is its own guarantee. It was not necessary to detain him or make him speak. The next man to come in was Watson, and after he had gone, two or three of the clerks, and later the receiving teller and one of the runners. All stopped long enough to insure Mr. Gryce a good view of their faces, and from each and all did Mr. Sylvester succeed in eliciting more or less conversation in response to the questions he chose to put.

===Chinese===
接下来的短短问答里说了些什么，并不打紧。杰萨普先生——那位三号柜员——是那种目光清朗、神情坦荡、面貌本身便是自身担保的人。既不必多留他，也不必非要他开口。下一位进来的是沃森（Watson）；沃森走后，又来了两三位办事员，再之后是收款柜员，还有一名跑街的。每个人停留的时间，都足以让格莱斯先生把他们的脸瞧个清楚；而西尔维斯特先生也成功地从他们每一个人、每一群人那里，借着自己有意抛出的问题，引出了或多或少的话头作答。

===Original===
With the disappearance of the last mentioned individual, Mr. Gryce peeped from behind the screen. "A set of as honest-looking men as I wish to see!" uttered he with a frank cordiality that was scarcely reflected in the anxious countenances about him. "No sly-boots among them; how about the janitor, Hopgood?"

"He shall be summoned at once, if you desire it," said Mr. Sylvester, "I have only delayed calling him that I might have leisure to interrogate him with reference to his duties, and this very theft. That is if you judge it advisable in me to tamper with the subject unassisted?"

"Your nephew can help you if necessary," replied the imperturbable detective. "I should like to hear what the man, Hopgood, has to say for himself," and he glided back into his old position.

===Chinese===
方才提及的最后那人退出之后，格莱斯先生从屏风后头探出头来。「一伙瞧着像我所愿见的诚实面孔！」他以一种坦率热切的口气说道——这口气与围在他身旁那些焦虑的脸几乎沾不上边。「里头没一个鬼头鬼脑的；那位看门人，霍普古德，又如何？」

「您若要他来，立刻便可传他。」西尔维斯特先生说，「我之所以迟迟没叫，只是为着能从容地就其本职、就这桩窃案本身盘问他。前提是——您认为我独自一人插手此事是得当的？」

「若有必要，您那位舍侄可以帮您。」那位处变不惊的侦探答道。「我倒想听听那个名叫霍普古德的人有何话为自己辩白。」说着，他又悄然滑回原来的位置。

===Original===
But Mr. Sylvester had scarcely reached out his hand to ring the bell by which he usually summoned the janitor, when the agent of Hicks, Saltzer & Co. came in. It was an interruption that demanded instant attention. Saluting the gentleman with his usual proud reserve, he drew his attention to the box lying upon the table.

"This is yours, I believe, sir," said he. "It was found in our vaults this morning in the condition in which you now behold it, and we are anxious to know if its contents are all correct."

"They have been handled," returned the agent, after a careful survey of the various papers that filled the box, "but nothing appears to be missing."

Three persons at least in that room breathed more easily.

===Chinese===
可西尔维斯特先生的手才伸向通常用来传看门人的那枚拉铃，希克斯、萨尔泽公司的代办便走了进来。这是一桩不能不立即应承的打岔。他以他惯有的矜持高傲向那位先生致意，便把桌上那只匣子指给他看。

「我相信这是您的，先生。」他说，「今早我们的保险库里发现了它，便是您此刻所见这副模样。我们急欲知道其中的物件是否一概无误。」

「有人动过。」那位代办把匣中满盛的各式单据仔细审阅一番之后答道，「可看去并未缺什么。」

那屋里至少有三个人，呼吸得轻快了些。

===Original===
