I have never suffered sorrow or experienced wrong, and cannot measure their power to carve the human face with such lines as I beheld on that woman's countenance today. But do not let us talk of her any more. She left us at last, and we found the child's father. Mr. Sylvester," she suddenly asked, "are there to be found in this city, men occupying honorable positions and as such highly esteemed, who like Damocles of old, may be said to sit under the constant terror of a falling sword in the shape of some possible disclosure, that if made, would ruin their position before the world forever?"

===Chinese===
西尔维斯特先生与妻子交换了一个眼色，随后前者问道：「她跟着你来了么，宝拉？」

「没有；她对我说我——可她说的话，我没法重复。」少女猛地一颤，失声叫道。「自从我回了家，」她若有所思地接着说，「我照着镜子，一遍又一遍地端详自己的脸，却无论如何也不能相信她那一番话是真的。我们之间毫无相似之处，过去也绝不可能有过：我断不能承认，在她这一辈子的哪一天里，曾见过镜子里那样一帧画像。」说着，宝拉猛地一扬手，站起身来，指向自己——她这会儿正立着，身影映在奥娜这间闺房里四处林立的高大穿衣镜中的一面里。

「她竟敢拿你与她那样堕落的自己作比？」西尔维斯特先生失声道，目光投在眼前这一幅纯真少女的绝美倩影上——此刻这倩影经镜子的映照，竟成了双份地呈到他眼前。

「不错，我如今是什么模样，她从前也曾是什么模样，至少她这么说。这话也许是真的。我从未尝过忧愁，也未曾受过冤屈，量不出它们究竟有多大的力气，能在人的脸上刻下我今日所见那女人面容上的那种线条。可我们别再谈她了。她到底走了，我们也找到了孩子的父亲。西尔维斯特先生，」她忽然问道，「在这城里，可有那样一些人身居清要之位、并因之而备受尊崇，却又好比古时的达摩克利斯（Damocles）那样，可谓终日坐在一柄行将坠下之剑的恒常恐吓之下——那剑便是某桩可能被揭发的事——一旦揭发出来，便将他们眼前的地位在人前永远毁去？」

===Original===
Mr. Sylvester started as if he had been shot. "Paula!" cried he, and instantly was silent again. He did not look at his wife, but if he had, he would have perceived that even her fair skin was capable of blanching to a yet more startling whiteness, and that her sleepy eyes could flash open with something like expression in their lazy depths.

"I mean," dreamily continued Paula, absorbed in her own remembrance, "that if what we overheard said by the father of that child today is true, some one of our prominent men, whose life is not all it appears, is standing on the verge of possible exposure and shame; that a hound is on his track in the form of a starving man; and that sooner or later he will have to pay the price of an unprincipled creature's silence, or fall into public discredit like some others of whom we have lately read." Then as silence filled the room, she added, "It makes me tremble to think that a man of means and seeming honor should be placed in such a position, but worse still that we may know such a one and be ignorant of his misery and his shame."

"It is getting time for me to dress," murmured Ona, sinking back on her pillow and speaking in her most languid tone of voice. "Could you not hasten your story a little Paula?"

But Mr. Sylvester with a hurried glance at the closing eyes of his wife, requested on the contrary that she would explain herself more definitely. "Ona will pardon the delay," said he, with a set, strained politeness that called up the least little quiver of suppressed sarcasm about the rosy infantile lips that he evidently did not consider it worth his while to notice.

"But that is all," said Paula. However she repeated as nearly as she could just what the boy's father had said. At the conclusion Mr. Sylvester rose.

===Chinese===
西尔维斯特先生猛地一惊，仿佛中弹一般。「宝拉！」他喊了一声，随即便又默不作声。他没看妻子，可他若是看了，便会察觉，就连她那身娇嫩的肌肤，也竟会白得更加骇人，而她那双惺忪的眼睛，也能在慵懒的深处倏地睁开，射出某种近乎神情的东西来。

「我的意思是，」宝拉恍惚地接着说，仍沉浸在自己的回忆里，「如果我们今日偷听到那孩子的父亲所说的话是真的，那么我们这座城里某一位显赫的人物——他的人生并不如表面所见的那般清白——此刻正站在随时可能被揭发、随时可能蒙羞的悬崖边上；有一只猎犬正循着他的踪迹追来，那猎犬化作了一个饿着肚子的人；或迟或早，他总得为这么一个无耻之徒的缄默付上一笔代价，要么便像我们近来所读到的那样几位一样，落得个身败名裂。」屋子里随即静了下来，她又补上一句，「一想到一个有身家、貌似正直的人竟会落到这般境地，我便止不住发抖，可更叫人不寒而栗的是，我们说不定正认识着这样一个人物，却对他所受的煎熬与耻辱一无所知。」

「我该去更衣了。」奥娜咕哝着，倒回枕上，用了她那最最倦怠的嗓音说话。「你不能把你的故事讲得稍快些么，宝拉？」

可西尔维斯特先生匆匆瞥了一眼妻子正阖拢的眼，反倒请她把话说得更明白些。「奥娜会原谅这一点耽搁的。」他说，语气里那一股刻意而紧绷的客气，引得她那玫瑰色的、稚气的双唇边浮起一丝难以察觉的讥讽的轻颤——他显然觉得这一丝轻颤不值得他费神理会。

「可我没有别的了呀。」宝拉说。但她还是尽力把那男孩父亲所说的话原原本本复述了一遍。话音落下，西尔维斯特先生站起了身。

===Original===
"What kind of a looking man was he?" said that gentleman as he crossed to the window.

"Well, as nearly as I can describe, he was tall, dark and seedy, with a shock of black hair and a pair of black whiskers that floated on the wind as he walked. He was evidently of the order of decayed gentleman, and his manner of talking, especially in the profuse use he made of his arms and hands, was decidedly foreign. Yet his speech was pure and without accent."

Mr. Sylvester's face as he asked the next question was comparatively cheerful. "Was the other man with whom he was talking, as dark and foreign as himself?"

"O no, he was round and jovial, a little too insinuating perhaps, in his way of speaking to ladies, but otherwise a well enough appearing man."

Mr. Sylvester bowed and looked at his watch. (Why do gentlemen always consult their watches even in the face of the clock?) "Ona, you are right," said he, "it is time you were dressing for dinner." And concluding with a word or two of sympathy as to the peculiar nature of Paula's adventures as he called them, he hastened from the room and proceeded to his little refuge above.

===Chinese===
「那人长相如何？」那位先生一面说，一面踱到窗边。

「呃，我尽力形容一下吧——他身量高，肤色黑，衣衫寒酸，一头浓密的黑发，两腮一捧黑须，走起路来随风飘动。他显然是那种破落了的绅士一类的人，谈吐的做派——尤其在他那一双手臂不停地大幅比画上——分明是外国派头。可他说话的措辞却很纯粹，并无口音。」

西尔维斯特先生问下一句话时，脸色相比之下倒是轻快了些。「与他对谈的那个人，可也和他一样黝黑、一样像外国人么？」

「嗳，不，那人圆滚滚的，一副和气生财的模样，对女士们说话的姿态或许略嫌太过谄媚了些，不过除此之外倒也算个体面的汉子。」

西尔维斯特先生一颔首，看了看表。（为什么绅士们对着墙上的钟也不肯信，总要瞧一瞧自己的表？）「奥娜，你说得对，」他道，「你该更衣用饭了。」接着，他对宝拉这一日所遇之事——他称之为她的奇遇——又安慰了几句，便匆匆走出房去，上了楼他那间小小的避难所。

===Original===
"He has not asked me what became of the child," thought Paula, with a certain pang of surprise. "I expected him to say, 'Shall we not try and see the little fellow, Paula?' if only to allow me to explain that the child's father would not tell me where they lived. But the later affair has evidently put the child out of his head. And indeed it is only natural that a business man should be more interested in such a fact as I have related, than in the sprained arm of a wretched creature's 'little feller.'" And she turned to assist Ona, who had arisen from her couch and was now absorbed in the intricacies of an uncommonly elaborate toilet.

"Those men did not mention any names?" suddenly queried that lady, looking with an expression of careful anxiety, at the twist of her back hair, in the small hand-mirror she held over her shoulder.

"No," said Paula, dropping a red rose into the blonde locks she was so carefully arranging. "He expressly said he did not know the name of the person to whom he alluded. It was a strange conversation for me to overhear, was it not?" she remarked, happy to have interested her cousin in anything out of the domains of fashion.

"I don't know—certainly—of course—" returned Mrs. Sylvester with some incoherence. "Do you think red looks as well with this black as the lavender would do?" she rambled on in her lightest tone, pulling out a box of feathers.

Paula gave her a little wistful glance of disappointment and decided in favor of the lavender.

"I am bound to look well tonight if I never do so again," said Ona. They were all going to a public reception at which a foreign lord was expected to be present. "How fortunate I am to have a perfect little hairdresser in my own family, without being obliged to send for some gossipy, fussy old Madame with her stories of how such and such a one looked when dressed for the Grand Duke's ball, or how Mrs. So-and-So always gave her more than her price because she rolled up puffs so exquisitely." And stopping to aid the deft girl in substituting the lavender feather for the red rose in her hair—she forgot to ask any more questions.

===Chinese===
「他竟没问我那孩子后来怎么样了。」宝拉心想，心里掠过一丝诧异的刺痛。「我原以为他会说，『宝拉，我们何不去瞧瞧那小家伙？』哪怕只是为了让我好解释，那孩子的父亲不肯告诉我他们住在哪里。可显然是后来的那桩事，把那孩子从他心里挤出去了。说来也是自然，一个做生意的人，对像我方才所述那样一桩事，自然比对一个可怜虫的『小家伙』那只扭伤的胳膊更有兴趣。」想着，她便转过身去帮奥娜——奥娜已从卧榻上起身，这会儿正埋头于一套格外繁复的梳妆的种种关窍之中。

「那两个人没提到什么名字么？」那位夫人忽然问道，把一面小手镜举过肩头，神情慎重而焦灼地端详着脑后发髻的盘法。

「没有。」宝拉说着，将一朵红玫瑰别进她正细心梳理的那一头金发里。「他还特意说，自己并不知道他所指的那个人的名字。这桩对话被我偷听了去，也真是奇了，是不是？」她说道，心里高兴，总算有件衣香鬓影以外的事，引得这位表姐上了心。

「我说不准——自然啦——当然啦——」西尔维斯特夫人答得有些语无伦次。「你看这红色配这身黑，可有淡紫色的好？」她用那最轻快的口气东拉西扯着，拖出了一匣羽毛。

宝拉望了她一眼，神色里有一丝怅然，便替她作主，选了那淡紫色的。

「今夜我定要打扮得好看，哪怕此后再不肯好好打扮一回也罢。」奥娜说。她们一家都要去出席一个公共招待会，据说有一位外邦贵人也将到场。「我多走运啊，自家就有这么一个十全十美的小梳头丫头，不必打发人去请那些多嘴多舌、大惊小怪的老夫人来，那些老婆子满肚子都是某某夫人当年盛装赴大公舞会时是何等模样、某某太太向来多给她赏钱、只因她卷那发卷儿卷得格外精巧之类的故事。」说着，她便停下来，帮这伶俐的姑娘把头发上的红玫瑰换成了淡紫色的羽毛——也便忘了再问什么。

---

===Original===
"Ona," remarked her husband, coming into the room on his way down to dinner—Mrs. Sylvester never dined when she was going to any grand entertainment; it made her look flushed she said—"I am not in the habit of troubling you about your family matters, but have you heard from your father of late?"

Mrs. Sylvester turned from her jewel-casket and calmly surveyed his face. It was fixed and formal, the face he turned to his servants and sometimes—to his wife. "No," said she, with a light little gesture as though she were speaking of the most trivial matter. "In one respect at least, papa is like an angel, his visits are few and far between."

Mr. Sylvester's eyebrows drew heavily together. For a man with a smile of strange sweetness, he could sometimes look very forbidding. "*When* was he here last?" he inquired in a tone more commanding than he knew.

She did not appear to resent it. "Let me see," mused she. "When was it I lost my diamond earring? O I remember, it was on the eve of New Year's day a year ago; I recollect because I had to wear pearls with my garnet brocade," she pettishly sighed. "And papa came the next week, after you had given me the money for a new pair. I have reason to remember *that*, for not a dollar did he leave me."

===Chinese===
「奥娜，」她丈夫开口道——他正下楼去吃饭，顺道进了这间屋子；西尔维斯特夫人但凡要去什么盛大的宴会，是从不吃正餐的，她说吃了会叫她脸上泛红——「我没有打扰你家务事的习惯，可近来你可曾收到过令尊的消息？」

西尔维斯特夫人从她的珠宝匣子前转过身来，从容地端详他的脸。那脸是绷着的、一板一眼的，是他对待仆人、间或——对待妻子时所摆出的那副面孔。「没有。」她说着，做了个轻轻的、毫不在意的小手势，仿佛在说一桩最不相干的小事。「至少在这一点上，爸爸像个天使——他的造访，寥寥无几，隔上好久才有一次。」

西尔维斯特先生的眉头沉沉地拢在了一处。一个笑容之中竟含着那样奇异甜美的人，有时候却也能露出一副极为骇人的脸色。「他上一回上这儿来，是*何时*？」他追问的口气，比他自己所察觉的还要咄咄逼人。

她似乎并不见怪。「让我想想，」她沉吟道，「我那回丢了一只钻石耳环，是什么时候来着？嗳，我想起来了，是一年前元旦前夜的事；我记得清楚，因为我只好戴珍珠配我那件石榴红的缎子衣裳。」她赌气似的叹了一声。「而爸爸是下一周才来的，那时你已经把钱给了我，让我去配新的一副。我可有理由把*那*一回记得清清楚楚，因为他一个子儿也没留给我。」

===Original===
"Ona!" exclaimed her husband, shrinking back in uncontrollable surprise, while his eyes flashed inquiringly to her ears in which two noble diamonds were brilliantly shining.

"O," she cried, just raising one snowy hand to those sparkling ornaments, while a faint blush, the existence of which he had sometimes doubted, swept over her careless face. "I was enabled to procure them in time; but for a whole two months I had to go without diamonds." She did not say that she had bartered her wedding jewels to make up the sum she needed, but he may have understood that without being told.

"And that is the last time you have seen him?" He held her eyes with his, she could not look away.

"The very last, sir; strange to say."

His glance shifted from her face and he turned with a bow towards the door.

"May I ask," she slowly inquired as he moved across the floor, "what is the reason of this sudden interest in poor papa?"

"Certainly," said he, pausing and looking back, not without some emotion of pity in his glance. "I am sometimes struck with a sense of the duty I owe you, in helping you to bear the burden of certain secret responsibilities which I fear may sometimes prove too heavy for you."

She gave a little rippling laugh that only sounded hollow to the image listening in the glass. "You choose strange times in which to be struck," said she, holding up two dresses for his inspection, with a lift of her brows evidently meant as an inquiry as to which he thought the most becoming.

"Conscience is the chooser, not I," declared he, for once allowing himself to ignore the weighty question of dress thus propounded.

His wife gave a little toss of her head and he left the room.

"I should like Edward very much," murmured she in a burst of confidence to her own reflection in the glass, "if only he would not bother himself so much about that same disagreeable conscience."

===Chinese===
「奥娜！」她丈夫失声叫道，不可遏制地惊得往后一缩，目光探询地直射向她双耳——那两只耳上，两颗华贵的钻石正灿烂地闪着光。

「嗳，」她叫了一声，只把一只雪白的手抬到那两件亮闪闪的饰物上，一抹淡淡的红晕——他素来犹疑它是否存在过——从她那张漫不经心的脸上掠过。「我总算及时把它们弄到手了；可足有两个整月，我不得不与钻石无缘。」她没说，她是把陪嫁的珠宝典当了，才凑齐了那一笔钱；可这种事，他不说也未必不明白。

「那便是你最后一次见到他了？」他的目光定定地锁住她的目光，叫她移不开眼去。

「正是最后一回，先生；说来也奇。」

他的目光从她脸上移开，一颔首，转身朝门走去。

「敢问一句，」他穿过屋子时，她慢悠悠地问，「突然这样关心起可怜的爸爸来，是为着什么？」

「自然，」他说着，停下脚步回头望她，目光里并非没有一丝怜悯之情。「我有时会猛然觉得，我对你负有一种义务——要帮你分担某些隐秘的责任之累，那些责任，我怕它有时候会压得你太重。」

她发出一串轻柔起伏的笑声——这笑声，唯有在镜中倾听的那个影子听来，才显得空空荡荡。「你挑的这个时候，可真叫古怪。」她说着，举起两件衣裙呈到他眼前，眉毛一挑，显然是在问他：哪一件更衬她。

「挑时候的是良心，不是我。」他断然道，这回破天荒地放任自己，对眼前这一桩重大的衣着之问不置一词。

他的妻子把头微微一扬，他走出了房门。

「我原会很爱爱德华（Edward）的，」她忽然朝着镜中自己的倒影推心置腹地咕哝道，「只要他不那么为着那个讨厌的良心自寻烦恼就好。」

---

===Original===
"You look unhappy," said Mr. Sylvester to Paula as they came from the dining-room. "Have the adventures of the day made such an impression upon you that you will not be able to enjoy the evening's festivities?"

She lifted her face and the quick smile came.

"I do not like to see your brow so clouded," continued he, smoothing his own to meet her searching eye. "Smiles should sit on the lips of youth, or else why are they so rosy."

"Would you have me smile in face of my first glimpse of wickedness," asked she, but in a gentle tone that robbed her words of half their reproach. "You must remember that I have had but little experience with the world. I have lived all my life in a town of wholesome virtues, and while here I have been kept from contact with anything low or base. I have never known vice, and now all in a moment I feel as if I have been bathed in it."

===Chinese===
「你看上去不开心。」他们一同从餐厅出来时，西尔维斯特先生对宝拉说，「今日的种种奇遇，给你的印象竟深到这般地步，连今夜的欢聚你也无心享受了么？」

她抬起脸，一抹迅疾的微笑浮了上来。

「我不愿见你眉头这样阴郁。」他接着说，一面抚平自己的眉头，迎上她那探询的目光。「笑意原该坐在青春的唇边，否则它们怎会这般红艳。」

「你难道要我头一回窥见邪恶，还能笑得出来么？」她问道，可语气是那样温柔，反倒把她话里那一半责备之意都消去了。「你该记着，我对这世间的事阅历甚浅。我这一生都住在一个风气淳厚的小镇上，到了这里以后，也一直与一切卑微下流之物隔绝。我从未识得罪恶，如今却一下子觉得自己仿佛整个儿沐浴在其中了。」

===Original===
He took her by the hand and drew her gently towards him. "Does your whole being recoil so from evil, my Paula? What will you do in this wicked world? What will you say to the sinner when you meet him—as you must?"

"I don't know; it's a problem I have never been brought to consider. I feel as if launched on a dismal sea for which I have neither chart nor compass. Life was so joyous to me this morning—" a flush swept over her cheek but he did not notice it—"I held, or seemed to hold, a cup of white wine in my hand, but suddenly as I looked at it, it turned black and—"

Ah, the outreach, the dismal breaking away of thought into the unfathomable, that lies in the pause of an *and*!

"And do you refuse to drink a cup across which has fallen a shadow," murmured Mr. Sylvester, his eyes fixed on her face, "the inevitable shadow of that great mass of human frailty and woe which has been accumulating from the foundation of the world?"

"No, no, I cannot, and retain my humanity. If there is such evil in the world, its pressure must drive it across the path of innocence."

"And you accept the cup?"

"I must; but oh, my vanished beliefs! This morning the wine of my life was pure and white, now it is black and befouled. What will make it clean again?"

With a sigh Mr. Sylvester dropped her hand and turned towards the mantelpiece. It was April as I have said, and there was no fire in the grate, but he posed his foot on the fender and looked sadly down at the empty hearthstone.

===Chinese===
他牵起她的手，轻轻将她拉向自己。「我的宝拉，你整个儿身心竟这般地厌拒邪恶么？在这罪恶的世间，你又将如何自处？当你——你必然要——遇见罪人时，你又将对他说些什么？」

「我不知道；这是我从被迫去想过的一个问题。我觉得自己仿佛被抛上了一片阴郁的海，手头既无海图也无罗盘。今天早上，人生于我还如此欢乐——」一阵红晕掠过她的脸颊，可他没留意到——「我手中端着，或者仿佛端着，一杯白葡萄酒，可我瞧着它时，它忽然变黑了，而且——」

唉，那一个「而且」的停顿里所藏的——那向着无底深渊伸出去的、阴郁的脱缰之思！

「那么，落下了阴影的一杯酒，你便不肯饮了么？」西尔维斯特先生低声道，目光定定地望着她的脸，「那是自开天辟地以来，日积月累、堆叠而成的那一大团人之脆弱与苦痛所投下的、无可逃避的阴影？」

「不，不，我不能饮，饮了便失了我的人之为人的本心。世上既有这等邪恶，它的重压，必然会逼着它越界，漫过无辜者的路。」

「那么你接过这杯酒了？」

「我不得不接；可嗳，我那消逝了的信念啊！今早我生命之酒还纯净而洁白，如今它却乌黑污浊。什么才能叫它再变清呢？」

西尔维斯特先生叹息一声，松开了她的手，转身朝壁炉架走去。此时是四月，我已说过，炉膛里并无炉火，可他还是把一只脚踩在炉挡上，伤感地俯视着那空空的炉石。

===Original===
"Paula," said he after a space of pregnant silence, "it had to come. The veil of the temple must be rent in every life. Evil is too near us all for us to tread long upon the flowers without starting up the adders that hide beneath them. You had to have your first look into the cells of darkness, and perhaps it is best you had it here and now. The deeps are for men's eyes as well as the starry heavens."

"Yes, yes."

"There are some persons," he went on slowly, "you know them, who tread the ways of life with their eyelids closed to everything but the strip of velvet lawn on which they choose to walk. Earth's sighs and deep-drawn groans are nothing to them. The world may swing on in its way to perdition; so long as their pathway feels soft, they neither heed nor care. But you do not desire to be one of these, Paula! With your great soul and your strong heart, you would not ask to sit in a flowery maze, while the rest of the world went sliding on and down into wells of destruction, you might have made pools of healing by the touch of your womanly sympathy."

"No, no."

===Chinese===
「宝拉，」经过一段意味深长的沉默，他才开口，「这是迟早要来的。圣殿的幔子，每一段人生里都必将被撕开。邪恶离我们每一个人都太近，我们在花上踩得久了，迟早要惊起藏在花下的蝮蛇。你总得有头一回向黑暗的囚室窥望一眼，而或许，就在此时、就在此地得到这一瞥，倒是最好的。幽深的深渊，与繁星的苍穹一样，都是为人之眼而设的。」

「是，是。」

「世间有一些人，」他缓缓地说下去，「你也认得他们的，他们走在人生路上，紧闭双眼，对一切视而不见，只望着自己脚下选定的那一条丝绒草坪。大地的叹息与深沉的呻吟，于他们毫无干系。这世界尽可以一路朝着沉沦滑去；只要他们脚下的路是软的，他们便既不留心，也不在意。可你并不愿做这种人之一啊，宝拉！以你这博大的灵魂、以你这强健的心，你不会请求坐进一座花团锦簇的迷宫，任由这世界其余的人一路滑向毁灭的深井——你本可以凭你那一颗女性同情心的抚触，造就一池池愈伤之水的。」

「不，不。」

===Original===
"I cannot tell you, I dare not tell you," he went on in a strange pleading voice that tore at the very roots of her heart, and rung in her memory forever, "what evil underlies the whole strata of life! At home and abroad, on our hearthstones and within our offices, the mocking devil sits. You can scarcely walk a block, my little one, without encountering a man or brushing against the dress of a woman across whose soul the black shadow lies heavier than any words of his or hers could tell. What the man you saw today, said of one unhappy being in this city, is true, God help us all, of many. Dark spots are easier acquired than blotted out, my Paula. In business as in society, one needs to carry the white shield of a noble purpose or a self-forgetting love, to escape the dripping of the deadly upas tree that branches above all humanity. I have walked its ways, my darling, and I know of what I speak. Your white robe is spotless but—"

"O there is where the pain comes in," she cried; "there, just there, is where the dagger strikes. She says she was once like me. O, could any temptation, any suffering, any wrong or misfortune that might befall me, ever bring me to where she is! If it could—"

"Paula!" This time his voice came authoritatively. "You are making too much of a frenzied woman's impulsive exclamation. To her darkened and despairing eyes any young woman of a similar style of beauty would have called forth the same remark. It was a sign that she was not entirely given up to evil, that she could remember her youth. Instead of feeling contaminated by her words, you ought to feel, that unconsciously to yourself, your fresh young countenance with its innocent eyes did an angel's work today. They made her recall what she was in the days of her own innocence; and who can tell what may follow such a recollection."

===Chinese===
「我不能告诉你，我不敢告诉你，」他用一种奇异的、哀求般的嗓音接着说，那嗓音扯动了她心头的根本，将在她的记忆里久久回响，「生命整个底层之下，潜伏着怎样的邪恶啊！家里与家外，我们的炉石之上、我们的写字间里，都坐着那个嘲弄万物的魔鬼。我的小家伙，你走过一个街区，都难免要撞上一个男人，或蹭过一个女人的裙裾——那人的灵魂上，那道黑色的阴影，比他或她口中所能说出的任何话语，都还要沉重。你今日所见的那个人，说起这城里某个不幸之人的一番话，求上帝怜悯我们众人吧，其实对许多人来说，都是真话。黑点子沾上容易，要抹去却难啊，我的宝拉。在商界正如在社交界，一个人得擎起一面白盾——那是一桩崇高的志向，或一份忘我的爱——方能逃过那棵罩在全人类头顶、滴着毒液的见血封喉树（upas tree）。我曾走过它底下的路，我的乖孩子，我说的句句都是我所亲历。你这一袭白袍是纤尘不染的，可是——」

「嗳，痛便痛在这里，」她叫道，「那里，就在那里，便是那匕首刺下去的地方。她说她从前也曾像我一样。嗳，难道有什么诱惑、什么苦楚、什么冤屈或厄运——倘若它们降临到我头上——竟能把我带到她如今那个地步！倘若能够——」

「宝拉！」这一回，他的声音带着一股威严。「你把一个癫狂妇人冲动之下的一句叫嚷，未免看得太重了。在她那一双幽暗、绝望的眼里，任何一位容貌风调与之相近的年轻女子，都会引出她同一番话来。她还能记起自己的青春，这恰恰说明她并未彻底沦亡于邪恶。你不仅不该觉得自己被她的话玷污了，反倒应当想到——你自己都不曾觉察——你那张清新年轻的容颜、那一双无辜的眼，今日其实做了一番天使所做的工。它们叫她回想起了她自己清白无邪时的光景；而这样一段回想之后会结出什么来，谁又能说得准呢。」

===Original===
"O Mr. Sylvester," said she, "you fill me with shame. If I could think that—"

"You can, nothing appeals to the heart of crime like the glance of perfect innocence. If evil walks the world, God's ministers walk it also, and none can tell in what glance of the eye or what touch of the hand, that ministry will speak."

It was her turn now to take his hand in hers. "O how good, how thoughtful you are; you have comforted me and you have taught me. I thank you very much."

With a look she did not perceive, he drew his hand away. "I am glad I have helped you, Paula; there is but one thing more to say, and this I would emphasize with every saddened look you have ever met in all your life. Great sins make great sufferers. Side by side came the two dreadful powers of vice and retribution into the world, and side by side will they keep till they sink at last into the awful deeps of the bottomless pit. When you turn your back on a man who has committed a crime, one more door shuts in his darkened spirit."

The tears were falling from Paula's eyes now. He looked at them with strange wistfulness and involuntarily his hand rose to her head, smoothing her locks with fatherly touches. "Do not think," said he, "that I would lessen by a hair's breadth your hatred of evil. I can more easily bear to see the shadow upon your cup of joy than upon the banner of truth you carry. These eyes must lose none of their inner light in glancing compassionately on your fellow-men. Only remember that divinity itself has stooped to rescue, and let the thought make your contact with weary, wicked-hearted humanity a little less trying and a little more hopeful to you. And now, my dear, that is enough of serious talk for today. We are bound for a reception, you know, and it is time we were dressing. Do you want me to tell you a secret?" asked he in a light mysterious tone, as he saw her eyes still filling.

She glanced up with sudden interest.

===Chinese===
「嗳，西尔维斯特先生，」她说，「您叫我无地自容。倘若我能那样想——」

「你能那样想。再没有什么，比一双全然无辜的目光，更能触动罪恶之心。邪恶若在这世间行走，上帝的使者亦在这世间行走，无人能料定，那一份职司将借着哪一道目光、哪一次轻触，而发声说话。」

这一回，轮到她把他的手握进自己的手里。「嗳，您真好，您真体贴；您既安慰了我，又教导了我。多谢您。」

以一种她不曾察觉的神情，他把手抽了回去。「宝拉，我很高兴能帮到你；只有一件事还要说，我要以你这辈子所见过的每一道忧伤的目光，来加重它的分量：大罪造就大苦主。罪恶与报应这两股可怖之力，是并肩来到这世上的，也将并肩同行，直到它们最终一齐沉入那无底深渊的幽暗深处。当你背过身去，不理一个犯了罪的人，他那幽暗的灵魂里，便又有一道门就此阖上。」

宝拉眼中的泪珠，这会儿正一颗颗落下来。他望着那泪水，神情里有一种奇异的渴望，不由自主地抬起手，抚上她的头顶，以慈父般的轻触，抚着她的发丝。「别以为，」他说，「我会让你对邪恶的憎恶，减少一根头发丝的分量。我宁可看你欢乐之杯上投着阴影，也不愿看你所擎的那面真理之旗上投着阴影。你这一双眼，在怜悯地望向你同类的路人时，它内里的那一点光，一丝一毫都不能失。只是要记得，神明本身尚曾屈身以拯救，愿这一念，叫你与这又疲乏又怀着恶念的世人相交接时，能少一分难堪，多一分指望。而今，亲爱的，今日这一席郑重的话，便说到这里够了。我们是要去赴招待会的，你知道，该去更衣了。你要不要我告诉你一个秘密？」他换上一种轻快的、神秘的口吻问道，因为眼见她的眼里还在不断盈起泪来。

她抬起眼，忽然来了兴趣。

===Original===
"I know it is treason," resumed he, "I am fully aware of the grave nature of my offence; but Paula I hate all public receptions, and shall only be able to enjoy myself tonight just so much as I see that you are doing so. Life has its dark portals and its bright ones. This is one that you must enter with your most brilliant smiles."

"And they shall not be lacking," said she. "When a treasure-box of thought is given us, we do not open it and scatter its contents abroad, but lay it away where the heart keeps its secrets, to be opened in the hush of night when we are alone with our own souls and God."

He smiled and she moved towards the door. "Nonetheless do we carry with us wherever we go, the remembrance of our hidden treasure," she smilingly added, looking back upon him from the stair.

And again as upon the first night of her entrance into the house, did he stand below and watch her as she softly went up, her lovely face flashing one moment against the dark background of the luxurious bronze, towering from the platform behind, then glowing with faint and fainter lustre, as the distance widened between them and she vanished in the regions above.

She did not see the toss of his arm with which he threw off the burden that rested upon his soul.

===Chinese===
「我知道这是大逆不道，」他接着说，「我也深知自己这桩罪过干系匪浅；可是宝拉，我痛恨一切公共招待会，今夜我能享几分乐，全要看我见你享了几分乐了。人生有它幽暗的门，也有它明亮的门。这一扇门，你须得以你最明媚的笑容，走进去。」

「这笑容，断不致缺席。」她说，「当一匣珍宝般的思绪赐给了我们，我们并不会把它打开，把里面的物事四处乱撒，而是把它妥帖收好，放在心底藏秘密的地方，等到夜里万籁俱寂、我们独对自身灵魂与上帝之时，才再打开它。」

他笑了笑，她朝门口走去。「可是无论我们走到哪里，」她含笑回眸，从楼梯上回头望他，「我们都随身带着那一匣暗自珍藏的宝贝呀。」

仿佛又重演了她初入这宅子那一夜的情景——他立在楼下，望着她轻轻地拾级而上，她那可爱的脸，在身后那座平台上方耸立的、那一架华美的古铜色装饰物的黝暗背景前，忽地闪亮了一瞬，随即随着他们之间的距离一点点拉开，发出越来越淡、越来越微弱的光，最终隐没在楼上的那一重天地里。

她没有瞧见，他挥臂一甩，把压在他心头的那个重担甩了开去。

## XLI The Work of an Hour / 四十一 一个时辰的功夫

===Original===
> "Base is the slave that pays."

> "Heaven has no rage like love to hatred turned,
> Nor hell a fury like a woman scorned."

===Chinese===
> 「付钱的便是下贱的奴才。」

> 「天庭之怒，无过爱化为恨；
> 地狱之愤，不及女子遭轻慢。」

===Original===
Mr. Sylvester upon leaving the bank, had taken his usual route up town. But after an aimless walk of a few blocks, he suddenly paused, and with a quiet look about him, drew from his pocket the small slip of paper which Bertram had laid on his table the night before, and hurriedly consulted its contents. Instantly an irrepressible exclamation escaped him, and he turned his face to the heavens with the look of one who recognizes the just providence of God. The name which he had just read, was that of the old lover of Jacqueline Japha, Roger Holt, and the address given, was 63 Baxter Street.

===Chinese===
西尔维斯特先生离开银行后，便照往常的路线往上城走去。可漫无目的地走过几个街区之后，他忽地站住了，不动声色地朝四下里一望，从口袋里掏出那张伯特兰前一夜摆在他桌上的小纸条，匆匆又看了一遍上面的字。一声抑制不住的惊叹立刻从他唇间逸出，他抬起脸仰望长天，那神情正如一个认出了上帝公正安排的人。他方才读到的那个名字，正是雅克琳·雅法（Jacqueline Japha）昔日的情人罗杰·霍尔特（Roger Holt），所写的住址，是巴克斯特街（Baxter Street）六十三号。

===Original===
Twilight comes with different aspects to the broad avenues of the rich, and the narrow alleys of the poor. In the reeking slums of Baxter Street, poetry would have had to search long for the purple glamour that makes day's dying hour fair in open fields and perfumed chambers. Even the last dazzling gleam of the sun could awaken no sparkle from the bleared windows of the hideous tenement houses that reared their blank and disfigured walls toward the west. The chill of the night blast and the quick dread that follows in the steps of coming darkness, were all that could enter these regions, unless it was the stealthy shades of vice and disease.

===Chinese===
暮色降临在富人的宽阔大道上，与降临在穷人的窄巷里，景象是迥然不同的。在巴克斯特街那些污浊发臭的贫民窟里，诗情怕是要苦寻许久，才能寻见那一抹紫色的光晕——正是那光晕，令白日将尽的一刻，在开阔的原野上、在芬芳的闺阁中，都显得那样美好。纵是太阳最后一道炫目的余晖，也无法从这些丑陋公寓那灰蒙蒙的窗户上唤出半点光辉；这些楼把一堵堵光秃秃、破烂不堪的墙朝着西方竖起。夜风带来的寒意，还有那随着黑暗的脚步接踵而至的、一闪而过的恐惧，是唯一能进到这些地方的东西；若说此外还有什么，那便是罪恶与疾病那鬼祟的阴影。

===Original===
Mr. Sylvester standing before the darkest and most threatening of the many dark and threatening houses that cumbered the street, was a sight to draw more than one head from the neighboring windows. Had it been earlier, he would have found himself surrounded by a dozen ragged and importunate children; had it been later, he would have run the risk of being garroted by some skulking assassin; as it was, he stood there unmolested, eying the structure that held within its gloomy recesses the once handsome and captivating lover of Jacqueline Japha. He was not the only man who would have hesitated before entering there. Low and insignificant as the building appeared—and its two stories certainly looked dwarfish enough in comparison with the two lofty tenement houses that pressed it upon either side—there was something in its quiet, almost uninhabited aspect that awakened a vague apprehension of lurking danger. A face at a window would have been a relief; even the sight of a customer in the noisome groggery that occupied the ground floor. From the dwellings about, came the hum of voices and now and then the sound of a shrill laugh or a smothered cry, but from this house came nothing, unless it was the slow ooze of a stream of half-melted snow that found its way from under the broken-down doorway to the gutter beyond.

===Chinese===
西尔维斯特先生伫立在街上众多阴沉险恶的宅子中最阴沉、最险恶的一座跟前，这一副模样引得邻近窗口探出了不止一个脑袋。若来得早些，他早被十来个衣衫褴褛、缠人不休的孩童围住了；若来得晚些，他便要冒着被哪个潜伏的凶手从背后扼住喉咙的风险；眼下这个时辰，他安然无事地立在那里，端详着这座把雅克琳·雅法昔日那位俊美迷人的情人困在幽暗深处的屋宇。他并不是唯一一个在这样的门前会踟蹰的人。这房子瞧着又低矮又不起眼——它那两层楼在两旁两座高耸的公寓夹峙之下，确实显得矮小可怜——可它那副安静、几乎像无人居住的模样里，却有种说不清的东西，叫人隐隐觉出一种暗藏凶险的不安。要是有张脸从窗口露一露，倒还能叫人松一口气；哪怕是底层那家臭气熏天的酒铺里有位主顾也好。四下的住户里，传来一片嘈杂的人声，时而还有一声尖锐的笑、或一声压抑的喊叫；可这座房子里却什么声响也没有，若说有什么，那不过是半融的雪水从塌坏的门槛底下缓缓淌出，一直淌到外头的街沟里去的那一道细流。

===Original===
Stepping bravely forward, Mr. Sylvester entered the open door. A flight of bare and rickety steps met his eye. Ascending them, he found himself in a hall which must have been poorly lighted at any time, but which at this late hour was almost dark. It was not very encouraging, but pressing on, he stopped at a door and was about to knock, when his eyes becoming accustomed to the darkness, he detected standing at the foot of the stairs leading to the story above, the tall and silent figure of a woman. It was no common apparition. Like a sentinel at his post, or a spy on the outskirts of the enemy's camp, she stood drawn up against the wall, her whole wasted form quivering with eagerness or some other secret passion; darkness on her brow and uncertainty on her lip. She was listening, or waiting, or both, and that with an entire absorption that prevented her from heeding the approach of a stranger's step. Struck by so sinister a presence in a place so dark and desolate, Mr. Sylvester unconsciously drew back. As he did so, the woman thrilled and looked up, but not at him. A lame child's hesitating and uneven step was heard crossing the floor above, and it was towards it she turned, and for it she composed her whole form into a strange but evil calmness.

===Chinese===
西尔维斯特先生壮起胆子往前迈步，进了那扇洞开的门。映入眼帘的是一道光秃秃、摇摇欲坠的楼梯。登上楼梯，他来到一个过厅——这过厅无论何时想必都是光线昏暗的，而此刻这个钟点，已几乎是漆黑一片了。这光景实在叫人提不起精神，可他仍硬着头皮往前走，在一扇门前停下，正要叩门，双眼渐渐习惯了黑暗，却察觉到通往楼上那道楼梯的脚下，立着一个高大的、无声无息的女人身影。这绝不是寻常的景象。她紧贴着墙立着，像一个守在岗位上的哨兵，又像一个潜伏在敌营外围的细作；她整个瘦削的身形因急切、或某种别的隐秘的激情而微微颤抖；眉宇间一片阴翳，唇边游移不定。她在倾听，或在等候，或兼而有之，而且全神贯注到了这般地步，竟没留神到一个陌生人正走近身来。在这样一处幽暗荒凉的地方，撞见这样一个阴森可怖的身影，西尔维斯特先生不由自主地往后一缩。他这一缩，那女人猛地一激灵，抬起头来，可看的却不是他。楼上有一阵跛足孩童那迟疑而深一脚浅一脚的脚步声穿过地板传下来，她正是朝着那脚步声转过身去，为了那脚步声，她把自己整个身形敛成了一种古怪而邪恶的镇定。

===Original===
"Ah, he let you come then!" Mr. Sylvester heard her exclaim in a low smothered tone, whose attempted lightness did not hide the malevolent nature of her interest.

"Yes," came back in the clear and confiding tones of childhood. "I told him you loved me and gave me candy-balls, and he let me come."

===Chinese===
「啊，他到底让你来了！」西尔维斯特先生听见她用一种低低的、压抑的声调失声说道——那声调里强装的轻快，掩不住她那份关心里那股恶毒的劲儿。

「嗯，」一个清澈而毫不设防的童声答道，「我告诉他你喜欢我，还给我糖球吃，他就让我来了。」

===Original===
A laugh quick and soon smothered, disturbed the surrounding gloom. "You told him I loved you! Well, that is good; I do love you; love you as I do my own eyes that I could crush, crush, forever having lingered on the face of my betrayer!"

The last phrase was muttered, and did not seem to convey any impression to the child. "Hold out your arms and catch me," cried he; "I am going to jump."

She appeared to comply; for he gave a little ringing laugh that was startlingly clear and fresh.

===Chinese===
一声急促的、旋即被按捺下去的笑，扰动了四下的幽暗。「你告诉他我喜欢你！哈，这可真好；我是喜欢你；像喜欢我自己的眼睛一样喜欢你——那双眼睛我恨不能把它们抠出来、揉碎，它们偏要久久地、久久地留在我那个负心人的脸上！」

末了这一句是咬牙切齿地低声嘟囔出来的，似乎并未叫那孩子听出什么名堂。「伸出胳膊接住我，」他喊道，「我要跳下去啦。」

她似乎是依了；因为孩子发出了一声清脆的、银铃般的笑，那笑声清亮新鲜得惊人。

===Original===
"He asked me what your name was," babbled he, as he nestled in her arms. "He is always asking what your name is; Dad forgets, Dad does; or else it's because he's never seen you."

"And what did you tell him?" she asked, ignoring the last remark with an echo of her sarcastic laugh.

"Mrs. Smith, of course."

===Chinese===
「他问过我你叫什么名字，」孩子偎在她怀里，咿咿呀呀地说，「他老爱问你叫什么；爸爸记性不好，爸爸就是那样；要不，就是他从没见过你。」

「那你怎么告诉他来着？」她问，把那句末的话撇开不顾，只回了一串讥诮的笑。

「史密斯太太呗，那还用说。」

===Original===
She threw back her head and her whole form acquired an aspect that made Mr. Sylvester shudder. "That's good," she cried, "Mrs. Smith by all means." Then with a sudden lowering of her face to his—"Mrs. Smith is good to you, isn't she; lets you sit by her fire when she has any, and gives you peanuts to eat and sometimes spares you a penny!"

"Yes, yes," the boy cried.

"Come then," she said, "let's go home."

===Chinese===
她把头往后一仰，整个身形立时显出一种叫西尔维斯特先生看了直打寒颤的神气。「好极了，」她嚷道，「无论如何，就叫我史密斯太太吧。」随即忽然把脸俯到孩子面前——「史密斯太太待你好，是不是；她有火的时候，就让你坐在她火炉边，还给你花生吃，时不时还赏你一个铜板呢！」

「是，是。」男孩嚷着说。

「那么来吧，」她说，「咱们回家去。」

===Original===
She put him down on the floor, and gave him his little crutch. Her manner was not unkind, and yet Mr. Sylvester trembled as he saw the child about to follow her.

"Didn't you ever have any little boys?" the child suddenly asked.

The woman shrank as if a burning steel had been plunged against her breast. Looking down on the frightened child, she hissed out from between her teeth, "Did he tell you to ask me that? Did he dare—" She stopped and pressed her arms against her swelling heart as if she would smother its very beats. "Oh no, of course he didn't tell you; what does he know or care about Mrs. Smith!" Then with a quick gasp and a wild look into the space before her, "My child dead, and her child alive and beloved! What wonder that I hate earth and defy heaven!"

===Chinese===
她把孩子放到地上，递给他那只小拐杖。她的举止倒也并非不和善，可西尔维斯特先生瞧着那孩子就要跟着她走，还是禁不住一阵发颤。

「你难道从没生过小男孩吗？」孩子忽然问道。

那女人猛地一缩，像有一根烧红的钢条扎进了她的胸口。她低头看着那吓了一跳的孩子，从牙缝里嘶嘶地挤出话来：「是他叫你来问我的吗？他敢——」她打住了，把双臂紧紧压在那鼓胀的心口上，像是要把那心跳本身都掐灭。「哦不，当然他没叫你问；史密斯太太的事，他知道什么、又在乎什么！」随即她猛地倒抽一口气，狂乱地朝眼前的虚空望过去，「我的孩子死了，她的孩子却活着、被人疼着！我恨这尘世、我对抗这老天，又有什么可怪的！」

===Original===
She caught the boy by the hand and drew him quickly away. "You will be good to me," he cried, frightened by her manner yet evidently fascinated too, perhaps on account of the faint sparks of kindness that alternated with gusts of passion he did not understand. "You won't hurt me; you'll let me sit by the fire and get warm?"

"Yes, yes."

"And eat a bit of bread with butter on it?"

"Yes, yes."

"Then I'll go."

===Chinese===
她一把攥住孩子的手，急匆匆把他拉走。「你会对我好的，」他嚷着，被她这副神情吓住了，却分明又像被什么勾住了似的——也许是她那阵难懂的暴怒之间，不时闪现的那一丝微弱的善意，叫孩子着迷。「你不会伤害我的；你会让我坐在火炉边暖暖身子，是不是？」

「是，是。」

「还能吃一片抹了黄油的面包？」

「是，是。」

「那我就跟你去。」

===Original===
She drew him down the hall. "Why do you like to have me come to your house?" he prattled away.

She turned on him with a look which unfortunately Mr. Sylvester could not see. "Because your eyes are so blue and your skin is so white; they make me remember her!"

"And who is *her*?"

She laughed and seemed to hug herself in her rage and bitterness. "Your mother!" she cried, and in speaking it, she came upon Mr. Sylvester.

===Chinese===
她拉着孩子顺着过厅往里走。「你为什么喜欢我上你家来呀？」他一路咿咿呀呀地问个不停。

她朝他转过脸去，那神情可惜西尔维斯特先生没能看见。「因为你的眼睛这么蓝，你的皮肤这么白；它们叫我想起她！」

「*她*是谁呀？」

她笑了起来，在那股怨毒与愤恨里像是把整个人都抱紧了。「你娘！」她嚷道。她正嚷着这一声，冷不防撞见了西尔维斯特先生。

===Original===
He at once put out his hand.

"I don't know who you are," said he, "but I do not think you had better take the child out tonight. From what you say, his father is evidently upstairs; if you will give the boy to me, I will take him back and leave him where he belongs."

"You will?" The slow intensity of her tone was indescribable. "Know that I don't bear interference from strangers." And catching up the child, she rushed by him like a flash. "You are probably one of those missionaries who go stealing about unasked into respectable persons' rooms," she called back. "If by any chance you wander into his, tell him his child is in good hands, do you hear, in good hands!" And with a final burst of her hideous laugh, she dashed down the stairs and was gone.

===Chinese===
他立刻把手伸了出去。

「我不认得你是谁，」他说，「可我想，今儿晚上你最好不要把这孩子带出去。听你方才所说，他爹分明就在楼上；你若肯把孩子交给我，我便把他送回去，安顿在他该待的地方。」

「你倒想！」她那一句拖长了的话里那份咬牙切齿的劲儿，简直叫人形容不出。「你且听明白，我向来受不了外人横插一杠。」说着她一把抄起孩子，像一道闪电似的从他身边冲了过去。「你大概是那种传教士罢，不请自来、偷偷摸摸地钻进体面人的屋子里去的，」她回头嚷道，「你要是瞎撞进了他的屋子，就告诉他，他的孩子落在了好人家手里，听见没有，落在了好人家手里！」随着最后一声那难听的笑，她一阵风似的冲下楼梯，转眼便不见了。

===Original===
Mr. Sylvester stood shocked and undecided. His fatherly heart urged him to search at once for the parent of this lame boy, and warn him of the possible results of entrusting his child to a woman with so little command over herself. But upon taking out his watch and finding it later by a good half-hour than he expected, he was so struck with the necessity of completing his errand, that he forgot everything else in his anxiety to confront Holt. Knocking at the first door he came to, he waited. A quick snarl and a surprised, "Come in!" announced that he had scared up some sort of a living being, but whether man or woman he found it impossible to tell, even after the door opened and the creature, whoever it was, rose upon him from a pile of rags scattered in one corner.

"I want Mr. Holt; can you tell me where to find him?"

"Upstairs," was the only reply he received, as the creature settled down again upon its heap of tattered clothing.

===Chinese===
西尔维斯特先生又惊又疑地站在那里，一时没了主意。他那一颗为父的心催着他立刻去寻这跛足孩子的亲人，警示他：把孩子托付给这么一个管不住自己的女人，会有怎样的后果。可他掏出怀表一看，发现竟比自己所料的晚了足足半个钟头，急着要办完这一桩差使的心情当下便占了上风，他满心想的就是赶紧见到霍尔特，别的一切都顾不上了。他在所到头一扇门上叩了叩，便等着。屋里一声急促的恶吼，外加一句惊讶的「进来！」表明他惊动了某种活物；可究竟是男是女，他却无从分辨，纵使门开了，那东西——管它是谁——从角落里一堆破烂的衣絮中朝他探起身来，他依旧辨不出来。

「我找霍尔特先生；能告诉我在哪儿寻得见他吗？」

「楼上。」这是他所得到的唯一一句答话，那东西又重新瘫坐到它那堆破衣烂絮上去了。

===Original===
Fain to be content with this, he went up another flight and opened another door. He was more successful this time; one glance of his eye assured him that the man he was in search of, sat before him. He had never seen Mr. Holt; but the regular if vitiated features of the person upon whom he now intruded, his lank but not ungraceful form, and free if not airy manners, were not so common among the denizens of this unwholesome quarter, that there could be any doubt as to his being the accomplished but degenerate individual whose once attractive air had stolen the heart of Colonel Japha's daughter.

===Chinese===
他无可奈何地只好以此为足，又上了一层楼，推开了另一扇门。这一回他得着了便宜；只消一眼，他便断定他所要找的那个人正坐在眼前。他从未见过霍尔特先生；可眼前这位不速之客所撞见的那个人——五官纵然带了几分堕落的痕迹，却依旧端正匀称；身形瘦削却不失潇洒；举止纵然不似从前那般飘逸，却仍透着几分洒脱——这副品貌，在这污浊不堪的地段居民之中，实属罕见，因此绝无半点疑义：他便是当年那位风度翩翩、如今却堕落了的人，正是他那曾经叫人倾倒的神采，偷走了杰法上校（Colonel Japha）女儿的那颗心。

===Original===
He was sitting in front of a small pine table, and when Mr. Sylvester's eyes first fell upon him, was engaged in watching with a somewhat sinister smile, the final twirl of a solitary nickle which he had set spinning on the board before him. But at the sound of a step at the door, a lightning change passed over his countenance, and rising with a quick anticipatory "Ah!" he turned with hasty action to meet the intruder. A second exclamation and a still more hasty recoil were the result. This was not the face or the form of him whom he had expected.

===Chinese===
他正坐在一张松木小桌前，西尔维斯特先生的目光初次落到他身上时，他正带着几分阴笑，瞧着面前桌板上他自己转起来的一枚孤零零的镍币，看它滴溜溜转到末了。可一听见门口的脚步声，他的脸色便如闪电般一变，立刻站起身，带着一声急促的、期待的「啊！」，匆匆转身来迎这位不速之客。随之而来的，是第二声惊呼，以及一个更为仓促的后退。来者并非他所期待之人的那张脸、那个身形。

===Original===
"Mr. Holt, I believe?" inquired Mr. Sylvester, advancing with his most dignified mien.

The other bowed, but in a doubtful way that for a moment robbed him of his usual air of impudent self-assertion.

"Then I have business with you," continued Mr. Sylvester, laying the man's own card down on the table before him. "My name is Sylvester," he proceeded, with a calmness that surprised himself; "and I am the uncle of the young man upon—whom you are at present presuming to levy blackmail."

===Chinese===
「想必是霍尔特先生罢？」西尔维斯特先生以他最庄重的气度上前问道。

对方鞠了一躬，可那鞠躬的姿态带着几分犹疑，一时之间竟叫他素日那副厚颜无耻、自命不凡的神气去了几分颜色。

「那么，我有一桩买卖要与你谈谈，」西尔维斯特先生接着说，一面把那人自己的名片摆到桌上他面前。「我姓西尔维斯特，」他以一种连自己都惊讶的平静往下说，「我便是眼下被你斗胆敲诈的那位年轻人的叔父。」

===Original===
The assurance which for a moment had deserted the countenance of the other, returned with a flash. "His uncle!" reechoed he, with a low anomalous bow; "then it is from you I may expect the not unreasonable sum which I demand as the price of my attentions to your nephew's interest. Very good, I am not particular from what quarter it comes, so that it does come and that before the clock has struck the hour which I have set as the limit of my forbearance."

"Which is seven o'clock, I believe?"

"Which is seven o'clock."

===Chinese===
方才一时从对方脸上退去的那份镇定，一闪之间又回来了。「他的叔父！」他应声重复，鞠了一个古怪的低躬，「那么，我所索要的、作为我关照令侄利益之代价的那一笔不算过分的款项，便指望从您这儿得了。很好，这笔钱从哪儿来我倒不计较，只要它到手，而且在钟敲响我所定的忍耐限度那个钟点之前到手，便成。」

「那个钟点，想必是七点罢？」

「正是七点。」

===Original===
Mr. Sylvester folded his arms and sternly eyed the man before him. "You still adhere to your intention, then, of forwarding to Mr. Stuyvesant at that hour, the sealed communication now in the hands of your lawyer?"

The smile with which the other responded was like the glint of a partly sheathed dagger. "My lawyer has already received his instructions. Nothing but an immediate countermand on my part, will prevent the communication of which you speak, from going to Mr. Stuyvesant at seven o'clock."

===Chinese===
西尔维斯特先生抱着双臂，冷眼打量着面前这个人。「这么说，你仍旧执意要在那个钟点，把你律师手中那封密封的函件，转交给斯泰弗森特先生？」

对方答以一笑，那笑意恰似一柄半藏半露的匕首上一闪的寒光。「我的律师已经得了吩咐。除非我当下立时撤回成命，否则你所说的那封信，七点钟便会送到斯泰弗森特先生手里。」

===Original===
The sigh which rose in Mr. Sylvester's breast did not disturb the severe immobility of his lip. "Have you ever considered the possibility," said he, "of the man whom you overheard talking in the restaurant in Dey Street two years ago, not being Mr. Bertram Sylvester of the Madison Bank?"

"No," returned the other, with a short, sharp, and wholly undisturbed laugh, "I do not think I ever have."

===Chinese===
西尔维斯特先生胸中涌起的一声叹息，并未搅动他那嘴唇上严厉的、纹丝不动的神色。「你可曾想过，」他说，「两年前在戴伊街（Dey Street）那家餐馆里，你无意中听见说话的那个人，或许并不是麦迪逊银行（Madison Bank）的伯特兰·西尔维斯特先生？」

「没想过。」对方答道，发出一声短促、尖锐、却毫无慌乱的笑，「我想我从没想过。」

===Original===
"Will you give me credit, then, for speaking with reason, when I declare to you that the man you overheard talking in the manner you profess to describe in your communication, was not Mr. Bertram Sylvester?"

A shrug of the shoulders, highly foreign and suggestive, was the other's answer. "It was Mr. Sylvester or it was the devil," proclaimed he—"with all deference to your reason, my good sir; or why are you here?" he keenly added.

Mr. Sylvester did not reply. With a sarcastic twitch of his lips the man took up the nickle with which he had been amusing himself when the former came in, and set it spinning again upon the table. "It is half-past six," remarked he. "It will take me a good half hour to go to my lawyer."

===Chinese===
「那么，我郑重地告诉你，你听见那般说话的人——如你在那封信里所形容的那般——并非伯特兰·西尔维斯特先生，你可肯信我这话并非无的放矢？」

对方只耸了耸肩，那姿态带了几分洋气，又颇有几分意味深长。「不是西尔维斯特先生，便是魔鬼，」他断然道——「我这话对你那一份道理，已是十二分的敬重了，我的好先生；不然，你又何必上这儿来？」他尖锐地补了一句。

西尔维斯特先生没有作答。那人讥诮地把嘴角一撇，又拈起他进来之前自己玩弄的那枚镍币，重新在桌上转了起来。「这会儿六点半，」他说，「我上我律师那里去，得足足花上半个钟头。」

===Original===
Mr. Sylvester made a final effort. "If you could be convinced," said he, "that you have got your grasp upon the wrong man, would you still persist in the course upon which you seem determined?"

With a dexterous sleight-of-hand movement, the man picked up the whirling nickle and laid it flat on the table before him. "A fellow whose whole fortune is represented by a coin like that"—tapping the piece significantly—"is not as easily convinced as a man of your means, perhaps. But if I should be brought to own that I had made a mistake in my man, I should still feel myself justified in proceeding against him, since my very accusation of him seems to be enough to arouse such interest on the part of his friends."

===Chinese===
西尔维斯特先生作了最后一次努力。「要是叫你信了，」他说，「你抓错了人，你还会这么死心眼地照着你似乎打定的主意办下去吗？」

那人手腕极为灵巧地一探，便拈起那枚滴溜溜转着的镍币，平平地摆到面前桌上。「一个家当全在一枚这样的铜板上的汉子，」他意味深长地敲了敲那枚钱，「可不像您这般身家的人那么容易被说服，也许罢。可就算我承认我看错了人，我依旧觉得自己有理由照旧办下去，因为光是我对他的这一桩指控，似乎便已足以叫他的朋友们这般上心了。」

===Original===
"Wretch!" leaped to Mr. Sylvester's lips, but he did not speak it. "His friends," declared he, "have most certainly a great interest in his reputation and his happiness; but they never will pay anything upon coercion to preserve the one or to insure the other."

"They won't!" And for the first time Roger Holt slightly quavered.

"A man's honor and happiness are much, and he will struggle long before he will consent to part from them. But a citizen of a great town like this, owes something to his fellows, and submitting to blackmail is but a poor precedent to set. You will have to proceed as you will, Mr. Holt; neither my nephew nor myself, have any money to give you."

===Chinese===
「无赖！」这两个字直冲到西尔维斯特先生嘴边，可他到底没说出口。「他的朋友们，」他正色道，「自然是大大的关心他的名誉与幸福的；可他们绝不会在胁迫之下，掏一个钱来保住这一桩、或担保那一桩。」

「他们不肯！」罗杰·霍尔特的声音，头一回微微发起颤来。

「一个人的名誉与幸福是要紧的，他必得挣扎良久，才肯松手。可一个大城市里的市民，对他的同胞也负着几分责任；向敲诈低头，立下的可不是什么好榜样。你爱怎么办便怎么办罢，霍尔特先生；无论是我的侄子，还是我自己，都没有一个钱好给你。」

===Original===
The glare in the man's eyes was like that of an aroused tiger. "Do you mean to say," cried he, "that you will not give from your abundance, a paltry thousand dollars to save one of your blood from a suspicion that will never leave him, *never leave him* to the end of his miserable days?"

"I mean to say that not one cent will pass from me to you in payment of a silence, which as a gentleman, you ought to feel it incumbent upon you to preserve unasked, if only to prove to your fellow-men that you have not entirely lost all the instincts of the caste to which you once belonged. Not that I look for anything so disinterested from you," he went on. "A man who could enter the home of a respectable gentleman, and under cover of a brotherly regard, lure into degradation and despair, the woman who was at once its ornament and pride, cannot be expected to practice the virtues of ordinary manhood, much less those of a gentleman and a Christian. He is a wretch, who, whatever his breeding or antecedents, is open to nothing but execration and contempt."

===Chinese===
那人眼里射出的光，像一头被激怒的老虎。「你是要说，」他嚷道，「你竟不肯从你那万贯家财里头，拿出区区一千块钱，来救你一个骨肉至亲，免他背上那永远洗不掉的嫌疑——*永远洗不掉*，直到他那可悲的一生走到尽头？」

「我是要说，休想从我手里过一分钱给你，当作买你这缄默的代价——这缄默，身为一个君子人，你本该觉得不待人求便理当守住的；哪怕只为着向你同类证明，你并未曾把你出身的那个阶层的一切秉性，丢得一干二净。倒并非我指望你做出这等大公无私的事来，」他接着说，「一个人，能踏进一位体面先生的家门，借着一份兄弟般的情谊做幌子，把那家里既是荣耀又是骄傲的女子，诱入堕落与绝望的深渊——这样的人，休指望他恪守寻常男子应守的德行，更不必说一个君子人、一个基督徒应守的德行了。这种无赖，无论他的教养与来历如何，除了招人唾骂、受人鄙夷，再不配得到别的。」

===Original===
With an oath and a quick backward spring, Roger Holt cried out, "Who are you, and by what right do you come here to reproach me with a matter dead and buried, by heaven, a dozen years ago?"

"The right of one who, though a stranger, knows well what you are and what you have done. Colonel Japha himself is dead, but the avenger of his honor yet lives! Roger Holt, *where is Jacqueline Japha*?"

The force with which this was uttered, seemed to confound the man. For a moment he stood silent, his eye upon his guest, then a subtle change took place in his expression; he smiled with a slow devilish meaning, and tossing his head with an airy gesture, lightly remarked:

"You must ask some more constant lover than I. A woman who was charming ten years ago—Bah! what would I be likely to know about her now!"

===Chinese===
罗杰·霍尔特咒骂一声，猛地往后一跳，失声喊道：「你是什么人，凭什么上这儿来，拿一桩老天在上、早埋了十二年的旧事来数落我？」

「凭的是一个虽是外人、却深知你为人、也深知你所行之事的人的资格。杰法上校本人已经死了，可替他雪耻的人还活着！罗杰·霍尔特，*雅克琳·雅法在哪里*？」

这一句问出来的那股气概，似乎把那人镇住了。他默然立了一刻，眼睛盯着他的来客，随即脸上的神情起了微妙的变化；他缓缓地笑了起来，那笑里含着一种阴毒的意味，把头那么潇洒地一甩，轻飘飘地说道：

「这你得去问一位比我更痴情的情人。十年前的一位美人——呸！这会儿我还能知道她什么呢！」

===Original===
"Everything, when that woman is Jacqueline Japha," cried Mr. Sylvester, advancing upon him with a look that would have shaken most men, but which only made the eye of this one burn more eagerly. "Though you might easily wish to give her the slip, she is not one to forget you. If she is alive, you know where she is; speak then, and let the worth of one good action make what amends it can for a long list of evil ones."

"You really want to see the woman, then; enough to pay for it, I mean?"

"The reward which has been offered for news of the fate or whereabouts of Jacqueline Japha, still stands good," was Mr. Sylvester's reply.

The excited stare with which the man received this announcement, slowly subsided into his former subtle look.

===Chinese===
「那便能知道一切，当这女子是雅克琳·雅法，」西尔维斯特先生嚷道，一面逼上前去——那神情早叫大多数人胆寒，可眼前这个人的眼里，却只是烧得更急切了。「你或许巴不得甩脱她，她却不是那种肯把你忘了的人。她若还活着，你便知道她在哪里；那么说罢，让这一桩善举的价值，尽可能地抵偿你那一长串的罪过罢。」

「这么说，你当真想见这女子；我是说，肯出钱来见？」

「为打听雅克琳·雅法的下落或生死而悬赏的那一笔赏金，至今依然作数。」这便是西尔维斯特先生的回答。

那人听见这话，那一阵兴奋的瞪视，缓缓地又化作了先前那副阴鸷的神气。

===Original===
"Well, well," said he, "we will see." The truth was, that he knew no more than the other where this woman was to be found. "If I happen to come across her in any of my wanderings, I shall know where to apply for means to make her welcome. But that is not what at present concerns us. Your nephew is losing ground with every passing minute. In a half-hour more his future will be decided, unless you bid me order my lawyer to delay the forwarding of that communication to Mr. Stuyvesant. In that case—"

"I believe I have already made it plain to you that I have no intentions of interfering with your action in this matter," quoth Mr. Sylvester, turning slowly toward the door. "If you are determined to send your statement, it must go, only—" And here he turned upon the bitterly disappointed man with an aspect whose nobility the other was but little calculated to appreciate—"only when you do so, be particular to state that the person whose story you thus forward to a director of the Madison Bank, is not Bertram Sylvester, the cashier, but Edward Sylvester, his uncle, and the bank's president."

===Chinese===
「好，好，」他说，「咱们走着瞧。」实情却是，这女子究竟在何处，他所知的并不比对方更多。「我要是东游西荡的时候撞见了她，自然晓得该上哪儿去讨一笔钱，好生接待她。可这桩眼下与我们无干。令侄每过一刻便越发不妙。再过半个钟头，他的前程便要定局了——除非你叫我吩咐我的律师，把那封信送往斯泰弗森特先生手里的事往后挪一挪。那样的话——」

「我想我已经跟你说得够明白了：我无意拦你在这一桩事上的手脚，」西尔维斯特先生说着，慢慢地朝门口转过身去。「你若执意要把你的话送去，那便送罢，只是——」说到此处，他朝这个大失所望的人转过脸来，那神情之庄严，对方实在是少有能领会几分——「只是你送出去的时候，务必把话说清楚：你如此这般把他的故事，送给麦迪逊银行的一位董事，故事的主角却并非那位出纳员伯特兰·西尔维斯特，而是爱德华·西尔维斯特（Edward Sylvester），他的叔父，这家银行的行长。」

===Original===
And the stately head bowed and the tall form was about to withdraw, when Holt with an excited tremble that affected even his words, advanced and seized Mr. Sylvester by the arm.

"His uncle!" cried he, "why that is what you—Great heaven!" he exclaimed, falling back with an expression not unmixed with awe, "you are the man and you have denounced yourself!" Then quickly, "Speak again; let me hear your voice."

And Mr. Sylvester with a sad smile, repeated in a slow and meaning tone, "It is but one little *fuss* more!" then as the other cringed, added a dignified, "Good evening, Mr. Holt," and passed swiftly across the room towards the door.

===Chinese===
那高贵的头颅一点，那高大的身形正要转身退去，霍尔特却抢步上前，一把抓住西尔维斯特先生的胳膊，激动得连话音都发着颤。

「他的叔父！」他失声道，「那岂不就是——老天爷在上！」他嚷着，直往后退，脸上的神情里夹着几分骇然，「你便是那个人，你来自首了！」紧接着又道，「你再说一遍；让我听听你的声音。」

西尔维斯特先生带着一丝凄然的笑，以一种缓慢而意味深长的声调，又念了一遍：「这不过是再添一桩小小的*fuss*（折腾）罢了！」见对方缩了一下，又端然补了一句：「霍尔特先生，晚安。」便大步流星地穿过屋子，朝门口走去。

===Original===
What was it that stopped him halfway, and made him look back with such a startled glance at the man he had left behind him? A smell of smoke in the air, the faint yet unmistakable odor of burning wood, as though the house were on fire, or—

Ha! the man himself has discerned it, is on his feet, is at the window, has seen what? His cry of mingled terror and dismay does not reveal. Mr. Sylvester hastens to his side.

===Chinese===
是什么叫他走到一半便站住了，叫他回过头，那样惊愕地望了一眼他所撇在身后的那个人？是一股烟味儿飘在空气里，一股微弱却再分明没有的、烧木头的焦味儿，像是这屋子着了火，要不——

哈！那人自己也闻见了，他一跃而起，扑到窗口，他看见了什么？他那声交织着恐惧与惊慌的叫喊，并未说出来。西尔维斯特先生急忙赶到他身边。

===Original===
The sight which met his eyes, did not for the moment seem sufficient to account for the degree of emotion expressed by the other. To be sure, the lofty tenement-house which towered above them from the other side of the narrow yard upon which the window looked, was oozing with smoke, but there were no flames visible, and as yet no special manifestations of alarm on the part of its occupants. But in an instant, even while they stood there, arose the sudden and awful cry of "Fire!" and at the same moment they beheld the roof and casements before them, swarm with pallid faces, as men, women and children rushed to the first outlet that offered escape, only to shrink back in renewed terror from the deadly gulf that yawned beneath them.

===Chinese===
他眼前所见的景象，一时之间似乎不足以解释对方那般剧烈的神情。诚然，从窗口望出去那片窄院子的对面、高耸在他们头顶之上的那座公寓楼，正往外国着烟，可还看不见火苗，住户们也尚无什么特别的惊扰。可就在一霎之间，便在他们立在那儿的时候，猛地响起了那突如其来、骇人的喊声：「着火啦！」同一刻，他们看见面前那座楼的屋顶和窗户，密密麻麻挤满了苍白的脸——男男女女、老老小小涌向第一个能逃命的出口，却只在重起的恐惧之下，又从他们脚下大张着的、深不见底的险渊前缩了回去。

===Original===
It was horrible, all the more that the fire seem to be somewhere in the basement story, possibly at the foot of the stairs, for none of the poor shrieking wretches before them seemed to make any effort to escape downwards, but rather surged up towards the top of the building, waving their arms as they fled, and filling the dusk with cries that drowned the sound of the coming engines.

The scene appeared to madden Holt. "My boy! my boy! my boy!" rose from his lips in an agonized shriek; then as Mr. Sylvester gave a sudden start, cried out with indiscribable anguish, "He is there, my boy, my own little chap! A woman in that house has bewitched him, and when he is not with me, he is always at her side. O God, curses on my head forever letting him out of my sight! Do you see him, sir? Look for him, I beseech you; he is lame and small; his head would barely reach to the top of the windowsill."

===Chinese===
那光景可怖极了，更可怕的是：那火似乎起在底下哪一层的地下室，也许就在楼梯脚下，因为眼前那些可怜的、尖叫着的苦命人，似乎没有哪一个在往下逃，反倒都朝着楼顶涌上去，一边逃一边挥着胳膊，把那一片暮色塞满了喊声，把救火车赶来的声响都淹没了。

这情景像是把霍尔特逼疯了。「我的孩子！我的孩子！我的孩子！」这一声带着痛楚的尖叫从他唇间冲出；随即，见西尔维斯特先生猛地一怔，他便带着一种无法形容的绝望失声喊道：「他在那里，我的孩子，我自己的小家伙！那楼里有个女人把他迷住了，他不跟着我的时候，总在她身边。哦老天，我竟让他离开过我的眼皮底下，真该万死！你瞧见他了吗，先生？求你帮我找找他；他又跛又小；他的头还够不到窗台的上沿呢。」

===Original===
"And that was your boy!" cried Mr. Sylvester. And struck by an appeal which in spite of his abhorrence of the man at his side, woke every instinct of fatherhood within him, he searched with his glance the long row of windows before them. But before his eye had travelled halfway across the building, he felt the man at his side quiver with sudden agony, and following the direction of his glance, saw a wan, little countenance looking down upon them from a window almost opposite to where they stood.

"It is my boy!" shrieked the man, and in his madness would have leaped from the casement, if Mr. Sylvester had not prevented him.

"You will not help him so," cried the latter. "See, he is only a few feet above a bridge that appears to communicate with the roof of the next house. If he could be let down—"

===Chinese===
「那便是你的孩子！」西尔维斯特先生失声道。这一声哀求，尽管他厌恶身边这个人，却仍把他那一颗为父的天性全都唤醒了；他举起目光，在面前那一长排窗户上来回搜寻。可他的目光还没扫过楼的一半，便觉出身边的人猛地一阵痛苦的颤栗，顺着他的目光望去，只见几乎正对着他们所立之处的那个窗口，一张憔悴的小脸正往下望着他们。

「是我的孩子！」那人一声惨叫，情急发狂之下便要从窗口跳出去，幸而西尔维斯特先生一把拉住了他。

「你这样救不了他，」后者喊道，「你瞧，他离一座桥不过几尺高，那桥像是和隔壁那座楼的屋顶通着。要是能把他顺下去——」

===Original===
But the man had already precipitated himself towards the door of the room in which they were. "Tell him not to jump," he called back. "I am going next door and will reach him in a moment. Tell him to hold on till I come."

Mr. Sylvester at once raised his voice. "Don't jump, little boy Holt. If there is no one there to drop you down, wait for your father. He is going on the bridge and will catch you."

The little fellow seemed to hear, for he immediately held out his arms, but if he spoke, his voice was drowned in the frightful hubbub. Meanwhile the smoke thickened around him, and a dull ominous glare broke out from the midst of the building, against which his weazen little face looked pallid as death.

===Chinese===
可那人早已冲向他们所在的这间屋子的门口。「叫他别跳，」他回头喊，「我上隔壁去，一忽儿便到他那儿。叫他撑住，等我来。」

西尔维斯特先生立刻拔高了嗓门。「别跳，小霍尔特。要是那儿没人把你顺下去，就等你爹。他正上那座桥去，会接住你的。」

那小家伙像是听见了，因为他立时伸出了胳膊，可他若是喊了什么，那声音也被这片可怕的喧闹淹没了。与此同时，他周遭的烟越积越浓，楼当中透出一股暗沉的、不祥的红光，他那皱巴巴的小脸映着那光，白得像死人一样。

===Original===
"His father will be too late," groaned Mr. Sylvester, feeling himself somehow to blame for the child's horrible situation; then observing that the other occupants of the building had all disappeared towards the front, realized that whatever fire-escapes may have been provided, were doubtless in that direction, and raising his voice once more, called out across the yard, "Don't wait any longer, little fellow; follow the rest to the front; you will be burned if you stay there."

But the child did not move, only held out his arms in a way to unman the strongest heart; and presently while Mr. Sylvester was asking himself what could be done, he heard his shrill piping tones rising above the hiss of the flames, and listening, caught the words:

"I cannot get away. She is holding me, Dad. Help your little feller; help me, I'm so afraid of being burnt." And looking closer, Mr. Sylvester discerned the outlines of a woman's head and shoulders above the small white face.

===Chinese===
「他爹要来不及了。」西尔维斯特先生痛苦地喃喃道，觉得自己不知怎的，竟对这孩子这般可怕的处境负有几分干系；随即他察觉到楼里其余的住户都已朝前头不见了，便明白无论预备了什么样的太平梯，想必都在那一边，便又拔高了嗓门，隔着院子喊道：「别再等了，小家伙；跟着大伙儿往前头去；你待在那儿要烧死的。」

可那孩子一动也不动，只是伸出胳膊，那副模样足以叫最硬的心肠也受不住；不多时，西尔维斯特先生正自问怎么办才好，便听见他那尖尖细细的嗓音从火舌的嘶嘶声里透出来，他侧耳一听，听清了这几句：

「我走不掉。她拉着我不放，爸爸。救救你的小家伙罢；救救我，我好怕烧着。」西尔维斯特先生再一细看，在那张小小的白脸之上，辨出了一个女人的头与肩的轮廓。

===Original===
A distinct and positive fear at once seized him. Leaning out, the better to display his own face and figure, he called to that unknown woman to quit her hold and let the child go; but a discordant laugh, rising above the roar of the approaching flames, was his only reply. Sickened with apprehension, he drew back and himself made for the stairs in the wild idea of finding the father. But just then the mad figure of Holt appeared at the door, with frenzy in all his looks.

"I cannot push through the crowd," cried he, "I have fought and struggled and shrieked, but it is all of no use. My boy is burning alive and I cannot reach him." A lurid flame shot at that moment from the building before them, as if in emphasis to his words.

"He is prisoned there by a woman," cried Mr. Sylvester, pointing to the figure whose distorted outlines was every moment becoming more and more visible in the increasing glare. "See, she has him tight in her arms and is pressing him against the windowsill."

===Chinese===
一阵分明而真切的恐惧立刻攫住了他。他把身子探出去，好把自己的脸和身形更清楚地显给那陌生女人看，高声唤她松手、放那孩子走；可回敬他的，只有一声刺耳的笑，从愈来愈近的火焰的呼啸声中透出来。他满心的忧虑叫他几乎作呕，便缩回身子，自己也朝楼梯冲去，发疯似的想去寻那孩子的父亲。可就在这时，霍尔特那疯了似的身影出现在门口，浑身上下都是一股狂乱。

「我挤不过那人堆，」他嚷道，「我又打又挣又叫，全都没用。我的孩子要活活烧死了，可我够不着他。」恰在此时，面前那座楼里射出一道惨红的火光，像是为他的话作一个注脚。

「他被一个女人关在那儿了，」西尔维斯特先生失声喊道，指着那个身影——在越发炽烈的光里，那身影扭歪的轮廓一刻比一刻看得更分明。「你瞧，她把他紧紧抱在怀里，把他往窗台上按。」

===Original===
The man with a terrible recoil, looked in the direction of his child, saw the little white face with its wild expression of conscious terror, saw the face of her who towered implacably behind it, and shrieked appalled.

"Jacqueline!" he cried, and put his hands up before his face as if his eyes had fallen upon an avenging spirit.

"Is that Jacqueline Japha?" asked Mr. Sylvester, dragging down the other's hands and pointing relentlessly towards the ominous figure in the window before him.

"Yes, or her ghost," cried the other, shuddering under a horror that left him little control of his reason.

"Then your boy is lost," murmured Mr. Sylvester, with a vivid remembrance of the words he had overheard. "She will never save her rival's child, never."

===Chinese===
那人猛地一缩，朝着孩子那个方向望去，看见了那张小小的白脸、那脸上带着意识到恐惧的狂乱神情，又看见了在孩子身后冷峻地耸立着的那个女人的脸，骇然失声叫了出来。

「雅克琳！」他喊道，双手抬起来捂住脸，仿佛他的双眼撞见了一个复仇的恶鬼。

「那便是雅克琳·雅法吗？」西尔维斯特先生问，一把拽下对方的双手，毫不容情地指着面前窗口那个不祥的身影。

「是她，要不便是她的鬼魂。」对方颤声嚷道，在一阵让他几乎不能自持的恐惧之下直哆嗦。

「那么你的孩子没救了。」西尔维斯特先生喃喃道，脑海里鲜明地记起他当年无意中听见的那几句话。「她绝不会救她情敌的孩子，绝不会。」

===Original===
The man looked at him with dazed eyes. "She shall save him," he cried, and stretching far out of the window by which he stood, he pointed to the bridge and called out, "Drop him, Jacqueline, don't let him burn. He can still reach the next house if he runs. Save my darling, save him."

But the woman as if waiting for his voice, only threw back her head, and while a bursting flame flashed up behind her, shrieked mockingly back:

"Oh I have frightened you up at last, have I? You can see me now, can you? You can call on Jacqueline now? The brat can make you speak, can he? Well, well, call away, I love to hear your voice. It is music to me even in the face of death."

===Chinese===
那人眼神茫然地望着他。「她得救他，」他喊道，把半个身子远远地探出窗外，指着那座桥大声嚷，「把他放下来，雅克琳，别让他烧着。他要是一跑，还来得及到隔壁那座楼。救救我的心肝，救救他罢。」

可那女人像是就等着他这一声，只把头往后一仰，一团迸射的火光在她身后蹿起的当儿，她讥诮地回嚷过来：

「哦，我到底把你吓出来了，是吗？这会儿你瞧得见我了，是不是？这会儿你会叫雅克琳了？这小崽子能叫你开口，是不是？好，好，你尽管叫罢，我爱听你的声音。便是死到临头，它在我听来，依旧是音乐。」

===Original===
"My boy! my boy," was all he could gasp; "save the child, Jacqueline, only save the child!"

But the harsh scornful laugh she returned, spoke little of saving. "He is so dear," she hissed. "I love the offspring of my rival so much! the child that has taken the place of my own darling, dead before ever I had seen its innocent eyes. Oh yes, yes, I will save it, save it as my own was saved. When I saw the puny infant in your arms the day you passed me with *her*, I swore to be its friend, don't you remember! And I am so much of a one that I stick by him to the death, don't you see?" And raising him up in her arms till his whole stunted body was visible, she turned away her brow and seemed to laugh in the face of the flames.

===Chinese===
「我的孩子！我的孩子！」他只能这样喘着气，「救这孩子，雅克琳，只要救这孩子！」

可她还他以一声尖刻、轻蔑的笑，那笑里全无半点要救人的意思。「他可真叫人疼呢，」她咬牙嘶声道，「我多么爱我情敌的骨血！那个顶替了我那心肝的孩子——我的孩子，我还没来得及看一眼它那双无辜的眼睛便死了。哦，是，是，我会救他的，会像救我自己的孩子那样救他。那天你从我跟前走过，怀里抱着那个孱弱的婴孩，身边是*她*——那一天我便发誓要做他的朋友，你可还记得！我便是这样一个人——我守着他，守到死，你瞧见没有？」说着，她把孩子举了起来，直举到他那一身瘦小的身子整个露了出来；她掉过脸去不看，像是当着火舌的面大笑。

===Original===
The father writhed below in his agony. "Forgive," he cried, "forgive the past and give me back my child. It's all I have to love; it's all I've ever loved. Be merciful, Jacqueline, be merciful!"

Her face flashed back upon him, still and white. "And what mercy have you ever shown to me! Fool, idiot, don't you see I have lived for this hour! To make you feel for once; to make you suffer for once as I have suffered. You love the boy! Roger Holt, I once loved you."

And heedless of the rolling volume of smoke that now began to pour towards her, heedless even of the long tongues of hungry flame that were stretched out as if feeling for her from the distance behind, she stood immovable, gazing down upon the casement where he knelt, with an indescribable and awful smile upon her lips.

===Chinese===
那父亲在下头像这般痛苦地扭动着身子。「饶了我罢，」他嚷道，「饶了过去的那些事，把孩子还给我罢。这是我唯一所爱；这也是我这辈子唯一爱过的。发发慈悲罢，雅克琳，发发慈悲罢！」

她的脸一闪，又转向他，凝然惨白。「可你几曾对我发过慈悲！傻瓜、白痴，你看不出我这些年活着便是为了这一刻么！为的是叫你也尝一尝这滋味；叫你也像我那样，受一次苦。你爱这孩子！罗杰·霍尔特，我曾经爱过你。」

她全然不顾那一团一团朝她涌来的浓烟，甚至全然不顾那一道道贪婪的长长火舌，正从她身后的远处探过来，像是在摸索着找她——她就那样一动不动地立着，俯瞰着他跪着的那个窗口，唇边挂着一丝难以言喻的、可怖的笑。

===Original===
The sight was unbearable. With an instinct of despair both men drew back, when suddenly they saw the woman start, unloose her clasp and drop the child out of her arms upon the bridge. A hissing stream of water had fallen upon the flames, and the shock had taken her by surprise. In a moment the father was himself again.

"Get up, little feller, get up," he cried, "or if you cannot walk, crawl along the bridge to the next house. I see a fireman there; he will lift you in."

But at that moment the flames, till now held under some control, burst from an adjoining window, and caught at the woodwork of the bridge. The father yelled in dismay.

"Hurry, little feller, hurry!" he cried. "Get over towards the next house before it is too late."

===Chinese===
那光景叫人不堪再看。两个人在一种绝望的本能之下，一齐往后一缩，忽然只见那女人浑身一震，松开两臂，把孩子从怀里放下去，落在了那座桥上。原来一道嘶嘶作响的水柱已经浇到了火上，这一下突如其来的惊吓，叫她猝不及防。转眼之间，那父亲又振作了起来。

「站起来，小家伙，站起来，」他嚷道，「你要是走不动，就顺着桥爬到隔壁那座楼去。我瞧见那儿有个救火员；他会把你抱进去。」

可就在这时，方才还稍稍被压制住的火焰，从相邻的一个窗口里猛地蹿了出来，舔向那座桥的木结构。那父亲失声惊叫。

「快，小家伙，快！」他喊道，「趁还来得及，快爬到隔壁那座楼那边去。」

===Original===
But a paralysis seemed to have seized the child; he arose, then stopped, and looking wildly about, shook his head. "I cannot," he cried, "I cannot." And the woman laughed, and with a hug of her empty arms, seemed to throw her taunts into the space before her.

"Are you a demon?" burst from Mr. Sylvester's lips in uncontrollable horror. "Don't you see you can save him if you will? Jump down, then, and carry him across, or your father's curse will follow you to the world beyond."

"Yes, climb down," cried the fireman, "you are lighter than I. Don't waste a minute, a second."

"It is your own child, Jacqueline, your own child!" came from Holt's white lips in final desperation. "I have deceived you; your baby did not die; I wanted to get rid of you and I wanted to save him, so I lied to you. The baby did not die; he lived, and that is he you see lying helpless on the bridge beneath you."

===Chinese===
可那孩子像是被一种麻痹摄住了；他站起身，又站住，茫然四顾，摇了摇头。「我不能，」他嚷道，「我不能。」那女人便笑了起来，空着两臂做出一个搂抱的样子，像是把她的讥嘲抛向眼前的虚空。

「你是魔鬼吗？」这一句话按捺不住地从西尔维斯特先生唇间冲了出来，带着一阵不可抑制的恐惧。「你没瞧见，只要你肯，便能救他吗？那么你跳下去，抱他过去，不然你父亲的诅咒，便要追随你到另一个世界去。」

「对，爬下来，」那救火员喊道，「你比我轻。一分钟、一秒也别耽搁。」

「这是你自己的孩子，雅克琳，你亲生的孩子！」这一句从霍尔特那张惨白的嘴唇上绝望地挤了出来。「我骗了你；你的婴孩并没有死；我要甩脱你，又要救那孩子，便对你撒了谎。那婴孩没有死；他活了下来，你瞧见的那个，无助地躺在你脚下桥上的，便是他。」

===Original===
Not the clutch of an advancing flame could have made her shrink more fearfully. "It is false," she cried; "you are lying now; you want me to save *her* child, and dare to say it is mine."

"As God lives!" he swore, lifting his hand and turning his face to the sky.

Her whole attitude seemed to cry, "No, no," to his assertion but slowly as she stood there, the conviction of its truth seemed to strike her, and her hair rose on her forehead and she swayed to and fro, as if the earth were rolling under her feet. Suddenly she gave a yell, and bounded from the window. Catching the child in her arms, she attempted to regain the refuge beyond, but the flames had not dallied at their work while she hesitated. The bridge was on fire and her retreat was cut off. She did not attempt to escape. Stopping in the centre of the rocking mass, she looked down as only a mother in her last agony can do, on the child she held folded in her arms; then as the flames caught at her floating garments, stooped her head and printed one wild and passionate kiss upon his brow. Another instant and they saw her head rise to the accusing heavens, then all was rush and horror, and the swaying structure fell before their eyes, sweeping its living freight into the courtyard beneath their feet.

===Chinese===
便是逼到跟前的一团火舌，也不能叫她比此刻更骇然地往后一缩。「这是假的，」她嚷道，「这会儿你又在撒谎；你要我救的是*她*的孩子，竟敢说他是我的。」

「皇天在上！」他举起手，把脸转向天空，起誓道。

她的整个姿态似乎都在对他的话喊着「不，不」，可她立在那儿，慢慢地，那话里的真意像是击中了她的心，她前额上的头发都竖了起来，身子前仰后合地晃着，像是脚下的地在打转。忽然她一声尖啸，从窗口纵身跃出。她一把将孩子搂进怀里，想要奔回那一头的避难之所，可她犹豫的那会儿，火焰并没有耽搁它们的工作。桥已经着了火，她的退路被切断了。她没有试图逃生。她在这摇摇欲坠的桥身中央站住，以一个母亲在最后痛苦之中才有的那种神情，俯看怀里紧紧抱住的孩子；随即火舌舔上她飘动的衣衫，她低下头，在他额上印下一个疯狂而炽烈的吻。再一瞬，他们看见她的头抬起来，朝着那谴责她的老天；接着便是一片轰然与恐怖，那摇摇欲坠的桥在他们眼前坍塌下去，把那一船活生生的货物，一齐扫进了他们脚下的院子里。

## XXXIII Two Letters / 三十三 两封信

===Original===
> "I have no other but a woman's reason,

 I think him so, because I think him so."

A woman who has submitted to the undivided attentions of a gentleman for any length of time, feels herself more or less bound to him, whether any special words of devotion have passed between them or not, particularly if from sensitiveness of nature, she has manifested any pleasure in his society. Paula therefore felt as if her wings had been caught in a snare, when Mr. Ensign upon leaving her that evening, put a small note in her hand, saying that he would do himself the pleasure of calling for his reply the next day. She did not need to open it. She knew intuitively the manly honest words with which he would be likely to offer his heart and life for her acceptance; yet she did open it almost as soon as she reached her room, sitting down in her outside wraps for the purpose. She was not disappointed. Every line was earnest, ardent, and respectful. A true love and a happy cheerful home awaited her if—the stupendous meaning latent in an *if*!

===Chinese===
> 「我没有别的理由，不过是女人的理由：
> 我之所以觉得他是这样，是因为我觉得他是这样。」

一位女子，但凡容受一位先生那殷殷不分的殷勤有些时日，无论彼此之间可曾吐露过什么特别的盟誓之语，心里总觉得自己多少已与他有了牵系，倘或她天性敏感、又曾在他陪伴时露出过些许欢悦之色，便尤其如此。因此之故，那天傍晚恩赛先生（Mr. Ensign）向她告辞之际，将一封短笺塞进她手里，说自己次日要赏脸登门恭候回音，宝拉顿觉自己的双翅仿佛落进了罗网。她原不必拆那短笺。她凭直觉便知，他要以怎样磊落诚恳的言辞，将自己的心与一生捧上，求她俯允；可她几乎一回到自己房中，便顾不得脱下外面的披风便坐下来拆了它。她并未失望。字里行间无一不恳切、热烈而敬重。一份真情，一个美满欢愉的家，正在那里等候着她——只要——一个小小的「*只要*」里，竟藏着这般惊天动地的分量！

===Original===
With folded hands lying across the white page, with glance fixed on the fire always kept burning brightly in the grate, she sat querying her own soul and the awful future. He was such a charming companion; life had flashed and glimmered with a thousand lights and colors since she knew him; his very laugh made her want to sing. With him she would move in sunshiny paths, open to the regard of all the world, giving and receiving good. Life would need no veils and love no check. A placid stream would bear her on through fields of smiling verdure. Dread hopes, strange fears, uneasy doubts and vague unrests, would not disturb the heart that rested its faith upon his frank and manly bosom. A breeze blew through his life that would sweep all such evils from the path of her who walked in trust and love by his side. In trust and love; ah! that was it. She trusted him, but did she love him? At one time she had been convinced that she did, else these past few weeks would have owned a different history. He came upon her so brightly amid her gloom; filled her days with such genial thoughts, and drew the surface of her soul so unconsciously after him. It was like a zephyr sweeping over the sea; every billow that leaps to follow seems to own the power of that passing wind. But could she think so now, since she had found that the mere voice and look of another man had power to awaken depths such as she could not name and scarcely as yet had been able to recognize? that though the billows might flow under the genial smile of her young lover, the tide rose only at the call of a deeper voice and a more imposing presence?

===Chinese===
她双手交叠着搁在那雪白的信笺之上，目光定定地望着炉里那始终旺燃着的火，坐着诘问自己的灵魂，也诘问那可畏的未来。他是这样一个迷人的伴侣；自结识他以来，生活便闪烁起千万种光与色；单是他的笑声，便能叫她生出想唱歌的冲动。有他相伴，她便可走在阳光普照的小径上，坦坦荡荡地任世人瞩目，施与受皆是美好。生活不必再蒙上面纱，爱情也不必再有遮拦。一道平静的溪水会载着她，穿过微笑着的一片青翠原野。种种可怖的希冀、莫名的恐惧、不安的疑虑、混沌的焦烦，都扰不乱那颗将信赖停靠在他那磊落男子胸膛上的心。他的生命里有一阵清风，足以将这一切阴霾，从那个怀着信赖与爱意走在他身侧的女子脚下的路上一一拂去。怀着信赖与爱意——啊！症结便在这里。她信赖他，可爱他吗？曾几何时，她也确信自己是爱他的，否则过去这几个星期的光景，便该另有一番来历。他在她那一片阴霾中那般明亮地向她走来；用那般和煦的念头充盈她一日日的时光，又那样不知不觉地牵着她灵魂的表层随他而去。那宛如一阵微风拂过海面；每一道跳荡着紧随其后的波浪，似乎都甘心臣服于那一缕过境之风的力量。可如今她还能这般想吗？自从她发觉，单是另一个人的声音与神色，便足以唤醒她心底那些她唤不出名字、至今尚且几乎辨认不清的深处的波澜——自从她发觉，纵然她那年轻爱人的和煦微笑能教波涛顺流而走，那潮水，却只在另一种更沉的声音、更具威仪的身影的召唤之下，才真正涨起来？

===Original===
She was a thinking spirit and recoiled from yielding too readily to any passing impulse. Love was a sacrament in her eyes; something entirely too precious to be accepted in counterfeit. She must know the secret of her inclinations, must weigh the influence that swayed her, for once given over to earth's sublimest passion, she felt that it would have power to sweep her on to an eternity of bliss or suffering.

===Chinese===
她是一个惯于思索的灵魂，对轻易屈从于任何一时心血来潮，本能地退避三舍。在她眼中，爱情是一件圣事；是太过珍贵的东西，断不能以膺品承之。她非得弄清自己这番心之所向究竟有何隐衷，非得权衡那左右着她的影响，因为一旦将自己交托予人世间这一份至高的激情，她觉得它便有了力量，将她卷向永恒的福乐，抑或永恒的苦痛。

===Original===
She therefore forced herself to probe deep into the past, and pitilessly asked her conscience, what her emotions had been in reference to Mr. Sylvester before she positively knew that love for her as a woman had taken the place of his former fatherly regard. Her blushing cheek seemed to answer for her. Right or wrong, her life had never been complete away from his presence. She was lonesome and unsatisfied. When Mr. Ensign came she thought her previous unrest was explained, but the letter from Cicely describing Mr. Sylvester as sick and sorrowful, had withdrawn the veil from the delusion, and though it had settled again with Mr. Sylvester's studied refusal to accept her devotion, was by this evening's betrayal utterly wrenched away and trampled into oblivion. By every wild throb of her heart at the sound of his voice in her ear, by every out-reaching of her soul to enter into his every mood, by the deep sensation of rest she felt in his presence, and the uneasy longing that absorbed her in his absence, she knew that she loved Mr. Sylvester as she never could his younger, blither, and perhaps nobler rival. Each word spoken by him lay treasured in her heart of hearts. When she thought of manly beauty, his face and figure started upon her from the surrounding shadows, making all romance possible and poetry the truest expression of the human soul. While she lived, he must ever seem the man of men to charm the eye, affect the heart, and move the soul. Yet she hesitated. Why?

===Chinese===
于是她强逼着自己往深处里去探问过去，毫不留情地拷问自己的良知：在西尔维斯特先生（Mr. Sylvester）对她那昔日如父的眷顾，确然变为对一个女子的爱恋之前，她对他怀的，究竟是怎样一番情愫？她那泛上红晕的双颊，似乎已替她作了回答。是也好，非也好，凡不在他跟前，她的生命便从未曾完整过。她是寂寞的，是不满足的。恩赛先生到来之时，她原以为自己先前那一阵不宁已有了交代；可西塞莉（Cicely）那封说他形容憔悴、满目愁烦的信，却已将那一重自欺的幔子撩开了；其后西尔维斯特先生那有意为之、不肯受她一片痴心的婉拒，虽使幔子重又落下，今夜这一番情不自禁的泄露，却到底将它彻底扯下，践踏得不留痕迹。凭他声音在她耳畔响起时心头的每一番狂跳，凭她灵魂那伸展开去、欲入他每一重情绪的每一次探求，凭她在他跟前所觉的那一份深沉的安宁，凭她不在他身边时那吞噬了她的不安的渴念——她知道，她爱西尔维斯特先生，是断不能以爱他那更年轻、更明朗、也许更高尚的情敌之方式去爱的。他所说的每一个字，都如珍宝一般藏在她心的最深处。每当她想起男性的俊美，他的容颜与身影便从四下的阴影里浮现出来，教一切罗曼蒂克皆有可能，教诗歌成为人类灵魂最真切的表达。只要她一息尚存，他便永远是那须眉之中之须眉，夺目、摄心、动魄。然而她仍犹豫。为什么？

===Original===
There is nothing so hard to acknowledge to ourselves as the presence of a blemish in the character of those we love and long to revere. It was like giving herself to the rack to drag from its hiding-place and confront in all its hideous deformity, the doubt which, unconfessed perhaps, had of late mingled with her great reverence and admiring affection for this not easily to be comprehended man. But in this momentous hour she had power to do it. Conscience and self-respect demanded that the image before which she was ready to bow with such abandon, should be worthy her worship. She was not one who could carry offerings to a clouded shrine. She must see the glory shining from between the cherubim. "I must worship with my spirit as well as with my body, and how can I do that if there is a spot on his manhood, or a false note in his heart. If I did but know the secret of his past; why the prisoner sits in the dungeon! He is gentle, he is kindly, he loves goodness and strives to lead me in the paths of purity and wisdom, and yet something that is not good or pure clings to him, which he has never been able to shake loose. I perceive it in his melancholy glance; I catch its accents in his uneven tones; it rises upon me from his most thoughtful words, and makes his taking of a vow fearfully and warningly significant. Yet how much he is honored by his fellow-men, and with what reliance they look up to him for guidance and support. If I only knew the secrets of his heart!" thought she.

===Chinese===
世间最难向自己承认的一件事，便是我们所爱、所渴望敬仰之人，其品性上竟有一处瑕疵。要把那一份疑虑——也许向来未尝说破、近来自隐约地混进了她对这个不易索解的男子那一片深切的崇仰与爱慕里去的疑虑——从它藏身的角落拖出来，让它那副丑陋不堪的本来面目与自己对峙，那无异于将自己送上拉肢刑架。可在这要紧的一刻，她竟有这股力量做这件事。良知与自尊都要求：那尊她打算如此一无保留地俯首膜拜的神像，必当配得上她的敬礼。她原不是那种肯向一座蒙了尘的神龛献祭的人。她非得亲眼看见那荣耀从基路伯之间发亮不可。「我必须以我的灵魂来敬拜，一如以我的肉身来敬拜；可他男子汉的品性上若有一处污点，他心里若有一个错音，我又怎能做得到？但愿我能知道他过去的秘密；那囚犯究竟为何坐在地牢里！他是温文的，他是仁厚的，他爱善，亦勉力引我走在纯洁与智慧的路上；然而有某种既不善、亦不洁的东西缠绕着他，他始终甩它不脱。我从他忧悒的目光里窥见它；从他那不匀的声调里听见它的口吻；它从他最深沉的话语间向我涌来，叫他立下一个誓愿的那一番举动，带上一种既骇人、又含着警诫的意味。然而世人又是何等敬重他，又是怀着何等的倚赖仰望他的指引与扶持啊。要是我能晓得他心里的秘密就好了！」她心想。

===Original===
It was a trembling scale that hung balancing in that young girl's hand that night. On one side, frankness, cheerfulness, manly worth, honest devotion, and a home with every adjunct of peace and prosperity; on the other, love, gratitude, longing, admiration, and a dark shadow enveloping all, called doubt. The scale would not adjust itself. It tore her heart to turn from Mr. Sylvester, it troubled her conscience to dismiss the thought of Mr. Ensign. The question was yet undecided when she rose and began putting away her ornaments for the night.

===Chinese===
那天夜里，那杆秤便在这少女手中颤巍巍地左右悬着。一头，是坦率、开朗、男子的品格、诚挚的痴情，和一处家宅——含着种种安宁与兴旺的附丽；另一头，是爱、是感念、是渴慕、是钦仰，还有一团裹住了这一切的沉沉黑影，名为疑虑。秤盘迟迟不肯持平。要舍下西尔维斯特先生，撕裂了她的心；要撇开恩赛先生这一桩念头，又搅扰了她的良知。这桩抉择尚悬而未决，她已立起身来，开始收拾首饰，预备就寝。

===Original===
What was there on her dressing-table that made her pause with such a start, and cast that look of half beseeching inquiry at her own image in the glass? Only another envelope with her name written upon it. But the way in which she took it in her hand, and the half guilty air with which she stole back with it to the fire, would have satisfied any looker-on I imagine, that conscience or no conscience, debate or no debate, the writer of these lines had gained a hold upon her heart, which no other could dispute.

===Chinese===
梳妆台上究竟是件什么东西，叫她这般猛地一惊，停下脚步，朝着镜中自己的影子，投去那样一缕半带恳求的探询目光？不过是又一只信封，上头写着她的名字罢了。可她把它拿在手里的那副样子，还有她带着它悄悄踅回炉火跟前那半含负疚的神情，我想，已足以令任何一个旁观者确信：不论良心作不作难，不论权衡不权衡，写这封信的人在她心里所占的那一处位置，已是旁人再争不动了的。

===Original===
It was a compactly written note and ran thus:

> "A man is not always responsible for what he does in moments of great suspense or agitation. But if, upon reflection, he finds that he has spoken harshly or acted unwisely, it is his duty to remedy his fault; and therefore it is that I write you this little note. Paula, I love you; not as I once did, with a fatherly longing and a protective delight, but passionately, yearningly, and entirely, with the whole force of my somewhat disappointed life; as a man loves for whom the world has dissolved leaving but one creature in it, and that a woman. I showed you this too plainly tonight. I have no right to startle or intimidate your sweet soul into any relation that might hereafter curb or dissatisfy you; if you can love me freely, with no back-lookings to any younger lover left behind, know that naught you could bestow, can ever equal the world of love and feeling which I long to lavish upon you from my heart of hearts. But if another has already won upon your affections too much for you to give an undivided response to my appeal, then by all the purity and innocence of your nature, forget I have ever marred the past or disturbed the present by any word warmer than that of a father.

===Chinese===
那是一封字迹密密的短笺，写道：

> 「人在极度紧张或激动的当口所作所为，并非总是难辞其咎。但若事后再三思量，发觉自己出言生硬，或行事失当，便有责任去补救自己的过错；我之所以写下这封短笺，正因如此。宝拉，我爱你；不再是从前那一种如父的渴念、护持的欣悦，而是炽烈的、渴切的、毫无保留的，倾尽我这份多历失意的一生之全力；是一个男人那般的爱——对这个男人，世间已消散净尽，只余其一物存焉，而那是一 个女子。今夜，我已将这一切表露得太露骨了。我无权惊吓或胁迫你那温柔的灵魂，去缔结一种日后或会拘束了你、教你不快的牵系；你若能自由地爱我，不再频频回望身后那一位更年轻的爱人，便请知悉：你所能赐予我的一切，皆比不上我渴望从我心的深处尽情倾注于你的那一片爱与情之海。但若另一个人已赢得了你过多的芳心，使你无力对我这一番恳求作一无二的回答，那么，凭你天性里那一切的纯洁与天真，便请忘却我曾以任何比父亲之言更热些的言语，惊扰了过往，搅动了眼前。

===Original===
> "I shall not meet you at breakfast and possibly not at dinner tomorrow, but when evening comes I shall look for my soul's dearer and better half, or my childless manhood's nearest and most cherished friend, as God pleaseth and your own heart and conscience shall decree.

> **Edward Sylvester**

===Chinese===
> 「明日早饭时我将不与你相见，晚饭时多半也不会；可待到傍晚来临，我便要候着我灵魂那更亲、更美好的另一半，或者，我这份无子的余生里至亲至爱的一位朋友——悉随天意，也悉随你自己的心与良知所裁决。

> **爱德华·西尔维斯特（Edward Sylvester）**

===Original===
Miss Belinda was very much surprised to be awakened early the next morning, by a pair of loving arms clasped yearningly about her neck.

Looking up, she descried Paula kneeling beside her bed in the faint morning light, her cheeks burning, and her eyelids drooping; and guessing perhaps how it was, started up from her recumbent position with an energy strongly suggestive of the charger, that smells the battle afar off.

"What has happened?" she asked. "You look as if you had not slept a wink."

For reply Paula pulled aside the curtain at the head of her bed, and slipped into her hand Mr. Ensign's letter. Miss Belinda read it conscientiously through, with many grunts of approval, and having finished it, laid it down with a significant nod, after which she turned and surveyed Paula with keen but cautious scrutiny. "And you don't know what answer to give," she asked.

===Chinese===
第二天清晨，贝琳达小姐（Miss Belinda）被早早叫醒，只觉一双爱意盈盈的手臂渴慕地紧紧搂住了她的脖颈，这一下着实叫她吃了一惊。

她抬眼一瞧，只见宝拉跪在她床边，浸在晨光微明之中，双颊烧得通红，眼皮低垂着；她大约已猜到了七八分，便以一种令人联想起那闻得远处战阵气息的战马的劲头，从卧榻上一跃而起。

「出了什么事？」她问。「你这模样，竟像是一夜没阖过眼。」

宝拉伸手把床头那帘子一撩，将恩赛先生那封信塞进了她手里，权作回答。贝琳达小姐认认真真地把它从头读到尾，一路读一路发出好几声赞同的哼哈之声；读罢，把它放下，意味深长地点了一点头，随即转过身，以一种又锐利又审慎的目光打量起宝拉来。「这么说，你还不知该回一封怎样的信。」她问。

===Original===
"I should," said Paula, "if—Oh aunt, you know what stands in my way! I have seen it in your eyes for some time. There is someone else—"

"But he has not spoken?" vigorously ejaculated her aunt.

Without answering, Paula put into her hand, with a slow reluctance she had not manifested before, a second little note, and then hid her head amid the bedclothes, waiting with quickly beating heart for what her aunt might say.

===Chinese===
「我原该知道的，」宝拉说，「只要——唉，姨母，您晓得挡在我前面的是什么！这一阵子，我都从您眼里看出来了。还有另一个人——」

「可他并没有开口？」姨母铿然地迸出这一句。

宝拉没有作答，以一种先前未曾有过的、缓慢而迟疑的样子，将第二张小笺塞进了她的手里，随即便把头埋进了被褥之中，心头怦怦地急跳着，等候她姨母或会说出什么话来。

===Original===
